context.description: ClickHouse® is a real-time analytics database management system

signals.title: Support Iceberg tables in Unity Catalog and Delta Lake tables in Glue Catalog
signals.text: ## Motivation Both AWS Glue and Databricks Unity Catalog are general-purpose metastores that can host tables in multiple open table formats. In practice: - Unity Catalog supports `DELTA`, `ICEBERG`, `PARQUET`, `CSV`, etc. as `data_source_format`. Iceberg-managed tables in UC have become common (Databricks "Managed Iceberg"). - Glue Data Catalog routinely stores Delta tables alongside Iceberg ones, distinguished by the `table_type` table parameter (`ICEBERG` vs `DELTA`, or by the presence of a `_delta_log/` directory under the storage location). Today ClickHouse hardcodes a single table format per catalog: - `UnityCatalog` accepts only `DELTA` — `src/Databases/DataLake/UnityCatalog.cpp`. - `GlueCatalog` accepts only `ICEBERG` — `src/Databases/DataLake/GlueCatalog.cpp`. As a result, users with mixed-format warehouses cannot expose all of their tables through a single ClickHouse `DataLakeCatalog` database — Iceberg tables in UC are reported as unreadable, and Delta tables in Glue are reported as unreadable. We should drop this assumption and choose the metadata reader per table, based on what the catalog reports. ## Current architecture (relevant pieces) - `DataLake::ICatalog` — `src/Databases/DataLake/ICatalog.h` — catalog interface. Returns `TableMetadata` which carries location, schema, credentials, and optional `DataLakeSpecificProperties` (currently just `iceberg_metadata_file_location`). - `DatabaseDataLake::getConfiguration` -- switches on `catalog->getCatalogType()` and `DatabaseDataLakeStorageType` (S3/Azure/HDFS/Local/Other) to return a hardcoded `Storage{S3,Azure,Local,HDFS}{Iceberg,DeltaLake,Paimon}Configuration`. The choice between Iceberg and Delta is currently a static property of the catalog type: - `UNITY` branch always returns a `*DeltaLakeConfiguration`. - `GLUE` branch always returns a `*IcebergConfiguration`. - The actual table-format-specific metadata reader is selected at template instantiation time via `DataLakeConfiguration<BaseStorageConfig, DataLakeMetadata>` — `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/DataLakeConfiguration.h`. There is no runtime polymorphism on the metadata reader per table within one configuration object. - `getConfiguration` is invoked from `DatabaseDataLake.cpp:646`, after `tryGetTableMetadata` has already been called and `DataLakeSpecificProperties` are available. So at the call site, we already know everything we need to know per table — we just lack a way to thread the "format" through. ## Proposed design ### 1. Add a per-table format to `TableMetadata` Introduce a `DataLakeTableFormat` enum in `src/Databases/DataLake/ICatalog.h`: ```cpp enum class DataLakeTableFormat : uint8_t { Iceberg, DeltaLake, Hudi, Paimon, Unknown, }; ``` Add `setTableFormat` / `getTableFormat` to `DataLake::TableMetadata`. This is the single source of truth that catalog implementations populate per table. ### 2. Teach catalogs to detect both formats - **`GlueCatalog::tryGetTableMetadata`** -- Replace the strict `table_type == "ICEBERG"` check with: - `table_type == "ICEBERG"` → `DataLakeTableFormat::Iceberg`, keep current `metadata_location` resolution. - `table_type == "DELTA"` → `DataLakeTableFormat::DeltaLake`, location points at the table root; no `metadata_location` parameter is expected (the `_delta_log` directory under `Location` is what `DeltaLakeMetadata` reads). - **`UnityCatalog::tryGetTableMetadata`** -- Remove the hardcoded `READABLE_TABLES`/`READABLE_DATA_SOURCE_FORMAT` filter (lines 36-37). Inspect both `securable_kind` and `data_source_format`: - `data_source_format == "DELTA"` → `DataLakeTableFormat::DeltaLake`. - `data_source_format == "ICEBERG"` → `DataLakeTableFormat::Iceberg`. For managed UC Iceberg tables, also retrieve the metadata file location (UC exposes it under a different field than Glue — needs verification against the UC `GET /tables` response, likely via the Iceberg REST shim that UC ships with). - Keep the existing `setTableIsNotReadable` path for anything we still don't recognise (e.g., `PARQUET`, `CSV`). - Vended credentials code paths in both catalogs are format-agnostic and need no changes. ### 3. Route to the right configuration in `DatabaseDataLake::getConfiguration` Change the signature of `getConfiguration` to take the table format as an extra argument, and within the `UNITY` and `GLUE` branches dispatch on it: ```cpp case DatabaseDataLakeCatalogType::GLUE: switch (format) { case DataLakeTableFormat::Iceberg: return std::make_shared<StorageS3IcebergConfiguration>(...); case DataLakeTableFormat::DeltaLake: return std::make_shared<StorageS3DeltaLakeConfiguration>(...); ... } ``` The call site at `DatabaseDataLake.cpp:646` already has the `TableMetadata` in scope, so it can pass `table_metadata.getTableFormat()` directly. For "fake" (`Other`) storage tables, fall back to `StorageLocalIcebergConfiguration` as today — the goal there is just `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, not reading.
signals.author: alesapin

signals.title: Parallelize Iceberg delete-manifest processing
signals.text: ### Problem `IcebergIterator`'s constructor synchronously drains every DELETE manifest in the snapshot before it starts the background data-file producer: ```cpp auto delete_file = deletes_iterator.next(); while (delete_file.has_value()) { if (delete_file.value()->parsed_entry->equality_ids.has_value()) equality_deletes_files.emplace_back(std::move(delete_file.value())); else position_deletes_files.emplace_back(std::move(delete_file.value())); delete_file = deletes_iterator.next(); } std::sort(equality_deletes_files.begin(), equality_deletes_files.end()); std::sort(position_deletes_files.begin(), position_deletes_files.end()); producer_task.emplace(...); ``` This means: 1. **Query startup is blocked** on a sequential walk of all DELETE manifests. Each manifest fetch is an object-storage round-trip; their parsing is independent and fully parallelizable. 2. The data-file producer thread does not start until deletes are fully loaded — wasted overlap with the network-bound delete reads. For snapshots with many delete manifests (large copy-on-write / merge-on-read tables under heavy update load), this dominates planning time. ### Proposed approach **Parallel delete-manifest fetch.** Replace `SingleThreadIcebergKeysIterator` walking DELETE manifests one-by-one with a worker pool that fetches and parses K manifests concurrently. `ManifestFileIterator` is already thread-safe internally (atomic `current_row_index`, mutex-guarded output vectors), so the only change is to dispatch multiple manifest fetches in parallel and merge the results.
signals.author: alesapin

signals.title: parallel_hash join algorithm does not support join conditions with multiple ORs
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Use case The `parallel_hash` join algorithm currently does not support `JOIN ... ON` conditions that contain multiple OR-ed equality groups (disjuncts), e.g.: ```sql SELECT * FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON (t1.a = t2.a AND t1.b = t2.b) OR (t1.c = t2.c) SETTINGS join_algorithm = 'parallel_hash'; ``` Only the `hash` algorithm supports this. When `parallel_hash` is requested for such a query, planning fails with: > **NOT_IMPLEMENTED**: Only `hash` join supports multiple ORs for keys in JOIN ON section This is a important feature-completeness gap: users who rely on `parallel_hash` (for throughput) or `grace_hash` (for memory-bounded joins of large tables) lose those capabilities as soon as their `ON` condition uses multiple ORs. ### Describe the solution you'd like Add support for multiple OR-ed disjuncts in the `parallel_hash` algorithm so it reaches parity with the `hash` algorithm. ### Describe alternatives you've considered Falling back to the `hash` algorithm (current behavior with `join_algorithm` lists that include `hash`/`auto`), which loses the parallelism / memory-bounding benefits the user asked for. ### Additional context Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107591 Both algorithms partition rows by join keys: - `parallel_hash` (`ConcurrentHashJoin`) dispatches blocks into buckets by hashing the key columns. - `grace_hash` (`GraceHashJoin`) spills/partitions data into buckets on disk by the key columns. With multiple disjuncts, each disjunct has a *different* set of keys, so a single partitioning of the data is no longer sufficient - conceptually we would need multiple simultaneous partitionings of the same data (one per disjunct, or some unified scheme). This affects the core design of both algorithms, not just a guard check.
signals.author: ayakovlev-clickhouse

signals.title: Flaky test: 02669_alter_modify_to_nullable (ALTER MODIFY -> Nullable metadata-only optimization falls back to full rewrite)
signals.text: **Flaky test:** `02669_alter_modify_to_nullable` **Check:** `Fast test` (and occasionally regular `Stateless tests`) CIDB (90 days): 11 failures across 6 distinct PRs, **0 on master**. 6 on `Fast test`, 5 on randomized `Stateless tests` jobs. ### Symptom The test creates two parts, then `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN s Nullable(String)` and asserts the metadata-only conversion optimization fires for the Default-serialized part 1 (no data rewrite, `read_rows = 0`) while part 2 (Sparse) is fully rewritten. Reference: ``` 1_1_1_0_3 String Default <- part 1: metadata-only (type stays String, read_rows 0) 2_2_2_0_3 Nullable(String) Default ... 1_1_1_0_3 0 2_2_2_0_3 10000 ``` On the flaky runs, **part 1 is fully rewritten instead** (`read_rows = 10000`, type becomes `Nullable(String)`): ``` -1_1_1_0_3 String Default +1_1_1_0_3 Nullable(String) Default -1_1_1_0_3 0 +1_1_1_0_3 10000 ``` Data results are always correct (the `count/groupUniqArray` lines match) - only the optimization-detail assertion flips. ### Root cause (confirmed locally) `MutateTask.cpp::canSkipConversionToNullable` returns `false` (forcing a full rewrite) for part 1 when **any** of: 1. serialization kind != `DEFAULT`, 2. the column has statistics (`column_desc->statistics` not empty), 3. the `MODIFY COLUMN` mutation is combined with another data mutation on the same part. For the test's intended scenario (isolated single `MODIFY`, Default-serialized part, `auto_statistics_types = ''`) all three are excluded, so the metadata-only path is taken deterministically - I confirmed this with ~4500 local runs (isolated, under concurrent-mutation load, `-j 16` parallel runner, memory pressure): 0 reproductions. I could reproduce the full-rewrite signature deterministically only by either (a) giving the column statistics (e.g. not overriding the global default `auto_statistics_types = 'minmax, uniq'`), or (b) **batching the `MODIFY` with another pending data mutation** - then part 1 is fully rewritten and `read_rows = 10000`, matching the CI failure exactly. This strongly suggests the CI flake is the `MODIFY` mutation **not running in isolation** on the loaded Fast-test runner (it gets scheduled/combined with another mutation entry, so the per-part metadata-only optimization no longer applies). The test implicitly assumes the mutation is standalone. ### Proposed fix Make the assertion robust to mutation scheduling without weakening what it verifies. Options: 1. Assert the optimization more directly/deterministically (e.g. via `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` around the `INSERT`s and an explicit single-mutation submission), or 2. Relax only the per-part `read_rows` assertion while keeping the type/serialization assertions that prove the optimization fired. I have the full local analysis (exact reproductions of each trigger) and am happy to open a PR with whichever direction you prefer. Since the optimization is yours, I wanted to confirm the intended approach before touching the test rather than guess. Reference report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/108734/169355a72b46da8dfb8b43cfb4d9abface24ca50/fast_test
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Apply `SETTINGS` from the `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` definition to it's inserts
signals.text: ### Feature description Currently, query-level settings that affect MV writes (e.g. `deduplicate_blocks_in_dependent_materialized_views`) can only be controlled via the INSERT statement or user profiles. They propagate correctly from the INSERT context to the MV's write context, but there is no way to declare them on the `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` definition itself. The existing workarounds all require controlling the insert caller rather than the MV: - Set the setting on every INSERT statement (requires all callers to cooperate) - Set the setting in the user profile of the inserting user (requires controlling which user performs inserts, or creating a dedicated profile per use case) Neither approach lets the MV owner encode the intended behavior directly in the MV definition, where it is most discoverable and closest to the logic it affects. ### Proposed solution Allow a `SETTINGS` clause on `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` that would be applied to the MV's internal write context, overriding the session/profile value for that specific MV. Example: ```sql CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv TO target_table SETTINGS deduplicate_blocks_in_dependent_materialized_views = 0 AS SELECT ... ``` ### Settings that would be valuable at the MV level | Setting | Why | |---|---| | `deduplicate_blocks_in_dependent_materialized_views` | Pin dedup behavior on the MV regardless of the caller | | `materialized_views_ignore_errors` | Currently all-or-nothing across all MVs — per-MV would let you mark specific MVs as best-effort without silently swallowing errors in critical ones | | `async_insert` | Force the MV's writes through the async insert path without requiring the insert caller to set it — useful for high-fanout MVs where MV writes shouldn't block the source insert | | `insert_deduplicate` | Control whether the MV's write to the target table deduplicates at all | | `insert_quorum` / `insert_quorum_timeout` | Per-MV write quorum for replicated targets — some MVs may need strong consistency, others don't | | `max_insert_block_size` | Tune memory/throughput tradeoff per MV independently of the source insert block size | ### Use case The MV owner wants to declare write behavior as part of the MV definition itself — making it self-contained and not dependent on how callers or user profiles are configured. This is especially useful when the MV is part of a shared schema managed independently from the inserting services. ### Related - `deduplicate_blocks_in_dependent_materialized_views` - Similar precedent: `CREATE TABLE ... SETTINGS`, `POPULATE` clause on MVs

signals.title: Apache Polaris REST Catalog with Vended Credentials on On-Prem Deployment
signals.text: ### Company or project name Lowes ### Question I am using an on-premises Apache Polaris custom REST catalog with ClickHouse. I have configured vended credentials and provided the STS endpoint, AWS Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, and Session Token. However, ClickHouse does not appear to persist or use these credentials. As a result, when ClickHouse attempts to access the S3 storage, it fails with a 403 Forbidden error. Could you please clarify: Whether ClickHouse currently supports vended credentials with an on-premises Apache Polaris REST catalog? If there are any additional configuration steps required to enable STS-based temporary credentials? Whether this is a known issue or a limitation in the current implementation? Any guidance would be appreciated

signals.title: A `WHERE` predicate on an `arrayJoin`'d column can be rewritten into `arrayFilter` so the array is filtered before expansion
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse customer ### Use case Queries that unnest one or more `Array` columns with `arrayJoin` (or `ARRAY JOIN`) and then select a few specific elements in `WHERE` are a very common pattern (tag/label arrays, event attribute arrays, key-value arrays stored as parallel arrays). Today ClickHouse first materializes the full expansion and only then applies the filter, so a query that ultimately returns one row per source row can transiently produce `length(A) * length(B) * length(C)` rows per source row. The work and the memory spent on those rows is unnecessary, and with several `arrayJoin` calls in one query it's multiplicative. Example: ```sql SELECT arrayJoin(A) AS a, arrayJoin(B) AS b, arrayJoin(C) AS c FROM t WHERE a = 'X-A' AND b = 'X-B' AND c = 'X-C'; ``` is equivalent to, but much slower and more memory hungry than, the manual rewrite: ```sql SELECT arrayJoin(arrayFilter(x -> x = 'X-A', A)) AS a, arrayJoin(arrayFilter(x -> x = 'X-B', B)) AS b, arrayJoin(arrayFilter(x -> x = 'X-C', C)) AS c FROM t; ``` ### Describe the solution you'd like Add an optimization that pushes a WHERE conjunct that constrains an arrayJoin'd column into an arrayFilter over the source array, i.e. rewrite `arrayJoin(expr) AS a ... WHERE f(a)` into `arrayJoin(arrayFilter(x -> f(x), expr)) AS a` and drop the conjunct from WHERE when it becomes redundant. Conditions under which the rewrite is applicable: 1. The predicate is a top-level conjunct of WHERE (an AND operand). OR across different array-join columns must not be rewritten. 2. The conjunct depends on exactly one arrayJoin'd column. Other columns it references must be row-constant (not produced by an arrayJoin); those are captured by the lambda, which arrayFilter already supports. A conjunct relating two different arrayJoin'd columns (e.g. a = b) cannot be rewritten. 3. The predicate must be deterministic and stateless (exclude rand, runningAccumulate, neighbor, and anything else whose result depends on evaluation order or position in the stream). 4. Multi-array `ARRAY JOIN a, b` is not supported ### Describe alternatives you've considered Writing `arrayJoin(arrayFilter(...))` by hand. This works and is the current workaround. ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: Parquet fails to write Nullable(Tuple) correctly
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe the unexpected behaviour When writing a Nullable(Tuple(...)) column (including the geo aliases, Nullable(Point), Nullable(Ring) element types, Array(Nullable(Point))) to Parquet, the tuple's own null map is discarded: the schema written is a required group with nullable leaves, so Nullable(Point) comes out as Tuple(1 Nullable(Float64), 2 Nullable(Float64)). Reading the file back with the original schema fails with Code: 53 ... Requested type of column p doesn't match parquet schema: parquet type is Tuple, requested type is Nullable(Point) (TYPE_MISMATCH); reading with schema inference turns NULL row into (NULL,NULL) Parquet can express this (an optional group), and Arrow, ArrowStream, & ORC all round-trip correctly. `output_format_parquet_use_custom_encoder` 1 and 0 produce the same schema. ### How to reproduce Repro on 26.6.1.431: ``` -- clickhouse local --allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type=1 INSERT INTO FUNCTION file('/tmp/np.parquet', Parquet, 'p Nullable(Point)') SELECT * FROM values('p Nullable(Point)', (1,2), (NULL)); DESCRIBE file('/tmp/np.parquet', Parquet); -- p Tuple(`1` Nullable(Float64), `2` Nullable(Float64)) SELECT * FROM file('/tmp/np.parquet', Parquet, 'p Nullable(Point)'); -- Code: 53. DB::Exception: ... parquet type is Tuple, requested type is Nullable(Point). (TYPE_MISMATCH) SELECT * FROM file('/tmp/np.parquet', Parquet); -- (1,2) then (NULL,NULL), NULL row lost ``` Same for `Nullable(Tuple(a UInt8, b String))` & `Array(Nullable(Point))` ### Expected behavior round trip preserves NULL ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: Introspection (plan fragment dependencies, open telemetry, ...)
signals.text: Extend the existing single-node telemetry/tracing infrastructure so that it also covers distributed execution, giving full end-to-end visibility into how a query plan is broken up and executed across the cluster. This should include: - Plan fragment dependencies: capturing which plan fragments are sent to which nodes, and how fragments depend on/relate to one another (parent/child relationships, data exchange between fragments). - Cross-node trace propagation: ensuring the OpenTelemetry trace context (trace ID, span ID) initiated on the coordinator/initiator node is correctly propagated to all participating nodes, so spans from remote fragments attach to the same distributed trace rather than starting new, disconnected traces. - Per-fragment spans: each node should emit spans for the fragment(s) it executes, mirroring the granularity already available for single-node execution (e.g., per-stage/per-operator spans), so a full trace shows both the "shape" of the distributed plan and per-node execution detail. - Consistency with existing single-node model: reuse the current telemetry/tracing abstractions and conventions where possible, rather than introducing a parallel mechanism, so single-node and distributed traces are structurally consistent and can be visualized/analyzed the same way. - Current Plan: - **[done]** PR 1: **Fix distributed trace propagation** by adding the OpenTelemetry context to the AsyncTaskExecutor Obj allowing OpenTelemetry to be part of the task execution like the ThreadPool behaviour, one telemetry span per AsyncTask. As a result, CLIENT span appears for distributed SELECTs and remote SERVER spans parent correctly under it. - **[doing]** PR 2: **Write sampled trace context back into ClientInfo** and enable trace id inside the client info when the query span is created. - **[doing]** PR 3: **Per-shard spans on the classic distributed path**. Make the PR1 fiber holder the per-shard fragment span so RemoteQueryExecutor can attach clickhouse.cluster, clickhouse.shard_num, clickhouse.processed_stage, clickhouse.query_id, clickhouse.initial_query_id, clickhouse.target_host. - PR 4: **Parallel replicas coverage: coordinator spans** Full coordinator coverage (PR1 already fixes propagation for replicas; PR3 gives per-replica connection spans and this PR will make sure the information from replicas are emitted and summarized. - PR 5: **Trace propagation to stateless workers + worker task span** Make the make_distributed_plan worker path traced. - PR 6: **Initiator-side fragment DAG spans.** Record the fragment DAG at execution time on the initiator. So a trace shows both the shape of the distributed plan and where each fragment ran. - PR 7: **EXPLAIN DISTRIBUTED** A new ExplainKind that builds the fragment DAG without executing and renders stages, dependencies, exchanges, and (optionally) task-to-host assignments. Introspection surface.
signals.author: diegomestre2

signals.title: Parsing a Tuple to JSON fails when a string field stores unencoded binary data
signals.text: ### Company or project name Use Case: I am ingesting event data to a self-hosted clickhouse instance that may include fields with raw binary objects without an encoding. Due to the dynamic nature of the upstream sources (potentially breaking schema changes at any given restart) I want to use JSON for the dynamic pathing and type inference it provides. ### Describe what's wrong The String data type from my understanding is used to store binary data of any description and does not need to necessarily be utf8 encoded data, in fact string assumes no encoding. However, when a string column with binary data is part of a tuple that is parsed to JSON, the parsing fails when converting, seemingly due to the fact that the strings may contain invalid utf-8 characters. The error I have seen is as below. Received exception from server (version 26.7.1): Code: 117. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Cannot parse JSON object here: {"test":"e�\u0013��-\u0010\u0013 ��R�Q8�"}: while executing 'FUNCTION CAST(__table1.event :: 2, 'JSON'_String :: 1) -> CAST(__table1.event, 'JSON'_String) JSON : 0'. (INCORRECT_DATA) (query: SELECT event::JSON FROM test_table; -- Fails) I have reproduced with a bare-bones example here: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/f253f905-4692-40f1-89e8-22245383d726 ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce On latest clickhouse version, the below script shows a way to replicate the failure condition. ``` CREATE TABLE test_table ( event Tuple(test String), ) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO test_table (event) VALUES (('this is a test',)); SELECT event::JSON FROM test_table; -- Succeeds INSERT INTO test_table (event) VALUES ((randomString(16),)); SELECT event::JSON FROM test_table; -- Fails ``` ### Expected behavior _No response_ ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: Logical error "No set is registered for key" in `ReadFromMerge::getModifiedQueryInfo` for a `merge()` table with ALIAS columns
signals.text: Found by AST fuzzer inside a stress test run (arm_msan), on a branch that had just merged `master` (the PR only touches the `UNDROP TABLE` busy-wait, and no frame of the trace involves that code): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113263&sha=b035f1d93d57d9465ec2e650e661dcb1dc1e01d0&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29 The query: ```sql SELECT * FROM merge(currentDatabase(), '.+') LIMIT -326, 33 FORMAT ORC ``` failed with a logical error and aborted the server (sanitizer build): ``` Logical error: 'No set is registered for key __set_787892275130216495_1729409850012015669(UInt8)'. ``` Stack trace (key frames): ``` 13. src/Planner/PlannerActionsVisitor.cpp:802: DB::(anonymous namespace)::PlannerActionsVisitorImpl::visitImpl(...) 14. src/Planner/PlannerActionsVisitor.cpp:802: DB::(anonymous namespace)::PlannerActionsVisitorImpl::visitImpl(...) 15. src/Planner/PlannerActionsVisitor.cpp:1443: DB::PlannerActionsVisitor::visit(DB::ActionsDAG&, ...) 16. src/Storages/StorageMerge.cpp:1220: DB::ReadFromMerge::getModifiedQueryInfo(...) 17. src/Storages/StorageMerge.cpp:877: DB::ReadFromMerge::createChildrenPlans(DB::SelectQueryInfo&) const 18. src/Storages/StorageMerge.cpp:687: DB::ReadFromMerge::filterTablesAndCreateChildrenPlans() 19. src/Storages/StorageMerge.cpp:1827: DB::ReadFromMerge::applyFilters(DB::ActionDAGNodes) 20. src/Processors/QueryPlan/SourceStepWithFilter.h:60: DB::SourceStepWithFilterBase::applyFilters() 21. src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizePrimaryKeyConditionAndLimit.cpp:83: DB::QueryPlanOptimizations::optimizePrimaryKeyConditionAndLimit(...) ``` Server version 26.8.1.1, git hash `b03887595ef5428ba9a171c6f7cb713ed2568388` (the CI build of the PR branch merged with `master` as of 2026-08-06). The failing code path: `ReadFromMerge::getModifiedQueryInfo` handles ALIAS columns of a `merge()` child table by resolving the alias expression with a fresh `QueryAnalysisPass` and then feeding the resolved node to a `PlannerActionsVisitor` constructed over `modified_query_info.planner_context` (`src/Storages/StorageMerge.cpp:1206-1228`). If the alias expression (or another column expression reached this way) contains an `IN`, the corresponding set is looked up in the planner context's `PreparedSets`, where it was never registered — hence `No set is registered for key __set_…`. The exact table definitions that triggered it in the stress run are unknown (the database contained leftover tables from many stateless tests); a standalone reproducer with a plain `x IN (1, 2, 3)` ALIAS column does not trigger it, so an additional condition (e.g. a specific filter shape reaching `applyFilters`, or a specific child-table schema mix) is involved. Possibly related (same error message, different reported paths): https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107603, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112219 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113263 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #113757 - Merged into: `26.8.1.951` (included in `26.8` and later) - Backported to: `26.7.5.7`, `26.6.4.6`, `26.5.8.8` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` takes no merge guard and collides with a concurrent merge on the same temporary directory: `Temporary part tmp_merge_all_1_1_1 already added`
signals.text: ### Describe the bug `MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun` runs a real `MergeTask`, but unlike the real optimize and merge paths it takes no `CurrentlyMergingPartsTagger` and no merge lock, so it never registers its source parts as being merged. A concurrent merge (background, or another `DRY RUN`) over the same parts therefore computes the same result part name and reserves the same `tmp_merge_<result>` directory. The second reservation trips `TemporaryParts::add`: ``` Logical error: 'Temporary part tmp_merge_all_1_1_1 already added' ``` This aborts the server on debug and sanitizer builds. On a release build it is a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception, so the `OPTIMIZE` fails instead. ### How to reproduce * ClickHouse version: `26.8.1.1` (git hash `199c583bffc735ff2994f9fee1c9dcc6d3b746c6`), reproduced on all sanitizers and both architectures. * Non-default settings: none required. Reached whenever `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` overlaps a merge on the same parts. Failing query, from the AST fuzzer in `Stress test (amd_debug)`: ```sql OPTIMIZE TABLE table_for_concurrent_alter DRY RUN PARTS 'all_1_1_0' CLEANUP ``` `query_log` for that server shows 9 concurrent `OPTIMIZE TABLE table_for_concurrent_alter` statements against the same table inside the same second (`10:41:57.016` .. `10:41:57.371`, mixing plain, `FINAL` and `CLEANUP`), so the dry run and a real merge over the same source parts overlap. Race window: `MergeTask::ExecuteAndFinalizeHorizontalPart::prepare` computes `local_tmp_prefix + future_part->name` and calls `getTemporaryPartDirectoryHolder` on it. For the dry run the suffix is empty, so the name is byte-identical to the name the real merge of the same parts derives. ### Expected behavior `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` is side-effect free by contract, so it must never make a concurrent merge fail, and must never abort the server. ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 2026.08.11 10:41:57.462234 [ 10293 ] {4dbac054-4094-40cf-a43d-b223bafe8dfa} <Fatal> : Logical error: 'Temporary part tmp_merge_all_1_1_1 already added'. 2026.08.11 10:41:57.463010 [ 10293 ] {4dbac054-4094-40cf-a43d-b223bafe8dfa} <Fatal> : Format string: 'Temporary part {} already added'. 5. src/Storages/MergeTree/TemporaryParts.cpp:28:15: DB::TemporaryParts::add(String const&) 6. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeData.cpp:3888:21: DB::MergeTreeData::getTemporaryPartDirectoryHolder(String const&) const 7. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeData.cpp:3939:44: DB::MergeTreeData::claimTemporaryPartDirectory(std::shared_ptr<DB::IDisk> const&, String const&, bool) const 8. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp:587:66: DB::MergeTask::ExecuteAndFinalizeHorizontalPart::prepare() const 9. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp:1293:16: DB::MergeTask::ExecuteAndFinalizeHorizontalPart::execute() 10. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp:2620:24: DB::MergeTask::execute() 11. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.h:622:18: DB::MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun(...) 12. src/Interpreters/InterpreterOptimizeQuery.cpp:135:26: DB::InterpreterOptimizeQuery::execute() 13. src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:1956:40: DB::executeQueryImpl(...) 15. src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:2373:27: DB::executeASTFuzzerQueries(...) ``` ### CI occurrences CIDB `default.checks`, 30-day window, `test_name LIKE '%Temporary part%already added%'`: 17 rows, 17 distinct pull requests, none on master, first `2026-07-17 20:22:10`, last `2026-08-11 08:23:45`. Every architecture and sanitizer is represented (`amd_debug`, `amd_tsan`, `amd_msan`, `arm_debug`, `arm_release`, `arm_tsan`, `arm_msan`, `arm_asan_ubsan, s3`), all in `Stress test (*)`. 15 of the 17 carry `optimizeDryRun` on the throwing thread. The remaining 2 throw from the real merge side of the same collision, so the dry run is the holder rather than the victim: `StorageMergeTree::optimize` -> `MergePlainMergeTreeTask` (PR 102499), and `MergeFromLogEntryTask::executeInnerTask` -> `ReplicatedMergeMutateTaskBase` (PR 111842). CIDB does not record who held the directory, so for those two the holder is inferred rather than proven. Sample report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112788&sha=fefac8e9d3ccc43a53f8091e8d07a29b6d4761d2&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 Filed at the request of @alexey-milovidov in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112788#issuecomment-5260029553. The earlier issue for the same message, #86050, was closed as completed on 2026-02-08; #91132 was closed on the same grounds, attributed to #91792 (`MergePlainMergeTreeTask`). Neither covers the `optimizeDryRun` producer, whose first CI sighting is 2026-07-17. ### Fix My open PR #110916 fixes this by naming the throwaway dry-run directory `tmp_merge_dry_run_<uuid>` instead of after the result part, which makes the collision impossible on both `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`. The guard is still absent from master (`DRY_RUN_TEMP_INFIX` has 0 hits in `src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.h` on `origin/master`).

signals.title: Settings profile with a Map setting (`http_response_headers`) does not survive a serialization round trip
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe the unexpected behaviour An access entity with a Map-valued setting — e.g. a settings profile with `http_response_headers` — is serialized into a form that ClickHouse's own parser cannot read back. The stored entity becomes permanently unloadable. ### How to reproduce ```sql -- A string literal is the only accepted way to write a Map setting in a profile -- (map literals {...}, array literals [...], and map(...) are all rejected here): CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE test_profile SETTINGS http_response_headers = '{''Content-Type'':''application/json'', ''Access-Control-Allow-Origin'':''*''}' CONST; SHOW CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE test_profile; -- CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE `test_profile` SETTINGS http_response_headers = [('Content-Type', 'application/json'), ('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*')] CONST -- Feeding the emitted statement back — which is exactly what DiskAccessStorage and -- ReplicatedAccessStorage store and re-parse via deserializeAccessEntity: CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE test_profile2 SETTINGS http_response_headers = [('Content-Type', 'application/json'), ('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*')] CONST; -- Code: 62. DB::Exception: Syntax error: failed at position 72 ([): -- Expected one of: literal, NULL, NULL, number, Bool, TRUE, FALSE, string literal, end of query ``` No value of the setting round-trips — even an empty map serializes as `[] CONST`, which is rejected the same way. ### Root cause The write path and the read path disagree: - Write: `SettingsProfileElement` (`src/Access/SettingsProfileElement.cpp`) casts the value to the setting's native type (`Map`), and the AST formats the Field as a literal, producing an array-of-tuples literal `[('k', 'v'), ...]`. - Read: `ParserSettingsProfileElement` (`src/Parsers/Access/ParserSettingsProfileElement.cpp`) parses the value with a scalar-only literal parser. Unlike the query-level `SETTINGS` clause parser, it was never extended to accept collection literals (cf. #75065, where the query-level parser expects `literal or map, ..., OpeningCurlyBrace`). So `serializeAccessEntity` → `deserializeAccessEntity` fails for any user/role/profile whose profile elements contain a collection-valued setting (`http_response_headers`, `additional_table_filters`, ...). > *Generated by [Nerve](https://github.com/ClickHouse/nerve)* <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #114620 - Backported to: `26.7.5.6`, `26.6.4.5`, `26.5.8.7`, `26.3.20.10` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq changes results: uniq*(tuple(nullable)) drops NULLs and depends on constant folding
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq` (default `true`) strips injective functions from `uniq*` arguments. When the stripped function is `tuple()` and its argument is `Nullable`, the rewrite is not semantics-preserving: `tuple(NULL)` is a value that `uniq*` counts, but a bare `NULL` is skipped by `uniq*`. So the optimization silently changes the result. ```sql SELECT uniqExact(tuple(x)) FROM values('x Nullable(Int32)', 1, 2, NULL); -- 2 (with the optimization, i.e. by default) SELECT uniqExact(tuple(x)) FROM values('x Nullable(Int32)', 1, 2, NULL) SETTINGS optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq = 0; -- 3 (correct: (1), (2) and (NULL) are three distinct tuples) ``` `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` shows the rewrite dropping the tuple: ```sql EXPLAIN SYNTAX SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin([NULL]))); -- SELECT uniqExact(arrayJoin([NULL])) ``` A second, related symptom: with the analyzer, whether the optimization applies at all depends on whether the argument happens to be constant-foldable, so semantically identical expressions disagree with each other: ```sql SELECT countDistinct(tuple(NULL)); -- 1 SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin([NULL]))); -- 0 SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin( emptyArrayToSingle([]::Array(Nullable(Int32)))))); -- 0 ``` `tuple(NULL)` has all-constant arguments, so it is folded into a `ConstantNode` during query analysis, and the pass no longer recognises it as a function to unwrap. The `arrayJoin` variants are not folded , so there the `tuple()` is stripped. With `enable_analyzer = 0` all three return `0`, because the legacy `TreeOptimizer` does the same rewrite on the un-folded AST. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/718dd23f-a726-4218-92f5-7b78048bda57 Also reproduces with `uniq`, `uniqHLL12`, `uniqCombined64` and `uniqTheta` (every function listed in `isUniqFunction`), and with `countDistinct` via `count_distinct_implementation`. ### Expected behavior `uniqExact(tuple(x))` should not depend on `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq`, on whether the argument is constant-foldable, or on `enable_analyzer`. `tuple()` is injective on the values it receives, but it also removes nullability, and `uniq*` treats NULL specially — so it must not be eliminated when its argument is `Nullable` and its own result type is not. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115466 - Backported to: `26.7.5.8` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: INSERT rejected with NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK when an ALIAS column declares STATISTICS
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A table created with an ALIAS column carrying explicit `STATISTICS(...)` accepts INSERTs on 26.4-26.7 but rejects every INSERT after this PR: `Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. The table becomes effectively read-only after upgrade; SELECT, merges and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` keep working.** - **Root cause:** The insert path uses `ColumnsStatistics::build` (hard `getByName`) while the merge path uses `ColumnsStatistics::buildIfExists`, which skips columns absent from the block ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:690-700`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L690-L700)). Statistics on non-physical columns are otherwise treated as unsupported — `addImplicitStatistics` skips Alias/Ephemeral columns (Statistics.cpp:927-929) and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS` rejects them via `columns.hasPhysical` (StatisticsDescription.cpp:181) — but the inline `CREATE TABLE ... col T ALIAS expr STATISTICS(...)` form has no such check (ColumnsDescription.cpp:260-261). Flipping `materialize_statistics_on_insert` to `true` turns that latent inconsistency into a hard INSERT failure. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeSink::writeNewTempPart` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp:409`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp#L409)) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:848`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L848)) -> `ColumnsStatistics` ctor collects every column whose statistics description is non-empty, including ALIAS columns ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:644-647`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L644-L647)) -> `ColumnsStatistics::build` looks the column up with `block.getByName` ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684)), and an ALIAS column is never in the written block. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:849`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L849) — insert path calls ColumnsStatistics::build on the written block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684) — build() uses block.getByName, which throws for a column not in the block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:646`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L646) — ColumnsStatistics ctor does not skip Alias/Ephemeral columns - [`src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp:181`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp#L181) — ALTER path rejects statistics on non-physical columns; the inline CREATE path does not **Impact:** Any table whose DDL puts `STATISTICS(...)` on an ALIAS column stops accepting INSERTs after upgrading to 26.8 (or after `SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1`). The error is an internal-sounding `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` at write time with no hint that statistics caused it, and there is no DDL-time warning. `ALTER TABLE ... DROP STATISTICS <alias_col>` is not a workaround either, since that path also refuses non-physical columns. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `2746afad95f`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/63424d1d-98a2-4f38-92d8-552f32129820) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that INSERT works when an ALIAS column declares statistics. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; SET allow_statistics = 1; SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; CREATE TABLE t_alias_statistics (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT a, b FROM t_alias_statistics ORDER BY a; DROP TABLE t_alias_statistics; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 1 2 2 3 3 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 10. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.1:19020. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (query: INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3);) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Use `statistics.buildIfExists(block)` on the insert path (matching `MergeTask`'s `BuildStatisticsTransform`), or skip Alias/Ephemeral columns in the `ColumnsStatistics` constructor the way `addImplicitStatistics` does. Rejecting the DDL instead is the wrong lever: the same code path parses metadata on ATTACH/startup, so existing tables would fail to load. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same `build` vs `buildIfExists` asymmetry would also fire for any other future column kind that is present in the metadata but absent from the written block. Found during automated review of [PR #109454](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109454). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr109454_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov @rschu1ze @egor-click (from #109454)

signals.title: Iceberg writer serializes day/hour partition transforms as non-canonical `days`/`hours`, breaking external readers (pyiceberg: UnknownTransform)
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** The Iceberg writer serializes the `day` and `hour` partition transforms under the non-canonical plural names `days` / `hours` in the table metadata. The [Iceberg spec](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#partition-transforms) defines the transform names as `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour` (singular), and that is what other writers emit. Spec-following readers do not recognize the plural forms: pyiceberg 0.10.0 parses them as `UnknownTransform(transform='days')`, so a ClickHouse-written time-partitioned Iceberg table silently loses its partition information (and with it partition pruning) in external readers. The writer is also internally inconsistent: the *sort order* serialization path maps the same functions to the canonical singular names (`{"toRelativeDayNum", "day"}, {"toRelativeHourNum", "hour"}` in `parseFunction`, `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp`), while the *partition spec* path emits the plural (`getPartitionField` writes `"days"` / `"hours"`, same file). `year` and `month` are emitted correctly in both paths. ClickHouse's own reader is lenient (`parseTransformAndArgument` accepts `day`, `date`, `days`, `dates`, …), so the bug is invisible in ClickHouse-only round-trips — it only breaks interoperability, which is the main reason to write Iceberg metadata in the first place. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master 26.8.1.1375, on every write. **How to reproduce** ```bash clickhouse local --path . --query " CREATE TABLE t (k Int64, ts DateTime) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('\$PWD/ice/', 'Parquet') PARTITION BY (toRelativeDayNum(ts)) SETTINGS allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, toDateTime('2026-01-01 00:00:00') + number * 3600 FROM numbers(100) SETTINGS allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1; " grep -ho '"transform" : "[^"]*"' ice/metadata/*.json | sort -u ``` **Expected behavior** ``` "transform" : "day" ``` **Actual behavior** ``` "transform" : "days" ``` And through pyiceberg 0.10.0: ```python from pyiceberg.table import StaticTable t = StaticTable.from_metadata('ice/metadata/<latest>.metadata.json') print([repr(f.transform) for f in t.spec().fields]) # ["UnknownTransform(transform='days')"] ``` `PARTITION BY (toRelativeHourNum(ts))` produces `"transform" : "hours"` with the same result. `toYearNumSinceEpoch` / `toMonthNumSinceEpoch` correctly produce `year` / `month`. Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).
signals.author: zlareb1

signals.title: Positional Tuple hint over Parquet: tupleElement rewrite yields default values
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('x.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)')` returns zeros/empty strings instead of the file's values once the tuple-element rewrite is enabled for `StorageFile`. `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matches 0 rows instead of 1. With `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the same query throws `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN: Column t.1 was not found in parquet schema`.** - **Root cause:** For an unnamed `DataTypeTuple` the element name produced by `getSubcolumnForElement` is the ordinal (`"1"`, `"2"`), so `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement` builds the subcolumn name `t.1`. Its guards check the DECLARED structure only (`canOptimizeToSubcolumn` queries the storage snapshot built from the structure argument), which of course contains `t.1`. Nothing checks whether the format resolves that element by name or by position — and Parquet resolves the tuple type positionally (`SchemaConverter.cpp:723-731`) but the flattened subcolumn name by string. The PR's opt-in comment 'a tuple element is a real leaf in the file, so the format can serve `t.x` on its own' is false for a positional tuple hint. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `getTypedNodesForOptimization` (FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:858) now admits `StorageFile` via `storageAllowsTransformer` -> `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` (StorageFile.h:132) -> `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement` (FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:428) replaces the function with a `ColumnNode` named `t.1` -> the Parquet reader resolves that flattened name by string lookup (`SchemaConverter.cpp:232`, `sample_block->findPositionByName(node.name, ...)`) against the file's real field names `t.x`/`t.y` -> no match -> synthetic missing column filled with defaults. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Analyzer/Passes/FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:428`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Analyzer/Passes/FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp#L428) — builds `t.<element>` subcolumn name; new guards do not check `hasExplicitNames` - [`src/Storages/StorageFile.h:132`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/StorageFile.h#L132) — `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` returns true unconditionally - [`src/Storages/StorageURL.h:374`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/StorageURL.h#L374) — same opt-in for `url()` - [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.h:106`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.h#L106) — same opt-in for `s3()`/`azure()` - [`src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/SchemaConverter.cpp:232`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/SchemaConverter.cpp#L232) — flattened subcolumn name resolved by string lookup, never positionally **Impact:** Silent wrong results for any `file()`/`s3()`/`url()` Parquet read that declares a positional (unnamed) `Tuple` in the structure argument — a documented, supported way to read a struct written by an external writer (Spark, pandas, Arrow) without repeating its field names. Affects both the v3 and the legacy Parquet reader. With `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query is rejected instead. ORC is not affected. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `5c9f28ed5a2c5`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/43170dc7-eed8-4aac-9ac4-ab16ab01d90b) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that a positional (unnamed) Tuple structure hint still returns the file's values. SET enable_analyzer = 1; SET optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 1; INSERT INTO FUNCTION file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(x UInt64, y String)') SELECT tuple(number, toString(number)) FROM numbers(3) SETTINGS engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; SELECT tupleElement(t, 1), tupleElement(t, 2) FROM file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)') ORDER BY 1; SELECT count() FROM file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)') WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 0 0 1 1 2 2 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 0 0 0 0 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> In `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement`, refuse the rewrite when `!data_type_concrete.hasExplicitNames()` and the storage only opted in through `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` (the element name is an ordinal that no file schema carries). Alternatively make `SchemaConverter` resolve an ordinal-named subcolumn positionally when the parent tuple hint is unnamed, matching what it already does for the whole tuple. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same declared-vs-physical name mismatch may exist for other formats reached through `StorageFile`/`StorageObjectStorage` that resolve subcolumns by name; only Parquet, ORC, CSV and JSONEachRow were probed here (CSV and JSONEachRow behave identically with and without the rewrite). Found during automated review of [PR #113383](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113383). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr113383_001` </details> cc @groeneai @alexey-milovidov (from #113383)

signals.title: Wrong result: optimize_trivial_count_query makes count(arrayJoin(arr)) return the table's row count instead of the number of array elements
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong - With the default `optimize_trivial_count_query = 1`, `SELECT count(arrayJoin(arr)) FROM t` returns the number of rows in the table instead of the number of array elements. - arrayJoin is a row-multiplying operator, so the aggregate must observe the post-expansion stream. The trivial-count optimization replaces the entire table read with a stored row counter and never evaluates count's argument, so the ARRAY JOIN expansion is silently dropped. No error, no warning. - The optimization rests on the premise "the number of rows the aggregate sees equals the number of rows stored in the table." That holds for `count()`, `count(1)` and `count(non_nullable_col)`, but arrayJoin breaks it, and nothing in the guard list checks for it. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce - https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/a93a2cb4-e0f1-450b-a97e-0acef509da3b ``` ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────┬──────────┐ │ Query │ Result │ Correct? │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ count(arrayJoin(A)) │ 2 │ ✗ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ count(arrayJoin(A)) SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 0 │ 5 │ ✓ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ count(*) FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(A) ...) │ 5 │ ✓ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ sum(length(A)) │ 5 │ ✓ │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────┴──────────┘ ``` ### Expected behavior - The `count(arrayJoin(A))` should return the total number of array elements across all rows, equivalent to sum(length(A)). ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115227 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1681` (included in `26.8` and later) - Backported to: `26.7.5.3`, `26.6.4.4`, `26.5.8.6`, `26.3.21.6`, `25.8.31.12` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL on ReplacingMergeTree Can Spontaneously Fail with Code 236 ABORTED
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong When running OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL on a ReplacingMergeTree table, the merge operation can be canceled and fail with an ABORTED exception. This is a significant issue because OPTIMIZE ... FINAL is an explicit command to force a merge, and it should not be aborted arbitrarily without a clear, actionable reason . The error appears to be non-deterministic and can occur even when the table is small and uncomplicated, making it difficult to predict or avoid in production systems. This issue report aims to provide a straightforward and reliable test case to reproduce the problem, which is a key requirement for ClickHouse's bug bounty program . ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce Create a new atomic database. Create a ReplacingMergeTree table populated with data. Run OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL. Recreate the same table with the same data. Run OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL again. Observe the error. signals.title: Empty LowCardinality(String) optimization
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the situation There's a table with json event and two materialized columns from it. Both are empty (has only empty strings) ```sql CREATE TABLE t ( event String, s String MATERIALIZED JSONExtractString(event, 'foo'), lc_s LowCardinality(String) MATERIALIZED JSONExtractString(event, 'bar') ) ENGINE = MergeTree() ... SETTINGS default_compression_codec = 'ZSTD' ``` They have such sizes and compression ratio ``` column, compressed_size, uncompressed_size, ratio lc_s, 2351522, 701140666, 298.16 s, 300584, 2036637, 6.78 ``` ```sql SELECT event FROM t WHERE s != '' LIMIT 1 ``` 0 rows in set. Elapsed: **0.881 sec.** ```sql SELECT event FROM t WHERE lc_s != '' LIMIT 1 ``` 0 rows in set. Elapsed: **318.643 sec.** It's meaningful to make this select fast cause if a column has data `SELECT ... LIMIT 1` returns fast. It's slow only if there's no or a few data in a column. It's an improvement for entire class of queries, not just an exotic case for empty column. ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? 26.3 ### How to reproduce Fill the table with lots of rows (insert empty strings in `event` field). Run SELECTs over String and LowCardinality(String) columns. ### Expected performance It's expected that LC(String) would detect it has single default value and works as fast as String variant in this case. ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: DeltaLake: SELECT * + delta_lake_snapshot_version expands * from live table schema, not the snapshot schema
signals.text: ### Company or project name Datazone ### Describe what's wrong For a named `ENGINE = DeltaLake` table, `SELECT *` is expanded from the current attached table schema. `delta_lake_snapshot_version` is applied only to which snapshot files are read. After a column is added, `SELECT *` on an older snapshot fails because ClickHouse requests columns that did not exist in that snapshot. `*` expansion itself is expected analyzer behavior. The gap is that time travel does not use the snapshot schema when expanding `*`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/85295 The `deltaLake(...)` table function can DESCRIBE the requested snapshot schema (see the test in that PR). A persisted `ENGINE = DeltaLake` table does not: `*` still uses live metadata. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce 1. Create a Delta Lake table with columns `id`, `amount`. 2. Attach it as a ClickHouse table: CREATE TABLE orders ENGINE = DeltaLake(...) 3. Confirm latest read works: SELECT * FROM orders; -- returns id, amount 4. Evolve the Delta table: add column `status`. Refresh or recreate the ClickHouse table so its metadata has `id`, `amount`, `status`. 5. Time-travel to the old snapshot: SELECT * FROM orders SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_version = 0; ### Expected behavior `SELECT *` at snapshot 0 should use snapshot 0's schema (`id`, `amount` only) and succeed. Time travel should mean columns and data as of that snapshot. ### Error message and/or stacktrace Column-not-found / unknown identifier for the column added after the snapshot (for example `status`). EXPLAIN / analyzer shows `*` already expanded to the live column list (`id`, `amount`, `status`) before the snapshot is read. ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context ClickHouse expands `*` from table metadata during analysis: - Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select (Asterisk: expanded to all table columns when the query is analyzed) - `src/Parsers/ASTAsterisk.h`: SELECT * is expanded to all visible columns of the source table. - `src/Interpreters/TranslateQualifiedNamesVisitor.cpp`: Replace *, alias.*, database.table.* with a list of columns. `delta_lake_snapshot_version` only selects `snapshot` vs `snapshot_at_version` in `TableSnapshot.cpp`. It does not change that expansion. Workaround: do not send inner `SELECT *`. Project the snapshot's own column names: SELECT * FROM ( SELECT id, amount FROM orders SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_version = 0 ) AS orders; Suggested fix: when `delta_lake_snapshot_version` is set on an `ENGINE = DeltaLake` table, resolve `SELECT *` and DESCRIBE from that snapshot's schema, same as the `deltaLake(...)` table function.

signals.title: Uncompressed Keeper snapshots are written as 0-byte files; node cannot restart
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format=false`, every snapshot Keeper writes to a local disk is 0 bytes although it logs `Created persistent snapshot N`. On the next restart Keeper dies with `Failure to load from latest snapshot ... Cannot read all data. Bytes read: 0 ... Manual intervention is necessary for recovery. Problematic snapshot can be removed but it will lead to data loss (CORRUPTED_DATA)`.** - **Root cause:** In the non-zstd branch the file buffer is wrapped BY REFERENCE (`std::make_unique<CompressedWriteBuffer>(*writer)`), so finalizing `compressed_writer` (:903) only pushes bytes into `writer`'s in-memory buffer; `compressed_writer->sync()` (:906) is the base no-op for that class and `writer.reset()` (:910) destroys the file buffer without `finalize`/`next`, discarding everything. The zstd branch passes ownership (`wrapWriteBufferWithCompressionMethod(std::move(writer), ...)`), so finalize/sync propagate — which is why only the uncompressed path is broken. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `KeeperStateMachine::create_snapshot` -> `writeSnapshotToDisk` -> `KeeperSnapshotManager::writeSnapshotFile` (KeeperStateMachine.cpp:1027, local-disk branch) -> KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:896. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:896`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp#L896) — non-owning CompressedWriteBuffer over the file write buffer - [`src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:910`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp#L910) — writer.reset() without finalize/sync - [`src/Coordination/KeeperStateMachine.cpp:1027`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperStateMachine.cpp#L1027) — local-disk snapshots go through writeSnapshotFile **Impact:** Any Keeper/ClickHouse deployment with `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format=false` silently writes empty snapshots. The node refuses to start after any restart and recovery requires deleting the snapshot, which ClickHouse's own message describes as data loss; a leader also has nothing usable to send to a recovering follower. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `ac58c4e749468`). ### How to reproduce ```python import pytest import helpers.keeper_utils as keeper_utils from helpers.cluster import ClickHouseCluster cluster = ClickHouseCluster(__file__) node_zstd = cluster.add_instance( "node_zstd", main_configs=["configs/keeper_zstd.xml"], stay_alive=True, with_remote_database_disk=False ) node_plain = cluster.add_instance( "node_plain", main_configs=["configs/keeper_plain.xml"], stay_alive=True, with_remote_database_disk=False ) SNAPSHOT_DIR = "/var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots" @pytest.fixture(scope="module") -- def started_cluster(): -- try: cluster.start() yield cluster -- finally: cluster.shutdown() @pytest.mark.parametrize("node_name", ["node_zstd", "node_plain"]) -- def test_snapshot_survives_restart(started_cluster, node_name): node = cluster.instances[node_name] keeper_utils.wait_until_connected(cluster, node) zk = keeper_utils.get_fake_zk(cluster, node.name) zk.create("/test_uncompressed_snapshot", b"somedata") idx = keeper_utils.send_4lw_cmd(cluster, node, cmd="csnp").strip() node.wait_for_log_line(f"Created persistent snapshot {idx} with path") sizes = node.exec_in_container(["bash", "-c", f"stat -c '%n %s' {SNAPSHOT_DIR}/snapshot_*"]).strip() print(f"{node_name} SNAPSHOT_FILES: {sizes}") node.restart_clickhouse() keeper_utils.wait_until_connected(cluster, node) zk = keeper_utils.get_fake_zk(cluster, node.name) assert zk.get("/test_uncompressed_snapshot")[0] == b"somedata" # configs/keeper_zstd.xml and configs/keeper_plain.xml are identical single-node keeper # configs (tcp_port 9181, server_id 1, local log/snapshot paths, four_letter_word_white_list *), -- # except that keeper_plain.xml adds inside <coordination_settings>: # <compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format>false</compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format> ``` ### Expected behavior ``` Both parameterizations pass: the snapshot file is non-empty for both settings and the node restarts and still serves /test_uncompressed_snapshot. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` node_zstd SNAPSHOT_FILES: /var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots/snapshot_13_ebe6b90817820fc1.bin.zstd 440 -> PASSED node_plain SNAPSHOT_FILES: /var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots/snapshot_15_4d88ed92c255dd85.bin 0 -> FAILED (Exception: Cannot start ClickHouse, see additional info in logs) node_plain clickhouse-server.err.log: 2026.08.19 01:42:55.320161 <Error> void DB::KeeperDispatch ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Finalize and sync the underlying file buffer in the non-zstd branch, e.g. after `compressed_writer->finalize()` add `writer->finalize(); writer->sync();` (or give the LZ4 branch ownership of `writer` the way the zstd branch does). </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same non-owning wrap exists at KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:687 (`serializeSnapshotToBuffer`), but there the sink is `WriteBufferFromNuraftBuffer` whose `getBuffer()` finalizes, so that path is correct. Found during automated review of [PR #111715](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111715). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr111715_001` </details> cc @al13n321 @antonio2368 (from #111715) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115553 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1802` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
