signals.title: Record TopK-filtered granules in the query condition cache
signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Granules fully filtered by the dynamic threshold of an `ORDER BY ... LIMIT n` (TopK) read are now recorded in the query condition cache, so repeat runs of such queries skip them at the mark-selection stage instead of re-reading and re-filtering most of the table. On the ClickBench Q24/Q26 shapes (`SELECT SearchPhrase FROM hits WHERE SearchPhrase <> '' ORDER BY EventTime LIMIT 10`), a warm run drops from ~95M rows / ~12000 granules read to ~1.3M rows / ~160 granules, and from ~15–30 ms to ~8 ms on a 96-core machine. The `ORDER BY ... LIMIT n` (TopK) optimization pushes a dynamic `__topKFilter` threshold into the `MergeTree` read as a PREWHERE, dropping rows that cannot beat the running top-N. But the granules it emptied were never recorded in the query condition cache: the PREWHERE write path in `MergeTreeSelectProcessor::read` rejects non-deterministic conditions, and `__topKFilter` is one. Only the downstream WHERE `FilterTransform` wrote entries, at whole-chunk granularity, which learns almost nothing (a single surviving row voids the attribution of the whole chunk) — measured on hits, warm runs still selected 11766 of 12348 granules and re-read ~95M of 100M rows. The original out-of-tree build of this optimization (PR #81944, commit `2e2f594308f4` plus the follow-up making the TopN dynamic filters deterministic and reusable for the cache) recorded them and skipped ~98% of granules on warm runs — that is the 2–3x Q24/Q26 gap measured in issue #114639. Recording these granules is sound: for a fixed plan and data, the running threshold only tightens, so a granule none of whose rows survive the filter contains no row that could reach the final top-N, regardless of the threshold trajectory. The entries are keyed with the TopK plan salt (`TopKFilterInfo::condition_hash`: sort column, type, `LIMIT`, direction, `NULLS` direction, collation locale, number of sort columns, and the part-set snapshot), mirroring what the WHERE write path already does since #104478/#110507 — only the same TopK plan over the same part set ever reuses them. Changes: - `isDeterministicAllowingTopKFilter` (two identical static copies in `updateQueryConditionCache.cpp` and `ReadFromMergeTree.cpp`) moved into `VirtualColumnUtils`. - The TopK salt is plumbed to the reader via `MergeTreeReaderSettings::query_condition_cache_top_k_salt`. - The PREWHERE write path accepts a `__topKFilter`-bearing condition when the salt is present, folding the salt into the cache key. Any other non-deterministic condition is still never cached. - The PREWHERE consult path (`filterPartsByQueryConditionCache`) applies the salt exactly when the PREWHERE contains `__topKFilter`, so the keys match the write side; deterministic user PREWHERE conditions keep using plain, unsalted entries shared with non-TopK queries. - `04217_query_condition_cache_topk` and `04242_query_condition_cache_topk_collate` pin exact cache entry counts, which double (each TopK plan now writes a WHERE entry and a PREWHERE entry per part). - New test `04891_query_condition_cache_topk_prewhere_granules` isolates the PREWHERE write path with a WHERE-less TopK query (on current master such a query writes no cache entries at all), asserts that the ASC and DESC plans do not share granule decisions, and that a warm run selects fewer marks. - New performance test `topk_query_condition_cache.xml` with the ClickBench Q24/Q26 shapes over `hits_100m_single`. Measured on the 100M-row single-part ClickBench `hits` (96-core aarch64, hot, interleaved runs): warm Q24/Q26 at 0.007–0.009 s, on par with the original bench-opt build (0.009–0.011 s), against 0.015–0.03 s for current master; warm runs read 159 of 12348 granules against master's 11766. A first run with an empty cache shows no measurable overhead (0.016–0.019 s with the mechanism on and off). Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114639 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110507 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114659&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114659](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114659+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Allow overriding the HTTP method for SELECT through the url table function and URL engine
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/62352 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `http_method='POST'` — as a key-value argument of the `url` table function and the `URL` table engine, or through the `http_method`/`method` named collection keys — now applies to `SELECT` queries: reads use `POST` instead of the default `GET`, for servers that accept only `POST`. Schema inference follows the configured method. `PUT` keeps its write-only meaning: a `SELECT` through a configuration with `http_method='PUT'` still uses `GET`. ### Implementation notes - `IStorageURLBase::getReadMethod()` now returns `POST` when the configured `http_method` is `POST`. `PUT` still applies to writes only (pre-signed upload URLs, #44326), and `INSERT` behavior is unchanged: `POST` by default, `PUT` when configured. - The write path no longer mutates the shared `http_method` member when defaulting to `POST` — the storage instance is shared between queries, so persisting the write default would have flipped subsequent reads of the same table from `GET` to `POST` (and raced concurrent reads). - Schema inference (`getTableStructureAndFormatFromData` and the URL read-buffer iterator) uses the same effective read method instead of hardcoded `GET`, for both `url()`/`URL` and `urlCluster`. - The `http_method = '...'` (or `method = '...'`) key-value argument is parsed by `StorageURL::evalArgsAndCollectHeaders` alongside `headers(...)`, kept in the `CREATE` AST (so it survives `SHOW CREATE TABLE` and DETACH/ATTACH), validated to be `POST`/`PUT`, and rejected when the URL scheme dispatches to another backend (`file://`, `s3://`, ...), mirroring `headers(...)`. - In the analyzer, the argument's left-hand identifier is excluded from column resolution (`skipAnalysisForArguments`), like `headers(...)`. - Documentation for the `url` table function and the `URL` engine is updated. The new stateless test `04869_url_select_http_method` asserts the method actually used on the wire via `system.query_log.http_method`: default `GET`, `POST` override for both the data and the schema-inference requests, `PUT`-configured `SELECT` staying on `GET`, the `URL` engine path, rejection of unsupported methods, and persistence of the argument in the table DDL. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Do not hold the DDL guard during TRUNCATE
signals.text: `TRUNCATE TABLE` held the table's DDL guard while removing data, and truncate can wait for running merges or for other replicas to process `DROP_RANGE`. Any DDL on that name — including background threads that need it — was blocked for that whole time. Release the guard before `IStorage::truncate` for databases with UUIDs, matching `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`, which never took it. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `TRUNCATE TABLE` no longer blocks concurrent `DROP`, `RENAME` and other DDL queries on the same table while the data is being removed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114672&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114672](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114672+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix ANY/SEMI RIGHT JOIN with OR conditions emitting rows twice or losing matches
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112640 `ANY RIGHT JOIN` and `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` emit every row of their right table at most once, and exactly once when the row has a match. With several OR-ed conditions in `ON` the claim for that was taken with a single CAS on the head row of the matched key's `RowRefList`, while `addFoundRowAll` then emitted every row of that list and discarded the result of the per-row `setUsedOnce` it called afterwards. With `OR` a right row is reachable through several keys in several hash maps, so a per-key claim does not partition the right rows: a list whose head row was claimed through another condition was skipped whole, orphaning its other rows, and a list whose head row was still free re-emitted rows another left row had already taken. Some right rows then appeared twice and others lost their match — padded with defaults for `ANY RIGHT JOIN`, dropped entirely for `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` — varying from run to run with the probe order under `max_threads > 1`. The claim is now taken per emitted row: `addFoundRowAll` claims a row before appending it and skips the rows whose CAS it loses, and returns whether it appended anything so the left row is filtered in only then. A single disjunct keeps the per-key claim, which is exact there, since one key owns all of its rows. The residual-condition path (`joinRightColumnsWithAdditionalFilter`) already claimed per row and is unchanged. Besides writing `ANY RIGHT JOIN` / `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` directly, this is reached by a plain `ANY LEFT JOIN` whenever the planner swaps the tables (`query_plan_join_swap_table`, `auto` by default), which is how the issue was reported. Measured on the reported query before and after, at `max_threads = 8`: 20 of 60 runs returned 5 or 6 rows for a 4-row left table, now 60/60 return 4. On a 1000-row shape, `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` returned 200 rows instead of 1000; `ANY LEFT JOIN` padded 416–736 rows with defaults although they had a match, and with `max_joined_block_size_rows = 7` also returned 1008 rows for 1000 left rows. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ANY RIGHT JOIN` and `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` with several `OR`-ed conditions in the `ON` section returning some rows of the right table twice and losing the matches of others. A written `ANY LEFT JOIN` was affected too, because the planner may swap the tables and execute it as `ANY RIGHT JOIN`.

signals.title: Adaptive lazy execution of short-circuit function arguments (continues #73776)
signals.text: This continues #73776 by @lgbo-ustc, whose branch was ~17 months behind `master` and could no longer be merged mechanically (27 conflicting files in the hottest central code). The author's commits are preserved; on top of them this reconciles the change with the current `master` and reworks the plumbing. Short-circuit evaluation decides *statically* which arguments of `and`, `or`, `if` and `multiIf` are executed lazily. Lazy execution is not free: the rows which are not needed are filtered out and the result is expanded back to the original size. When the filtered out part is small, or the argument itself is cheap, this overhead is larger than the work it saves. This adds an opt-in adaptive mode: the execution of every function is profiled (elapsed time and processed rows), and every 20000 rows the decision is revisited per action - lazy execution is turned off when the estimated cost of the full execution is lower than the measured cost of the lazy execution, and turned back on when the per-row cost of the action grows significantly. Actions whose function can throw an exception on invalid input values (for example `intDiv(1, 0)`) are never switched to eager execution, so the short-circuit protection is preserved. The mode is disabled by default and enabled with the new experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`. Changes on top of the original branch: * The flag no longer travels through `ExpressionStep`/`FilterStep` constructors, the query plan optimizations, the planner and the step serialization. It lives in `ExpressionActionsSettings` next to `enable_lazy_columns_replication`, which removes ~20 files from the change and all the ripple through `QueryPlan/Optimizations`. * `ExpressionActions::execute` and `executeOnColumns` stay `const`; the free `executeAction` became a member with three virtual hooks (`shouldExecuteLazily`, `executeFunction`, `finalizeBlockExecution`) which `AdaptiveExpressionActions` overrides. * The profile plumbing follows the current `IExecutableFunction` chain, including `executeWithoutReplicatedColumns`, which did not exist when the branch was written. * `is_no_except` is computed only when the setting is enabled, so nothing changes for the default path. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`, which enables dynamic evaluation of whether a short-circuit function's argument should be lazily executed. The execution of the functions is profiled at runtime, and the lazy execution of an argument is disabled when it costs more than executing the argument on all the rows. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73776 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114734&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114734](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114734+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW`
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `WINDOW VIEW` feature is removed, together with the `WATCH` statement and the `windowID` function. It has been non-functional since version 24.12 (inserts into the source table were silently not delivered to window views) and was never supported by the analyzer, which is enabled by default since 24.3. The settings `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, and `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` are kept as obsolete no-ops. The time-window functions `tumble`, `tumbleStart`, `tumbleEnd`, `hop`, `hopStart`, and `hopEnd` are kept. If you still have window views defined, drop them before upgrading: a server that finds a window view in its metadata fails to start (`Cannot parse definition from metadata file ... (SYNTAX_ERROR)`), the same way the removal of the `Lazy` database engine behaves. Similar functionality will be reimplemented on top of streaming queries (issue [#114738](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738)). The removal, in detail: - `src/Storages/WindowView/` (`StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`), `WatermarkTransform`, the `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery` parser, and the whole `WATCH` statement stack (`ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual) — window views were the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` statement was already documented as deprecated. - The `ASTCreateQuery` watermark/lateness fields and their AST JSON serialization and validation. The `clickhouse_json` boundary fails closed rather than silently reinterpreting legacy payloads: `ASTCreateQuery::readJSON` rejects a set `is_window_view`, watermark strategy or `allowed_lateness` flag and the `watermark_function` / `lateness_function` children (otherwise such a payload deserialized as an ordinary `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and was executed as an immediate-population table create), while `ASTViewTargets::readJSON` rejects the `Inner` target kind, which nothing produces any more and which formatted back to parser-impossible `INNER ENGINE ...` SQL. Both are covered by `04892_ast_json_removed_window_view_state`; the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder`; window-view special cases in `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`, `StorageFactory`, `DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DDLDependencyVisitor`, `QueryFuzzer`, BuzzHouse, and the ArrowFlight table-type mapping. - The `windowID` function and the `UInt32` single-argument forms of `tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` (they only accepted `windowID` output). The rest of the time-window function family stays, since these are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY` and are exactly the vocabulary for the streaming-queries replacement. - The keywords `WATCH`, `EVENTS`, `ALLOWED_LATENESS`, and `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` (the `WATERMARK` keyword stays: the streaming-queries `WATERMARK FOR` clause uses it), the error code `QUERY_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_WINDOW_VIEW`, and the corresponding fuzzer dictionary and ANTLR grammar entries. - Kept for compatibility: `QueryViewsLogElement::ViewType::WINDOW` (so existing `system.query_views_log` tables keep their schema) and `ViewTarget::Inner` (so old DDL log entries still parse), following the same pattern as the `LIVE VIEW` removal. - The `allow_experimental_window_view` constraint in `tests/docker_scripts/stress_tests.lib` is kept (only the constraint, not the profile value, which would mark an obsolete setting as changed and add a `system.warnings` entry): the upgrade check runs the previous release's suite under the previous release's binary, whose window-view tests are not dropped afterwards because `--upgrade-check` implies `--fake-drop`, and the leftover metadata would then stop the new server from starting. - Tests: the four remaining window-view tests are removed. The pure time-window-function coverage of `01049_window_view_window_functions` moved to a new `04891_time_window_functions` test, which also pins the new `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` behavior of `tumbleStart(UInt32)`. - Docs: the `Window View` section of `CREATE VIEW`, the `WATCH` page (with its navigation entries and locale twins) are removed and the old-slug redirects retargeted; the window-view entries are removed from the generated settings/functions reference pages (second commit, hence the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label): the `window-view.mdx` settings page, the four settings' entries in the pages/manifest/navigation/settings explorer, and the `windowID` section of `time-window-functions.mdx`. The unrelated drift accumulated on master since the last nightly regeneration is deliberately not included; the nightly docs-autogen job will pick it up. Why now: the feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024 — commit `ceae84c87a2` removed the explicit view-dependency registration and `DDLDependencyVisitor` never extracted the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so inserts into the source table were silently not pushed to window views, and direct inserts failed with `std::out_of_range` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years. It was never ported to the analyzer (with `enable_analyzer = 1`, the default, existing window views load permanently inert), its tests were removed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 because they were inherently flaky, and it kept costing triage time (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 is a recent server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`). The full assessment, including the plan for reimplementing this functionality on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`, `WATERMARK FOR`, emit-on-watermark windowed aggregation), is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114747](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114747+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Propagate NDV through functions with constant arguments
signals.text: ## Summary - Propagate expression NDV bounds through deterministic functions with exactly one row-varying argument. - Track the row-varying argument instead of assuming it is the first child. - Cover `dateTrunc('month', date)`, where the first argument is constant. ## Root cause NDV propagation only handled deterministic single-argument functions and always traversed the first child. As a result, a deterministic expression with constant arguments, such as `dateTrunc('month', order_date)`, lost the NDV of its row-varying input. Aggregation planning then fell back to the input row count. ## Testing - `git diff --check` - Added `ColumnStatsDerivation.FunctionWithConstantArgumentsPropagatesBound` Closes ClickHouse/clickhouse-private#68097 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry: Fixes inaccurate cardinality estimates for deterministic functions with constant arguments, which can improve aggregation query plans for expressions such as `dateTrunc`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114755&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114755](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114755+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Keep a text index direct read from widening a filter step's output header
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113320 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114460 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Cannot find input column ... on its position in inputs of expression actions DAG`) when a query has a `JOIN` above a table whose text-indexed column is used by both a `PREWHERE` and a `WHERE` text-search predicate. ### Description #114460, the fix for #113320, introduced the column retention this change works alongside. It is unreleased, so no released version is affected. On default settings, a `JOIN` over a table with a text index fails when the same indexed column is read by both a `PREWHERE` and a text-searchable `WHERE` predicate: ```sql SELECT t.id FROM tab AS t GLOBAL JOIN (SELECT toUInt32(number) AS rid FROM numbers(2)) AS r ON t.id = r.rid PREWHERE hasTokenCaseInsensitive(t.key, 'foo') WHERE hasAllTokens(t.key, 'foo'); -- Logical error: 'Cannot find input column key on its position in inputs of -- expression actions DAG, expected inputs [__table1.id, key], [__table2.rid]' ``` Found by the AST fuzzer ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111867&sha=775787f0654602c107b33178c068b3ef74665b35&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29), STID 2409-5283); that PR does not touch the planner. Root cause: the rewrite drops the indexed column from a filter DAG's inputs, but the column stays in the reading step's output header under its raw storage name because it is deliberately kept in the read set for another reader - the `PREWHERE`, or a row policy. `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` appends such an unmatched header column to its result. The rewrite runs in the second optimization pass, after all header reconciliation, so the widened header reaches the join, whose DAG inputs lack it. The retention step already computes which columns it keeps for another reader, and now makes each an input of the filter DAG at that same point, so nothing is appended to the output header. Both the `WHERE` and the `PREWHERE` rewrite go through that one step, and the column still reaches the reader that needs it. The test is the query above. Removing any one of its elements makes it succeed on the pre-fix binary. The test for issue 113320 stays green. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114771&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114771](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114771+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Propagate OpenTelemetry trace context into AsyncTaskExecutor fibers
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112738 The OpenTelemetry trace context is stored in a `FiberLocal`, but the fibers created by `AsyncTaskExecutor` (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`) started with an empty fiber-local context. Remote queries of a distributed query were parented directly to the trace context supplied by the client, bypassing the spans of the initiator, and no spans were produced for the async tasks themselves. ## Changes - `AsyncTaskExecutor` captures `OpenTelemetry::CurrentContext()` on the thread that constructs it and installs a `TracingContextHolder` inside the fiber routine. This seeds the fiber-local context from the creating query and opens one span per task execution, named after the executor (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`). It is a no-op when tracing is not enabled. - `FiberLocal` is now a per-type singleton (obtained via `FiberLocal<T>::instance`, the constructor is private). The address of the single object keys the per-fiber data, so a fiber suspended on one thread and resumed on another resolves to the same data. ## Span hierarchy change Remote queries now descend from the initiator through the `Connection::sendQuery` CLIENT span instead of appearing as direct children of the client-supplied trace context: ``` client span └─ query (initiator) └─ Connection::sendQuery [CLIENT] └─ query (remote server) ``` The expectations of `01455_opentelemetry_distributed` are updated accordingly: only the initial query span is now a direct child of the input trace context. A new test `04869_opentelemetry_async_remote_query_spans` covers the async paths, including `use_hedged_requests=1` (asserting `ConnectionEstablisherAsync` and `PacketReceiver` spans) and fiber cancellation. This is the first part of the distributed tracing improvements discussed in the linked issue ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Propagate the OpenTelemetry trace context into the fibers used for asynchronous connection establishment and remote query execution (hedged requests, `async_socket_for_remote`, `async_query_sending_for_remote`). Spans of remote queries in a distributed query are now correctly parented under the initiator's `Connection::sendQuery` span instead of being attached directly to the client-supplied trace context, and each asynchronous task execution produces its own span. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114813&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114813](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114813+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Hold the table lock across a lightweight UPDATE pipeline
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort (`Logical error: Part patch-... doesn't exist`) when a `DROP TABLE` runs concurrently with a lightweight `UPDATE` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table. The update now holds the table's shared lock until its patch part is committed, so the `DROP` waits instead of removing it. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #104431: an `Upgrade check (amd_release)` abort with no fix on master, STID `3208-458f`, 4 hits on 4 unrelated PRs in 6 days ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104431&sha=7970f08a82eaf2ad5217d57a7796ae1c5e920030&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade+check+%28amd_release%29)). **What breaks.** A lightweight `UPDATE` racing a `DROP TABLE` aborts the server, release builds included: `Transaction::commit`'s `modifyPartState` sits in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose catch-all is `std::terminate`. **Root cause.** `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute` takes `lockForShare` into a function-local holder and parks only the *storage* in the returned pipeline; `QueryPlanResourceHolder` keeps `storage_holders` and `table_locks` separately, so the lock dies when `execute()` returns, long before the sink commits the patch part. A concurrent `DROP` then takes the exclusive lock, `dropAllData()` clears `data_parts_indexes`, and the commit cannot find its own part. It needs a UUID-less database (`Memory`/`Ordinary`), where `DROP` removes data inline, hence the intermittency. **The change.** Move the already-acquired lock into the pipeline's resources, as the INSERT path does at `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1297`. Three entry points: `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute`, `InterpreterAlterQuery::executeToTable`, and `StorageAlias::updateLightweight`, which resolves a *different* storage and so needs the target's own lock, as `StorageAlias::read` does. `DELETE FROM` rewrites to `UPDATE` and is covered transitively. A concurrent `DROP` or `DETACH` now waits for an in-flight lightweight update, as it already does for `INSERT`. `TRUNCATE` takes no exclusive lock for `MergeTree`. **Validation.** New test `04905_lwu_drop_race_table_lock.sh`, one arm per fixed carrier. A pauseable failpoint parks the replicated sink between the patch-part rename and the commit, while the update still holds the lock; the arm then drops the table and waits for the drop to block on that lock. Nothing is timed, so an arm cannot miss a window or pass quietly. Aborts without the fix, passes with it, 50/50 green. <details> <summary>Both-directions matrix (every cell measured, Build IDs asserted against the running server)</summary> | binary | `UPDATE` | `ALTER ... UPDATE` | via `Alias` | |---|---|---|---| | base (fix reverted) `ea8e869d` | ABORT | ABORT | ABORT | | interpreters only `3651f11d` | pass | pass | ABORT | | full fix `1884b944` | pass | pass | pass | The middle row is the control that shows the `StorageAlias` change is necessary: with both interpreter fixes applied, the alias arm is the only one that still aborts. The lock demonstrably serializes the two queries: with the sink parked after the patch-part rename, the `DROP` becomes a waiting writer and stays one until the sink is released, then completes. Deadlock check: the change only extends the lifetime of a *Read* acquisition, and no sink on this path takes the table lock. `update_sequential_consistency = 1` and a following `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` both complete normally. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1813` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Add byte-weighted bytes_to_do and progress to system.mutations
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114678 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `system.mutations` now exposes byte-weighted mutation progress: `bytes_to_do` (the on-disk size of the data parts that still need to be mutated) and `progress` (an estimated finished fraction from 0 to 1, including the live fraction of the parts currently being rewritten). Part counts are a poor work proxy — parts are unequal in size and a regular merge can retire many pending parts at once — so the byte view is the honest one; the docs gain an "Estimating mutation progress" section with an equivalent parameterized-view recipe for older releases. Implements the conclusion of the research on the issue in two layers: **Columns** (`bytes_to_do` UInt64, `progress` Float64 in `system.mutations`): derived on read like `parts_to_do` — no persisted state, no replication protocol or znode format change. For plain `MergeTree` the sizes ride along the existing per-part scan in `getMutationsStatus`; for replicated tables the queue keeps returning name-only statuses under its state lock and the storage resolves sizes afterwards, so no parts lock is ever taken under the queue mutex (parts gone by then were retired and contribute nothing). The in-flight fraction comes from the merge list (`system.merges` rows with `is_mutation = 1`). Values are estimates by nature: a merge can retire pending parts at any moment, making `progress` jump forward. **Docs**: an "Estimating mutation progress" section on the `system.mutations` page explains why part-count percentages mislead and ships a parameterized-view recipe computing the same number on releases without the columns (the view was validated live against a running mutation, including a merge collapsing 9 pending parts mid-run), plus cross-links from `system.merges`, `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE`, and the knowledge base. The stateless test asserts exact values on both engines: with merges stopped (which parks mutation tasks), `bytes_to_do` equals the active parts' total size and `progress` is 0; after completion the entry reports 0 and 1. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114850&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114850](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114850+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Prometheus HTTP API: implement /api/v1/series
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Experimental Feature** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ****Prometheus HTTP API:** implement **`/api/v1/series`** for **`TimeSeries`** tables.** ### Why this matters **Prometheus clients** use **`/api/v1/series`** to discover the label sets stored for active series. This endpoint is used by **Prometheus-compatible tools** such as **Grafana** when they need to populate metric and label selectors. ClickHouse **`TimeSeries` tables** can store labels in the main **`tags` Map**, in dedicated columns configured with **`tags_to_columns`**, or in a mixture of both layouts. The endpoint needs to expose the **same logical series** regardless of how those labels are stored. ### Description This PR adds **Prometheus `/api/v1/series` support** for **`TimeSeries` tables**. The endpoint is available through both a **dedicated `/api/v1/series` handler** and the **combined `/api/v1` handler**. It supports **GET requests** and **`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` POST requests**. Supported parameters: - **`match[]`** selects series by metric name and label matchers. Repeated parameters are combined as a **union** and overlapping results are returned only once through **deduplication**. - **`start` and `end`** select series overlapping the requested **time range**. - **`limit`** limits the number of returned series and reports when the response was **truncated**. ### Changes - **Selector parsing:** parse Prometheus series selectors with equality, inequality, regular-expression, and negative regular-expression matchers. - **Storage compatibility:** support metric names, labels in the **`tags` Map**, dedicated tag columns, and mixed rows that use both storage layouts. - **Label normalization:** normalize missing labels to the **Prometheus empty-value semantics** and include the full logical label set in each response. - **PromQL compatibility:** support quoted label names and anchor regular expressions to the **complete label value**. - **Input validation:** validate selectors and timestamps before executing the query. - **Time ranges:** apply the time-range filter when trusted min/max data is available. When it is not available, keep the request valid and return the **compatible candidate superset** allowed by the Prometheus API. - **Result limits:** support zero and positive limits, exact-limit responses, truncation reporting, and invalid-value errors. - **Access control:** read the underlying series metadata through the **`TimeSeries` table-function path** after checking access to the configured **`TimeSeries` table**. Unknown routes are resolved before authorization, so they keep the normal **404 response**. - **Existing endpoints:** apply the configured **`TimeSeries` table access boundary** consistently to the existing Prometheus query endpoints. - **Query lifecycle:** run the generated query through the **normal query pipeline** and keep **query logging** and **query completion handling** intact. ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - **Matcher operators:** metric-name and label selectors with all matcher operators. - **Repeated selectors:** repeated **`match[]`** parameters, selector unions, and overlapping-result deduplication. - **Storage layouts:** Map labels, dedicated tag columns, missing labels, mixed carriers, conflicting carriers, and **`__name__`**. - **Regex and names:** quoted label names and whole-value regular-expression anchoring. - **Selector validation:** invalid and unbounded selectors, including the valid **`{host!~".*"}`** case. - **Time ranges:** two-sided, one-sided, inclusive, and invalid time ranges. - **Min/max behavior:** requests with and without trusted min/max metadata. - **Limits:** zero, exact, positive, maximum, and invalid **`limit`** values. - **HTTP methods:** GET and form POST requests. - **Authorization:** wrapper-only **`SELECT` grants**, access checks for all query endpoint families, and unknown-route handling. - **Observability:** query completion records and the existing query API limit behavior. Also ran **Python syntax checks** and **`git diff --check`**. ### Documentation **Documentation is written.** The **TimeSeries engine documentation** now covers the Prometheus handler configuration and the **`/api/v1/series` endpoint parameters**. ### Stack This is the **base PR** for the follow-up Prometheus API endpoints: - **#114868** adds **`/api/v1/labels`**. - **#114869** adds **`/api/v1/label/<name>/values`**. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114867&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114867](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114867+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Don't use JSON skip indexes for combined literal+sub-object subcolumns
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107039 --> `tryMatchJSONSubcolumnToIndex` rejected the sub-object prefix `^`, but not the combined prefix `@`, so ``json.@`a`` was matched against a `JSONAllPaths` index as a path literally named `` @`a` ``. No granule contains such a path, so all granules were pruned: ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE isNotNull(json.`@\`a\``); -- 0, wrong SELECT count() FROM t WHERE isNotNull(json.`@\`a\``) SETTINGS use_skip_indexes=0; -- 2 ``` Reject the `@` prefix as well. Both prefixes are now recognised as the prefix character followed by a back-quote (the rule `tryGetPrefixedSubcolumn` uses), so ordinary paths like `` json.`@timestamp` `` keep using the index. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results when a filter on a combined literal+sub-object `JSON` subcolumn (``json.@`a``) was analyzed against a `JSONAllPaths` skip index: the subcolumn was treated as a path literally named `` @`a` ``, so all granules were skipped and the query returned fewer rows than it should. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114873&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114873](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114873+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Follow-ups for CREATE HANDLER: parse limits of the stored query, docs, refactoring
signals.text: Follow-ups from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 (`CREATE HANDLER`). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 **Requested in review of #106231:** - The two predicates over `IAST::QueryKind` that describe the `readonly` mode - whether a query of that kind is rejected under it, and whether `readonly = 2` still lets it produce side effects - moved out of `SQLDefinedHandlerFromAST` into `Interpreters/QueryKindUnderReadonly.h`; `queryKindRequiresMutatingMethod` is renamed to `isQueryKindRejectedUnderReadonly` after the property it reports. The handler code keeps the statement-level refinements and the HTTP-method fences. - `currentHandler` and `currentRequestURL` were registered with `IntroducedIn` 26.6 (the development version when they were written); they are released in 26.8. **The one unresolved review finding:** a request could still lower the parse limits of a handler's query. `HTTPHandler::processQuery` relaxed `max_parser_depth` / `max_parser_backtracks` *before* applying the settings the request supplies, and a request names settings freely - so `GET /h?max_parser_depth=1` put the caller's value back and broke a handler the server itself had accepted. `max_query_size` had the same hole and did not even need a hostile request: a stored query longer than its default value is creatable and reloadable (both parse without a size limit) but failed on every invocation. The fix went through review iterations and landed as a per-query flag rather than context settings: `executeQuery` receives `QueryFlags::parse_server_owned_query_without_limits` (set by `PredefinedQueryHandler`, from which `SQLDefinedQueryHandler` inherits) and lifts `max_parser_depth` / `max_parser_backtracks` / `max_query_size` only while parsing the stored query text itself. The query context keeps the request's limits, so the request-controlled construction snippets (`select` / `filter` / `order` / `page`) and everything else are still parsed under the caller's own limits - the request can neither break the server's stored text nor borrow its unlimited parse. The flag propagates through `PARALLEL WITH` and `EXECUTE AS` subqueries. New tests `04897_handler_request_parser_limits` (including a `?max_parser_depth=1&filter=(((((1)))))` case that must keep failing) and `04898_handler_large_query_invocation`, both verified to fail without the fix. **Documentation:** the `CREATE HANDLER` page was written into `docs/en/sql-reference/statements/create/handler.md` - a path in the legacy Docusaurus tree that `9440ca729a3` had already removed - so the only documentation of `CREATE HANDLER` / `ALTER HANDLER` / `DROP HANDLER` was published nowhere. It moves to `docs/reference/statements/create/handler.mdx`, with the frontmatter and internal links converted to that tree's conventions and the page registered in `docs/reference/navigation.json`. `docs/en/operations/system-tables/handlers.md` was a leftover copy of the generated `docs/reference/system-tables/handlers.mdx` whose hand-written `SHOW HANDLERS` / secret-masking paragraph had been lost; that paragraph is restored and the legacy copy deleted. The statement is now cross-referenced from the HTTP interface page, the `DROP` page and the `ALTER` overview, and the anchored (`RE2::FullMatch`) semantics of `URL REGEXP` are documented. Verified locally: all 30 SQL-defined-handler stateless tests pass against a server built from this branch (the 31st match of the `handler` filter, `03354_tcp_handler_async_insert_bug`, is unrelated and needs a writable `/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files`), and `04844_handler_deep_query_invocation` still passes without the fix, confirming it covered only the session-level limit. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed HTTP handler invocation so request-level `max_parser_depth`, `max_parser_backtracks`, and `max_query_size` no longer break stored handler queries, and published the `CREATE HANDLER`, `ALTER HANDLER`, and `DROP HANDLER` documentation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114883&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114883](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114883+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix AI functions under-reporting provider usage
signals.text: AI functions under-report what the provider was actually called and billed for. With the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1`, a failing `aiEmbed` logs an exception row showing `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`; flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause 1: counters die while unwinding.** `embedTexts` accumulated into a local `EmbeddingResult` returned by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so failed calls are still counted. The providers lost their token counts the same way. **Cause 2: usage read after validation.** `call` and `embed` parsed `usage` only after validating the response body, so a `200` the provider had already billed for reported no tokens once a check rejected it. This is not only a `system.query_log` undercount: `AIQuotaTracker` never saw those tokens either, so `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query` could not trip and a query with `ai_function_throw_on_error = 0` kept issuing billed requests past its cap. **Fix.** One rule in three places: the accumulator lives in caller-owned storage and is published from a scope guard, so every exit reports it. `embedTexts`, `IAIProvider::call` and `IAIProvider::embed` fill an out-parameter instead of returning by value, and both providers read `usage` before the checks that can reject the body. **Not covered.** `aiSimilarity` scores rows only once every batch is embedded, so its row counters are zero on a throwing exit — no row was scored, even though the first row's operands were embedded and billed. A test pins that. The text path also still publishes its `ProfileEvents` at the end of `executeImpl`, so a throwing text query loses them there; https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 adds that guard. **Tests.** Seven integration tests. The six regression tests were each verified to fail with the source reverted and to pass with it restored; the `aiSimilarity` one records a deliberate choice rather than a fix, so it passes either way. signals.title: Make a table read by a scalar subquery in a CONSTRAINT a loading dependency
signals.text: Attaching a table analyzes its constraints in `InterpreterCreateQuery::getConstraintsDescription`, and the analysis executes the scalar subqueries of a constraint expression. The tables such a subquery reads were not registered as loading dependencies, because `DDLLoadingDependencyVisitor` only looks at functions, dictionary sources and the storage definition. Nothing prevented dropping such a table, and the server did not start afterwards - attaching the dependent table threw `UNKNOWN_TABLE` and loading the metadata failed: ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (conversation UInt64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK (SELECT id FROM t1 LIMIT 15) IN (conversation)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); DROP TABLE t1; -- accepted, and the server cannot start anymore ``` The referential dependency was recorded, since `DDLDependencyVisitor` visits `ASTTableExpression`, so `check_referential_table_dependencies = 1` rejected the `DROP`. But that setting is off by default, and it is the loading graph that the default `check_table_dependencies` check and the `DROP DATABASE` drop order (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057) use. A constraint declaration is now visited, and the tables of every subquery that the analysis executes are added to the loading dependencies. Subqueries which the analysis does not execute - the right argument of `IN` and the argument of `exists`, see `ExecuteScalarSubqueriesMatcher::visit` - are skipped, because what they read is needed only when the constraint is checked, not to attach the table. That keeps `02916_joinget_dependency`-style patterns working, in particular `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`, which drops the table read by an `x IN (SELECT ...)` constraint on purpose. Seen in CI as a `Cannot start clickhouse-server` stress failure, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110231&sha=4de836223549fd5224ca017b8c1a28e344ce38e9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87369 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115648 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A table read by a scalar subquery inside a `CONSTRAINT` is now a loading dependency of the table that declares the constraint. Previously such a table could be dropped, after which the server did not start, because attaching the dependent table executes the subquery. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114923&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114923](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114923+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix an unkillable hang when dropping a low-sorting-name TimeSeries table
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114259 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang when dropping a `TimeSeries` table whose name sorts lexicographically below its inner tables' names, for example `` DROP TABLE `-ts` `` or dropping a materialized view declared with `ENGINE = TimeSeries`. The drop self-deadlocked on the DDL guard and could not be cancelled with `KILL QUERY`. ### Description `DROP TABLE` of a `TimeSeries` table never returned and could not be killed when the table's own qualified name sorted below its inner tables' names: ```sql SET allow_experimental_time_series_table = 1; CREATE TABLE `-ts` ENGINE = TimeSeries; DROP TABLE `-ts`; -- hung forever ``` A materialized view's inner name is `.inner_id.<uuid>`, which always sorts below `.inner_id.metrics.<uuid>`, so dropping an `MV ... ENGINE = TimeSeries` hung too. **Root cause.** `executeDropQuery` takes the DDL guard for the inner table, then synthesizes an `ASTDropQuery` for that same table without setting `no_ddl_lock`, so the nested interpreter takes the guard for the identical name again. `DDLGuard::table_lock` wraps a non-recursive `std::mutex`, so the thread deadlocks against itself. A mutex wait is not a cancellation point, so `KILL QUERY` could not land and the guard stayed held for the server's lifetime. `need_ddl_guard = true` comes from one call site, `StorageTimeSeries::dropInnerTableIfAny`, which requests the inner guard only when the parent name sorts first. That predicate is correct and is kept: guards must be taken in increasing name order. Only its comment was wrong, claiming the inner name is "almost always less", which holds for `MaterializedView` but not `TimeSeries`. **The change.** `executeDropQuery` now sets `no_ddl_lock = need_ddl_guard`, so the inner name is guarded exactly once, by the caller, across the nested execute. `InterpreterCreateQuery` sets the same field for the same reason. The fix is inert for the other ten call sites, which all take the `need_ddl_guard = false` default. The `ddl_guard` null check is pre-existing hardening. **Validation.** Both shapes time out before the fix and succeed after, while a high-sorting-name control passes on both builds. Eight concurrent drops serialize and complete and the name is reusable afterwards, so the guard is still taken and released. New test `04920` covers both shapes and asserts no inner table is left behind.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Honour do_not_block_pipeline_on_failure for every non-ok job status
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107115 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109071 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description A job that sets `do_not_block_pipeline_on_failure` still blocked its whole downstream closure whenever it ended `ERROR` rather than `FAIL`. The two consumers disagreed. `hook_html.py:224` gates on `not result.is_ok()`, so dependees were correctly not marked `DROPPED`. `runner.py:910` gated on `result.is_failure()`, which is `FAIL`/`XPASS` only, so an `ERROR` was never exempted and the job emitted `pipeline_status=failure`. Every dependent job's guard is `!contains(needs.*.outputs.pipeline_status, 'failure')` over a transitive `needs`, so that one token skips the entire closure. The case that hits it: an integration shard exhausts its 7200 s parallel-phase budget and appends a synthetic `Timeout` child while every real test passes. One non-ok child means `force_ok_exit = True`, so the job declares itself non-blocking, but the same timeout sets the error flag and `set_error()` makes the status `ERROR`. That skipped 107 of 175 results on #107115 and 112 of 177 on #109071, including all five `Bugfix validation (*)` jobs. Because those never ran, `new_tests_check.py` read them as `PENDING` and failed `Finish Workflow` with "it's not actually a regression test for the fix", reporting a timeout in an unrelated shard as a verdict on the author's regression test. 8 occurrences across 8 PRs and 5 of the 6 shards in 30 days. `runner.py` now uses the same predicate as `hook_html`, extracted so it is reachable from a test. They have been asymmetric since the `runner.py` consumer was added in `b35b5fd41f28412`. `functional_tests.py:1527` passes the same flag after a path that can also end `ERROR`, so it is fixed by the same line. **Merge-blocking is unchanged.** `ready_for_merge` is computed from `job.allow_failure` alone (`native_jobs.py:1102-1117`) and never reads this flag; all six shards are `allow_failure=False`, so a failing shard still blocks the merge and still reports red. Only downstream dispatch changes. `new_tests_check.py` is left as it is: its strict check is correct once the jobs actually run. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Every mutation below was applied to production code and the suite re-run. | arm | mutation | result | |---|---|---| | 0 | the fix | 45 passed | | A | predicate reverted to `is_failure()` (pre-fix behaviour) | 11 failed, incl. the end-to-end shard shape | | B | exemption made unconditional, flag ignored (negative control) | 14 failed (every `flag=False` row) | | C | `hook_html` predicate drifted to `is_failure()` | 1 failed (the agreement pin) | | D | output site re-derives the status inline, helper left unused | 1 failed (the delegation pin) | | E | merge gate made to read the flag | 1 failed (the merge-gate pin) | | F | emitted token hardcoded, or overridden after the call | 1 failed each (the emit pin) | Arm B is what rules out a vacuous oracle: a test that ignored the flag would stay green. Arms D, E and F each redden exactly one test, pinning the seams nothing else covers: the call site the extraction created, the token actually emitted, and the merge computation the paragraph above rests on. The new test parametrizes every non-ok member of `Result.Status` (`FAIL`, `ERROR`, `XPASS`, `DROPPED`, `UNKNOWN`, `PENDING`, `RUNNING`) and all three ok members against flag on/off, asserts the two consumers reach the same verdict, reproduces the measured production shape (903 `OK` + 17 `SKIPPED` + 1 `Timeout`), and pins `allow_failure=False` on the six shards. Full `ci/tests`: 972 passed / 31 skipped / 8 failed with the fix, versus 927 / 31 / 8 on pristine `runner.py`. The same 8 pre-existing environment failures on both arms (`clickhouse was not found in PATH`); the delta is the new tests. Exactly two production `complete_job(` call sites pass this flag, and both are covered by this one line. The only other writer of `pipeline_status` is the config job's unconditional `success`. The remaining `is_failure()` uses are test-level row filtering or rendering, not job-level gating. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1812` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not regenerate part names from part infos for tables with the deprecated syntax
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87206 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103537 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112457 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `BAD_DATA_PART_NAME` ("Trying to get part name in new format for old format version") on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` created with the deprecated positional syntax under `allow_deprecated_syntax_for_merge_tree`. A mutation could be reported as done on a replica that had not applied it, and the table could stay readonly after a restart. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #112457 ([`Upgrade check (amd_release)` report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112457&sha=f888781eb610bfabdc8c8675d835b99482bec8a2&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29)). No related open issue found. A table created with `ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree(date, key, granularity)` uses date-based (V0) part names. `MergeTreePartInfo::getPartNameAndCheckFormat` cannot produce one, because the min/max dates it needs are not part of a `MergeTreePartInfo`, so it throws. Two `ActiveDataPartSet` entry points take only an info and regenerate the name that way; each had exactly one caller, and both callers already held the name and threw it away. This change passes the name at both call sites, as in `536b611c96a757e`, which fixed the `ATTACH PARTITION` instance of this bug. V0 name formatting is untouched, and current-format tables are unaffected because the name-taking overload re-parses to the same info and runs the same insertion code. The linked report contains both failures: - `ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue::getPartNamesToMutate` builds `mutation.parts_to_do`. The throw left it empty, so a mutation reported `is_done` on a replica that never mutated its part, and `mutations_sync = 2` returned success while that replica still served pre-mutation values. Regressed by #87206, which changed `produced_parts` to hold infos instead of names. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkPartsImpl` builds the set of empty unexpected parts. The throw aborted `ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread`, leaving the table readonly. Regressed by my own #103537, which replaced a name-based call with an info-based one. The V0 gap in `MergeTreeData::restorePartFromBackup` that the throw-site comment describes is a different code path, absent from both stacks, and is not addressed. A new stateless test asserts `parts_to_do` on the frozen replica: it fails on master (`parts to do 0`) and passes here (`parts to do 2`), and 50/50 randomized runs pass. `checkPartsImpl`'s state needs parts fabricated on disk, so that half is covered by three V0 cases added to `gtest_active_data_part_set.cpp`, all of which fail with this change reverted. `00062_replicated_merge_tree_alter_zookeeper_long` and `00652_replicated_mutations_zookeeper` still pass.

signals.title: Fix logical error for IN with an identical non-constant tuple on both sides in the old analyzer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID 2508-3457: ```sql EXPLAIN PIPELINE graph = 0, graph = 0, compact = 1 SELECT 'null', (SELECT tuple(materialize(NULL), NULL) GLOBAL IN (materialize(NULL), NULL)) GROUP BY ALL SETTINGS transform_null_in = 1 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=38215c1758332de1ea8a4b5a620ba8364586f6c6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 It reaches the old interpreter through a scalar subquery, and reduces to `SELECT (materialize(1), 2) IN (materialize(1), 2) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0`. Release builds catch the exception but still reject the query with an empty identifier name: `Code: 47 ... Unknown identifier: ; there are columns: dummy, 1, materialize(1), 2, ...`. Root cause: a literal's `unique_column_name` is assigned lazily, only when `ActionsMatcher::visit(const ASTLiteral &)` runs, and `getNameAndTypeFromAST` requires it. The old interpreter's row-wise `IN` rewrite visits the left argument first, and here the right-hand `tuple` renders to the same column name as the left one, so `visit(right_argument, data)` takes the common-subexpression early return and never descends into the right-hand children. The loop that follows then asks for the name and type of each raw child, and a literal child is still unnamed. The fix visits each child before naming it. That call site was the only one of the eight `getNameAndTypeFromAST` callers in the file not already preceded by a `visit()` of the node it names. `visit` is idempotent, so the added call is a no-op when the child is already indexed. The abort is gone after the change, with the result now matching `enable_analyzer = 1` on 20 shapes (including `NULL` with `transform_null_in`, `nullIn`, `GLOBAL IN`, `LowCardinality`, array and tuple literal children, `indexHint`, and the query above). 13 shapes that already worked are unchanged, with byte-identical `EXPLAIN actions = 1` output. Removing the added line reinstates the abort. Introduced by #104993 and present only on master, so no backport is needed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993

signals.title: Label "submodule changed" only when a submodule actually changed
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) The `submodule changed` label is applied by matching the `contrib/` path prefix: ```python if "contrib/" in " ".join(changed_files): pr_labels_to_add.append(Labels.SUBMODULE_CHANGED) ``` Most of `contrib/` is not submodules. The `contrib/<lib>-cmake/` directories are ClickHouse's own build glue, `contrib/CMakeLists.txt` is ours, and some directories under `contrib/` are ordinary in-repo trees — `contrib/antlr4-grammars` and `contrib/antlr4-grammars-cmake` are not registered in `.gitmodules` at all. Editing any of them gets a PR labelled as changing a submodule although no gitlink moved. **Of the 77 open PRs currently carrying the label, 33 contain no submodule change at all.** I measured this by taking each PR's diff and looking for `Subproject commit` lines, which is what a gitlink change always renders as — that catches bumps, additions and removals without depending on any `.gitmodules` baseline. Representative cases: | PR | `contrib/` files touched | gitlink changed | | --- | --- | --- | | #63057 | `contrib/arrow-cmake/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #88857 | `contrib/jwt-cpp-cmake/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #78494 | `contrib/datasketches-cpp-cmake/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #80177 | `contrib/CMakeLists.txt`, `contrib/aws-sdk-cpp-*/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #107200 | `contrib/datasketches-cpp-cmake/include_patched/…` | no | | #113173, #112861, #114558 | `contrib/antlr4-grammars…/PromQLLexer.{g4,cpp,interp}` | no | This decides the label from the submodule lifecycle instead, using only the data the hook already has — the PR's changed-file list and the checkout's `.gitmodules`: - a **bump** leaves `.gitmodules` untouched, but the submodule path is in the changed-file list and is still registered, so the path intersection catches it; - **adding**, **removing** and **renaming** a submodule all edit `.gitmodules` itself, so that file appearing in the changed-file list is the signal. Both conditions are needed. A removal is invisible to the path intersection, because the removed path is no longer registered at the head — and a removal that forgets to clean up `.gitmodules` leaves the entry in place, where the intersection catches it. `ci/tests/test_pr_labels_submodule_changed.py` pins the whole lifecycle. Against those cases: | implementation | wrong | | --- | --- | | `contrib/` substring match | 3 of 11 — the `-cmake` glue and grammar false positives | | head `.gitmodules` paths only | 1 of 11 — the removal | | this PR | 0 of 11 | One thing this PR deliberately does not change: the label is only ever added, never removed, so a PR that once touched `contrib/` keeps it afterwards. That accounts for 9 of the 33 above, which touch no `contrib/` file at all today. Worth knowing when checking this fix against an existing PR — the stale label will not clear by itself.

signals.title: Reuse LowCardinality aggregation mappings across blocks
signals.text: Previously dictionary position to aggregate state mappings were only valid within a block. For parts where there's only a single dictionary, this is too restrictive and resulted in repeated work. This moves the mapping cache to the aggregation method, matching its lifetime to the aggregation hash table. We keep the successful mappings while the dict remains unchanged. Non-shared dictionaries remain block local. This gives a very nice speedup to the benchmark in the previous commit: | Width | LC before | LC after | Change | |-----------------|----------:|----------:|-------:| | `UInt8` | 0.1220 s | 0.1158 s | -5.1% | | `UInt16` | 0.1703 s | 0.1395 s | -18.1% | | `UInt32` | 0.1884 s | 0.1489 s | -20.9% | | `UInt64` | 0.1952 s | 0.1513 s | -22.5% | | `UInt128` | 0.5676 s | 0.5649 s | -0.5% | | `UInt256` | 0.9354 s | 0.9206 s | -1.6% | | `String` (6 B) | 0.2535 s | 0.1598 s | -37.0% | | `String` (26 B) | 0.2521 s | 0.1630 s | -35.4% | | `String` (56 B) | 0.2689 s | 0.1655 s | -38.5% | The improvements for UInt128 and UInt256 will be there after #114982 is merged. The benefit is largest when many blocks share the same dictionary, because dictionary-position mappings are reused across those blocks. _AI assisted, scratching an itch I've had for a while._ ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve aggregation performance by reusing LowCardinality aggregation mappings across blocks. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114993&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114993](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114993+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix reading a tuple element through a positional Tuple structure hint
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 Reading a tuple element through a positional structure hint returned default values instead of the file's data. Over a Parquet file written as `t Tuple(x UInt64, y String)`: ```sql SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('p.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)'); -- returned 0, 0, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2 ``` `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matched no rows, and with `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query failed with `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN`. Silent wrong results, on default settings. Root cause: an unnamed tuple names its elements `1`, `2`, ..., so `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` rewrote `tupleElement(t, 1)` to the subcolumn `t.1`. The existing guards there consult the storage snapshot, which is built from the structure argument and does contain `t.1`. The Parquet reader then resolves a flattened element name by string against the file's real field names `t.x`, `t.y`, found no match, and substituted a missing column filled with defaults. The fix suppresses the rewrite when the element name is a bare ordinal and the source resolves subcolumn names against a file schema. Named hints keep their pushdown, and storages serving subcolumns from their own metadata (MergeTree and friends) are unaffected. This regressed in #113383 and is master-only: that merge is an ancestor of no release branch and is in no release tag, hence `Not for changelog`. That category also skips `Bugfix validation`, so the reddening check below is the evidence. Validated on a Debug build, with a regression arm added to `04706_tuple_subcolumn_pushdown_parquet`: - Reddening: removing only the new guard term makes the new arm fail while the pre-existing arms stay green. - Preservation: `t.x` pushdown survives for a named hint by name and by ordinal, and `t.1` still pushes down for MergeTree's unnamed tuple. - `04706`, `04707`, `04708`, `04873` pass; a `subcolumn`/`tuple_element`/`functions_to_subcolumns` sweep has no failure absent from an unmodified-master control; 50 randomized runs pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115000&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115000](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115000+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support `Merge` tables with plan-based parallel replicas
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/67770 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972 Lets a `Merge` table be read with parallel replicas, implemented on top of the plan-based parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_plan_based`). `ReadFromMerge` is opaque to the parallel-replicas plan transformation: it unites the pipelines of its per-table subplans instead of their plans, so the underlying `MergeTree` reads do not exist yet while the plan is transformed. An eligible `ReadFromMerge` is therefore expanded into a plan-level `UnionStep` over those child reads, right before the reads to distribute are collected. A `Merge` then has exactly the shape the transformation already distributes - a union of `MergeTree` reads - so the reads are coordinated across the replicas, and the steps above the `Merge` (aggregation, joins) are distributed as well, without any `Merge`-specific code in the coordinator, in the serialization or in the local plan. The expansion is off by default, gated by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, and takes effect only together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`. A `Merge` is read by a single replica when one of its children is not a plain `MergeTree` read, when the read is `FINAL`, or when no table matches its regexp. This is an alternative to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972, which implements the same feature on the legacy (query-tree-based) path. There, the query text is reshipped and every replica re-analyzes it, which needs a fail-close handshake (`parallel_replicas_designated_table`, `_freshness_checked_tables`, `_merge_child_tables`) to guard against the set of underlying tables differing across replicas or changing between planning and reading. The plan-based path ships a serialized plan fragment with the tables already resolved, so none of that is needed. Tests: three new stateless tests - the core feature and its negative cases (`04907`), the query shapes a `Merge` can be read with, including the `merge` table function, a filter on the `_table` virtual column and reading in order with a limit (`04908`), and `Merge` tables inside JOINs on either side of the join (`04909`). Each of them checks the results against non-parallel execution and asserts through the plan how the query was distributed. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `Merge` table can now be read with parallel replicas: the reads from the underlying `MergeTree` tables are coordinated across the replicas, and the aggregations and joins above them are distributed too. Enabled by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, which takes effect together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115001&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115001](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115001+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
