signals.title: Add stateless and fuzzer jobs to the WeeklyCFI workflow
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100419 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112152 The `amd_cfi` build is the only test build with ThinLTO enabled — the same compile profile as official release builds — so besides CFI violations the WeeklyCFI workflow also catches ThinLTO-only behavior differences that no other CI job can see. The latest example is the `__functional` frame-name suppression surfaced by `test_crash_log` in the weekly runs of 2026-07-20 through 2026-08-10 and fixed in #112152. This PR broadens the workflow's coverage: - **Stateless tests** (parallel + sequential lanes, mirroring `amd_debug`). `clickhouse-test` now detects the CFI build from `-fsanitize=cfi` in the `CXX_FLAGS` row of `system.build_options`, so tests that cannot pass in this build profile can carry a `no-cfi` tag (the same generic `no-<flag>` skip mechanism the sanitizer builds use). CFI is deliberately not treated as a sanitizer: it has near-zero runtime overhead, so tests tagged `no-sanitizers` still run under CFI. - **AST fuzzer and BuzzHouse**: fuzzers assert only on crashes, never on exact query output, so the build profile cannot produce false positives there, and fuzzing reaches virtual-call combinations the curated suites never exercise. The fuzzer job configs are shared out into `_common_ast_fuzzer_job_config` / `_common_buzz_fuzzer_job_config`; master and PR workflows are unchanged. Not added, and why: unit tests (`ENABLE_CFI` is incompatible with `ENABLE_TESTS` — ThinLTO is disabled when building tests), performance comparison (it compares against the non-CFI master-head binary, so results are uninterpretable), upgrade/compatibility checks (version and data compatibility are orthogonal to CFI instrumentation), Keeper Jepsen (requires the standalone `clickhouse-keeper` build, which the CFI build omits). **Validation (complete):** the workflow was temporarily switched to a `pull_request` trigger (same approach as #100419) and all ten `amd_cfi` jobs passed on `baf56e50335` — stateless parallel + sequential, integration 4/4, stress, AST fuzzer, and BuzzHouse ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=baf56e50335c45adf2afb691d0a1ef72f49c8bc6&name_0=WeeklyCFI)). The schedule-only trigger is restored in the final commit. The first run surfaced two findings, both filed: a probabilistic server crash in gRPC response compression (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115121) and empty `symbols`/`lines` in `system.trace_log` under this build profile (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115122 — the two `03150` tests are left enabled, so the weekly stateless lane stays red until it is fixed; this workflow does not gate PRs). Workflow: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/workflows/weekly_cfi.yml ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115036](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115036+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Offer the `/`-commands of the client, and name them when misspelled
signals.text: Typing `/` at the beginning of the input now shows the client's own commands (`/clear`, `/help`, `/man`) as as-you-type hints, and typing more of a name narrows the list down. `Tab` completes the command being typed, which is also how they are completed when the instant hints are disabled (`--hints 0`, `--highlight 0`, `--disable_suggestion`). Until now these commands could only be found in the documentation; now the prompt itself lists them. A mistake in the name of a command is reported as such, with the commands it may have meant, instead of being parsed as SQL and reported as a syntax error at the `/`: ``` :) /hepl Exception on client: Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unknown command `/hepl`. Maybe you meant: ['/help']. Type `/` at the beginning of the line to see all the commands. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` An argument given to a command that takes none (`/clear now`) is reported the same way. Batch `clickhouse-client` still parses such input as the SQL it is, exactly like it already does for `help` and `clear`; `clickhouse-local` reports it like the interactive client. The commands come from a single list, `clientSlashCommands`, shared by the hints, the completion and the diagnostics. An offered command replaces the whole typed prefix including the `/`, which `replxx` counts as a word break character and would otherwise leave in place. The offer is off for `keeper-client` and `clickhouse-disks`: they reuse the same line reader, and a leading `/` is the beginning of a path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `/`-commands of the client (`/help`, `/man`, `/clear`) are now offered by the line editor: typing `/` at the beginning of the input lists them as hints, and `Tab` completes the command being typed. A mistake in the name of a command is reported with the similar commands suggested, instead of being parsed as SQL. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115039&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115039](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115039+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Tag functional tests averaging over 60s under MSan with `no-msan`
signals.text: MSan stateless jobs are the slowest functional-test jobs in CI and sit right at the edge of the 9000 s job timeout. In a recent run the private `Stateless tests (amd_msan, distributed cache, meta in keeper, s3 storage, sequential, 2/2)` job spent 8324 s of its 9000 s budget on tests and was then killed during teardown, even though all 526 tests had passed. MSan is ~5.8× slower than release on the same tests, and the cost is concentrated in a long tail: under MSan, 8 tests take over 180 s each, and the 30 slowest account for ~48% of a sequential shard's runtime. This tags every functional test whose mean duration under MSan exceeds 60 s with `no-msan`, except two tests that would otherwise lose all sanitizer coverage. ### How the set was chosen From `play.clickhouse.com`, over the public MSan stateless checks (`Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, N/M)` and `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, sequential, N/2)`, excluding the flaky-check and selected-tests flavors): ```sql SELECT test_name, count() AS runs, avg(test_duration_ms)/1000 AS avg_s FROM checks WHERE check_name LIKE 'Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, %' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%flaky%' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%selected%' AND test_status = 'OK' AND check_start_time >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY test_name HAVING runs >= 20 AND avg_s > 60 ORDER BY avg_s DESC ``` 351 tests matched. 30 of them no longer exist in `master` (reverted, split into smaller tests, or removed), leaving 321. One of those, `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata`, already carried `no-msan`; two more remain under MSan to retain their only sanitizer coverage, so 318 files change here. Only `OK` runs are counted, so timeouts and failures do not inflate the averages. ### Initial expected effect The following estimates were calculated before retaining the two sanitizer-coverage tests. | Flavor | MSan test time per commit | Removed | Share | |---|---|---|---| | parallel | 129025 s | 24766 s | 19.2% | | sequential | 11236 s | 4108 s | 36.6% | ### 25 slowest of the tagged tests | Test | Mean under MSan | Runs | |---|---|---| | `03988_cached_read_big_at` | 384.6 s | 9014 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_replicated` | 337.2 s | 9116 | | `03008_deduplication_several_mv_into_one_table_nonreplicated` | 308.8 s | 9118 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_nonreplicated` | 282.6 s | 9118 | | `04039_merge_tree_snapshot_teardown_race` | 275.2 s | 9347 | | `01195_formats_diagnostic_info` | 234.6 s | 9278 | | `02475_bson_each_row_format` | 206.1 s | 9264 | | `00626_replace_partition_from_table_zookeeper` | 202.5 s | 9323 | | `01019_alter_materialized_view_atomic` | 192.5 s | 9340 | | `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata` | 190.4 s | 1806 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long` | 182.8 s | 9339 | | `00746_sql_fuzzy` | 180.5 s | 9340 | | `03755_large_primary_key_explain` | 180.2 s | 9337 | | `02943_variant_type_with_different_local_and_global_order` | 180.2 s | 9284 | | `02448_clone_replica_lost_part` | 177.4 s | 9263 | | `02372_analyzer_join` | 176.3 s | 9345 | | `04327_cluster_functions_huge_num_streams_no_crash` | 171.8 s | 9261 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long_oldanalyzer` | 168.9 s | 9346 | | `01079_bad_alters_zookeeper_long` | 166.8 s | 9322 | | `01747_system_session_log_long` | 165.9 s | 9014 | | `03208_array_of_json_read_subcolumns_1` | 165 s | 9339 | | `00429_long_http_bufferization` | 160.9 s | 9277 | | `04411_deep_nested_field_to_type` | 156.8 s | 9262 | | `01383_log_broken_table` | 156.4 s | 9340 | | `03326_protobuf_schemas_race` | 155.1 s | 9279 | (318 tests are tagged in total; the full list is the diff.) ### Trade-off A large share of these are the ZooKeeper, replication, mutation and race tests — precisely where MSan is most likely to find real uninitialized-memory bugs. They continue to run under ASan, UBSan and TSan, but this is a genuine reduction in MSan coverage rather than a pure win. An alternative that keeps the coverage is duration-aware sharding of the sequential jobs: the split is currently `crc32(test filename) % total_batches`, which gave one recent shard 8248 s against its sibling's 5514 s (1.50×), so balancing alone would have reclaimed ~23 min on the shard that timed out. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115050&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115050](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115050+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Record an index's absent columns when materializing it on a wide part
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114990 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112484 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes an unreleased regression from #112484 (`master` only): `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX` produced an index that never prunes when the indexed column had been added by a metadata-only `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` and the part is wide. No stable release carries #112484, so no changelog entry and no backport are owed. ### Description Reported by @ clickgapai. #112484 merged on 2026-08-15 and is an ancestor of no release branch, so only `master` is affected. **What breaks.** `ADD COLUMN c ... DEFAULT ...` on a wide part is metadata-only, so the part holds no bytes for `c`. A following `MATERIALIZE INDEX idx` writes the index files but does not add `c` to the part's column list, and since #112484 the reader refuses an index whose columns the part does not describe. The index occupies disk and never prunes: `Granules: 16/16` on the reporter's fixture versus `1/16` before, results correct both ways. **Root cause.** `splitAndModifyMutationCommands` has two branches. The compact one turns an index's required-but-absent columns into `READ_COLUMN` commands; the wide one had no such step, so `c` never enters `updated_header` and `getColumnsForNewDataPart` erases it. The missing type is the defect, so the fix belongs on the write side. **The change.** On a wide part, `MATERIALIZE INDEX` now also reads the index's absent columns, so the part records them at the type the granules were built from. The column list belongs to the part, so it records the column only when every other index holding files there either does not read it or has its granules rebuilt by this same mutation: a carried-over granule keeps its build-time type, so recording the column now would hand the reader a matching type for a stale granule. What the mutation rebuilds is decided from its own commands, and an undecidable index counts as carried over, keeping the pre-fix behaviour. Compact parts and the reader are untouched, so every #112484 refusal holds. **Cost.** The mutation now writes column data: +247 bytes before, +806,931 after on a 200k-row wide fixture; the next merge writes it anyway. No format, serialization or default change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry. <details> <summary>Validation, rejected alternative, known-unfixed shape</summary> **Rejected alternative:** recording build-time types in a new per-part file - a format change needing ~9 seams, a protocol bump and upgrade/downgrade paths. **Known-unfixed:** on a part with orphan index files (#109595) `hasSecondaryIndex` is true, so the read is suppressed and the index stays inert - the status quo, never wrong results. | arm | absent arm | control arm | |---|---|---| | pristine master | `16/16` (inert) | 1/16 | | this PR | `1/16` | 1/16 | Counts identical with and without `use_skip_indexes` in every cell; the control prunes on both. Four mutation arms cover the restriction, each red on the build missing its guard: without it, a hardlinked granule's column is rewritten at the new type and the next read attempts a 4 EiB allocation; keyed to the index named in the command rather than the column, a second index over that column has its stale granules re-enabled and the next read aborts; without the rebuilt-sibling exemption, a batched update that does rebuild the sibling still suppresses it, leaving the new index inert - covered both for a sibling reached by a named column and for one reached via a TTL target. Tests: `04869_skip_index_stale_type_absent_column` gains cases 26 (the regression), 26b (subcolumn index, absent parent recorded), 27, 28 (two indices, one absent column), 29 and 30 (rebuilt sibling). Cases 11/22/23/24 moved from `ADD COLUMN` to a column TTL expiry, since the fix makes the old route no longer leave a column absent; each gained an `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` refusal assertion, and every such assertion now pins the granule count rather than matching a substring. `04246_materialize_index_force_recalc` (the #104872 compact tripwire), `04165`, `04870` and `04871` pass unchanged; 250/250 across a 50-run randomized loop. Unrelated columns stay hardlinked (by inode), so the mutation does not escalate to a full part rewrite. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115055&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115055](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115055+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reject invalid event numbers and durations in sequenceMatch patterns
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an `out_of_range` exception raised as an internal `Code: 1001` error when a `sequenceMatch`, `sequenceCount` or `sequenceMatchEvents` pattern contains the event number `0`, for example `sequenceMatch('(?0)')`. Such a pattern is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. A temporal condition holding a lone sign, such as `sequenceMatch('(?1)(?t>+)(?2)')`, was silently treated as `(?t>0)` and is now rejected with `SYNTAX_ERROR`. ### Description Event numbers are 1-based, but the bound check validated only the upper bound, so `(?0)` passed it. The conversion to a 0-based condition index then underflowed `UInt64` to `SIZE_MAX`, and `std::bitset<32>::set()` rejected that with `std::out_of_range`. Thrown from the aggregate function constructor during analysis, it surfaced as an internal `Code: 1001` error and aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds. Two further inputs reached the same state: an event number overflowing `UInt64`, and a sign with no digits, `(?+)`. In each case `tryReadIntText` fails after consuming a byte while its pointer overload discards the boolean, so the existing "Could not parse number" check does not fire and the output keeps its initialiser `0`. Adding the missing lower bound validates the parsed value and covers all three at once, error code and message unchanged. The sibling temporal branch shared that parse-success defect and is fixed here too, after review automation raised it: `(?t>+)` was accepted as `(?t>0)`. The duration is now read through the `ReadBuffer` overload so the boolean is available, and rejected when it is false. The position check is kept, because `tryReadIntText` also succeeds while consuming nothing for a leading non-digit, which is what rejects `(?t>)`. Only the sign form leaked; `(?t>-)` and an overflowing duration were already rejected, and `(?t>+5)` still equals `(?t>5)`. All three functions share this parser and were affected; all are covered by new assertions in `00222_sequence_aggregate_function_family`, which fail on an unfixed binary. One imprecision is left as is: an overflowing event number is reported as event number `0`. Found by `AST fuzzer (amd_tsan)`, `bitset set argument out of range` (STID 2508-34fb): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115019&sha=7be817c59e288cab7aa329a76ed1ba65b9d555e9&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29. Also seen on `Stress test (arm_tsan)`. Both carrier pull requests are bystanders; the defect reproduces on pristine master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115056&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115056](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115056+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1808` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not merge patch parts across the data version of an existing part
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/98898 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113998 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Found patch part ... that intersects mutation with version ...` (`LOGICAL_ERROR`) on tables with lightweight updates. A merge of patch parts could produce a patch whose range of data versions spans the data version of an existing part; that patch can then be neither applied nor skipped, so every later operation on the partition failed and the replication queue stalled. Such merges are no longer assigned. ### Description A patch part is applied to a part either wholly or not at all: `patchHasHigherDataVersion` asserts that the patch's data versions are either all newer or all older than the data version of the part, and throws a `LOGICAL_ERROR` otherwise. Merging patch parts unions their ranges of data versions, so the merged range must not span the data version of any part in the original partition. The merge predicate took that boundary from `getCurrentMutationVersion`, that is from the mutations it still knows about. Those records are not durable, while the data version a mutation gave to the parts is: * `ReplicatedMergeTree` removes a mutation from `mutations_by_partition` when the cleanup thread drops the finished `/mutations` znode, and immediately on `KILL MUTATION`; * `MergeTree` removes it from `current_mutations_by_version` in `clearOldMutations`. Once the record is gone, every patch on either side of the boundary maps to the same version, the pair looks mergeable, and the merge produces a patch that spans a version the parts have already crossed. From then on `DETACH`/`DROP`/`MOVE`/`REPLACE PARTITION`, applying patches and building a mutations snapshot all fail on that partition, and debug and sanitizer builds abort. The fix takes the boundary from the data versions of the parts. For `ReplicatedMergeTree` they come from `virtual_parts`, which is `current_parts` + `queue`, so a version that only a queued `MUTATE_PART` has assigned is seen before that entry is executed — the pending-mutation case, which #113998 addresses from the queue side, is covered as well. The versions are collected only when the table has patch parts, so tables without lightweight updates pay nothing. No assertion is relaxed. The refused merge is never needed: the patch on the older side of the boundary is fully applied, so `clearUnusedPatchParts` drops it, and the patches on the newer side still merge with each other. This does not repair a patch that already spans a version on disk; such a table stays stuck until the patch is removed. The test is deterministic: it keeps the applied patch with `remove_unused_patch_parts = 0`, removes the finished mutation record with `KILL MUTATION`, and forces the merge with `OPTIMIZE ... PARTITION ID '<patch partition>' FINAL`. On master it aborts with the exact message; with the fix the merge is refused, the patches stay separate and the data is correct. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=0fc2db3239a1bd6dd6581f103473834687408b7d&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 The same `LOGICAL_ERROR` accounts for 23 stress-test failures across 8 distinct stacks and every build flavor between 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-16, the most frequent one being a merged patch part reported from `MergeTreeData::MutationsSnapshotBase`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115064&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115064](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115064+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Hand the connection to the built-in web UI pages over `postMessage`
signals.text: The built-in web UI pages — `/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary` — take their connection from their own query string, which cannot carry a password: a URL ends up in browser history, `Referer` headers, server access logs and proxy logs. Only `/webterminal` could be handed credentials by the page embedding it, in a `postMessage` message. Every page now speaks that same exchange: ``` page -> host {type: 'clickhouse-hello'} host -> page {type: 'clickhouse-credentials', url, user, password} ``` The page announces itself as soon as it can apply a connection, and the host answers. The page has to speak first because a host that opened it with `window.open` cannot observe when a cross-origin document became ready, and an embedded page would otherwise race its host's `load` handler. Having adopted a connection, each page redoes what it had already loaded with the previous one, so the handover also works when it arrives after the page started querying: `/play` re-probes the credentials, `/docs` rebuilds its cross-link name cache and re-runs the displayed search, `/dashboard` and `/processors-profile` chain their reload behind the load already in flight (two concurrent loads would otherwise duplicate charts, or let a stale failure overwrite a good listing), `/schema` and `/jemalloc` reload, and `/binary` drops its cached tiles and redraws. ## Opening `/docs` from `/play` The Documentation icon in the `/play` sidebar is the first user of the handover. A plain click opens `/docs` through `window.open` — the anchor's `rel=noopener` would sever the handle — and hands the whole connection over, so the documentation search runs against the same server as the same user without the password appearing in a URL. A middle or modifier click keeps the browser's native new-tab handling, which carries `?user=` only, since such a window has no link back to `/play`. ## Security A reply is accepted only from the one window that opened or embeds the page, and only from an exact origin: the page's own, `https://console.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://console.clickhouse-staging.com` or `https://clickhouse.com`. The list is exact rather than a domain suffix on purpose — every ClickHouse Cloud service endpoint is a `*.clickhouse.cloud` host that serves content of its owner's choosing, and a trusted host can aim a page at a server of its own through `url`, which the user may then type credentials into believing it is still their own service. `webterminal.html` gated its own exchange on such a suffix and now uses the same exact list. `url` is optional and defaults to the server the page already points at, but the credentials are replaced wholesale: a message that names only a server cannot attach credentials it did not carry to it, which is what keeps a password filled in by the browser's password manager for this page's origin from following a `url` elsewhere. Outbound, credentials are always sent with an exact target origin, never `'*'`; the readiness announcement carries no secrets, only the fact that the page exists, which its host knows already. Verified in Chromium against a mock endpoint: the `/play` → `/docs` handover, the handover into an iframe for all eight pages, rejection of a handover from an untrusted origin and from a same-origin window that is not the page's host, the wholesale credential replacement, and the exactness of the origin list for all nine pages (`https://myserviceendpoint.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://evil.clickhouse.com`, `http://console.clickhouse.cloud` and `https://console.clickhouse.cloud.evil.com` are all rejected). The committed test asserts that every served page implements both halves of the exchange and that its origin list stayed exact. The protocol is documented in `docs/concepts/features/interfaces/web-ui-embedding.mdx`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The built-in web UI pages (`/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary`) can now be handed their connection — server URL, user and password — in a `postMessage` message by the page that opened or embedded them, instead of taking it from their own query string, where a password would be recorded in browser history, referrer headers and access logs. `/play` uses this when opening `/docs`, so the documentation search connects to the same server as the same user. A page accepts a connection only from the window that opened or embeds it, and only from an exact list of trusted origins. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115067&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115067](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115067+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add MergeTree settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed`
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063 Adds three new `MergeTree`-level settings that limit the total size of a table, for multi-tenant, temporary, and demo services: - `max_table_size_rows` — the maximum total number of rows in active data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_compressed` — the maximum total size on disk across all active and inactive data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` — the same for uncompressed bytes. The limits are checked against the current table size at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed to the working set; on exceeding a limit, the query fails with the new `TABLE_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` error. Inserts done by materialized views (including refreshable ones) and async insert flushes are checked as well, since they go through the same sinks and part commits. Data parts that have been already accepted into the working set by a concurrent operation (parts in the `PreActive` state, which are not active yet) are counted as well, so a batch of parts committed in a single transaction — for example by `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` — cannot overshoot the limits, and neither can an insert running concurrently with another one on the same replica. An operation that replaces the parts it covers with a not larger part never increases the size of the table, so it is always allowed even when the table already exceeds a limit. This makes it possible to get a table back under the limit with a merge, a row-removing mutation, or a lightweight delete, and not only by dropping whole parts. A mutation that increases the size of a table which is over the limit is rejected and will be repeated without finishing, which is intended. The check is skipped on replicated fetches and on the execution of replication log entries that add data already accepted by another replica (`ATTACH_PART`, `REPLACE_RANGE`), which permits a race condition when parallel inserts into multiple replicas overdraft the limit. Committing empty data parts is always allowed, so the data can be removed from a table that exceeds the limits, e.g. with `TRUNCATE` or `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`. The limit on the number of rows is counted only for active data parts, while the limits on the number of bytes are counted across all active and inactive data parts, because their purpose is to limit disk usage (inactive parts are removed in the background, so the observed size can decrease over time). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `MergeTree` settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, and `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` that limit the total size of a table. The limits are checked at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed (including the results of background merges and mutations), but not on replicated fetches. This closes [#115063](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115069&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115069](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115069+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not attach a cache writer to a detached file segment
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110029 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Cache file segment is in detached state`) when reading through the filesystem cache with the experimental `use_reader_executor` setting. The regression was introduced by #110029 and is not in any release, so no backport is owed. ### Description Related: #110029 **The problem.** `BuzzHouse` aborts the server with `Cache file segment is in detached state, operation not allowed`, on two unrelated PRs, first seen 8h41m after #110029 merged. CIDB STID `4043-43b7`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=97396ecebc7bcb7ee4d4921c71d1cfdd071a2895&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29). **Root cause.** `FileCache::getOrSet` can hand back a synthetic `DETACHED` placeholder rather than a real segment: `getImpl` fabricates one when the covering segment is being evicted or removed, and another when the range exceeds `bypass_cache_threshold`. Such a placeholder is outside the cache metadata, holds no bytes, and the downloader role cannot be acquired on it. `DiskCacheProvider::resolve` classified it as a *writable* miss, because `segmentCommittedEnd` falls back to the write offset, which for a placeholder equals the segment start. It attached a `DiskCacheWriter`, and `ReaderExecutor::readThroughCaches` then called `claimLeadRole` on it, whose `getOrSetDownloader` hit `assertNotDetachedUnlocked`: a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, aborting the server in debug and sanitizer builds. **The change.** `resolve` now emits a writer-less miss for a detached segment, so those bytes are read from source and nothing is cached. The legacy paths already do this: `CachedOnDiskReadBufferFromFile` dispatches `State::DETACHED` to a cache bypass before acquiring any role, and `CachedOnDiskWriteBufferFromFile` skips write-through caching on `isDetached()`. `claimLeadRole` was the only one of the five non-test `getOrSetDownloader` callers reachable with a detached segment; the assertion is a correct caller contract and stays. **Reachability.** `src/IO/DiskCacheProvider.cpp` exists on no active release branch (25.8, 26.3-26.7), and #110029 is an ancestor of none of them, so no released version can reach this. `use_reader_executor` is experimental and off by default; the abort affects the `BuzzHouse` checks, which randomize it as a session setting, plus anyone opting into the experimental path. **Validation.** Deterministic, no fuzzer needed: the test arms the existing failpoint `file_cache_simulate_evicting_segment`, which makes every segment the cache reports a placeholder. Without the fix the server dies with the CI stack; with it the test passes, 50/50 randomized. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115070&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115070](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115070+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Look up the SSH key and support ssh-agent in clickhouse-client
signals.text: `--ssh-key-file` can now be specified without a value. In that case the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it: - the identity files configured for this host in `~/.ssh/config` and in `/etc/ssh/ssh_config`; - the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`; - the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. A key held by the `ssh-agent` is preferred, because it does not need a passphrase. It is also used when `--ssh-key-file` names a key file that the agent holds - an encrypted key that was added with `ssh-add` no longer asks for the passphrase. Signing with the agent is implemented in `SSHAgent`, a small client of the agent protocol, which produces the same `SSHSIG` signature as `SSHKey::signString` does for a local key (for RSA keys it asks the agent for `rsa-sha2-256`, because agents sign with SHA-1 by default and the server rejects that). The configuration is read with the parser of `libssh`, so `Host` and `Match` sections, `Include`, and the `%`-tokens of `IdentityFile` and `IdentityAgent` (`%C`, `%d`, `%h`, `%i`, `%L`, `%l`, `%n`, `%p`, `%r`, `%u`) work the same way as in `ssh`. `IdentitiesOnly yes` is honored: the ssh-agent is not asked for an arbitrary key when none of the configured identity files exists. The client reports the key it has chosen: ``` $ clickhouse-client --user abcuser --ssh-key-file Using the SSH key 'the key of abcuser' from the ssh-agent. ``` Two related changes of the existing behavior: the passphrase is now asked only if the key file is really encrypted (before, `--ssh-key-file` always asked for it), and the message about a key that cannot be imported now names the file. Tests: a new stateless test `04908_ssh_key_file_lookup` covers the default identity file, an `IdentityFile` with the `%r` token, an `ed25519` key from the `ssh-agent`, an `ssh-rsa` key from the `ssh-agent` with an empty `~/.ssh`, `IdentityAgent none`, and `IdentitiesOnly yes`. `03780_failed_ssh` no longer expects the passphrase prompt. The existing `test_ssh_keys_authentication` integration tests pass. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-client` accepts `--ssh-key-file` without a value: the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it - the identity files configured for the host in `~/.ssh/config`, the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, and the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. Authentication with a key held by the `ssh-agent` is now supported, and it does not need a passphrase. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115072&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115072](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115072+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/libssh/pull/15

signals.title: Let the promql dialect keep tokens the SQL lexer rejects
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed PromQL queries with regex label matchers (`=~`, `!~`) being rejected under `--dialect promql`. Closes #115071. --- Under `--dialect promql`, `ParserPrometheusQuery` reads the raw query text and hands it to the PromQL grammar; it walks the SQL tokens only to find where the statement ends. But `tryParseQuery` scans those tokens for lexer errors *before* the parser runs, and `~` is not a SQL token, so the query was rejected before it ever reached the PromQL grammar: ``` $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance="host1"}' Code: 471. ... The name of a TimeSeries table to use with promql dialect is not specified $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance=~"host2|host3"}' Code: 62. ... Unrecognized token: Syntax error: failed at position 13 (~) ``` The equality matcher gets through to a missing-setting error; the regex matcher dies at the `~` with a **SQL** lexical error. It is not specific to `-q` — stdin and `--queries-file` fail identically. The grammar itself already has the tokens (`PromQLLexer.g4`: `RE : '=~'`, `NRE : '!~'`), and the same expression works when passed as a string to the table function, which is what makes the limitation easy to miss. `IParser` gains `consumesRawText()`, false by default and overridden by `ParserPrometheusQuery`. `tryParseQuery` skips its two lexical-error rejections for such parsers, since a token the SQL lexer does not recognise is not an error for a parser that reads the text itself. No call site changes, and any future dialect parser in the same position gets the behaviour by overriding one method. This is safe because the lexer does not stop at an unrecognised character — it consumes it and returns an `Error` token (`Lexer.cpp:546`), so statement-boundary detection still finds the terminating semicolon. Kusto solves the same problem with an entire parallel `parseKQLQuery.{h,cpp}`; PromQL needs only the boundary scan, so a virtual on `IParser` seemed proportionate. Happy to go the separate-entry-point route instead if maintainers prefer the consistency. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed
signals.text: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)` on #110479 @ `038667a9c024` reported a single failing leaf `Server died` while its own aggregate said `Failed: 0, Passed: 3872`. The server did not die: no `<Fatal>` line, no sanitizer report, empty `dmesg`, clean shutdown. The `--hung-check` liveness probe failed and the run was aborted. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110479&sha=038667a9c024695126415fe5f37b76f7a06662fa&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29 Root cause: `tests/clickhouse-test` collapses every in-band abort cause into `STOP_TESTING_EXIT_CODE = 2`, and the job side appends `Server died` for that code unconditionally. Master already carved two causes out of code 2 for this reason; this is the third. This adds `HUNG_CHECK_EXIT_CODE = 5` and `FailureReason.LIVENESS_CHECK_FAILED`, with the leaf `Server liveness check failed` at status FAIL. All four sites that conclude `SERVER_DIED` from a failed probe are changed; the site concluding it from a `<Fatal>` line is untouched, and its neighbour becomes an `elif` of it so fatal evidence is never downgraded. The stop cause travels through one locked first-writer-wins carrier, replacing a `global_time_limit_reached` flag. The leaf names the observation, not a diagnosis: `check_server_liveness` also fails on a non-200 *response*. It is a NEW CIDB `test_name`. The aggregate stays FAIL, so bugfix validation still counts a hang as a repro. Not claimed: a remaining `Server died` row still does not prove a death. Code 2 is generic, and a worker seeing a `<Fatal>` line reaches the parent through `stop_tests()`, exiting 143 - correct there, but decided outside the carrier. Validation: +50 tests asserting the process exit code end to end - the same command exits 2 on master and 5 here. Each changed site has a mutation arm reddening a named case. `ci/tests`: 705 passed, 655 on master. Successor to #112952, not an extension: that PR deliberately excludes exit code 2. Both touch the same region of `functional_tests_results.py`, so the second to merge needs a rebase. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1807` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Reload a persisted `url()` table with the storage its creation selected
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server that refuses to start after a table was created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS url('http://host/**/', ...)` while `allow_experimental_url_wildcard_from_index_pages` was enabled. Loading such a table's metadata re-evaluated the experimental check and failed with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, aborting startup. ### Description Reported by @ bacek on #104437, where `Stress test (amd_tsan)` failed with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` after a fuzzer created `url('/**/', JSONEachRow, 'x int')`. No fuzzer is needed: enable the setting, create such a table, restart with the default. Root cause is one defaulted parameter. `ITableFunction::execute` declares `bool is_insert_query = false`; `CREATE ... AS url(...)` passes `true` explicitly (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2403`), while metadata replay (`DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:117`) passes nothing. `TableFunctionURL::getStorage` computes `use_web_wildcard = !is_insert_query && ...`, so the two take opposite branches for the same stored table: creation builds a plain `StorageURL` and never reaches the experimental check, replay builds `StorageObjectStorage` and does. The check is dead at creation and live only on replay, and metadata loading rethrows. The fix treats a definition arriving with stored columns as a persisted one being replayed, so it resolves to the storage creation selected. The check is not suppressed, it becomes unreachable because the correct branch is taken. Suppressing it would instead enable index-page expansion with the setting disabled and give the table a read-only storage. `ENGINE = URL` was already fixed this way in 64abbdd31d85b15 ("Gate `URL` wildcard experiment check to creation"). Behaviour change: a persisted glob `url()` table that today rebuilds as `StorageObjectStorage` after a restart now rebuilds as the `StorageURL` its creation built. Both carriers are covered by the one change and both are tested: explicit structure, and `structure = 'auto'` via `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (the surface of an earlier `test_url_wildcard_schema_inference` failure). `urlCluster` cannot persist a table. The creation-time check in `getActualTableStructure` is deliberately untouched, since a columns-less `CREATE` reaches it before `execute`. Querying `url()` directly still requires the setting. Out of scope: the check stays dead at creation, so `CREATE` with a glob still succeeds with the setting off. `ytsaurus()` has the same problem by another mechanism. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104437&sha=bee15ffc5ec3d2a9b5479bd1fbc197ac6458eebc&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115095&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115095](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115095+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix compiled `if`/`multiIf` on a negative `Time` value
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `if` and `multiIf` returning a large positive value instead of a negative one when a `Time` branch is combined with `Time64`, `DateTime` or `DateTime64` and the expression is JIT-compiled. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115381 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114168 (found there in review; a separate mechanism) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103390 A negative `Time` value read through a JIT-compiled `if`/`multiIf` comes back as a huge positive number: ```sql SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-01:00:00'), toTime64('00:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(1); -- executions 1-3: -01:00:00.000 -- execution 4+: 999:59:59.000 ``` No `SETTINGS` clause is needed to hit this: `compile_expressions` defaults to `1` and `min_count_to_compile_expression` to `3`, so the 4th execution of the expression in a session silently changes the answer. `enable_time_time64_type` also defaults to `1`. The wrong value is ticks `4294963696` = `2^32 - 3600`, i.e. the negative `Int32` tick count zero-extended to 64 bits. Root cause: `typeIsSigned` in `src/DataTypes/Native.cpp` did not list the `Time` family, so the widening cast emitted by `FunctionIfBase::compileImpl` asked whether `Time` is signed, got `false`, and LLVM emitted `zext` where `sext` was required. `Time` is `DataTypeNumberBase<Int32>` and is the only member of the date/time family that widens on this path, which is why the defect is specific to it. `Time64` is included in the same predicate for correctness of the contract: `isDecimal()` matches only `TypeIndex::Decimal32..256` and so does not cover `TypeIndex::Time64` - the same reason `isDateTime64()` is listed separately. No wrong-result carrier reaches the `Time64` half today, so it is not given a test that could not fail. Validation: five wrong-result carriers plus a `Nullable(Time)` case are covered by the new test. The reference values were taken from the non-compiled path on an unpatched binary, so the oracle is independent of this change. With the predicate token removed the test fails on 7 of 13 lines; non-negative `Time`, large-negative `Time`, and `DateTime64` controls are unchanged. 50/50 runs under settings randomization pass.

signals.title: Enable the consecutive-keys cache for fixed-size aggregation keys
signals.text: The `keys128` and `keys256` aggregation methods had `consecutive_keys_optimization = false`, so aggregating data whose keys arrive in long runs of equal values (e.g. anything grouped by a fixed-size key that is a prefix of the table sort order) paid a full hash-and-probe per row. Enabling the existing `LastElementCache` for these methods (including the two-level variants) skips the hash table entirely within a run, at the cost of one wide key compare per row; the aggregator's adaptive hit-rate machinery already disables the cache on random keys, verified by a random-key `keys256` microbenchmark showing no regression (3.88 s baseline vs 3.82/3.88 s). On clustered keys (runs of ~200k equal `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` values, 400M rows) this saves ~10% of aggregation CPU. Session: ad94609b-7b39-4f96-af16-7947efc50974 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Aggregation by fixed-size keys of 17-32 bytes (the `keys128`/`keys256` methods, e.g. `GROUP BY` a `UUID` or a `Tuple(UInt64, UInt64)`) now uses the consecutive-keys cache, making aggregation of sorted or clustered data up to 10% faster; the cache disables itself adaptively on random keys. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115155&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115155](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115155+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Bound submodule cache population so it cannot kill the Config Workflow job
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114811 `Config Workflow` computes the workflow matrix, so when it dies no build and no test job is scheduled. On a submodule cache miss it clones 141 submodules inside its own `timeout=600` budget, and when that does not finish praktika SIGTERMs the job, silently dropping the matrix: the public `26.5` run at `f724d2da9360` recorded 4 checks against 102-155 on healthy commits, and the run still looks finished because `Finish Workflow` reports success afterwards. 7 occurrences over 7 refs in 30 days, including a release branch and three backport PRs. This bounds the clone with `timeout -s KILL` at 600s, above p99 494.5s and the slowest population that currently succeeds (517s), and raises the job cap to `SUBMODULE_CACHE_POPULATE_TIMEOUT_SEC + 600`, 1200s by default, above the 828s worst case (600 clone + 44 tar and upload + 184 rest of the job). Deriving the cap keeps it above the step bound under a per-repository override; were the two equal the job watchdog would fire first. A test pins that ordering. Per @ maxknv's review the step now fails when the cache cannot be populated, instead of reporting `OK` and accepting a miss. Accepting it only degrades cleanly if every dependant can run its own `git submodule update`; dependants clone unauthenticated while this path can use the App installation token, so under `ENABLE_SUBMODULE_CLONE_AUTH` a private submodule is unreachable to them and continuing would schedule checkout failures whose cause is no longer visible. The bound is what makes the timeout reportable: a job-level SIGTERM leaves no result at all. `retries` is dropped because `Shell.check` applies `timeout` per retry, not as a total. Verified by driving the real function both ways: an exhausted budget fails with the hash unset and nothing uploaded, a generous one still populates the cache. YAML regeneration is unchanged.

signals.title: Perf: Optimize PromQL or for exact groups
signals.text: ## What changed - add a fast path for the PromQL set operator `or` - use it when both inputs already match on the original `group` column - decide the fast path from the operator modifiers and `metric_name_dropped` flags, without building temporary match-key ASTs - send exact-group inputs directly to the existing `FULL ALL JOIN` merge - use a compact per-step presence mask in the general `or` path instead of counting every non-NULL value - keep `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, `on()`, and other transformed matching keys on the current general path - treat empty `ignoring()` like default matching when both groups are already exact ## Why this is safe `VECTOR_GRID` guarantees one row per `group`. The fast path is enabled only when the matching rules leave the original `group` column unchanged on both sides, so the join key is already unique and exact. This includes normal matching and empty `ignoring()` after both inputs have already dropped `__name__`. `on(...)`, `on()`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, and other transformed matching keys keep the existing general path. The exact-group path removes the redundant per-group aggregation, the RHS masking join, the materialized left CTE, and the second left-grid read. The final merge still uses the existing element-wise left-side preference for overlapping samples. For the general path, Step 1 only needs to know whether each timestamp has any left value. `groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(isNotNull, values))` stores that presence mask directly instead of materializing a wider count array. The masking behavior is unchanged. ## Benchmark These benchmarks use the same **8,000-series / 300-sample** workload. Higher QPS means higher throughput for the same query. ### End-to-end PromQL Setup: `tests/performance/promql_set_operators.xml`, **10 measured runs** per server. | Query | Baseline | Patch | Relative | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | exact-group `or` | 146.8 ms | 128.9 ms | **1.14x speedup (-12.2%)** | | exact-group `or`, repeat | 157.6 ms | 134.5 ms | **1.17x speedup (-14.7%)** | | `or on(instance)` control | 143.9 ms | 145.9 ms | within noise | | `or on(instance)` control, repeat | 155.5 ms | 158.1 ms | within noise | The exact-group case is **1.14x to 1.17x faster** across the two runs. The control remains on the general path and the patch adds no extra scans or joins; the measured 1.4% to 1.7% variation is within normal run-to-run noise. The compact presence mask also reduces the size of the general-path intermediate state. ### Focused SQL lowering Setup: persistent server, **20 measured runs**, `max_threads=4`, **8,000 rows / 4,000 groups / 300-step arrays**. | Workload | General full lowering | Exact full merge | Relative | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Full lowering | 28.1 QPS | 56.5 QPS | **2.01x throughput (+101%)** | Both forms returned **1,128,000** present samples. ## Tests - add grouped `or` coverage where both sides have already dropped `__name__`, including empty `ignoring()` - cover different missing timestamps and compare the result with Prometheus - add `tests/performance/promql_set_operators.xml` with an exact-group query and an `or on(instance)` control - document that the merge helper expects unique `VECTOR_GRID` groups ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL `or` expressions with an exact group key skip redundant matching stages and use compact presence masks for transformed matching. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115219&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115219](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115219+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not schedule Build profile diff when the profiled build is unaffected
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Requested by @ thevar1able in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163#issuecomment-5318430318: `Build profile diff` ran on changes involving no builds. His PR changes only `utils/exclude-authors.txt`, yet the job ran, found no profile data for the head and posted nothing. `digest_config` answers two questions: which changed files affect a job, and may its result be reused. `4e62df6112628621` gave this job a focused digest; `e64133b542327753` removed it to stop a cache hit skipping the job, whose output is a comment about one concrete commit. That also made the job always affected, and `only_docs` in `filter_job.py` compensated for docs-only diffs only. This splits the two. `Job.Config` gains `enable_cache` (default True, and in `drop_fields`, so no existing job's digest changes), honoured at both cache seams. The job gets its focused digest back plus `enable_cache=False`: the digest decides whether to run it, the flag keeps every selected run running. Whether the build can produce data for this head arrives through `requires=["Build (arm_release)"]`, covering the build's sources, submodules, docker image and packaging. `only_docs` and its gate are deleted. Side effect: no longer always affected, the job stops rescuing `Build (arm_release)`, so that build is skipped on build-free diffs too. Those two jobs are the whole newly-skipped set, and this already happens on the `only_docs` path today. `Generate LLVM Coverage Diff Report`, asked about in the same comment, has no such hole: it is a `Result` inside `llvm_coverage_job.py`, already gated on build affectedness. One pre-existing limitation is widened, not fixed: a skip and a cache hit look identical to the runner, so the comment writer does not run on a skip and the comment can outlive the head it describes. That already holds for docs-only PRs. Verified: `ci/tests/` passes, `praktika yaml` produces no diff, every job's config digest is byte-identical, and each new assertion reddens under a mutation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115221&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115221](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115221+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1806` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: PromQL/TimeSeries: materialize tags only for unique groups
signals.text: ## What changed - collect unique group IDs before looking up tags in vectorized one-input transforms - deduplicate vectorized two-input group pairs before materializing tags - materialize and transform tags once per unique group or pair - keep a simple path for near-unique pair batches, so a small number of duplicates does not trigger the extra component maps - preserve first-seen ordering and row order when remapping results ## Why Vectorized TimeSeries transforms used to materialize tag pointers for every input row before deduplicating repeated groups or group pairs. Repeated PromQL rows therefore did extra lookup and remapping work. The updated paths deduplicate first and only materialize the groups needed by the unique transforms. For two-input transforms, batches with at most roughly 10% duplicate pairs use the simpler materialization path and transform only the first occurrence of each pair. More repetitive batches keep the component-dedup path, where the extra indexing work is worth the saved tag materialization. ## Benchmark Collector-path microbenchmark on an Apple M1 Pro with `clang++ -O3`, median of 7 runs after 3 warmup runs: | Workload | Before | After | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | One-input dense repeated groups, 500,000 rows | 4.00 ms | 0.87 ms | 78% faster | | One-input sparse repeated groups, 500,000 rows | 3.85 ms | 0.84 ms | 78% faster | | One-input dense unique groups, 500,000 rows | 90.68 ms | 90.37 ms | unchanged | | Two-input repeated pairs, 200,000 rows / 32 pairs | 2.97 ms | 0.88 ms | 70% faster | | Two-input unique pairs, 200,000 rows | 80.88 ms | 77.48 ms | 4% faster | The committed performance workload also covers 100%, 99.9%, 95%, 75%, 50%, and 10% unique pair batches, plus realistic `group_left` and `group_right` PromQL matching. ## Tests - add crossed destination/source patterns instead of symmetric pair indexes - cover near-unique pairs through the simple path - cover sparse group IDs and repeated pairs whose transformed results collapse to one group - add repeated dense and sparse one-input group coverage with row order - add repeated dense and sparse two-input pair coverage with row order - add the full pair-cardinality performance curve and `group_left`/`group_right` workloads ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Avoid repeated tag materialization and extra remapping work for duplicate groups in vectorized TimeSeries transformations. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115223&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115223](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115223+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators.** ### Summary The PromQL `and`, `or`, and `unless` lowering only needs to know whether a value is present at each step. This targets the general set-operator path. The exact-group fast path is separate. ### Changes - Use `Array(UInt8)` presence masks instead of `Array(UInt64)` counts. - Use `groupBitOrForEach` for the per-step presence reduction. - Share the mask expression between `and`, `or`, and `unless`. - Keep the shared set-operator validation and presence-mask construction in a common lowering helper. - Keep the existing NULL filtering and join behavior. - Cover all three operators in the plan-shape test. - Keep the original 8,000-series baseline workload. - Add a sparse fan-in workload with 1,000 matching groups and four physical replicas per group, with `replica` excluded by `on(instance)`. The compact presence mask is built with: ```sql groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values)) ``` Because `isNotNull()` produces a `UInt8` 0/1 value, bitwise OR is exactly the presence reduction needed by the set operators. The aggregate state is a zero-initialized `UInt8`, avoiding the generic `max(UInt8)` initialized-state bookkeeping. ### Benchmark The checked-in workload contains two variants, each using 300 query steps: - Baseline: 8,000 series with one series per matching group. - Sparse fan-in: 8,000 series with four replicas per matching group and staggered 50% sample presence. Queries match on `instance` while retaining `replica` in the physical labels. The second variant exercises the actual per-step presence reduction across multiple rows in each `on(...)` group. ### Benchmark result This operator-step microbenchmark runs the old `countForEach(values)` expression and the new `groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values))` expression over the same workload shapes. - ClickHouse 26.7.3.19 - 200 iterations per case - QPS from `clickhouse-benchmark` - Memory from `system.query_log` | Workload | Before | After | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Baseline | 68.3 QPS, p50 13 ms, 40.0 MiB | 79.6 QPS, p50 11 ms, 30.1 MiB | +16.5% QPS, -24.9% memory | | Sparse fan-in | 119.4 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | 122.7 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | +2.8% QPS, no material memory change | ### Tests - Verified that `groupBitOr` is registered for integer inputs and that the `ForEach` combinator accepts array arguments. - Updated the plan-shape checks for `and`, `or`, and `unless` to require `groupBitOrForEach` and reject `countForEach`. - Existing end-to-end set-operator coverage continues to exercise mixed, NULL, and missing-step behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115224&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115224](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115224+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1796` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: CI: report why the LLVM coverage diff report was not generated
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 (touched the same files; closed unmerged, and it was never a fix for this) ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `ci/jobs/scripts/generate_diff_coverage_report.sh` produces no report directory in four cases: no coverable C/C++ files changed, no coverage data for the changed files, current coverage empty for them, and a hard failure under `set -euo pipefail`. `llvm_coverage_job.py` inferred all four from one bit, `_diff_report_dir.exists()`, and reported three of them as "No C/C++ source files changed" at three sites. Two are green runs where C/C++ files did change, so the job states the opposite of what happened. On a tool failure it also set the `Print Uncovered Code` sub-result to `OK` for analysis that never ran. Observed on PR #115101, which changed `src/Functions/array/arrayAUC.cpp`: the `gh api` compare call returned `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`, and the job made both false claims. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115101&sha=c00b1800c1fcae2cb2138af592a9b3e79b4c8275&name_0=PR&name_1=LLVM%20Coverage The script now names its outcome in `ci/tmp/diff_outcome.txt` before every `exit 0`, and the job reports the outcome it is told plus the script's exit status. It also drops a false claim that "LBC analysis will run separately" when current coverage is empty, and echoes each `gh api` compare endpoint, since `gh` reports a failure as a bare `HTTP 404` naming no resource. A script failure still stays RED, and no currently-green outcome becomes red. One behavioural change beyond the labels: `print_uncovered_code.py` now runs only when this run produced a coverage slice holding records, so no other outcome can report an earlier run's numbers, or call changed files "nothing coverable" when only their current coverage was empty. This does not fix the 404 itself, which was environmental: it stopped with the GitHub incident of 2026-08-17 13:40Z to 21:15Z and has not recurred. `ci/tests/test_llvm_coverage_gate.py` grows from 12 to 71 cases: one per outcome, a harness running the real script under stubbed tools, and cases executing the job's own call site and each dispatch it selects. 50 fail on master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115225&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115225](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115225+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix the Upgrade check silently validating against a stale previous release
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The Upgrade check starts a previous release, then upgrades to the build under test. `tests/ci/get_previous_release_tag.py` picks that baseline, and can silently pick one far too old. On PR #114376 commit `e1cb0dee5e9` it picked `v25.1.4.53` for a `26.8.1.1` build; that old server aborted on shutdown, reported as `Received signal 6` unrelated to the PR. Two commits earlier it resolved `v26.7.3.19`. 4 of 47 recent runs were affected. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114376&sha=e1cb0dee5e9bd972e9bbbdd8cd8d971ad1e39ee1&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29 Root cause: when no candidate on a page could be used, an unbounded `while not found:` advanced to page 2, 3 and answered from there. `/releases` returns entries roughly newest-created first, not in version order, and each later page's newest release is older than the previous page's newest (measured across all 9 pages), so page 1 holds the newest release overall. The only diagnostic was `logger.debug` under `basicConfig(level=INFO)`. This resolves from the first page only. A candidate still needs an uploaded package, so a release whose packages are still publishing keeps falling back to the previous patch release, now logged at WARNING rather than DEBUG. Three cases now raise: a first page with no usable candidate, a page shorter than the 100 requested, and an answer that is its page's oldest entry, which cannot show that no newer release precedes it. `upgrade_runner.sh` turns those nonzero exits into a job failure. No C++ change is needed: the abort is a use-after-free in `25.1`, fixed in `2920d338ea4` (#81473, released in `v25.6.1.3206`), so master and every active release branch carry the fix. Tests were removed at review request. The Upgrade check's digest now lists both release helpers `upgrade_runner.sh` runs, the resolver and `download_release_packages.py`; without them a change to either leaves the job cache-skippable, the same failure mode fixed here. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112974 (hardens the API helper; edits the same digest list, so whichever merges second rebases). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115228&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115228](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115228+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1805` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not build statistics for non-physical columns
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` on every `INSERT` into a table that declares `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` or `EPHEMERAL` column, which made such tables read-only. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 `CREATE TABLE t (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a` is accepted, and then every `INSERT` fails `Code: 10 ... Not found column b in block`, so the table is read-only. `materialize_statistics_on_insert` defaulting to `true` in 26.8 exposed it. **Root cause.** The `ColumnsStatistics` constructor collects every column with a non-empty statistics description without checking how the column is stored, and the insert path builds those with `build`, which does `block.getByName`. An `ALIAS` column is computed on read and never appears in the written block, so the lookup always throws. Merges use `buildIfExists` and skip absent columns, which is why they kept working. Such statistics are already unsupported in `addImplicitStatistics` and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS`. **The change.** Drop non-physical columns from the collector the insert path builds, in `MergeTreeDataWriter`, using the existing `ColumnsDescription::hasPhysical`. `build` stays strict, because its type-mismatch check is a deliberate diagnostic, so an absence for any other reason is still an error. A newly issued `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS <col>` naming such a column is still rejected before enqueue. An already queued one instead skips it, so a command persisted by a pre-upgrade server drains rather than retrying forever in the background task. `ALL` skips such a column and stays usable. **Deliberately unchanged.** The declaration stays accepted but inert: every candidate rejection site is also the ATTACH/startup or replica-addition path, so a check there would stop existing affected tables from loading. `DROP STATISTICS` stays permissive and recovers such a table. Covered by `02864_statistics_ddl`, which fails on master with `Code: 10` and passes with the fix. The queued-mutation drain under the old mutation analyzer is not covered by a test: it needs the server-level `use_analyzer_for_mutations` override, which a stateless test cannot set.
