signals.title: Fix Arrow export of JSON, Dynamic, QBit and AggregateFunction
signals.text:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115023 Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/91170 The `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types_as_binary` fallback wrote a column with no first-class Arrow mapping by calling `IColumn::getDataAt` per row. That method exposes a column's contiguous in-memory bytes, which most of the types reaching the fallback do not have: - `ColumnObject` (`JSON`), `ColumnVariant` (hence `ColumnDynamic`) and `ColumnQBit` throw `Method getDataAt is not supported`, so `SELECT ... FORMAT Arrow` failed on them — after the schema message had already been written, leaving the client with a truncated stream; - `ColumnAggregateFunction::getDataAt` returns the `AggregateDataPtr` itself, so exporting an aggregate state silently wrote raw heap addresses instead of the state, both corrupting the data and disclosing server addresses. Before the fallback existed these types were rejected with a clear `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, so both are regressions introduced together with the setting: ``` -- 26.4, before #91170 SELECT '{"a":1}'::JSON FORMAT Arrow; -- Code: 50. The type 'JSON' of a column 'j' is not supported for conversion into Arrow data format. (UNKNOWN_TYPE) SELECT sumState(number) FROM numbers(3) FORMAT Arrow; -- Code: 50. The type 'AggregateFunction(sum, UInt64)' ... (UNKNOWN_TYPE) -- 26.5 .. 26.8 SELECT '{"a":1}'::JSON FORMAT Arrow; -- Code: 48. Method getDataAt is not supported for Object(max_dynamic_paths=1024, max_dynamic_types=32). (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) SELECT sumState(number) FROM numbers(3) FORMAT Arrow; -- succeeds, writes 00D0A9C9D37F0000 ``` The fallback now serializes each value through `ISerialization`, whose `serializeText`/`serializeBinary` are pure virtual and therefore defined for every type, so the "do not fail a `SELECT *`" property that motivated the setting holds by construction instead of depending on an unrelated method's implementation status. The aggregate state written in binary mode is the `RowBinary` encoding and deserializes back into the original `AggregateFunction` type. `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types` (`throw` / `text` / `binary`) replaces the boolean, adding a `text` mode that writes what `CAST(col AS String)` would produce — useful for the BI clients that drive `SELECT *` over Arrow Flight SQL, and the workaround users had to apply by hand for `JSON`. Its default, `binary`, is the previous behavior, and its `SettingsChangesHistory` entry has identical previous and new values so `compatibility` never marks it changed. The boolean keeps working with full effect (`0` means `throw`, `1` means `binary`) and is only consulted while the new setting is left at its default, so an explicit mode wins whichever order the two are set in. Both writers — the native Arrow IPC one behind `FORMAT Arrow`/`ArrowStream` and the Apache-Arrow-library one behind Arrow Flight SQL — make the accept/reject decision in the schema converter, before the schema message is written, so a rejected type can no longer abort a stream whose schema the reader has already accepted. Both serialize the values with the query's own `FormatSettings`, so a setting the serialization depends on (`output_format_binary_write_json_as_string`, `output_format_json_quote_64bit_integers`, …) produces the same payload whichever writer serves the query. An opaque column is tagged in both writers with the `clickhouse.opaque` Arrow extension name and the original ClickHouse type name in `ARROW:extension:metadata`, so a consumer can tell it apart from a genuine string or binary column. Per the Arrow extension-type convention a reader that does not know the extension name ignores the metadata and sees the plain storage type, so no existing consumer changes behavior. `StorageArrowFlight::ArrowFlightSink` built its converter settings from scratch and never consulted the setting, so it always used the struct default. It now resolves the mode from the query context like the other Arrow Flight call sites, which makes `INSERT INTO ... ENGINE = ArrowFlight` of an `AggregateFunction` column follow the setting; `throw` reproduces the previous behavior exactly. `JSON` and `Dynamic` cannot reach that sink, because the storage rejects a dynamic-structure column when the table is created and the table function takes its header from the remote schema. Verified against a local ClickHouse Arrow Flight server as well as `FORMAT Arrow`: `SELECT *` over a table with `JSON` and `AggregateFunction` columns returns them as `clickhouse.opaque`-tagged `binary` fields carrying the ClickHouse type name, with a neighbouring `String` column left untagged; `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types = 'text'` switches them to tagged `string` fields holding the text; and the payloads match the native writer byte for byte under the serialization settings above. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `SELECT ... FORMAT Arrow` failing with `Method getDataAt is not supported` for `JSON`, `Dynamic` and `QBit` columns, and silently exporting heap addresses instead of the aggregate state for `AggregateFunction` columns. Added the `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types` setting (`throw` / `text` / `binary`, default `binary`) which supersedes `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types_as_binary`.

signals.title: fix loading old S3 tables with globbed paths
signals.text: Before ClickHouse `26.6`, `S3` tables could use a path like `**.parquet` together with `PARTITION BY`. These tables were read-only, so ClickHouse ignored `PARTITION BY`. https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86746 changed this in ClickHouse 26.6. https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107437 also changed how the default strategy is selected. ClickHouse now tries to use either `hive` or `wildcard`. Neither works with this kind of path unless it contains `{_partition_id}`. Because of this, tables created before 26.6 can fail to load after an upgrade. Use the old behavior for these tables when `partition_strategy` is not set. Invalid strategies that users set explicitly still fail. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114705 ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix loading old S3 tables with globbed paths and `PARTITION BY` after upgrading from versions before 26.6. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115277&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115277](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115277+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) cc @nikitamikhaylov --- Example of a local run: ``` Local double-check of PR #115465 @ 7bcd103f9966 TEST Q# CI@ CI old CI new CI Δ | L old L new L Δ pval RESULT ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ int_parsing 2 arm-only 208.1ms 260.5ms +25.2% | no local data join_main_loop 8 arm-only 37.8ms 31.7ms -16.1% | 29.8ms 26.4ms -11.4% 0.000 NOT REPRODUCED on amd (faster on arm in CI; |Δ| 11.4% <= threshold 15%) join_nullable_keys_small_table 5 arm-only 788.3ms 552.6ms -29.9% | 581.2ms 448.4ms -22.9% 0.000 CONFIRMED faster (local mirrors arm regression) join_nullable_keys_small_table 9 arm-only 830.0ms 545.9ms -34.3% | 561.1ms 417.2ms -25.6% 0.000 CONFIRMED faster (local mirrors arm regression) join_reserve 0 arm-only 306.4ms 265.3ms -13.5% | 104.2ms 102.0ms -2.1% 0.004 NOT REPRODUCED on amd (faster on arm in CI; |Δ| 2.1% <= threshold 15%) right_full_hash_join_with_multi_ 1 arm-only 423.8ms 374.0ms -11.8% | 332.6ms 310.3ms -6.7% 0.019 NOT REPRODUCED on amd (faster on arm in CI; |Δ| 6.7% <= threshold 15%) right_full_hash_join_with_multi_ 4 arm-only 497.9ms 447.0ms -10.3% | 426.6ms 397.3ms -6.9% 0.000 NOT REPRODUCED on amd (faster on arm in CI; |Δ| 6.9% <= threshold 15%) Summary: 2 confirmed, 4 not reproduced, 1 not measured Reference 8a4c746fd235, both AMD binaries from S3, CPU-pinned to 16 physical cores, ports shifted by 2000 so the ClickHouse-read_in_order session's server stayed untouched. signals.title: Remove deprecated XML way to declare a disk resource
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108286 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Removed the deprecated `read_resource` and `write_resource` disk options from `storage_configuration`. Attach a scheduler resource to a disk with `CREATE RESOURCE name (READ DISK disk, WRITE DISK disk)` instead. ### Why this is safe Declaring IO scheduler resources in XML has already been removed: #108286 deleted the XML-based `CustomResourceManager` (the `<resources>` config section), so `CREATE RESOURCE` / `CREATE WORKLOAD` (the SQL `WorkloadResourceManager`) is already the only way to define resources and workloads. The disk-level `read_resource` / `write_resource` options were the last XML remnant — they only pointed a disk at a resource *by name*, which `CREATE RESOURCE ... (READ DISK d, WRITE DISK d)` (or `READ ANY DISK` / `WRITE ANY DISK`) already expresses from the resource side. They were redundant, so this removes them together with the matching documentation. The keys are **ignored, not rejected** — deliberately: the option has been deprecated for a long time, and throwing on a config that still carries it would crash servers on upgrade. A disk that still lists the keys keeps starting and simply uses whatever resource is bound to it via SQL (or none if there is none). ### What to use instead ```sql CREATE RESOURCE network_read (READ DISK s3); CREATE RESOURCE network_write (WRITE DISK s3); ```

signals.title: Store only the keys in the join hash table when no right row is read
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `LEFT ANTI JOIN`, and `LEFT SEMI JOIN` where no column of the right table is selected, only need to know whether a join key is present on the right side. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111025 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113649 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **Do not merge this until NightlyFuzzers is green on this branch.** Dispatching it needs admin rights on the repository, so I am asking for a manual run first. Re-land of #111025, reverted in #113649 after the nightly `libFuzzer tests` job went red for a week. signals.title: Do not admit non-clonable read steps into the MergeTree direct join
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103473 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Cannot clone ReadFromPreparedSource plan step` (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) when joining against a `Buffer` table with `join_algorithm = 'direct'`. Such a right side is now declined with the same message as any other unsupported storage. ### Description `tryMakeDirectJoinWithMergeTree` admitted `ReadFromPreparedSource` as a right-side read step, then cloned the right plan unconditionally. That step has no `clone()` override, so the clone reached the throwing base `IQueryPlanStep::clone()`: ```sql CREATE TABLE t_left (id UInt64, name String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE t_right_mt (id UInt64, val String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE t_right_buf AS t_right_mt ENGINE = Buffer(currentDatabase(), t_right_mt, 1, 1000, 1000, 10000, 10000, 10000000, 10000000); INSERT INTO t_left VALUES (1, 'A'); SELECT * FROM t_left AS l LEFT JOIN t_right_buf AS r ON l.id = r.id SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, join_algorithm = 'direct'; -- Code: 48. DB::Exception: Cannot clone ReadFromPreparedSource plan step. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) ``` That arm never had a working case: `typeid_cast` matches the exact type, and neither `ReadFromPreparedSource` nor its subclasses implement `clone()`, so every plan it admitted threw. This removes it. The other two arms are kept, and `ReadNothingStep` (which does implement `clone()`) carries the empty-MergeTree case from #95935. The query now takes the pre-existing refusal for unsupported right-side storages, `Can't execute any of specified algorithms ...`, which is what a `Memory` or `StripeLog` right side already returns. This is the "make the exception message better" change @ vdimir asked for when he closed #103473 as not planned: `direct` does not support `Buffer`, so the right behaviour is the ordinary unsupported-storage refusal rather than a clone failure. It deliberately does not make `Buffer` work with `direct`. Two notes beyond the report. The failure is not limited to an empty underlying table as the issue title suggests: it also reproduces with a non-empty `Buffer` and with `INNER JOIN`. And it does not touch the second entry point @ zlareb1 reported, where correlated-subquery decorrelation clones the same step: that path does not go through this allow-list. Hence `Related:` below rather than `Closes:`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103473 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115309&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115309](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115309+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Remove `WasmEdge` in favor of `wasmtime`
signals.text: Removes the `WasmEdge` WebAssembly runtime, leaving `wasmtime` as the only engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime` has been the default and recommended engine, and `WasmEdge` was only reachable by explicitly setting `webassembly_udf_engine` to `wasmedge`. Keeping a second implementation of `IWasmEngine` alive costs a vendored C++ submodule (plus `spdlog`, which nothing else in the tree used), a second engine backend to maintain, and CI lanes configured to switch the server over to it. What is removed: - The `contrib/wasmedge` submodule and `contrib/wasmedge-cmake`, along with `contrib/spdlog`, which existed only to build `WasmEdge`. - `src/Interpreters/WebAssembly/WasmEdgeRuntime.{h,cpp}`, the `USE_WASMEDGE` build option and its `system.build_options` row. - `IWasmEngine::requiresFuelSpecialization`, which existed only to distinguish `WasmEdge` (no fuel specialization) from `wasmtime`. The per-fuel-mode module cache is now unconditional. - The `--wasm-engine` option of `tests/config/install.sh` and the `WasmEdge` CI job option, so the affected stateless lanes are renamed: - `amd_msan, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → `amd_msan, {parallel,sequential}` - `amd_llvm_coverage, old analyzer, s3 storage, DBReplicated, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → the same name without `WasmEdge` `webassembly_udf_engine` is kept as the engine selector; `wasmtime` is now its only accepted value, and any other value is rejected with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG` as before. Because `WasmModuleManager` is constructed eagerly during startup (`Server::main` → `Context::setUserScriptsPath` → `Context::initWasmModuleManager`), a server whose config still says `wasmedge` will refuse to start with `Unknown WebAssembly engine 'wasmedge', available engines: 'wasmtime'` rather than fail lazily on first use. Silently aliasing `wasmedge` to `wasmtime` was rejected on purpose: it would be a fallback that hides a stale config. Verified locally on an `aarch64` build: `system.build_options` reports `USE_WASMTIME = 1` with no `USE_WASMEDGE` row; all 23 stateless WebAssembly UDF tests pass (including `04259_wasm_udf_enable_fuel`, which exercises both fuel modes and therefore the module cache path simplified here); and a server configured with `wasmedge` fails startup with the message above. No test coverage is lost. `wasmtime` is disabled under MemorySanitizer (false positives from JIT-generated code), which is why the MSan lanes ran with `WasmEdge` — but every stateless test that executes a WebAssembly module is tagged `no-msan`, so those lanes exercised no WebAssembly UDF code; the option only rewrote the server config. The two `*_ast_json_*` tests that mention `LANGUAGE WASM` only round-trip the query through `parseQueryToJSON` and never instantiate a module. On the coverage lane, those tests now run against `wasmtime` instead of `WasmEdge`. On binaries where `wasmtime` cannot be built, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDF support is now disabled entirely. Enabling `allow_experimental_webassembly_udf` makes the server fail during startup with `WebAssembly UDF support is disabled because ClickHouse was built without wasmtime`; it no longer exposes a module manager that can only fail later at runtime. The `wasmedge` mentions left in `docs/reference/settings/server-settings/settings/other.mdx` and in the localized `docs/<locale>/` trees are generated output and are refreshed by the docs autogeneration workflow. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Removed the `WasmEdge` engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime`, which has always been the default, is now the only supported value of the `webassembly_udf_engine` server setting. A server configured with `<webassembly_udf_engine>wasmedge</webassembly_udf_engine>` will not start; remove that setting or set it to `wasmtime`. On binaries where `wasmtime` is unavailable, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDF support is unavailable and enabling it prevents server startup. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115316&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115316](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115316+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix timezoneOffset losing the whole-day component of the UTC offset
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115281 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `timezoneOffset` (alias `timeZoneOffset`) returning an offset wrong by exactly one day for time zones whose UTC offset differs from their 1970-01-01 offset by a whole day, such as `Pacific/Kiritimati` and `Pacific/Apia` after they crossed the international date line, and for most zones before 1970. This also fixes `parseDateTime`, `parseDateTimeOrNull`, `parseDateTime64`, `parseDateTimeInJodaSyntax`, `EXTRACT(TIMEZONE_HOUR / TIMEZONE_MINUTE ...)`, `formatDateTime`'s `%z`, `toUTCTimestamp` and `fromUTCTimestamp`, which consume that offset. Closes #115281. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115281#issuecomment-5327580058. `timezoneOffset` did not read the offset, it reconstructed it as `(lut[index].date - lut[epoch].date) % 86400` plus `offset_at_start_of_epoch`. That difference is `days * 86400 - (offset_now - offset_epoch)`, so the modulo keeps only the sub-day part of the change since the epoch and discards any whole-day part; the date-line zones stayed pinned at their pre-jump offset, correct before the jump and wrong after. Separately, `%` takes the sign of the dividend, so on a pre-epoch day the remainder is negative, the `res > 43200` wrap never fired, and the result came out near `+86400` instead of a small negative offset. The fix computes the offset directly as `day_number * 86400 - lut[index].date`: local midnight is that many seconds of local time from the epoch, and `date` is the UTC instant of the same midnight. Exact for either sign, no modulo, no wrap branches. The same-day `amount_of_offset_change` correction is unchanged. All 12 in-tree call sites checked. Seven were wrong and are repaired by this one change: the function itself, the `parseDateTime` family (including a zone named in the format string), `EXTRACT(TIMEZONE_HOUR / TIMEZONE_MINUTE ...)`, `formatDateTime`'s `%z`, and `toUTCTimestamp` / `fromUTCTimestamp`. The other five reduce the offset modulo a day (`CAST ... AS Time` / `Time64`, `localtime`), so an exact one-day error already cancelled; the test pins those as controls. Over all 597 rows of `system.time_zones` at 14 instants from 1900 to 2300, against Python `zoneinfo` as an independent oracle: 500 wrong samples across 307 zones before, 18 after, all 18 being `tzdata` differences between the bundled 2025a and the system 2026a. All 488 changed samples differ by exactly one day, so nothing sub-day moved. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Both directions through `tests/clickhouse-test`: on the base master debug snapshot (build id `09e3d57a4bbe30cd`) `01252_weird_time_zone` fails with a 39-line reference diff; with the fix (build id `485b33ed0bf6e99c`) it passes, including 50 of 50 randomized runs. `unit_tests_dbms --gtest_filter='*DateLUT*:*DateTime*:*Date*'` passes 7906 tests, so no calendar component moved. The `timezone` stateless suite passes 42 of 42. Six failures in the wider `datetime` and `extract` suites are pre-existing gaps in my local environment (no `remote()` cluster config, no parquet/iceberg fixtures, no `test.hits`) and reproduce identically on the base binary. New arms: the seven reported zones after their jump; the same zones before it and `Pacific/Chatham` (+13:45) as controls that must not move; the pre-1970 class; agreement between `parseDateTime*` and `toDateTime`; the other offset consumers; the modulo-a-day consumers as regression controls; DST transition days; agreement between the in-range and out-of-range paths; and a sweep over `system.time_zones` with no zone list hardcoded, comparing the reported offset to rendering the instant as local text and reading it back as UTC. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115332&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115332](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115332+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, event_date, event_time, key`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Resume a NATS JetStream subscription after a reconnect
signals.text: A `NATS` table reading from a JetStream stream can stop consuming for good after the NATS server restarts, while still looking subscribed and healthy. An asynchronous JetStream pull subscription asks for more messages only when one is delivered, and when the NATS client reconnects it re-sends the `SUB` line but not the pull request the broker was holding. A broker that goes away without answering that request - a hard kill, a network partition, or a graceful restart that lands in the milliseconds between a re-subscribe and its request being parked - leaves the table subscribed and permanently silent. That is what `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write` hits when the consumer is still behind at the moment the broker is stopped: all 100000 rows were published and acknowledged into the stream, but the ones not yet delivered are never fetched again, so the view stays short of them and the test fails with `ClickHouse lost some messages: 92807`. It fails this way on about 0.2% of runs since the NATS tests came back on 2026-07-30, and at the same rate before and after #112828 recovered the closed-subscription case on 2026-08-13 (88 of 46693 runs before, 27 of 15428 after), which is what points at the window that fix leaves open. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=c260929910ea94be9a359bb69bf5e33d7b3a40e4&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%204%2F4%29 Recovery so far keyed only on a subscription the NATS client had closed, which is what a graceful shutdown produces by answering the outstanding pull request. This reports a reconnect as well, by comparing the reconnect count the client keeps for the connection against the one taken when we subscribed, and re-subscribes through the same path. Only JetStream consumers do this: a core NATS subscription really is restored by the `SUB` line, and re-subscribing it would drop buffered messages nothing redelivers. The recovery is applied both by the background streaming task and by an in-flight direct `SELECT`, whose source retains its consumer until the query finishes. The window this closes is the residual documented in #112828, so `_restart_nats` no longer retries until a restart lands outside it, and a new test reaches that state deterministically with `SIGKILL`, which answers nothing and so leaves no closed subscription to fall back on. Verified locally with a release build, running the module through `ci.praktika`: - new test with the fix: passed twice (65 s, 146 s); - new test with `src/Storages/NATS` reverted to `master` and everything else unchanged: `AssertionError: consumption did not resume, view holds 10 of 20 keys` - the messages published after the restart never arrive; - the five existing restart tests plus `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write`, all six passed with the fix. signals.title: Aggregation pushdown below JOIN in the Cascades optimizer
signals.text: ## Motivation Queries like `SELECT count() FROM t1 LEFT JOIN t2 ON t1.key = t2.key GROUP BY t1.key` aggregate after the join, although most of the aggregation work can be done on one join input before the join. When the pushed side has few distinct group keys, aggregating first shrinks the join input dramatically. This is the classic *eager aggregation* transformation (Yan & Larson, VLDB 1995). It is not always a win — with nearly-unique group keys the extra aggregation is pure overhead — so it is implemented as a cost-based alternative in the Cascades optimizer: the memo keeps both plans and the cost model picks. ## What is implemented A new transformation rule `AggregationPushdown` with two variants: - **Partial pushdown**: a partial aggregation (`final = false`) below one join input, and a `MergingAggregated` step above the join. The pushed side's group keys are extended with every column of that side referenced by the join condition and residual filter, which makes all rows within a partial group indistinguishable to the join — the join then filters or duplicates whole groups uniformly, and merging `m` duplicated copies of a state equals processing the underlying rows `m` times. This is semantically exact, including for `ALL` joins with fan-out, and requires no uniqueness knowledge. - **Full pushdown**: when every `GROUP BY` key belongs to the pushed side, the join-condition columns are a subset of the `GROUP BY` keys, and the strictness rules out duplication (`ANY`/`SEMI`/`ANTI` with the join kind matching the pushed side), the aggregation stays final below the join and no merge is needed. When legal, it strictly dominates the partial variant and is emitted instead of it. The legality matrix was derived from the hash-join implementation and independently re-verified during review. Notably, `ANY INNER JOIN` is excluded from the matrix entirely: it emits at most one row per join *key* (`setUsedOnce`), not per probe row, so pushing aggregation below it would change results. The correctness test contains a tripwire scenario against future wrong enablement. Safety rules encoded in the rule (each bails out and leaves the classic plan): the pushed side must never be null/default-extended by the join (an unmatched preserved row would otherwise carry an empty aggregate state and silently contribute nothing); global aggregation (`GROUP BY ()`) is excluded (an empty join output must still produce one row); all aggregate arguments must resolve to the pushed side; `join_use_nulls`/`USING` type-changing joins, grouping sets, `overflow_row`, `max_rows_to_group_by`, in-order aggregation, and name collisions between the two sides are all rejected. Supporting changes: - `MergingAggregatedStep` gets an opt-in `allowInputWithoutAggregatedChunkInfo` mode (join output chunks carry no `AggregatedChunkInfo`, and special column representations must be materialized before merging). The `only_merge` aggregator consumes keys and states positionally, so the rebuilt join projects keys first, then state columns. - **Wire format**: the new mode is serialized as flag bit 64 of `MergingAggregatedStep`, gated behind query plan serialization version 9 (bumped from 8). On a mixed-version cluster the plan fails at plan time with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` (naming `SET cascades_aggregation_pushdown = 0` as the escape hatch) instead of a remote runtime error. Note that the version bump also excludes version-8 replicas from parallel-replicas distributed plans, per the documented design of `DBMS_QUERY_PLAN_SERIALIZATION_VERSION`. - `AggregatingStep::rebaseOntoInput` re-bases an aggregation onto a new input with a different key set; new memo helpers build the three-level (partial) and two-level (full) alternatives. The rule is gated by the new `EXPERIMENTAL` setting `cascades_aggregation_pushdown` (default on) and takes effect only together with `enable_cascades_optimizer = 1` and `make_distributed_plan = 1`. ## Testing - `04926_cascades_aggregation_pushdown`: EXPLAIN plan shapes for both variants and both sides, stat-hint steering in both directions, guard negatives (`FULL`, `ASOF`, `INNER ANY`, `join_use_nulls`, grouping sets, global aggregation, mixed-side aggregate arguments), executed queries with hand-verified values (including fan-out multiplicity and mixed equi+residual conditions), and a 3-join task-budget sanity check. - `04927_cascades_aggregation_pushdown_correctness`: 22+ scenarios, each executed with the optimizer on and off with identical results (fan-out duplication, unmatched rows, multi-key and expression join keys, residual conditions, `count`/`sum`/`min`/`avg`/`uniqExact`/`countIf`, keys from both sides, `SEMI`/`ANTI`/`ANY`, keys-only `GROUP BY`, empty inputs, full-pushdown cases), plus plan-shape canaries proving the pushed plans actually fire for the test's tables. - The full `*cascades*` and `*merging_aggregated*` stateless test sets pass locally on a test-config server. One pre-existing test (`04330_cascades_activation_gating`) pins the new setting off in one case whose own assertion (about subplan broadcasting) would otherwise be made vacuous by the new, cheaper plan. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added aggregation pushdown below `JOIN` (eager aggregation) to the experimental Cascades optimizer as a cost-based alternative: a partial aggregation is performed on one join input before the join and merged above it, or, when the join provably neither duplicates nor null-extends the aggregated side and the join keys are a subset of the `GROUP BY` keys, the aggregation is pushed below the join entirely. Controlled by the new setting `cascades_aggregation_pushdown` (enabled by default; takes effect only with `enable_cascades_optimizer = 1` and `make_distributed_plan = 1`). --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115354&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115354](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115354+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: The `_database` and `_table` virtual columns of a `Merge` table carry the matched child's name again
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113735 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/84139 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/63665 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/102471 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107418 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113242 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `WHERE _table = ...` or `WHERE _database = ...` filter over a `Merge` table silently returning no rows when the matched child reads through another table, for example a `Distributed`, a nested `Merge`, or a `Buffer` child. The `_database` and `_table` virtual columns of a `Merge` table now always carry the name of the matched child, as they did before 25.7, not the name of the table the child delegates its read to. ### Description `ReadFromMerge::getSelectedTables` prunes the children of a `Merge` table by evaluating a filter on `_database`/`_table` against each child's own name, but the values in the rows were stamped by whatever storage eventually read them - for a `Distributed` child, the remote table on the shards. The two sides contradicted each other, and every query where both fire silently returned wrong results: a filter naming the child returned no rows (pruning kept the child, but no row carried its name), and a filter naming the remote table returned rows only at processing stages where the pruning happened not to fire. ```sql CREATE TABLE t_leaf (s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY s; CREATE TABLE t_dist AS t_leaf ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_leaf); CREATE TABLE m (s String) ENGINE = Merge(currentDatabase(), '^t_dist$'); SELECT count() FROM m WHERE _table = 't_dist'; -- 0 on master, all rows with this fix ``` **History.** Before #63665 (25.7), the `Merge` engine substituted the child's own name for `_table`/`_database` itself (`WITH '<child>' AS _table` per child), so the values and the pruning agreed. #63665 gave every table its own `_table` virtual column, which disabled that gated substitution: the reader deep down stamps the name, and for a delegating child that is a different table. #102471 then removed the dead substitution machinery, and #107418 pinned the new values with a regression test - while the pruning kept matching child names all along. **The fix** makes the `Merge` engine produce these columns itself again, unconditionally: references to them are replaced with a constant carrying the child's name right in the child query tree (so expressions computed on the shards see it too; the analyzer path pins the action name via `__actionName`, the old interpreter path uses the `WITH` substitution), and at `FetchColumns` the constant columns are added to the child plan, inserted at the positions the columns have in the requested header, because a child whose execution names differ from the common header (a `Distributed` child) is matched by position in `convertAndFilterSourceStream`. **This is a deliberate semantic choice, and the alternative is #113735.** Only one of the two semantics can be consistent with pruning: the pruning can only ever match the child's name, since the `Merge` table cannot know which table a child delegates to without classifying every child. #113735 keeps the underlying-table values and therefore has to prove, per storage class and recursively through `Buffer`/`Alias`/proxy wrappers, whether a child stamps its own name - with a fail-closed carve-out for streaming engines. Under child-name semantics all of that machinery is unnecessary, streaming children keep being pruned exactly as before, and the docs' claim that "the `_table` column acts as an index" is actually true. The cost: `_table` through `Merge` over `Distributed` reads `t_dist`, not `t_leaf`; each nesting level of `Merge` reports its own child. Tests `00717` (whose leaf-name expectations were rewritten in #63665 itself), `03094`, `04338`, `04367`, `03031`, `01902`, `03988`, `04104` and `01155` are updated accordingly; the new test `05019_merge_virtual_columns_delegating_children` covers the pruning and the values over `Distributed`, nested `Merge` and `Buffer` children, with both analyzers. This also unblocks #113242, whose only functional CI failure was `00717_merge_and_distributed` newly reaching the pruning defect at `FetchColumns`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115356&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115356](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115356+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix `clickhouse-local` printing TSV instead of PrettyCompact in interactive mode
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105249 Interactive `clickhouse-local` on master renders query results as `TSV` instead of the terminal default `PrettyCompact`. `applyCmdOptions` seeds the `default_format` setting on `global_context` as the fallback format of the sessions of the embedded protocol listeners (`SYSTEM START LISTEN`), where it must match a real `clickhouse-server` (`TabSeparated`). `client_context` is copied from `global_context` and inherits the seed, and the per-query output-format resolution introduced in #105249 treats a non-empty `default_format` setting as the fallback format, so the seed overrode the interactive display default. (#105249 guarded `--vertical` against exactly this failure mode, but the plain interactive default slipped through: it is the one case where `is_default_format` stays true.) The fix clears the seeded value on `client_context`, in `makeFormatOptionsPrivateToTheClient`, which already handles the mirror image of this problem for the `format` / `input_format` / `output_format` settings. This client renders results from its own `ClientBase::default_output_format`, so the seed is not needed there. Explicit choices keep working: an explicit `--default_format` on the command line is left in place (guarded by `cmd_settings->isChanged`), and a later `SET default_format = ...` or an in-query `SETTINGS` clause lands on `client_context` after the clearing. The served sessions still get the fallback through `global_context`. Verified against the master CI binary (26.8.1.1658, where the regression reproduces): emulating the fix by forcing an empty `default_format` on the client restores `PrettyCompact`, while `SET default_format = 'JSONEachRow'` and `SETTINGS default_format = 'CSV'` continue to be honored. The added `04927_local_interactive_default_format.expect` test fails on current master and passes with the fix emulated; the listener-side default is already covered by `04501_local_http_default_format.expect`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a regression on master (not present in any release): interactive `clickhouse-local` rendered query results as `TSV` instead of `PrettyCompact`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115360&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115360](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115360+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: Optimize PromQL and for exact groups
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL `and` expressions with an exact group key skip redundant matching stages. ## What changed - add a fast path for the PromQL set operator `and` - use it when both inputs already match on the original `group` column - join the unique left and right `VECTOR_GRID` inputs directly - keep the left-hand values and filter them by right-side sample presence - keep `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, `on()`, and other transformed matching keys on the existing general path - add exact-output coverage for grouped `and` expressions - cover empty `ignoring()` when both inputs already have exact groups - add a performance fixture with an exact-group query and an `and on(instance)` control ## Why this is safe `VECTOR_GRID` guarantees one row per `group`. The fast path is enabled only when the matching rules leave the original `group` column unchanged on both sides, so the join key is already unique and exact. The exact-group path removes the right-side per-group count aggregation and the transformed-key join. It returns the left value only when the corresponding right value is present, which is the existing `and` masking behavior. `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, and other cases that transform the matching key keep the current general lowering. Empty `ignoring()` is treated like default matching when both inputs already have exact groups. ## Benchmark Ran `tests/performance/promql_set_operators_and.xml` on Apple Silicon with the Release build from this PR. - 8,000 series - 4,000 matching groups - 300 samples per series - 7 measured runs per query on each of two local server instances The table shows the average of the two per-server medians. Both queries are equivalent for this fixture. The default query uses the new exact-group fast path. The `and on(instance)` query keeps the existing generic implementation. | Query | Median | | --- | ---: | | exact-group `and` | 130.2 ms | | equivalent `and on(instance)` query | 139.8 ms | The exact-group query took 130.2 ms versus 139.8 ms for the existing implementation, which is 6.9% faster in this test. ## Tests - add grouped exact-output coverage for `and` - add exact-output coverage for empty `ignoring()` - keep the existing ungrouped and transformed-key `and` coverage - compile the changed translation unit with the ClickHouse warning set and `-Werror` Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115219 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115374&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115374](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115374+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Bound the shutdown wait for cancelled backups and restores
signals.text: Bound the shutdown wait for cancelled backups and restores <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): With `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0`, a `BACKUP` or `RESTORE` whose I/O did not return kept the server from terminating on a single `SIGTERM`, because shutdown waited for it to reach a final status with no timeout. That wait is now bounded by `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and new backups and restores are refused once shutdown has begun. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105 Reported by @ PedroTadim, who [asked me to take it](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105#issuecomment-5326577830). The issue stays open. **Cause.** Shutdown waits with `status_changed.wait` - no timeout, predicate on the operation status only, so it lasts as long as the operation. `cancelAll` does not help: cancellation is polled per file (`checkTimeLimit()` before `writeFile`), and within a file `BackupImpl` uses the `copyData` overload with no cancellation hook, so a thread parked in a read never sees it. **Change**, all inside the `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0` branch of `Server.cpp`: refuse new operations, bound the wait at `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and on non-convergence feed the forced exit that already handles `!joined_refresh_tasks`. That exit is `_exit`, so the unbounded `thread_pools->wait()` in `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` is never reached rather than bounded. `addInfo` refuses after its dedup early-return: `UNFINISHED` for internal operations (retriable in `DDLWorker`), `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` otherwise. **Not fixed here.** The default `= 1` branch is untouched, so the hang is still reachable with stock settings: that setting is documented as waiting for backups to *finish*, so capping it changes the guarantee and is your call. Also unchanged: the per-file cancellation granularity, and `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` reached without this guard (failed startup script), where bounding its status waits just moves the block to the pool join. An abandoned backup keeps its `CREATING_BACKUP` row and can leave partial files. **Validation.** The new tests wedge a backup with the existing `backup_pause_on_start` failpoint, which parks the thread before any `checkTimeLimit()` check, so the operation never sees its own cancellation. The oracle is whether `stop_clickhouse()` escalated to `SIGKILL`, not elapsed time and not a log line (`_exit` discards the async log queue). One arm requires self-exit and fails on master; a second raises the setting to 600 and requires the server to keep waiting, so a hardcoded deadline fails it. 50/50 stable; sibling shutdown and on-cluster cancel tests pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Query cache on disk, backed by the filesystem cache
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115361 The query cache can now additionally store its entries on disk, backed by a preconfigured filesystem cache (an entry of the `filesystem_caches` section of the server configuration), selected per query with the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`. Compared to the in-memory query cache, this gives the entries more space, makes them survive server restarts, and (with a distributed filesystem cache) provides a way to share them between servers. Design, following the RFC in the issue: - The entries are ordinary filesystem cache entries, indistinguishable from other data in the same filesystem cache: they are not held from deletion, they are evicted by the same rules, and there are no specific limits on their total size or number other than the limits of the filesystem cache itself. The keys are hashed with a salt so that they cannot intersect with other keys in the filesystem cache. - No extra in-memory state is kept: all metadata needed to validate an entry (TTL, user id, roles, the shared flag) is serialized into the entry itself, followed by the result payload in `Native` format, compressed with the codec from the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_codec` (default `ZSTD(3)`; reading is independent of the setting because the compressed frames are self-describing). - The on-disk cache works independently of the in-memory cache and can separately be enabled for reads and/or writes with the new settings `enable_reads_from_query_cache_on_disk` and `enable_writes_to_query_cache_on_disk` (both `true` by default, activated by setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`). If both caches are enabled for reads, the lookup is attempted first from memory and only on a miss from disk. If both caches are enabled for writes, the result is written to both. A result served from memory is not written to disk. - A stale (expired TTL), partially evicted, corrupt, or inaccessible (another user's non-shared) entry is treated as a cache miss; stale entries are overwritten on the next write. - Introspection of the on-disk entries in `system.query_cache` is out of scope, per the issue. New profile events: `QueryCacheOnDiskHits`, `QueryCacheOnDiskMisses`, `QueryCacheOnDiskReadBytes`, `QueryCacheOnDiskWrittenBytes`. Tests: `05019_query_cache_on_disk_local` proves persistence across process restarts (separate `clickhouse-local` invocations sharing one filesystem cache directory, including a cached non-deterministic result, TTL expiry, and disabled reads); `05020_query_cache_on_disk` covers the server path with user isolation, sharing via `query_cache_share_between_users`, and error cases (unknown cache name, invalid codec). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The query cache can now store its entries on disk, backed by a preconfigured filesystem cache: this gives the entries more space, makes them survive server restarts, and (with a distributed filesystem cache) provides a way to share them between servers. Select the filesystem cache with the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`; see also the new settings `query_cache_on_disk_codec`, `enable_writes_to_query_cache_on_disk`, and `enable_reads_from_query_cache_on_disk`. Closes [#115361](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115361). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115382&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115382](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115382+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not let an alias give `randConstant` a second value in one query
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112938 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `randConstant` returning two different values in one query when its calls carry different aliases. `randConstant` is documented to hold a single value for the whole query, and `SELECT randConstant() = randConstant()` already returned `1`, but adding aliases as in `SELECT randConstant() AS a, randConstant() AS b` produced two unrelated values. ### Description ```sql SELECT randConstant() = randConstant() -- 1 SELECT a = b FROM (SELECT randConstant() AS a, randConstant() AS b) -- 0 <-- wrong ``` `randConstant` is documented to return "a single random value that remains constant across all rows in the current query execution", and its argument is documented as existing only "to prevent common subexpression elimination when the same function call is used multiple times in a query". So two bare calls must agree, and asking for a second value is spelled `randConstant(1), randConstant(2)`. `RandomConstantOverloadResolver::buildImpl` draws a new value on every call, so identical calls have to share one built `FunctionBase` to fold to one constant. `resolveFunction` arranges that with `functions_cache`, keyed by `getTreeHash`. That hash covers the alias, so the two aliased calls missed each other in the cache, each folded to its own literal, and no later common subexpression elimination could bring them back together — by then they were two different literals. With `enable_analyzer = 0` the same query returns `1`, so this is analyzer-only. The key now ignores aliases. An alias renames an expression and never changes the value the `FunctionBase` captures, so aliased calls share what bare calls share. What separates two calls is still their arguments, which the hash covers. Dropping the alias from the key widens what the cache can match, and stateful functions must not be matched: the cache is global across query scopes, so two scalar subqueries that differ only by an alias would have ended up sharing one `blockNumber` counter and reading two different numbers. Stateful functions are therefore excluded from the cache alongside `getSetting` and `rowNumberInAllBlocks`, and the last row of the test covers it by comparing the two counters (their absolute values are not a property of the fix - they count the blocks the server has already passed through the function). The change is narrower than the cache's reach suggests. Only a function folded through its own `FunctionBase` can be split this way; anything evaluated per row, such as `rand` or `generateUUIDv4`, is deduplicated later by ordinary common subexpression elimination, which already ignored aliases — `SELECT rand() AS a, rand() AS b, a = b` reads `1` on `master` today. To bound it rather than argue it, I swept all 57 zero-argument non-deterministic functions, comparing each one aliased and bare, before and after: `randConstant` is the only function whose result changes, from `0` to `1`, and no bare result moves at all. Test `05028` fails on exactly its four aliased rows without the change. Its five controls — the bare comparison, the distinct-argument row (four arguments rather than two, so it cannot flake on a value collision), the across-rows row, and the `now` and `rand` rows — pass either way. Verified by building and running against the branch build: `05028` plus the five existing tests that read `randConstant` (`03611`, `01418`, `00912`, `04327` across shards, `03047` under mutations) all pass. The 382-test `analyzer` family was run on both arms of an exact A/B on the same tree — the one-line change reverted, rebuilt, rerun — and the two arms are identical: 352 pass and the same 18 fail on both, all of them for missing fixtures in my local server rather than for this change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115384&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115384](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115384+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Sync `BackupImpl` lock-file handling and the Cloud-only resume state
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/69709 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/69709 This is the public side of the private pull request above, and most of it is that sync. The shared files both touch -- `BackupImpl.h`, `BackupImpl.cpp`, `BackupSettings.h`, `BackupSettings.cpp`, `BackupFactory.h` -- are identical here and there, down to the blank lines, so `Check public build` can overlay the private ones unchanged and later syncs have nothing to reconcile in them. What stays private is where continuing an interrupted backup is implemented, because nothing outside ClickHouse Cloud resumes one. The part that changes this build is the lock-file handling. `open` runs from the constructor, so a failure there leaves no backup behind for anything else to clean up: whatever `open` does not undo, nothing will. It now removes the lock it created when anything that follows throws -- the verification, the rest of claiming the destination, and opening the archive. Otherwise the lock outlives the failed attempt and fences the destination against every later one, which cannot match it either: a retry picks a fresh backup UUID, so the orphaned lock belongs to nobody, and every subsequent `BACKUP` to that destination fails until someone deletes the file by hand. `removeLockFile` now reports whether the destination still holds the lock. `checkLockFile(false)` is false both for a foreign lock and for one it could not read, so a caller could not tell "not ours" from "unknown" while the lock was still there; `tryRemoveAllFiles` reports that as a failure rather than claiming the destination is clean. `createLockFile` asks for the lock with `writeFileIfNotExists` and, when that fails, compares what is there against what it would have written: its own contents mean a concurrent backup, a completed `.backup` means the backup already exists, and a lock that has since disappeared rethrows the original failure rather than guessing. `writeFileIfNotExists` is only exclusive where the storage can be -- `S3` and `Azure` implement it, every other writer falls back to an ordinary write. ### Known gaps Two of them, both predating this change and both worth naming rather than implying they are fixed. `File`, `Disk` and `Memory` destinations still have no exclusive create, so two backups started against one of them can each write `.lock`, each verify their own contents, and both proceed. The comparison above detects a lock that is already there; it cannot order two writers racing to create one. Closing this needs an exclusive create in those writers. An archive whose type `createArchiveWriter` refuses -- an unsupported extension, a compiled-out library -- still leaves the archive object behind, because the buffer it is given is created before the type is checked. The lock is removed, but the next attempt finds the archive and reports the destination as an existing backup. ### The rest Behind `CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD`, and compiling to nothing here: `CreateParams` carries the resume parameters, `open` hands them to a `BackupResumer` this build does not have, and the places that read them are the ownership check before anything becomes visible, the timestamp a continuation republishes, the lock a continuation is allowed to find, and the manifest it does not write again. `BackupSettings` carries the two batch-size settings that bound the work a continuation redoes; a macro list cannot hold a preprocessor conditional, so the conditional selects the list. `BackupImpl` keeps one member, `metadata_already_published`. So this build behaves as it did: it writes its own timestamp and always publishes metadata. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `BACKUP` no longer leaves a lock file behind in its destination when the attempt that created it fails before writing anything -- whether it fails while claiming the destination or while opening an archive. No later backup could match such a lock, so every retry to the same destination failed until the file was deleted by hand. Backups to `S3` and `Azure` destinations also create the lock exclusively, and a lock that belongs to another backup is reported as a concurrent backup rather than as whatever error the storage returned. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115387&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115387](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115387+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1800` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Self-contained binary: embedded CA certificates; DNS without resolv.conf and hosts in musl builds
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/musl/pull/6 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The ClickHouse binary is now self-contained and works in a container image built `FROM scratch` with no additional files when built with musl. CA certificates (the Chromium root store, taken from the gRPC submodule) are embedded into the binary and used as a fallback when no CA certificates are found on the filesystem. In musl builds, when `/etc/resolv.conf` does not exist, DNS falls back to well-known public resolvers instead of the unreachable localhost, and `localhost` resolves to loopback per RFC 6761 even without `/etc/hosts`. ### Description The goal is a self-contained binary: a musl build should run in a container image built `FROM scratch` (or as the init process of a minimal system) without any files in the image — no CA certificates, no `/etc/resolv.conf`, no `/etc/hosts`, no `/etc/passwd`. Only the kernel interfaces (`/proc` and the standard minimal `/dev` that every container gets) are expected. **Embedded CA certificates** (all builds, not only musl). Every TLS context is created by `Poco::Net::Context::init`, which loads default CA certificates from `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`, `/etc/ssl`, and a list of well-known distribution locations, and previously threw `Cannot load default CA certificates` when none were found — so in a bare container, the TLS listeners did not start and every HTTPS request (S3, Azure, `url`, dictionaries, secure ZooKeeper, `remoteSecure`) failed at context creation. Now the root store maintained in the gRPC submodule (`contrib/grpc/etc/roots.pem`, the Chromium root store, 115 roots) is embedded with C23 `#embed` and added to the trust store only when the filesystem yields nothing. Certificates found on the filesystem always take precedence, and the embedded ones are not loaded at all in that case. An existing but *empty* certificate directory (e.g. an `/etc/ssl/certs` left behind by a removed `ca-certificates` package) also engages the fallback, since a directory without hash-named files can never yield a certificate at verification time; previously it silently produced an empty trust store that failed at handshake time. The embedded certificates are visible in `system.certificates` with `path = '(embedded)'`, and the feature can be disabled with `-DENABLE_EMBEDDED_CA_CERTIFICATES=0`. **DNS without `/etc/resolv.conf`** (musl builds). musl is built from sources from the ClickHouse fork, so the fallback lives there (https://github.com/ClickHouse/musl/pull/6) and covers every consumer of `getaddrinfo` in the binary at once — Poco, NuRaft asio, and the client libraries in contrib. When the file does not exist, the resolver uses `1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`, `2606:4700:4700::1111` instead of the upstream fallback of `127.0.0.1`, which cannot answer in such an environment. A `resolv.conf` that exists but configures no nameservers — or exists but is unreadable — keeps the upstream localhost fallback, since it expresses an intentional local configuration. **`localhost` without `/etc/hosts`** (musl builds, same fork PR). `localhost` and any name under `.localhost` resolve to the loopback addresses per RFC 6761 when the hosts file yields nothing for them, and are never sent to DNS resolvers — matching c-ares and systemd-resolved. Without this, the public-resolver fallback above would leak `localhost` queries to the network. An `/etc/hosts` entry still takes precedence. Also fixed along the way: - The aarch64 openldap configuration lacked the musl guard for `bits/types.h` that the x86_64 one received when musl started to be built from sources (CI only has an x86_64 musl build), so aarch64 musl builds did not compile. - The server failed at startup with `FAILED_TO_GETPWUID` when there is no `/etc/passwd` and the effective user does not match the data owner, while merely trying to render the name for the diagnostic message; it now uses the numeric id, the same as for a null `getpwuid_r` result. Also fixed `getUserName` writing into unused string capacity. ### Verification Everything was verified on an aarch64 musl build (`cmake/linux/toolchain-aarch64-musl.cmake`) running in a chroot containing only the binary, `/proc`, and `/dev`: - `clickhouse local --query "SELECT count() > 0 FROM url('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/master/README.md', LineAsString)"` returns `1` — DNS through the embedded fallback resolvers plus TLS against the embedded root store, with no `/etc` at all. The same works with an existing but empty `/etc/ssl/certs`. - `strace` confirms `localhost` lookups produce zero DNS packets while resolving to `127.0.0.1`/`::1`, and that DNS queries go to the fallback resolvers. - `clickhouse server` starts (`Ready for connections`) and `clickhouse client` connects and executes queries inside the same bare chroot. The new integration test `test_embedded_ca_certificates` covers the certificate fallback in CI: it removes every certificate location from the container (and separately re-creates an empty `/etc/ssl/certs`), restarts the server, and checks that HTTPS still works and that `system.certificates` shows the embedded roots. The DNS part cannot be covered by CI tests, because the test builds link glibc; it is covered by the manual verification above. Not covered (possible follow-ups): client libraries in contrib that load CA certificates through their own code paths (librdkafka for Kafka broker TLS, NATS, MongoDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL clients, LDAP) — all of them have explicit CA configuration options; and glibc builds still need the resolver libraries and `resolv.conf` from the OS, as before. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115389&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115389](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115389+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
