signals.title: Fix singleValueOrNull state serialization
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105733 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105734 ## TL;DR `singleValueOrNull` can return the wrong result after an aggregate state crosses a merge, storage, distributed, or generic-format boundary. The function must return: - the value when exactly one distinct non-NULL value was seen - `NULL` when no value or multiple distinct values were seen The old state format stored only the first value. It did not store the semantic flags needed to distinguish these cases. This PR adds a versioned state format that preserves the complete semantic state and keeps old version `0` states readable. ## What was wrong `singleValueOrNull` keeps two pieces of state in addition to the stored value: - `first_value`: whether any value has been seen - `is_null`: whether different values have been seen, so the result must be `NULL` Before this change: - merging a state that was already `NULL` did not propagate `is_null` - serialization stored only the underlying value - deserialization lost both semantic flags This caused two user-visible problems: 1. A state containing one value, for example `42`, could be deserialized and finalized as `NULL`. 2. A state that had seen two different values could be deserialized as the first stored value, even though its correct result was `NULL`. The second case is especially dangerous because it can silently change a predicate result. ## Why this matters `singleValueOrNull` is used by ClickHouse for single-value and subquery semantics, including `ALL` and `ANY` comparisons. Returning a concrete value instead of `NULL` can change the result of a query. This is not only a display issue. It can change filtering and comparison behavior after: - MergeTree persistence - parallel aggregation - distributed aggregation - aggregate state exchange between servers - generic formats such as `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes` ## What this changes - Adds state version `1`. - Version `1` serializes both `first_value` and `is_null`. - Keeps version `0` readable for existing tables and older peers. - Treats a non-empty version `0` payload conservatively as `NULL`, because the old bytes cannot distinguish one value from multiple distinct values. - Adds protocol revision `54493`, so version `1` is used only when both peers support it. - Makes version selection consistent for combinator-wrapped states. - Fixes version forwarding for `ForEach`, `Map`, and `OrDefault` paths. - Updates the Native format and protocol documentation. The merge propagation part is already covered by #105734. This PR focuses on the serialization and state-versioning part. ## Compatibility Existing version `0` bytes remain readable. However, the old format did not contain enough information to recover every historical result exactly. In particular, a non-empty payload could mean either: - one value was seen - multiple distinct values were seen and the result should be `NULL` For that reason, version `0` is handled conservatively. New states use version `1`, which preserves the distinction correctly. ## Tests - MergeTree persistence for a valid single-value state. - MergeTree persistence for a multiple-values state. - Conservative handling of a legacy version `0` state containing multiple values. - `singleValueOrNullIf` round trip through `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes`. - `singleValueOrNullForEach` round trip through `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes`. - `singleValueOrNullMap` round trip through `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes`. - `quantileDeterministicForEach` state round trip through MergeTree. - Versioned type coverage for `singleValueOrNullOrDefault`. - Native format and protocol documentation updates. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Preserve `singleValueOrNull` semantic state during serialization. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115519&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115519](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115519+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Widen the Keeper request-size TSan suppression to the whole `bytesSize` subtree
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113552 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112695 On `amd_tsan` integration shards the Keeper container occasionally writes a ThreadSanitizer report for the request the dispatch thread just popped, which aborts the container. `helpers/cluster.py` then raises `Sanitizer assert found for instance zooN` during `cluster.shutdown()`, and whichever test happened to run last goes red - the victim is incidental. This time it was `test_database_replicated_settings/test.py::test_database_replicated_with_internal_replication[1-1]`: ``` WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race (pid=1) Read of size 1 ... by thread T32: #0 std::__1::basic_string<...>::__is_long() const #2 Coordination::GetRequest::bytesSize() const src/Common/ZooKeeper/IKeeper.h:532 #4 DB::getRequestBytesCost(...) src/Coordination/KeeperRequestDispatcher.cpp:94 #5 DB::KeeperRequestDispatcher::tryPopRequest(...) src/Coordination/KeeperRequestDispatcher.cpp:434 Previous write of size 8 ... by thread T5: #3 Coordination::GetRequest::GetRequest() src/Common/ZooKeeper/IKeeper.h:525 #18 Coordination::ZooKeeperRequestFactory::get(...) src/Common/ZooKeeper/ZooKeeperCommon.cpp:1786 #19 DB::KeeperTCPHandler::receiveRequest() src/Server/KeeperTCPHandler.cpp:787 ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=dddf61ccff5828bb6937cfe680874a04be35932f&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%206%2F6%29 There is no real race. `KeeperTCPHandler::receiveRequest` writes every payload field of the request - `xid`, then `readImpl`, then the tracing context - before publishing it with `putRequest`; the only post-publication write is on the consumer's own side. `getRequestBytesCost` reads the vptr and those fields. #113552 added the entry for this report as `race_top:^DB::getRequestBytesCost`. `race_top:` matches the innermost frame only, so it covered the vptr read, which ThreadSanitizer attributes to the call site inside `getRequestBytesCost`. Suppressing that does not stop the run: the very next racy access is the `path` read inside `Coordination::GetRequest::bytesSize`, one frame below, and it aborts the container all the same. That is the report above. So this switches the entry to `race:`, which matches any frame and therefore covers the whole callee subtree. The subtree is only `bytesSize`, a read-only size computation, and a use-after-free blinded there still surfaces on the next access to the same request in `dispatchThread`. ### Validation Against the real ThreadSanitizer runtime, with a harness whose handoff is deliberately unsynchronized so a report is produced on every run and the only variable is which patterns match the frame shape. Arms differ only in the string returned by `__tsan_default_suppressions`. `banner` counts runs printing the `==================` line, which is exactly what the integration harness greps to raise the assert. | suppression string | vptr shape (#113552) | `bytesSize` shape (this report) | |---|---|---| | (empty) | 8/10 | 10/10 | | `race_top:^DB::getRequestBytesCost` | 8/10 | 9/10 | | `race:^DB::getRequestBytesCost` | **0/20** | **0/20** | In the `race_top:` / vptr-shape cell the surviving report is exactly the one master hit: `race_top:` suppresses the vptr read, the run continues, and the `path.size()` read inside `bytesSize` is reported instead. Controls: a typo'd pattern (`race:^DB::getRequestBytesCostXX`) parses but suppresses nothing (10/10 banner), so the entry's liveness is not assumed; a mangled type token (`raceX:`) makes the runtime die with `failed to parse suppressions`, confirming this hook is the live channel; `print_suppressions=1` shows the new entry being hit. `ci/jobs/scripts/check_style/check_cpp.sh` passes. Non-TSan builds are unaffected - the hook is inside `#ifdef THREAD_SANITIZER`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115524&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115524](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115524+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support PromQL count_values
signals.text: **TL;DR** - **Adds** PromQL `count_values` support for ClickHouse `TimeSeries` data. - **Matches** Prometheus value-label, grouping, float-formatting, and stale-marker behavior. - **Includes** integration tests, compliance cases, and user documentation. **Why this matters** - **PromQL compatibility:** Queries using `count_values` can run through the ClickHouse PromQL path instead of being rejected as unsupported. - **State metrics:** This is useful for counting how many series currently have each value, such as service states, status codes, or rollout phases. - **Existing queries:** Users can keep Prometheus queries that already use `by()` and `without()` without rewriting them for ClickHouse. - **Correct results:** Matching label and float semantics is important for dashboards, recording rules, and alerts that compare ClickHouse results with Prometheus. Adds native lowering for the PromQL `count_values` aggregation operator over ClickHouse `TimeSeries` data. **What changed** - **PromQL lowering:** Adds `count_values` to the PromQL-to-SQL aggregation path. - **Value labels:** Formats every sample value as a Prometheus label string and stores it under the requested label name. - **Grouping:** Applies the generated value label before `by()` and `without()` grouping, matching Prometheus label-set behavior. - **Counting:** Counts equal values for each output label set and evaluation step. - **Sparse results:** Packs the counts back into the vector-grid shape and keeps missing samples as `NULL`. - **Float formatting:** Adds a dedicated formatter for `Float32` and `Float64` values. - **Label validation:** Accepts non-empty valid UTF-8 label names and rejects empty names. - **Special values:** Covers `NaN`, `+Inf`, `-Inf`, `-0`, and large values such as `1e21`. - **Stale markers:** Filters the Prometheus stale-marker payload without dropping regular `NaN` values. **Tests** - **Integration coverage:** Adds `by()` grouping, UTF-8 label names, empty labels, stale markers, and float-formatting cases. - **Compliance coverage:** Adds `by()`, `without()`, empty-vector, dynamic `time()`, and invalid-label cases. - **Validation:** Python test files compile successfully and the patch passes whitespace checks. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added native PromQL-to-SQL lowering for `count_values` over ClickHouse `TimeSeries` data. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description A job's summary line carried only `Failures: N/M`. When a job dies in a step outside the node named by `result_name_for_cidb` (`Install ClickHouse`, `Start ClickHouse Server`), that count is the only text in the job's own info, so the cause reaches neither CIDB's job-level row, nor the report page, nor the GitHub issue body. It survives only inside `job.log`. 152 failing master job instances land in this shape over 30d; at `b03544a19bc` the failing `Start ClickHouse Server` node carried 301 lines and CIDB got 13 bytes ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b03544a19bc3e7046b8ac5eb6467bf444f295038&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29)). `_add_job_summary_to_info` now names each failing direct child after the count line. The count line stays first and keeps its exact old text, so readers and queries written against it keep matching. Fixing it here rather than in `cidb.py` lifts every surface that renders a job summary, per review. Two bounds, both measured. `from_commands_run` puts the cause near the front in its error-centered branch but at the tail in its default branch, so a one-ended trim drops it in one of the two; the trim keeps both ends. And a job whose direct children are test cases already publishes a row per case, so naming all of them grew this row with the failure count (40 cases gave 120 KB); at most the first few are named. Not addressed: a job whose info is already non-empty when the summary runs, so a later fallible sibling (`Collect logs`) still publishes no cause. That predates this change, identically, and reaching it needs the final result tree at serialization time. `Keeper Stress` naming a `result_name_for_cidb` no child carries is likewise unchanged. Validation: `ci/tests/test_job_summary_names_failed_step.py`, 21 cases including both payload branches, both trim directions, the per-shape bound, and the path through the real publisher. 15 mutations, one per property, each reddens the suite; the whole `ci/tests` suite passes. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115526&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115526](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115526+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a TOLERANCE clause to ASOF JOIN
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109034 `ASOF JOIN` matches the closest row however far away it is, so a trade can be matched against a quote from hours earlier. `TOLERANCE` bounds that distance: ```sql SELECT trades.time, trades.price, quotes.bid FROM trades ASOF LEFT JOIN quotes ON trades.symbol = quotes.symbol AND trades.time >= quotes.time TOLERANCE INTERVAL 5 SECOND ``` The bound is inclusive. With `ASOF LEFT JOIN` a row whose closest match is out of tolerance is kept with default or `NULL` values on the right, following `join_use_nulls`, which is what `pandas.merge_asof(tolerance=...)` does. With `ASOF JOIN` it is dropped, like a row with no match at all. It can be written as an `INTERVAL`, or as a plain number in the units of the `ASOF` column. For a `DateTime64(3)` column `TOLERANCE 5000` and `TOLERANCE INTERVAL 5 SECOND` are the same bound. ### Implementation notes The bound is converted into the units of the `ASOF` key once, during planning, so the join implementation compares it against key values directly with no per-probe conversion. `findAsof` already returns the closest match in the direction the inequality fixes, so if that one is out of bounds no other can be closer and the probe has no match. The interval unit is read from the result type rather than from the shape of the expression: `INTERVAL 5 SECOND` is written `toIntervalSecond(5)` but is constant folded during resolution into a constant whose value is `5` and whose type is `IntervalSecond`, so treating it as a bare number silently means five milliseconds against a `DateTime64(3)` key. ### Rejected rather than approximated - `MONTH`, `QUARTER` and `YEAR`, which are not fixed lengths of time. - An `INTERVAL` against an `ASOF` key that is not a date or time, where the unit would be undefined. - A bound finer than the key's resolution, such as `INTERVAL 1 MICROSECOND` against `DateTime64(3)`, which would otherwise round down to "exact matches only". - A negative bound, which nothing can satisfy. - `enable_analyzer = 0`, which builds `TableJoin` without the query tree the bound travels on and would silently ignore it. - `full_sorting_merge`, which matches through `IColumn::compareAt` and so has ordering but not distance. The planner falls back to another enabled algorithm; if only `full_sorting_merge` is enabled the query fails. Each of these silently returns matches further away than the query asked for if it is accepted instead, which is the failure this clause exists to prevent. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `TOLERANCE` clause to `ASOF JOIN`, bounding how far apart the left and the matched right value of the `ASOF` column may be, so that stale rows are not matched. The bound can be given as an `INTERVAL` or as a number in the units of the `ASOF` column, for example `ASOF LEFT JOIN quotes ON trades.symbol = quotes.symbol AND trades.time >= quotes.time TOLERANCE INTERVAL 5 SECOND`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115530&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115530](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115530+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Bound the response wait of the GCP OAuth token request instead of inheriting the caller's request timeout
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109455 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang of up to one hour in `BACKUP`/`RESTORE ... TO S3`, GCS disks and the `s3` table function when the named collection sets `http_client = 'gcp_oauth'` and the Google OAuth2 token endpoint accepts the connection but never answers. The bearer token request no longer inherits the caller's data transfer request timeout; its response wait is bounded at 10 seconds, matching the STS `AssumeRole` request cap. ### Description Found in CI: `BACKUP TABLE ... TO S3(<collection with http_client = 'gcp_oauth'>)` sat for 695 s with `read_rows: 0` until the test budget expired and the job reported `Some queries hung`. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107108&sha=7b0f0efd7803a3f3a603fe10adf92811bf16f468&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%203%2F3%29 `BackupIO_S3.cpp` sets `requestTimeoutMs = 60 * 60 * 1000` because backup data transfers can legitimately take that long. That single value becomes both the send and the receive socket timeout, and `PocoHTTPClientGCPOAuth` reuses the same `timeouts` member for its bearer token round trip, so a credential request that should take milliseconds parked in the TLS header read for an hour (`SecureSocketImpl::mustRetry` under `HTTPHeaderStreamBuf::readFromDevice`). The S3 endpoint in the failing case is plain HTTP on localhost, so the TLS peer can only be the hardcoded Google token URL. This bounds the response wait of that round trip at 10 seconds, independently of the data transfer timeouts, at both mint sites (explicit ADC triple, and the metadata service branch). The connect timeout is left as the caller set it: `metadata_service` is a user-configurable host, so its connect budget belongs to the deployment that configured it, and connect was never the unbounded phase (`BackupIO_S3` already bounds it at 10 s). Data plane requests keep the full hour, and an already tighter timeout is kept. The 10 s matches the STS `AssumeRole` request cap, so it is named once in `S3Defines.h`. Validated against a mock that accepts and never answers: the value passed before was still blocked after 40 s, the value passed now fails in 10.0 s. Exactly one request arrived in each arm, so `backup_restore_s3_retry_attempts` (default 1000) does not multiply the mint. Not bounded here: session creation is retried up to 5 times, each attempt carrying the caller's connect budget, and the mint is not cancellation aware within the 10 s. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115531&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115531](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115531+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1803` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Bind an unqualified dictGet name to the current database
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85181 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/44301 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/46424 The dictionary name of `dictGet` and its variations is resolved against the current database of the server that *evaluates* the function. A shard of a `Distributed` table evaluates it in a session whose current database comes from the cluster configuration — `default` unless `<default_database>` is set — and not from the initiator. So: ```sql USE demo; SELECT code, dictGet('dict_test', 'value', code) FROM demo.test; ``` fails on the shards with ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Dictionary (`dict_test`) not found: In scope SELECT __table1.code AS code, dictGet('dict_test', 'value', __table1.code) ... FROM demo.test_local AS __table1. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` and — worse — when a dictionary of the same name also exists in the shard's own database, no error is raised at all and the values of the *wrong* dictionary are returned silently. This binds the name in the analyzer, while the current database of the initiator is still known, so the bound name travels to the shards inside the query tree. The old analyzer already does the same in `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` for the query it sends to the shards. The binding happens after the projection names of the arguments have been calculated, so the column name of the expression stays exactly as it was written by the user: `dictGet('dict_test', 'value', code)`, not `dictGet('demo.dict_test', 'value', code)`. `qualifyDictionaryNameWithDatabase` leaves the name alone when it is already qualified, when it belongs to an XML dictionary, and when no such dictionary exists in the current database — in the last case the name may still be meant for a dictionary that only exists on the shards. Notes: - The `EXPLAIN SYNTAX run_query_tree_passes=1` references of the inverse dictionary lookup tests now show the bound name; only the printed query changes there, no result changes. - Existing test `04054_dictget_unqualified_name_distributed` deliberately runs in the `default` database so that the shard can resolve the unqualified name, which is why it never caught this. The new test runs in the test's own database with `prefer_localhost_replica = 0`, which is what makes the shard query travel over a real connection. - The old analyzer keeps failing here with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`, because the header it computes on the initiator keeps the unqualified column name while the query it ships to the shards carries the qualified one. Fixing that needs a separate change, so the new test is tagged `no-old-analyzer`. - `joinGet` has the same defect (`Table default.jt does not exist. Maybe you meant demo.jt?`); its first argument is a table name with temporary-table and access-control semantics of its own, so it is left for a separate change. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `dictGet` and its variations in distributed queries: an unqualified dictionary name is now bound to the current database of the initiator, instead of being resolved against the current database of each shard, where it either was not found or resolved to a different dictionary of the same name. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115541&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115541](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115541+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1789` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix `STREAM BOUNDED` returning no rows on a stale enrichment round
signals.text: Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110653 `MergeTreeData::scheduleStreamingJob` read the visible parts *before* it iterated the registered subscriptions, so a subscription registered in that window was credited with an enrichment round computed from a parts snapshot taken before it existed. For a subscribing stream that is harmless — the next round fixes the cursor. For a bounded stream it is not: `handleBoundedReconfiguration` treats the first completed round as authoritative, so an empty stale round makes the source finish immediately and the query silently returns fewer rows (usually none) than were committed before it started. That is how `04545_streaming_queries_bounded` failed on master. The first query in the test (`STREAM BOUNDED` over the still-empty table) triggers the background streaming job; the job snapshots an empty part set and is then descheduled; by the time it reaches `executeOnEachSubscription` the two `INSERT`s and the second query have already run, so the second query's subscription is handed that empty round: ``` empty 0 -all 10 45 450 +all 0 0 0 ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=8d5be603139a198bdfd2ea225d2e998554316178&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20parallel%29 The fix collects the subscriptions first and reads the parts only afterwards. Everything in the collected list was registered before the collect, so the parts snapshot is at least as fresh as every subscription served from it. A subscription registered after the collect is picked up by the next round instead: its own `triggerStreamingSubscriptionEnrichment` re-schedules the job even while the job is running, because `BackgroundSchedulePoolTaskInfo::execute` re-queues a task that was scheduled during execution. `executeOnEachSubscription` is replaced by `collectSubscriptions`, which returns strong pointers under the shared lock — the callback form invited exactly this ordering mistake, and there was only one caller. The race is timing-dependent (one failure in 2629 master runs of this test over 90 days), so there is no deterministic functional test for it; the added unit tests cover the `collectSubscriptions` contract the fix relies on, including that a subscription registered after a collect is not part of that round. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a race that could make a `STREAM BOUNDED` query return fewer rows than were committed before it started, usually none. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115543&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115543](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115543+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1779` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Add min_partition_age_to_force_merge_seconds to compact partitions that no longer receive inserts
signals.text: ## Summary Closes #79697. Reworked per review: the previous `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... MERGE SMALLPARTS` syntax is reverted. Instead this adds an opt-in `MergeTree` setting, `min_partition_age_to_force_merge_seconds`, addressing the issue's use case in the background merge selector itself (similar in spirit to #105454). When set to a non-zero value and every part in a partition is at least that many seconds old — i.e. the partition no longer receives inserts — the `Simple` and `StochasticSimple` merge selectors: - consider all part ranges in that partition for merging, bypassing the base heuristic that otherwise refuses "unbalanced" merges of a large part with small ones, and - skip the right-tail heuristic that removes small parts from the right side of a candidate range. Each merge still respects `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool`, so a partition larger than that limit converges to a few max-size parts. Unlike `min_age_to_force_merge_seconds` with `min_age_to_force_merge_on_partition_only`, the partition does not have to fit into a single merge, and unlike plain `min_age_to_force_merge_seconds`, actively written partitions are unaffected. The default is `0` (disabled), preserving existing behavior. Merged parts start with age 0, which re-arms the threshold, so compaction of an idle partition proceeds in naturally throttled rounds. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added the `min_partition_age_to_force_merge_seconds` `MergeTree` setting: when every part in a partition is at least this old, the `Simple` and `StochasticSimple` merge selectors compact the partition's parts (including its tail of small parts) within the `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool` limit. ### Documentation entry: - [x] Documentation is generated from the setting description in `MergeTreeSettings.cpp`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Report an HTTP handler config error as itself, not a listen failure
signals.text: Report an HTTP handler config error as itself, not a listen failure Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114883 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): An invalid `<http_handlers>` configuration is now reported with its own error instead of being wrapped into `NETWORK_ERROR "Listen [host]:port failed"`. Previously, when `listen_try` was in effect, the error was only logged as a warning about `<listen_host>` and the server started without serving HTTP at all. The same applies to the Prometheus listener on `prometheus.port`, to the Keeper control endpoints on `keeper_server.http_control`, and to `SYSTEM START LISTEN HTTP` in `clickhouse-local`, which blamed `listen_host` and `http_port`. ### Description `Server::createServers` built the HTTP and HTTPS handler factory tree inside the `createServer` callback, whose only error handler is about listen addresses. So a handler-configuration error surfaced as ``` Code: 210. DB::Exception: Listen [0.0.0.0]:8123 failed: Code: 318. DB::Exception: Unknown handler type 'x' in config here: http_handlers.rule.handler.type. (INVALID_CONFIG_PARAMETER) (NETWORK_ERROR) ``` which points at the socket layer instead of the real cause. With `listen_try` it is not reported at all: it becomes a warning advising the operator to change `<listen_host>`, and the server starts without HTTP. `clickhouse-local` reaches the same two exits from `SYSTEM START LISTEN HTTP`, naming `listen_host` and `http_port` while both are correct. Handler construction is configuration validation and cannot fail for any socket reason, so I hoisted it above `createServer` at all four sites, behind a port guard matching `createServer`'s own early return, so a server without `http_port` still does not parse `<http_handlers>`. The custom-protocol block a few lines up already does this. `createServer.cpp` is untouched, so a genuine bind failure reports byte-identically before and after, for both `listen_try` values. Worth weighing: a server that today starts silently without HTTP on an invalid handler configuration will now refuse to start. I believe that is the safer direction, but it is a behaviour change. On a runtime reload the update is abandoned with the error reported to the caller, while the process and unrelated listeners keep running; with `listen_try` the reload used to complete and leave the listener silently gone. Every other listener reading a handler section wrapped its factory the same way and is hoisted behind the same guard: the Prometheus listener on `prometheus.port`, and the Keeper control endpoints on `keeper_server.http_control`, in `clickhouse-keeper` and embedded in `clickhouse-server`. That is the whole family. <details> <summary>Test coverage</summary> One integration case per exit of the error handler (plain, and `listen_try`), one for the HTTPS listener, two for the standalone Prometheus listener, one locking each port guard, two for the runtime reload path (HTTP and Prometheus), plus stateless tests covering `clickhouse-local` and `clickhouse-keeper`. Each case reddens if its own half of the fix is reverted. The HTTPS listener has its own textual copy of the construction, so it needs its own case: it configures `https_port` with `http_port` removed, which leaves HTTPS the only reader of `<http_handlers>`. Verified by mutation, restoring the pre-change shape for HTTPS alone reddens that case and no other. The unconfigured-port cases are deliberately not both-directions arms (they pass before the change too, because the parse already sat behind the same condition); deleting a guard makes the matching case fail, verified for the Prometheus one by rebuilding with the guard removed, which refuses startup instead. The reload cases assert on the error returned to the `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG` caller. `updateServers` reuses `createServers`, so it re-enters the hoisted code; before the change the reload returned success while HTTP, or the Prometheus handler change, was silently dropped. The Prometheus one first requires its listener to be serving, so it cannot pass against a build that never started it. A genuine bind failure on an occupied port, and a valid handler configuration, are the negative controls: both behave identically before and after, in both `listen_try` settings, so the new assertions discriminate the diagnosis rather than merely detecting a refusal to start. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115548&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115548](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115548+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix uncompressed Keeper snapshots being written as empty files
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115388 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed Keeper snapshots being written as empty files when `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format` is disabled. The server logged `Created persistent snapshot` but the snapshot file was 0 bytes, and the node then refused to start with `CORRUPTED_DATA`. Closes #115388. ### Description With `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format=false`, every snapshot written to a local disk came out as a 0-byte file, and the node could not restart afterwards. The reported recovery is to delete the snapshot, which ClickHouse's own message calls data loss. Root cause: `KeeperSnapshotManager::writeSnapshotFile` wraps the snapshot file buffer in a `CompressedWriteBuffer` **by reference** on the non-zstd branch, while the zstd branch moves ownership into the compression decorator. `CompressedWriteBuffer` deliberately does not finalize the buffer it writes into, and it declares no `sync()`, so `finalize()` only moved the compressed blocks into the file buffer's 1 MiB memory buffer and `sync()` never reached the file descriptor. `writer.reset()` then destroyed a non-finalized `WriteBufferFromFile`, whose destructor only closes the fd. Snapshots under 1 MiB compressed came out empty; larger ones were truncated to a multiple of the buffer size. The by-reference wrap was correct when introduced, because `~WriteBufferFromFile()` called `finalize()` at the time. That destructor finalize was later removed as a general policy change, which turned this call site into a data-losing one without touching it. `f1ab91191041d8f` is present in all active release branches. The fix finalizes and syncs the file buffer on the non-zstd branch, which is what the two sibling write paths in this file already do. The other three snapshot write paths were checked and are correct as written. The on-disk format is unchanged, verified rather than assumed: the bytes the fixed path produces are md5-identical to those written through `serializeSnapshotToBuffer` plus `serializeSnapshotBufferToDisk`, so existing snapshots stay readable. Tests: two `TEST_P`s in `gtest_coordination_snapshot.cpp`, each covering both compression settings - one round trip through the fixed path, one asserting a failed fsync is surfaced and the partial files cleaned - and an integration test that forces a snapshot and restarts the node. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115553&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115553](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115553+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1802` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Retry a job image pull that failed DNS resolution
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113611 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113611 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Retry the praktika job's Docker image pull when the registry proxy's name fails to resolve, so a transient DNS failure no longer kills the whole job before any test runs. ### Description The retried job image pull added in #113611 declines to retry a DNS resolution failure, so the job aborts with zero tests run. From a failing job's log: ``` Run command: [timeout --verbose 300 docker pull clickhouse/stateless-test:...] failed to copy: ... dial tcp: lookup dockerhub-proxy.dockerhub-proxy-zone on 127.0.0.53:53: server misbehaving Retry 1/3: command failed, exit code: 1 No retryable errors found, stopping retries ERROR: command failed after 1/3 attempt(s), exit code: 1 ``` **Root cause.** `_IMAGE_PULL_RETRY_ERRORS` allowlists transport-class phrases. Go's resolver renders a SERVFAIL as `server misbehaving`, absent from that list, so a transient DNS blip takes the `break` path meant for permanent errors and the pull's non-fatal failure falls through to the implicit `docker run` pull, which has no retry wrapper. **The change** adds that one phrase: a nameserver was reached and answered badly, so the same name can resolve on a later attempt. `no such host` is deliberately not added: that is NXDOMAIN, i.e. permanent, so a misnamed image host would burn all three attempts instead of failing fast, and it has 0 occurrences in 90 days. A broader substring (`dial tcp`, `lookup `) was rejected for the same reason, since both prefix NXDOMAIN too. A new arm pins that the NXDOMAIN line is still not retried. **Breadth.** 4 jobs across 4 pull requests in 30 days, 0 on master, each carrying this phrase in the pull's own stderr. Each produced 0 test rows while sibling jobs on the same commit produced 55 to 950, so a whole check is lost, not one test. **Validation.** The suite drives the real `Shell.run` loop, so its arms exercise the production matcher. Without the fix the new arms report 1 attempt instead of 3; with it, 25 passed, identical over 30 runs. No related open issue found. <details> <summary>New test arms and their controls</summary> The new arm feeds the verbatim production line rather than a bare phrase, because there the phrase is the tail of a nested resolver error inside a URL. It carries its own negative control: the same line matched against the allowlist with the entry removed must stop after one attempt. Without that control the arm could not distinguish this entry working from some other entry already matching, which is what the pre-fix job disproved by stopping after attempt 1. Note also that the two errors in the log above differ, which is why the gap looks covered: the retried attempt got `server misbehaving`, the later `docker run` got the allowlisted `connection refused`, by which point no retry wrapper is in play. Only the second reaches the CI database, so the pull's own error appears only in the job log. | Arm | Pre-fix | Post-fix | |---|---|---| | `test_each_transport_phrase_is_retried[server misbehaving]` | 1 attempt (red) | 3 attempts | | `test_the_production_dns_failure_is_retried` | 1 attempt (red) | 3 attempts, `on_retry` reports the phrase | | its in-arm control (entry removed) | 1 attempt | 1 attempt | | `test_the_permanent_resolver_failure_is_not_retried` (`no such host`) | 1 attempt | 1 attempt | | `test_permanent_error_is_not_retried`, `test_named_permanent_errors_are_not_retried` | green | green | Deleting the entry reddens exactly the 2 arms that pin it and no others; widening it to `dial tcp` reddens the NXDOMAIN arm, so that arm is load-bearing rather than decorative. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115555&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115555](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115555+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: format PromQL instant-vector timestamps once per block
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **PromQL instant-vector responses reuse the formatted evaluation timestamp within each result block.** ## What changed - Format the instant-vector timestamp once per result block. - Reuse the serialized timestamp for every returned series in that block. - Keep label and value serialization unchanged. - Keep empty blocks from accessing row zero. ## Why this is safe - Instant-vector finalization requires the start and end times to be equal. - The generated query uses `<start_time> AS timestamp`, so every row has the same timestamp. - The cached text lives only for one result block. - Multi-block responses still format each block independently. - Empty results keep the existing behavior. This removes repeated `getInt()` calls and decimal-to-text formatting from the per-series loop. It is most useful for high-cardinality `/api/v1/query` responses. ## Benchmark Local Release build with `max_threads=1` and `max_block_size=1000000`. The benchmark used a persistent HTTP connection, 2 warmup requests, and 5 measured requests. The response had 500,000 series and was about 39 MB. The same fixture and build were used for both versions, with only the response serializer object changed. | | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Median endpoint time | 1.13 s | 0.96 s | This is about **15% faster** for the high-cardinality response. Smaller result sets are dominated by query setup and JSON/label output, so the difference is much smaller there. ## Tests - Existing `test_multiple_instant_vectors` covers the same timestamp across multiple result series. - Existing `test_multiblock_instant_vector_json` covers instant responses split into multiple blocks. - Release build of the changed translation unit passed. - Patched endpoint returned valid JSON for 61,439 series, all with timestamp `1000`. - Run `git diff --check`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115567&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115567](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115567+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Take the Cascades planning node count from the plan, not the ambient context
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115545 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113422 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115398 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the node count the Cascades optimizer plans for when `distributed_plan_workers_num` and `distributed_plan_execute_locally` are set inside a subquery's `SETTINGS` clause. The count was re-read from the ambient query context, which for a separately-planned subquery holds the outer query's values, so the subquery was planned for the configured worker cluster instead of the requested number of workers, and on a server with no worker cluster a valid query was rejected with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`. Closes #115545. ### Description A scalar subquery gets its own `QueryPlanOptimizationSettings`, but `CascadesOptimizer::buildContext` resolved the node count through `getCascadesPlanningNodeCount(getQueryContextOrThrow())`, the query-level context, i.e. the outer query's. It read both settings from there, while two lines below taking `distributed_plan_execute_locally` from `optimization_settings`. Measured on `90a20ccf81cd348`: with a worker cluster configured, a subquery asking for 4 workers under an outer query asking for 8 was planned for 8 (wrong parallelism, silent). With no cluster the count resolved to 0 and a valid query was refused with `Code 344 SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, while the same settings applied to the whole query answered correctly. Every setting involved is experimental and off by default, so this needs an unusual but supported configuration. Same defect class as #113422 (merged), at a consumer it did not touch, and the fix extends that seam. `QueryPlanOptimizationSettings` gains the missing `distributed_plan_workers_num` field, and `getCascadesPlanningNodeCount` takes both settings as parameters, keeping `context` only for the server-level worker configuration, which cannot differ per subquery. The Cloud discovery lease in `TaskToHostMap` gets the same value, otherwise the planner would use the subquery's count while the lease still leased the outer one. That branch is Cloud-only and untested here. The new test asserts the resolved node count via `system.text_log`. It fails on master and passes with the fix; reverting only the argument at the call site reddens it again while the top-level control arm stays green. The `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` half needs a server with no worker cluster, which stateless CI never provides, so it rests on the counted arms over the same reads. Also noticed, not fixed here: `sort_settings` and the statistics hint in the same function are read from the ambient context too. Neither has a measured consequence, and both are separate root causes, so I am not raising them. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115571&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115571](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115571+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Assert the socket timeout exception instead of wall-clock time in test_secure_socket
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112938 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `test_secure_socket` guarded each of its three timeout arms with `assert end - start < 10`. That bound measures host load, not the behaviour under test, so it fails on a loaded CI host even when the timeout is honoured. It failed at 35.47 s here: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112938&sha=81483c13ee7fed39a69f62b13e5a98827ae7357a&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_asan_ubsan%2C%20db%20disk%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%204%2F6%29 Root cause is a whole-host scheduling stall, not a timeout defect: unrelated periodic tasks and another pytest worker froze over the same window. CIDB over 90 days: 4 failures, 0 on master. The three literals are replaced by an assertion on the `SOCKET_TIMEOUT` exception each arm must produce, which is what the test means: `receive_timeout=5` is honoured instead of the query hanging on the remote's `sleep_in_send_data_ms = 1000000`. Each arm also asserts the socket description its own code path formats, so an ignored `async_socket_for_remote` or `use_hedged_requests` cannot collapse two arms. Arm 1 had none before. Two `assert error.find("DB::ReadBufferFromPocoSocket::nextImpl()") == -1` guards go too: vacuous since `89205d78a688793` moved `nextImpl()` to `ReadBufferFromPocoSocketBase`, so `find()` returned -1 always. The per-arm assertions cover their intent. `send_timeout` drops from 5 to 4 so the asserted `5000 ms` is attributable: at 5 both settings render the same value, so a regression reading the send timeout on the read path stayed green. It goes below `receive_timeout` rather than to its default because a blocking secure read waits `max(receive_timeout, send_timeout)`, so raising it left the assertion unchanged while elapsed time went to 9.10 s at 9 and 300.11 s at the default. Hang detection is unchanged (`pytest.ini` sets `timeout = 900`). Latency tightness is given up: the asserted `5000 ms` is the configured value the message prints, not the elapsed time. signals.title: Docs: Bring the insert deduplication guide up to date
signals.text: The guide `Deduplicating inserts on retries` no longer matched the code. It presented `insert_deduplicate` as the query-level switch and named `insert_select_deduplicate` for `INSERT ... SELECT`. Both are superseded. `deduplicate_insert` is the main switch and defaults to `enable` since 26.2, `deduplicate_insert_select` governs `INSERT ... SELECT`, and `insert_select_deduplicate` is obsolete. The guide also said nothing about asynchronous inserts, although they are deduplicated by default since 26.2. Changes to `docs/concepts/features/operations/insert/deduplicating-inserts-on-retries.mdx`: - New `Settings that control insert deduplication` section. It separates the table-level requirement (a deduplication log) from the query-level one, and lists `deduplicate_insert`, `deduplicate_insert_select`, `insert_deduplication_token`, and `deduplicate_blocks_in_dependent_materialized_views` with their current defaults. - New `Precedence` subsection and a `Legacy and obsolete settings` table, plus a note on how the `compatibility` setting affects the 26.2 defaults. - New `Deduplication for INSERT ... SELECT` section. It defines when a `SELECT` is stable and documents the four values of `deduplicate_insert_select`. - New `Deduplication for asynchronous inserts` section. It covers the per-user-query deduplication granularity, the `DuplicatedAsyncInserts` and `SelfDuplicatedAsyncInserts` events, and the materialized view restriction. - Corrected the statement that non-replicated tables deduplicate by default. `non_replicated_deduplication_window` is `0`. - Corrected the materialized view section. `deduplicate_blocks_in_dependent_materialized_views` is enabled by default since 26.2. Changes to `docs/snippets/_async_inserts.mdx`: the snippet still claimed that deduplication is disabled for asynchronous inserts and must not be enabled with dependent materialized views. That restriction was removed by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/89140. English content only. The locale trees are generated. signals.title: Map kv tokenizer minimal
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110757 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110454 Adds a `keyValuePairs` text-index tokenizer for `Map(String, String)` columns. Every `(key, value)` pair of a row becomes one token, so `WHERE m['key'] = 'value'` is answered by a single exact token lookup with direct read, instead of reading the map column. An index on `mapKeys(m)` or `mapValues(m)` cannot do this: it knows that some key exists and that some value exists, but not that they belong to the same pair. This is a minimal first increment of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110757 by @UnamedRus, split up as discussed in the review of that pull request. Only the tokenizer and `m['key'] = 'value'` are here; `m['key'] IN (...)`, `mapContainsKey`, `mapContainsValue`, the `LIKE` and prefix/suffix forms, and the new `mapContainsKeyValue` / `mapContainsKeyValueLike` functions are left for follow-ups. As a result nothing outside the tokenizer, the index aggregator and the index condition needs to change: `TextIndexAnalyzer`, `MergeTreeReaderTextIndex` and `optimizeDirectReadFromTextIndex` are untouched. The token layout is `varint((length(key) << 1) | is_rest) ‖ key ‖ value`. The length prefix keeps the key/value boundary unambiguous, so keys and values may contain arbitrary bytes, and it makes the tokens of one key a contiguous range of the sorted dictionary, which a later range scan can use. `is_rest` marks a key's non-first occurrence in a row, so the lookup matches the same occurrence as `m['key']` when a row contains duplicate keys. Restrictions, all rejected at table creation: keys and values must be `String` or `LowCardinality(String)` (`FixedString` would store padding bytes that a searched constant does not have, silently missing rows), and `preprocessor`, `postprocessor` and `support_phrase_search` are not accepted. `m['key'] = ''` is also true for rows that do not contain the key at all, so that predicate falls back to a scan. This doesn't close issue #110454, because it asks for Map text-index support broadly and this only covers exact element equality. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): New text index tokenizer `keyValuePairs`, which indexes a `Map(String, String)` column directly and answers `map['key'] = 'value'` from the index without reading the map column. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115579&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115579](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115579+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not delete staged Iceberg files when a catalog commit outcome is unknown
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed data loss on catalog-backed Iceberg tables when a write's catalog commit was accepted but its response was lost: the staged files of what had become the table's current snapshot were deleted, leaving the table unreadable. The catalog step now confirms the outcome first, and one it cannot establish is reported as `UNKNOWN_STATUS_OF_TRANSACTION` with the files kept. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112081 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115390 **What breaks.** A catalog-backed Iceberg write stages `v<N>.metadata.json`, then points the catalog at it. A commit the catalog had **accepted** but whose response was lost read as "the commit did not happen", so the caller deleted the staged files of what was by then the current snapshot. This is the catalog half of the family #112081 names; #115390 fixes the storage one. **Root cause.** `RestCatalog::updateMetadata` returned `false` for any `HTTPException`, and `GlueCatalog::updateMetadata` threw one error code for any AWS failure. `false` means "another writer won, retry", and all three destructive call sites clean up on it, so a third outcome, "cannot tell", had nowhere to go. **The change.** Each outcome is classified where the information exists. The REST commit POST becomes single-attempt, because a re-POST is refused by the requirement the first attempt satisfied, making every status ambiguous. A 409 is then a proven lost race; a non-retryable status, and any failure raised before the request reached the wire, keep their error and their cleanup; anything else reconciles against the `main` ref. Glue reconciles every failed outcome, since its client retries `UpdateTable` with no per-request pin; it reads the raw `metadata_location`, as the derived one matches the staged file. Only an unresolved outcome becomes `UNKNOWN_STATUS_OF_TRANSACTION`, which the cleanup handlers skip. An orphaned file is recoverable; a deleted snapshot is not. **Validation and scope.** Twelve REST and six Glue integration arms cover the insert, delete and compaction commit paths, asserting on object existence and readability; 30 of 30 repeated runs pass. Reverting the reconciliation, single-attempt pin, pre-dispatch guard, 409 branch, non-retryable branch or a cleanup guard each reddens a named arm. `updateSchema` and `EXPIRE SNAPSHOTS` are out of scope, as neither deletes staged files on failure; `DeltaLakeSink` commits through a Delta transaction, not this interface. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115580&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115580](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115580+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Explain why `url` rejects a pattern that `s3` accepts
signals.text: `s3('https://clickhouse-public-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/wikistat/original/pageviews-20200101-{0..10000}{0..10000}00.gz', LineAsString)` works, while the very same pattern passed to `url` fails with ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Table function 'remote': first argument generates too many result addresses. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` which names a table function the user did not call, does not say how many addresses were generated, does not say what the limit is, and does not say which setting controls it. The behaviour itself is not a bug. Object storage compiles a pattern into a regular expression and matches it against the bucket listing, so an enormous key space costs nothing. HTTP has no listing at all, so for `url` a pattern is a *generator* of addresses rather than a *filter* over the files that exist, and every generated address is materialized before the query starts - a direct product of two ranges of ten thousand elements cannot be served. What was wrong is that nothing in the error said so. The message now reports the table function that was actually called, the number of addresses the pattern generates, the limit, the setting that raises it, and - for `url` - why `s3` accepts the same pattern: ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Table function 'url': first argument generates too many result addresses: 10001, while at most 1000 are allowed (see the 'glob_expansion_max_elements' setting). Note that 'url' has to read every address generated by the pattern, because HTTP provides no way to list the existing files. Use 's3' (or another object storage table function) if the pattern is meant to be matched against the list of existing objects instead. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` `remote` keeps its own setting name (`table_function_remote_max_addresses`) and does not get the object storage hint. The Cartesian product check is also made overflow-safe, and the documentation of `url` gained a section describing the difference from the object storage table functions. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/49234 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When a glob pattern in the `url` table function expands to more addresses than allowed, the error message now names the `url` table function instead of `remote`, reports how many addresses the pattern generates and what the limit is, names the `glob_expansion_max_elements` setting that controls it, and explains that unlike `s3`, `url` cannot match a pattern against a listing. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115581&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115581](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115581+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Pin the ORC corrupt-stripe-footer test blob to valid hexadecimal
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114924 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04856_orc_corrupt_stripe_footer` builds its fixture with `unhex('<blob>')`, and the blob contained one non-hex character: a `\0` escape that the SQL parser turns into a NUL byte landing on the first half of a hex pair. `unhex`'s result for a non-hex character is [documented as implementation-defined](https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/functions/encoding-functions#unhex), so that byte is whatever the current decoder produces - `0xF0` today. It is what truncates the stripe footer. Any legal change to hex decoding moves it, the footer stops being corrupt, ORC parses it cleanly, and both expected error lines disappear while the well-formed control arm keeps passing. The test then silently asserts nothing about the abort that #114924 fixed. On #91993 (optimised hex decode) it fails 57/57 runs with randomized settings and 58/58 without: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=91993&sha=2b0b6ff04a0320e586cea3455a4b9a1d08a5327e&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29 The first commit replaces that escape with the valid digit `f`, which yields the same nibble from a valid character: `unhex(old) = unhex(new)`, so the ORC reader receives a byte-identical 289-byte input and `.reference` is unchanged. Every decoder agrees on all 22 valid hex characters, so the fixture no longer depends on implementation-defined behaviour. Coverage is exactly preserved; no setting is disabled and no tag is added. Because both revisions decode identically, the ORC assertion cannot tell them apart on today's decoder, so a second commit adds a shell guard requiring the literal to be even-length `[0-9a-f]`. Without it, reverting the one-character fix would leave the test green. The guard runs before any side effect and exits non-zero with a message on stderr. Validated by varying only that byte on one binary: `0xF0` (the fix) and `0xFF` both produce the two expected error lines, `0x00` reproduces the CI diff exactly. 50/50 runs pass with and without randomized settings. `02477_single_value_data_string_regression.sql` has the same fragility and is deliberately left alone, since #91993 already rewrites it as an explicit byte literal. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115583&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115583](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115583+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1788` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Bound each statement of the stateful data preparation
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109745 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Found triaging #115351, whose [`Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115351&sha=7a37de207136a2f10132b2a0835447f151dde5a3&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29) burned its full 9000 s budget with no test result at all. No related open issue. **What breaks.** `prepare_stateful_data` occasionally wedges on one `clickhouse-client` statement, then sits silent until praktika's watchdog kills the job: `clickhouse-test` never starts, CIDB gets only a job-level `error` row with an empty `test_name`, and the server logs are lost, since a killed job never reaches `COLLECT_LOGS`. Five occurrences in 60 days, all `amd_tsan`. **Root cause.** The prep script runs as one unbounded `Shell.run`. Under `set -e` plus an ERR trap a statement that *fails* is named and aborts the step, but one that never returns is no error at all: nothing fires, and `Shell.run` blocks in `proc.wait()` until the watchdog. **The change.** Each prep statement is prefixed with `timeout --verbose --signal=TERM --kill-after=60 N`. A bound reached exits 124 (137 after the kill), which `set -e` and the *existing* trap turn into a line naming the statement, and the job fails fast so log collection preserves the server logs. `N` is derived from the job budget (35 %, so 3150 s). Per statement rather than one wrapper: against a client ignoring SIGTERM, `--kill-after` delivers an uncatchable SIGKILL, and only a per-statement bound leaves the trap alive to name it. `Shell.run(timeout=)` fails likewise, SIGTERMing the process group with no exit code and no stderr. Both contrasts are asserted in `ci/tests/test_stateful_prep_bounded.py`, as is the local-run path. This does not fix the hang, whose cause is unknown; it produces the evidence to find it. Complementary to #109745, which skips most of this block on `--no-stateful` jobs: that decides whether statements run, this bounds each that does, and the flaky check is not such a job. `terminate()`'s log flush is unbounded too, but no CIDB row in 90 days implicates it. <details> <summary>Sizing of the bound, and validation</summary> 3150 s is 3.1x the worst prep wall-clock observed over 30 healthy job logs across 7 flavours (1010 s; worst `amd_tsan` 671 s) and above the script's own 1800 s `max_execution_time`, so it cannot pre-empt a legitimate INSERT. The five recorded hangs were each silent for 8414 s or more, so the two populations do not overlap. Both limits are read from the production configs and asserted for all 61 jobs that run `functional_tests.py`, so a retuned budget cannot silently push the bound under a legitimate INSERT or past the room log collection needs. | check | result | |---|---| | `ci/tests/test_stateful_prep_bounded.py` | 14/14 pass | | full `ci/tests/` suite | 825 pass, 2 pre-existing failures (`test_max_failures_exit_code.py`, identical on unmodified master) | | `ruff check` repo-wide | clean | | rendered script, s3 x non-s3 x bound x unbound | `bash -n` clean, 24 bounded statements each | | statement order and content vs master | byte-identical after stripping the prefix | | mutation arms | 14, each reddens its own assertion | Both directions, end to end with a stub client that hangs on one statement: ``` without the bound: still running past the observation cap, stateful_setup_error = None with the bound: returns in 3.0s, stateful_setup_error names the statement: timeout: sending signal TERM to command 'clickhouse-client' prepare_stateful_data: command [$PREP_TIMEOUT clickhouse-client --query "RENAME TABLE datasets.hits_v1 TO test.hits"] at line 40 failed with exit 124 ``` A TERM-ignoring statement gives exit 137 and is still named; `Shell.run(timeout=)` gives neither line. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115585&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115585](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115585+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix lost text index optimization for queries with ORDER BY ... LIMIT
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/issues/68580 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/93545 A query that filters on a text index and also has `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` could stop using the index to answer the filter, and read and tokenize the whole text column instead: ```sql SELECT count() FROM (SELECT id, v FROM t WHERE hasToken(s, 'error') ORDER BY v DESC, id LIMIT 10) ``` The two optimizations did not compose: the one that speeds up `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` reshaped the plan in a way the text index optimization no longer recognized, and it silently fell back to reading the column. Nothing indicated this in the query plan or the logs, and the results stayed correct, but the query got much slower and used much more memory. On a full-text search benchmark over ~30M rows the affected queries took ~300 ms and ~500 MB instead of ~30 ms and ~15 MB. Whether a query was affected depended on the order of the columns in `SELECT`, which made it look arbitrary: `SELECT v, id ... ORDER BY v` was fine while `SELECT id, v ... ORDER BY v` was not. All the settings involved are enabled by default. Both optimizations now apply together. A `TRACE` log entry was also added for the remaining cases where the text index optimization cannot be used, so a silent fallback is visible in the logs. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression where a query combining a text index filter with `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` stopped answering the filter from the index and read the whole text column instead. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115586&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115586](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115586+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Docs: Generate dictionary source pages from embedded documentation
signals.text: Moves the complete content of the 14 existing dictionary-source reference pages into the `Documentation.description` registered by each source. signals.title: Do not treat the CFI build as a sanitizer build in the test harnesses
signals.text:
### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: #115122 Two test harnesses decide whether a build is a sanitizer build by testing `CXX_FLAGS LIKE '%-fsanitize=%'`. The `amd_cfi` profile adds `-fsanitize=cfi-vcall,cfi-derived-cast` (`CMakeLists.txt:527`), so the substring matches even though `-DSANITIZE=` is empty: - `tests/config/install.sh:227` installs `config.d/trace_log_no_symbolize.xml`, so `TraceLog.cpp:298-299` inserts a zero-length array into `symbols` and `lines`, failing the two `03150_trace_log_*` tests. - `tests/integration/helpers/cluster.py:5152` `is_built_with_sanitizer()` makes 50 no-argument call sites across 35 integration test files skip themselves, `test_trace_log_build_id` saying "trace_log is disabled with sanitizers", which is not true under CFI. Both now test `-DSANITIZER`, which `cmake/sanitize.cmake:30` puts into `SAN_FLAGS` and which reaches `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` in all 5 branches of `if (SANITIZE)` and nowhere else. The named `address` / `thread` / `memory` checks keep testing `-fsanitize=`. **The reporter's open question is answered, and negatively: official release builds are not affected.** `amd_cfi` and `amd_release` differ by exactly one flag (`-DENABLE_CFI=1` versus `-DBUILD_STANDALONE_KEEPER=1`), so ThinLTO with split-debug and stripping is already the shipped configuration. Validated on the exact binary from the failing job (build ID `e3992b92...`): with the override present both `03150_*` tests fail; with the patched script both pass. That binary is now classified as not sanitized while a real ASan binary still is, the regression risk this PR's ASan/TSan/MSan lanes cover. No existing check can show the `03150_*` tests green: `WeeklyCFI` on master runs only build, integration and stress (`ci/workflows/weekly_cfi.py:30-34`), and the stateless `amd_cfi` lane arrives with #115036, still open. Since both consumers react by skipping work, a revert would stay green, so `ci/tests/test_cfi_not_a_sanitizer_build.py` pins both predicates against the measured `CXX_FLAGS` of nine profiles, running the installer's own function with a stub `clickhouse`. It runs on every PR, and both predicate files are now `CI Tests` digest inputs so a later edit cannot reuse a cached pass. #113107 edits the same block, so whichever lands second may need a rebase. [CI report.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=30c47a7d9420ba1e86365979016e7765cbc080da&name_0=WeeklyCFI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_cfi%2C%20parallel%29)
Other users of an -fsanitize string test, left unchanged (click to expand) I checked every in-tree consumer of the same "is this a sanitizer build" idea and changed the two that are reachable under CFI and change test outcomes: | consumer | reachable under CFI? | why left alone | |---|---|---| | `install.sh:92` `is_fast_build` | no | its only call site needs `FAST_TEST=1`, whose only producer builds with `-DENABLE_THINLTO=0` and no CFI, and CFI without ThinLTO is a cmake `FATAL_ERROR` | | `tests/clickhouse-test:5135` `collect_build_flags` | yes | already correct: it maps sanitizer names, so CFI yields no flag and `SANITIZED` stays false. It must keep the name map to emit per-sanitizer `no-asan`/`no-tsan` tags, which a boolean marker cannot express | | `tests/docker_scripts/upgrade_runner.sh:171` | no | there is no `amd_cfi` upgrade job | | `tests/integration/test_userspace_page_cache/test.py:31` | yes | its own local probe, run before the cluster starts so it cannot use the helper. The consequence is one extra container under CFI, not a wrong result | | `ci/jobs/scripts/functional_tests/setup_log_cluster.sh:102` | yes | the value is only echoed, never read again anywhere in the tree - a dead diagnostic | `Stress test (amd_cfi)` also runs `install.sh` on master, so that predicate is exercised there, but that suite asserts nothing about symbolized `trace_log`. Each remaining one is a separate question with no observed consequence today, so widening this PR to them would be unmeasured churn.
