signal.title: Display named Tuple columns in Pretty formats as subcolumns
signal.text: ### Changelog category: - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Named Tuple columns in `Pretty` formats are now displayed split into subcolumns, with the names of the elements in additional header (and footer) lines. Controlled by the new setting `output_format_pretty_named_tuples_as_subcolumns` (enabled by default). A named tuple rendered inside a single cell (e.g. nested in an `Array`, or when the new setting is disabled) is still displayed according to `output_format_pretty_named_tuples_as_json`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/65388 Example: ``` SELECT 'hello' AS x, (1, 'world')::Tuple(a UInt8, b String) AS t ┏━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━┓ ┃ x ┃ t ┃ ┃ ┣━━━┳━━━━━━━┫ ┃ ┃ a ┃ b ┃ ┡━━━━━━━╇━━━╇━━━━━━━┩ 1. │ hello │ 1 │ world │ └───────┴───┴───────┘ ``` It works for all three styles (`Pretty`, `PrettyCompact`, `PrettySpace`), arbitrary nesting depth, and is mirrored in the footer: ``` SET output_format_pretty_display_footer_column_names = 1, output_format_pretty_display_footer_column_names_min_rows = 0; SELECT 'hello' AS x, (1, 'world')::Tuple(a UInt8, b String) AS t FORMAT PrettyCompact ┌─x─────┬─t─────────┐ ├───────┼─a─┬─b─────┤ 1. │ hello │ 1 │ world │ ├───────┼─a─┴─b─────┤ └─x─────┴─t─────────┘ ``` The implementation recursively flattens named Tuple columns into their elements before rendering, so all the existing width, row, and separator machinery works on the flattened columns unchanged; the hierarchy is kept as a small list of groups plus per-boundary junction levels, from which the extra header and footer lines are derived. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=78927&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/78927](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F78927+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed
signal.text: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)` on #110479 @ `038667a9c024` reported a single failing leaf `Server died` while its own aggregate said `Failed: 0, Passed: 3872`. The server did not die: no `<Fatal>` line, no sanitizer report, empty `dmesg`, clean shutdown. The `--hung-check` liveness probe failed and the run was aborted. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110479&sha=038667a9c024695126415fe5f37b76f7a06662fa&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29 Root cause: `tests/clickhouse-test` collapses every in-band abort cause into `STOP_TESTING_EXIT_CODE = 2`, and the job side appends `Server died` for that code unconditionally. Master already carved two causes out of code 2 for this reason; this is the third. This adds `HUNG_CHECK_EXIT_CODE = 5` and `FailureReason.LIVENESS_CHECK_FAILED`, with the leaf `Server liveness check failed` at status FAIL. All four sites that conclude `SERVER_DIED` from a failed probe are changed; the site concluding it from a `<Fatal>` line is untouched, and its neighbour becomes an `elif` of it so fatal evidence is never downgraded. The stop cause travels through one locked first-writer-wins carrier, replacing a `global_time_limit_reached` flag. The leaf names the observation, not a diagnosis: `check_server_liveness` also fails on a non-200 *response*. It is a NEW CIDB `test_name`. The aggregate stays FAIL, so bugfix validation still counts a hang as a repro. Not claimed: a remaining `Server died` row still does not prove a death. Code 2 is generic, and a worker seeing a `<Fatal>` line reaches the parent through `stop_tests()`, exiting 143 - correct there, but decided outside the carrier. Validation: +50 tests asserting the process exit code end to end - the same command exits 2 on master and 5 here. Each changed site has a mutation arm reddening a named case. `ci/tests`: 705 passed, 655 on master. Successor to #112952, not an extension: that PR deliberately excludes exit code 2. Both touch the same region of `functional_tests_results.py`, so the second to merge needs a rebase. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1807` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Do not schedule Build profile diff when the profiled build is unaffected
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Requested by @ thevar1able in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163#issuecomment-5318430318: `Build profile diff` ran on changes involving no builds. His PR changes only `utils/exclude-authors.txt`, yet the job ran, found no profile data for the head and posted nothing. `digest_config` answers two questions: which changed files affect a job, and may its result be reused. `4e62df6112628621` gave this job a focused digest; `e64133b542327753` removed it to stop a cache hit skipping the job, whose output is a comment about one concrete commit. That also made the job always affected, and `only_docs` in `filter_job.py` compensated for docs-only diffs only. This splits the two. `Job.Config` gains `enable_cache` (default True, and in `drop_fields`, so no existing job's digest changes), honoured at both cache seams. The job gets its focused digest back plus `enable_cache=False`: the digest decides whether to run it, the flag keeps every selected run running. Whether the build can produce data for this head arrives through `requires=["Build (arm_release)"]`, covering the build's sources, submodules, docker image and packaging. `only_docs` and its gate are deleted. Side effect: no longer always affected, the job stops rescuing `Build (arm_release)`, so that build is skipped on build-free diffs too. Those two jobs are the whole newly-skipped set, and this already happens on the `only_docs` path today. `Generate LLVM Coverage Diff Report`, asked about in the same comment, has no such hole: it is a `Result` inside `llvm_coverage_job.py`, already gated on build affectedness. One pre-existing limitation is widened, not fixed: a skip and a cache hit look identical to the runner, so the comment writer does not run on a skip and the comment can outlive the head it describes. That already holds for docs-only PRs. Verified: `ci/tests/` passes, `praktika yaml` produces no diff, every job's config digest is byte-identical, and each new assertion reddens under a mutation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115221&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115221](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115221+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1806` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Add batched key hashing to HashMethodHashed
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/80414 Joins whose keys map to `HashJoin::Type::hashed` (composite or mixed-type keys, where the SipHash128 digest of the key columns is the hash map key) hashed every row with one virtual `updateHashWithValue` call per key column per row. The key getter now takes the rows selected at construction and precomputes their keys in one batch. `Set` gets the same batching automatically, since composite `IN` uses the same key getter. The idea originally implemented in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/80414 by @taiyang-li. Here extended to take `parallel_hash` join algorithm. Results from `hashjoin_composite_keys.xml`: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve performance of hash joins with composite or mixed-type keys and of composite `IN` with mixed-type tuples by batching the computation of the key hashes. --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112294&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112294](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112294+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signal.title: Wake idle streaming exchange sinks and sources on backward stop
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114806 When a `LIMIT` in a distributed plan is satisfied, the stop signal travels backward through the exchanges. It stalled at idle stages: a `StreamingExchangeSink` with an empty input waited only on its input port and did not read `NoMoreDataNeeded` from the socket, and a `StreamingExchangeSource` on a silent socket did not notice that its output port was closed, so it did not forward the stop upstream. Stages that no longer produce anything kept reading and computing until the query timed out. Now both wake while idle: each sink and source waits on a small epoll that holds the socket and a wakeup pipe written by `onUpdatePorts`. The sink asks for socket writability only while it has unsent bytes, so an idle socket does not cause a busy loop. The wire protocol is unchanged. Local in-memory exchanges have the same gap and are not covered here. In the new test the unfixed server hits `max_execution_time = 25` although the result is ready after ~2 s; fixed, the query ends in ~3 s and all worker tasks finish cleanly. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Distributed query plans (`make_distributed_plan`) now stop idle upstream stages promptly after a satisfied `LIMIT`: an idle exchange sink reads `NoMoreDataNeeded` as soon as it arrives, and an idle exchange source notices its closed output and forwards the stop upstream. Previously such stages kept reading and computing data that nobody consumes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115690&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115690](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115690+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: The `_database` and `_table` virtual columns of a `Merge` table carry the matched child's name again
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113735 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/84139 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/63665 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/102471 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107418 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113242 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `WHERE _table = ...` or `WHERE _database = ...` filter over a `Merge` table silently returning no rows when the matched child reads through another table, for example a `Distributed`, a nested `Merge`, or a `Buffer` child. The `_database` and `_table` virtual columns of a `Merge` table now always carry the name of the matched child, as they did before 25.7, not the name of the table the child delegates its read to. ### Description `ReadFromMerge::getSelectedTables` prunes the children of a `Merge` table by evaluating a filter on `_database`/`_table` against each child's own name, but the values in the rows were stamped by whatever storage eventually read them - for a `Distributed` child, the remote table on the shards. The two sides contradicted each other, and every query where both fire silently returned wrong results: a filter naming the child returned no rows (pruning kept the child, but no row carried its name), and a filter naming the remote table returned rows only at processing stages where the pruning happened not to fire. ```sql CREATE TABLE t_leaf (s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY s; CREATE TABLE t_dist AS t_leaf ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_leaf); CREATE TABLE m (s String) ENGINE = Merge(currentDatabase(), '^t_dist$'); SELECT count() FROM m WHERE _table = 't_dist'; -- 0 on master, all rows with this fix ``` **History.** Before #63665 (25.7), the `Merge` engine substituted the child's own name for `_table`/`_database` itself (`WITH '<child>' AS _table` per child), so the values and the pruning agreed. #63665 gave every table its own `_table` virtual column, which disabled that gated substitution: the reader deep down stamps the name, and for a delegating child that is a different table. #102471 then removed the dead substitution machinery, and #107418 pinned the new values with a regression test - while the pruning kept matching child names all along. **The fix** makes the `Merge` engine produce these columns itself again, unconditionally: references to them are replaced with a constant carrying the child's name right in the child query tree (so expressions computed on the shards see it too; the analyzer path pins the action name via `__actionName`, the old interpreter path uses the `WITH` substitution), and at `FetchColumns` the constant columns are added to the child plan, inserted at the positions the columns have in the requested header, because a child whose execution names differ from the common header (a `Distributed` child) is matched by position in `convertAndFilterSourceStream`. **This is a deliberate semantic choice, and the alternative is #113735.** Only one of the two semantics can be consistent with pruning: the pruning can only ever match the child's name, since the `Merge` table cannot know which table a child delegates to without classifying every child. #113735 keeps the underlying-table values and therefore has to prove, per storage class and recursively through `Buffer`/`Alias`/proxy wrappers, whether a child stamps its own name - with a fail-closed carve-out for streaming engines. Under child-name semantics all of that machinery is unnecessary, streaming children keep being pruned exactly as before, and the docs' claim that "the `_table` column acts as an index" is actually true. The cost: `_table` through `Merge` over `Distributed` reads `t_dist`, not `t_leaf`; each nesting level of `Merge` reports its own child. Tests `00717` (whose leaf-name expectations were rewritten in #63665 itself), `03094`, `04338`, `04367`, `03031`, `01902`, `03988`, `04104` and `01155` are updated accordingly; the new test `05019_merge_virtual_columns_delegating_children` covers the pruning and the values over `Distributed`, nested `Merge` and `Buffer` children, with both analyzers. This also unblocks #113242, whose only functional CI failure was `00717_merge_and_distributed` newly reaching the pruning defect at `FetchColumns`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115356&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115356](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115356+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add memory-pressure-adaptive read sizing to the experimental ReaderExecutor
signal.text: Brings the `MemoryPressureMonitor` from the ReaderExecutor redesign to master as a self-contained, experimental slice (gated by the existing experimental `ReaderExecutor`). A global monitor classifies server-total and per-query memory pressure into four levels using a snap-up / cooldown-down state machine. The executor samples the level once per read window and shrinks its window and block size under pressure, floored at 128 KiB. Thresholds are three experimental server settings, validated and applied on startup and on `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG`. Prefetch-aware sizing is deferred to the later prefetch/scheduler slice. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `ReaderExecutor` now shrinks its read window under memory pressure, configurable via `reader_executor_memory_pressure_level_{1,2,3}_pct`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115635&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115635](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115635+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Infer a physically nullable Parquet struct as Nullable(Tuple)
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112427 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results when reading a Parquet file with a nullable struct column without an explicit schema. Schema inference pushed the nullability down to the tuple elements and returned `Tuple(Nullable(...), ...)`, which cannot hold a struct-level NULL, so a NULL struct was read as a tuple of NULLs. Such a column is now inferred as `Nullable(Tuple(...))` when `allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type` is enabled. That setting was also added to the Parquet schema inference cache key, so a schema cached under one of its values is no longer reused under the other. ### Description Reading a Parquet `optional group` (a nullable struct) without a schema returned wrong data: ```sql DESCRIBE file('np.parquet', Parquet); -- p Tuple(`1` Nullable(Float64), `2` Nullable(Float64)) SELECT * FROM file('np.parquet', Parquet); -- (1,2) -- (NULL,NULL) <- the file holds NULL here ``` **Root cause.** `SchemaConverter::processSubtreeTuple` already reads such a group correctly, but only with a `Nullable` type hint. Without a hint each leaf takes its own def-level nullability and the assembled type is a bare `Tuple` of `Nullable` elements. Writing and hinted reading were already correct; `ORC`, `Arrow` and `Native` infer `Nullable(Tuple(...))` from the same data. **The change.** Inference now names `Nullable(Tuple(...))` for an `OPTIONAL` group with an all-`REQUIRED`, non-array subtree. Only the type is named: the read-time null-map machinery stays hint-only, because the inferred type reaches the read as its type hint and the existing hinted path re-derives that state itself. Inference mode is selected by `sample_block == nullptr`, the converter's own mode invariant, rather than by a missing node type hint, which in read mode a `JSON` hint on a struct also produces. Gated on `allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type`, matching `ArrowColumnToCHColumn` so inference cannot return a type `CREATE TABLE` rejects, and on `schema_inference_make_columns_nullable`. `allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type` defaults to `false`, so inferred types at default settings are unchanged and no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry is needed. Every other group shape keeps a plain `Tuple`; the table lists them with the reason. Nested-optional and optional-leaf groups are rejected with a hint today too, so those remain a separate pre-existing limitation. <details> <summary>Invariant carriers, all measured</summary> | Carrier | Before | After | |---|---|---| | top-level `optional group`, all-required subtree | `Tuple(Nullable,...)` -> `(NULL,NULL)` | `Nullable(Tuple(...))` -> `\N` | | named elements | same defect | fixed | | `Array` element struct | `Array(Tuple(...))` -> `[(1,2),(NULL,NULL)]` | `Array(Nullable(Tuple))` -> `[(1,2),NULL]` | | `Map` value struct | `Map(String, Tuple(...))` | `Map(String, Nullable(Tuple))` | | `Map` `key_value` tuple | plain Tuple | unchanged (`DataTypeMap` requires `Tuple(keys, values)`) | | `Map` key that is an `optional` group | plain Tuple | unchanged (`DataTypeMap` rejects a `Nullable` key) | | `optional` group whose only child is a childless group | plain Tuple | unchanged (no leaf carries the null map) | | `JSON` hint over a struct with a nested `optional` group | reads the struct | unchanged | | nested optional group | plain Tuple | unchanged (rejected with a hint too) | | optional leaf under an optional group | plain Tuple | unchanged (same) | | `REQUIRED` group | `Tuple(...)` | unchanged | | GeoParquet geometry column (a WKB binary leaf, resolved by the geo path) | `Point` | unchanged | | `schema_inference_make_columns_nullable = 0` | `Tuple(Float64, Float64)` | unchanged | | `allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type = 0` | `Tuple(Nullable,...)` | unchanged | | tuple element subcolumn read | leaf read | unchanged | | hinted read, all elements missing | `TYPE_MISMATCH` | unchanged | | optional group, all children skipped as unsupported | silently skipped, `Tuple()` | unchanged | | schema cache key | 2 entries for 4 setting combinations | keyed on the setting | </details> `04065_tuple_inside_nullable_parquet_roundtrip.reference` pinned the buggy `(NULL,NULL)` output as a limitation; signal.title: Rename refresh dependencies when restoring under a new name
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115645 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `RESTORE ... AS <new name>` leaving the `REFRESH ... DEPENDS ON` list of a refreshable materialized view pointing at the original database. The restored view refreshed in response to a table it no longer read, ignored refreshes of its own parent, and stopped refreshing entirely once the original database was dropped. ### Description `RESTORE DATABASE db AS db_restored` rewrote every table reference in a stored refreshable materialized view definition except the `REFRESH ... DEPENDS ON` list: ``` CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW db_restored.child REFRESH AFTER 1 SECOND DEPENDS ON db.parent ... AS SELECT a FROM db_restored.parent ^^ TO/FROM rewritten, DEPENDS ON not ``` `DDLRenamingVisitor::visit` dispatches on `ASTCreateQuery`, `ASTTableExpression`, `ASTFunction`, `ASTDictionary` and `ASTStorage`; `ASTRefreshStrategy` was missing, so the node was walked but never touched. The refresh scheduler keys its dependency graph on the full table name, so a dependency naming the pre-restore database occupies a different graph slot than the restored parent. Measured: refreshing the *source* parent fired the restored child, three consecutive refreshes of its *own* parent did not, and dropping the source database left the restored view at `MissingDependencies`. The fix adds the missing visit, running the renaming map over the dependency list exactly as the existing `create.targets` loop does. `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` already visits this node to qualify the same list at CREATE time, so this is the renaming counterpart of an established pass. The visitor is the only transform applied at all four sites that rewrite a stored definition, so this covers backup-side and restore-side renaming together, and the corrected definition is what gets persisted, so later `ATTACH`es are right with no separate fixup. A dependency pointing outside the restored set is left alone, and so is one whose table is not itself renamed by a `RESTORE TABLE ... AS`; the test pins both as controls. Backups already written are not affected: the defect was in the rename transform, not the backup, so restoring an existing backup with a fixed server gives the correct dependency (verified against a backup taken by an unfixed binary). No settings or formats change; a definition without `DEPENDS ON` is untouched. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115689&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115689](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115689+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Prune the unasked-for right keys of a multi-disjunct join under the old analyzer too
signal.text: Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115465, which stopped a join with several disjuncts (`... ON a = b OR c = d`) from adding right key columns the query does not ask for. That pruning was gated on `enableAnalyzer()`, out of caution about a path I had not measured, so on the legacy planner every right key is still added. `TableJoin::requiredRightKeys` works on both paths: the planner fills `columns_added_by_join` through `setUsedColumns`, and `TreeRewriter::collectJoinedColumns` fills it through `addJoinedColumn`. So the gate can go. It matters beyond the columns themselves: the key-only join hash tables of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115301 are chosen for `LEFT SEMI` only when the join produces no right value at all, so with `enable_analyzer = 0` a query like `SELECT count() FROM l SEMI LEFT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k OR l.s = r.s` would stay on the mapped tables while the same query on the analyzer gets the key-only ones. With this change it gets them on both. Checked against a build of the parent commit, all with `enable_analyzer = 0`: - seven `OR` join shapes - `ALL`/`SEMI`/`ANTI`, `LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FULL`, with and without a right key or a payload column selected - return the same results as with the analyzer; - `05023_join_several_disjuncts_right_keys` passes; - the `join` tests have the same six reference mismatches as the parent commit, all of them tests that read differently on the legacy planner (`00826_cross_to_inner_join`, `01115_join_with_dictionary`, `02220_array_join_format`, `02784_parallel_replicas_automatic_decision_join`, `04653_distributed_plan_auto_rewrite_in_to_join`, `04670_any_join_take_last_row_no_swap`). signal.title: Fix stale MATERIALIZED column values read through a chain while a mutation is pending
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100613 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50237 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99281 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103182 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115371 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115372 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115638 **Scope changed.** The staging half of this pull request — recomputing a chain of `MATERIALIZED` columns one dependency level at a time during a mutation — landed on master in the meantime via #103182, which also generalizes it to `APPLY PATCHES`, so all of it was dropped here. What remains is the read path, which master still gets wrong: the read set is closed in `AlterConversions`, and `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` keeps a single line of change, resolving `MATERIALIZED` defaults against the whole table instead of the read task's columns. The two defects that belong to the staging path are split out into #115371 and #115372. ## Problem With a mutation still pending, reading a `MATERIALIZED` column that reaches the updated column only through another `MATERIALIZED` column returns the stale on-disk value, while reading the whole chain returns the recomputed one: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x Int32, y Int32, m1 Int32 MATERIALIZED x + 1, m2 Int32 MATERIALIZED m1 + 1, m3 Int32 MATERIALIZED m2 + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t (x, y) VALUES (10, 0); SYSTEM STOP MERGES t; SET alter_sync = 0, mutations_sync = 0, apply_mutations_on_fly = 1; ALTER TABLE t UPDATE x = 20 WHERE 1; -- stays pending ``` ``` SELECT m2 FROM t; -- 12 (stale; must be 22) SELECT m3 FROM t; -- 13 (stale; must be 23) SELECT x, m1, m2, m3 FROM t; -- 20 21 22 23 (correct) ``` - The result of a query depends on which columns it selects, so the same value read two ways disagrees. - The same happens for a `MATERIALIZED` column defined over a subcolumn (`m1 MATERIALIZED t.a + 1` with a pending `UPDATE t = ...`): `SELECT m1` returns the stale value unless the query happens to select `t` as well. - Selecting a `MATERIALIZED` column together with a column the mutation updates fails outright with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` whenever the first one's dependencies are not in the select list, even when that column has nothing to do with the mutation. - Once the mutation finishes, the values are correct — only the pending window is affected. ## Root cause Reading with `apply_mutations_on_fly` builds the pending commands into the read pipeline. `AlterConversions::addColumnsRequiredForMaterialized` decides which extra columns must be read so that the `MATERIALIZED` columns being selected can be recomputed, and it only looked one hop deep: ```cpp for (const auto & column_name : read_columns_set) if (default is MATERIALIZED) for (const auto & dependency : TreeRewriter(context).analyze(expression, source_columns)->requiredSourceColumns()) if (all_updated_columns.contains(dependency)) required_source_columns.insert(dependency); ``` For `m2 MATERIALIZED m1 + 1` the only dependency is `m1`, which is not in `all_updated_columns`, so nothing is added, `filterMutationCommands` drops the `UPDATE x` command as irrelevant to the read set, and `m2` is returned from disk. Two further details of the same analysis: - the default expression is not normalized with `replaceSubcolumnsToGetSubcolumnFunctionInQuery`, so `m MATERIALIZED t.a` is seen to depend on `t.a` rather than on `t`, and a pending `UPDATE t` is filtered out (or the analysis fails with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` when the subcolumn does not resolve against `source_columns`); - a `MATERIALIZED` column whose expression reads an `EPHEMERAL` column can never be recomputed outside `INSERT`, so analysing it against physical columns must be avoided rather than attempted. ## Solution Two sites, because the read set has two consumers that must agree. ### `AlterConversions::addColumnsRequiredForMaterialized` — close the read set 1. **Transitive closure.** A breadth-first walk seeded with the read columns replaces the single pass, so the `MATERIALIZED` columns in between are read too and the interpreter recomputes the whole chain instead of `filterMutationCommands` dropping the `UPDATE` as irrelevant. 2. **Only a column that is recalculated pulls in dependencies, and it pulls in all of them.** The walk asks of the column it visits whether the interpreter recalculates it, and if so takes its whole expression, because the stage that rewrites it evaluates that expression against the block — including the part reading a column no mutation touches (`c MATERIALIZED m1 + y`, where `y` is untouched). A column that keeps its stored value contributes nothing, so a chain whose value cannot change is not read. 3. **Subcolumn rewrite.** Dependencies are analysed after `replaceSubcolumnsToGetSubcolumnFunctionInQuery`, matching what `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` does before analysing the same expression. Without it `m MATERIALIZED t.a + 1` is seen to depend on `t.a` while `all_updated_columns` holds `t`; the names do not match and a pending `UPDATE t` is filtered out. This is a one-hop defect, independent of the chain. 4. **`EPHEMERAL` columns added to the analysis source list.** `getAllPhysical` excludes them, so analysing `me MATERIALIZED x + e` threw `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` inside this function. Measured on master, `SELECT me` with any pending `UPDATE` fails this way. Also a one-hop defect, and analysing every hop of a chain would have multiplied its reach. 5. **The `EPHEMERAL` test mirrors the interpreter's policy, and keeps a pass of its own.** `MutationsInterpreter` never recomputes a `MATERIALIZED` column that reads an `EPHEMERAL` one, so such a column is not treated as recalculable here either — the read set must not promise a recomputation the interpreter refuses. It cannot share the loop that looks for a changed dependency: that loop stops at the first one it finds, while this test quantifies over all of them, so interleaving them skips it exactly when a dependency is updated. 6. **Memoised lookups.** `getMutationSteps` runs per read task per part, so each default expression is analysed at most once per call and each reachability question answered at most once. ### `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` — resolve defaults against the whole table `available_columns` was serving two different roles: which `MATERIALIZED` columns need recalculating, and which columns their expressions may be resolved against. For a plain `UPDATE` the two coincide. A table carrying a `MATERIALIZED` column the mutation does not affect breaks the coincidence — its dependencies are legitimately outside the read set — and the analysis failed with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, taking the query with it: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x Int32, y Int32, m Int32 MATERIALIZED x + 1, n Int32 MATERIALIZED y + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); ALTER TABLE t UPDATE x = 20 WHERE 1; -- stays pending SELECT m, n FROM t; -- Missing columns: 'y' while processing: 'y + 1' SELECT x, n FROM t; -- the same, and this one fails on master too ``` Deciding whether a column has to be recalculated must not require reading what it reads, so the default expressions are now resolved against every column of the table. Only an on-fly read has a narrow list: a materialising mutation passes `getNamesOfPhysical()`, so the only columns this adds there are virtual ones, which a `MATERIALIZED` default cannot reference — `CREATE` and `ALTER` both reject that. The list is built on first use. Copying it costs a node per column of the table, the loop needs it only for a `MATERIALIZED` column the task reads, and an on-fly read reaches it per part. Widening `need_materialized_analysis` instead would have been wrong: `validateUpdateColumns` runs at the end of the same block, so guarding the block would drop the check that rejects an `ALTER UPDATE` of a key or `MATERIALIZED` column on every table without `MATERIALIZED` columns. ### Taken from #115638 @Avogar tried an alternative on top of this branch in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115638 and asked for it to be moved here. It is in as of `4bec5ca8a1a`, applied verbatim — the test files this branch already carried are byte-identical in it, and `Settings::apply_on_fly_for_read` is kept. What it adds over the two sites above: - **`MaterializedColumnDependencies`** — the dependency graph over a table's `MATERIALIZED` columns, built once and shared by the read path and `MutationsInterpreter` instead of being derived separately in each, so the two can no longer disagree about how a dependency is spelled. This is also the graph @Avogar needs in #112717. - **The closure and the command filter now run to a fixed point.** `filterMutationCommands` puts the columns a surviving command reads into the read set, and one of those can itself be a `MATERIALIZED` column of a chain (`DELETE WHERE m2 > 100`), which can in turn keep an older command alive. Closing and filtering used to run once each, in that order, so a chain reached from a `DELETE` predicate or an `UPDATE` expression stayed stale. They now iterate until the set stops growing; it only grows and is bounded by the width of the table, so it terminates. - **A command may name a subcolumn as written (`t.a`)** while the read set is keyed on storage columns, which made every read of the table fail with `NO_SUCH_COLUMN_IN_TABLE`. Names now go through `getNameInStorage` on the way in. This one reproduces on master. - **One `buildMutationChainForRead`** shared by `getMutationSteps` and `getMutationActions`, instead of each recomputing the read set and the command filter. ### A `MATERIALIZED` column over an `ALIAS` column Also fixed here, in `aeda9610380`, because after the extraction there is exactly one place to do it. A `MATERIALIZED` default may read an `ALIAS` column, and that made **every** mutation on the table throw, including one updating a column the expression never mentions: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x Int32, z Int32, a Int32 ALIAS x + 100, m Int32 MATERIALIZED a + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); ALTER TABLE t UPDATE z = 5 WHERE 1; -- Code: 47. Missing columns: 'a' while processing: 'a + 1' ... (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) ``` The list the default is analysed against is the physical one and an `ALIAS` is physical-excluded. Merely adding aliases to it would let `TreeRewriter` resolve the name, but the expression would then still read `a` at execution time and no part has such a column, so the recompute stage would fail on it instead. The reference is replaced by the expression it stands for, with `ReplaceAliasByExpressionMatcher` — the same visitor `IndexDescription::initExpressionInfo` uses so a skip index can reference an `ALIAS` column. `MaterializedColumnDependencies` hands the same expression to the dependency analysis and to the recompute stage, so one expansion reaches both; it runs before the subcolumn rewrite, so a subcolumn reached through an alias is normalised too. Unlike the `EPHEMERAL` case next to it there is no trade-off: `m` recalculates correctly from the stored `x`, and an `ALIAS` column is recomputed per query so it can never itself be stale. ### Not proposed for backport The change started as a narrow read-path fix, but with the dependency graph extracted into a new component shared by two subsystems it is no longer a good backport candidate, and it is not labelled for one. ### Coverage Regression test `04869_materialized_chain_on_fly_read` covers six cases, each measured individually against master `5bd006cd298`: - the plain chain read tail-only — returns the stale value; - the chain read next to the updated column, without the intermediate hop — throws `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, because the surviving command makes the interpreter analyse a default whose dependency is not in the read set; - one command assigning two columns, with the query reading the other assignment target — throws for the same reason, after the command is narrowed and loses the assignment the chain depends on; - a pending `DELETE` that keeps a command alive while the set of updated columns stays empty — returns the stale value, since the analysis is skipped entirely; - columns the mutation does not affect, read on their own and next to the updated column, and a recalculated column reading an untouched one — stale value or `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` depending on the select list; - the subcolumn default and the `EPHEMERAL`-derived column — stale value and `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` respectively. `04926_on_fly_mutation_read_set_closure` covers the cases the read-set closure loop repairs: the chain reached from a pending `DELETE` predicate, a subcolumn spelled as written in a command, and the cases that must not move. `05024_materialized_over_alias_column_mutation` covers the `ALIAS` case, measured both ways on a Debug build: without the expansion `UPDATE z = 5` and `UPDATE x = 20` both throw `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`; with it the first leaves `m` alone and the second gives `x, a, m = 20, 120, 121`, on the settled part and on the on-fly read alike. `05023_materialized_ephemeral_stale_warning` is unchanged and still passes. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed reading a table while a mutation is in progress: a `MATERIALIZED` column could return a stale value, and selecting one together with an updated column could fail with an error. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114561&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114561](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114561+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Refactor columns deserialization to avoid all assumeMutable calls, simplify the substreams cache, and remove rows_offset
signal.text: PR #109105 replaced `assumeMutable` with `IColumn::mutate` in the some pars of the deserialization code. When a column is shared via the substreams cache, `IColumn::mutate` clones the whole accumulated column, giving O(rows × granules) cost and a 3–4× deserialization slowdown. Rework the deserialize path so it never clones: - `deserializeBinaryBulkWithMultipleStreams` and its helpers take `IColumn &` instead of `ColumnPtr &`. - The substreams cache never shares a `ColumnPtr`; consumers copy the current range out via `insertRangeFrom`. - `assumeMutable`/`IColumn::mutate`/`const_cast` are removed from the deserialize paths; mutable children come from non-const accessors. - Cache-shared members are dropped from the `Deserialize*State` structs. - The MergeTree reader stack reads into `MutableColumns`. Additionally, remove `rows_offset` from the deserialization API. `rows_offset` (the number of leading rows to skip while deserializing a range) is provably always `0` for every caller, so it is dropped from `deserializeBinaryBulkWithMultipleStreams`, `deserializeBinaryBulk` and all their helpers. This deletes the read-side skip machinery: - the skip loops / `istr.ignore(size * rows_offset)` seeks; - the `Map` bucketed reorder-with-skipped-rows path (which also removes a latent substreams-cache over-count on bucketed `Map`); - the `Object` shared-data `granules_offsets` / `last_incomplete_granule_offset` cursors (the load-bearing `StructureGranule` continuous-read state is kept); - the `SerializationArrayOffsets` helper (`rows_offset`-only); - assorted dead offset arithmetic. <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. signal.title: Add MergeTree settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed`
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063 Adds three new `MergeTree`-level settings that limit the total size of a table, for multi-tenant, temporary, and demo services: - `max_table_size_rows` — the maximum total number of rows in active data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_compressed` — the maximum total size on disk across all active and inactive data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` — the same for uncompressed bytes. The limits are checked against the current table size at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed to the working set; on exceeding a limit, the query fails with the new `TABLE_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` error. Inserts done by materialized views (including refreshable ones) and async insert flushes are checked as well, since they go through the same sinks and part commits. Data parts that have been already accepted into the working set by a concurrent operation (parts in the `PreActive` state, which are not active yet) are counted as well, so a batch of parts committed in a single transaction — for example by `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` — cannot overshoot the limits, and neither can an insert running concurrently with another one on the same replica. An operation that replaces the parts it covers with a not larger part never increases the size of the table, so it is always allowed even when the table already exceeds a limit. This makes it possible to get a table back under the limit with a merge, a row-removing mutation, or a lightweight delete, and not only by dropping whole parts. A mutation that increases the size of a table which is over the limit is rejected and will be repeated without finishing, which is intended. The check is skipped on replicated fetches and on the execution of replication log entries that add data already accepted by another replica (`ATTACH_PART`, `REPLACE_RANGE`), which permits a race condition when parallel inserts into multiple replicas overdraft the limit. Committing empty data parts is always allowed, so the data can be removed from a table that exceeds the limits, e.g. with `TRUNCATE` or `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`. The limit on the number of rows is counted only for active data parts, while the limits on the number of bytes are counted across all active and inactive data parts, because their purpose is to limit disk usage (inactive parts are removed in the background, so the observed size can decrease over time). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `MergeTree` settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, and `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` that limit the total size of a table. The limits are checked at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed (including the results of background merges and mutations), but not on replicated fetches. This closes [#115063](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115069&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115069](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115069+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Positional Tuple hint over Parquet: tupleElement rewrite yields default values
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('x.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)')` returns zeros/empty strings instead of the file's values once the tuple-element rewrite is enabled for `StorageFile`. `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matches 0 rows instead of 1. With `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the same query throws `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN: Column t.1 was not found in parquet schema`.** - **Root cause:** For an unnamed `DataTypeTuple` the element name produced by `getSubcolumnForElement` is the ordinal (`"1"`, `"2"`), so `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement` builds the subcolumn name `t.1`. Its guards check the DECLARED structure only (`canOptimizeToSubcolumn` queries the storage snapshot built from the structure argument), which of course contains `t.1`. Nothing checks whether the format resolves that element by name or by position — and Parquet resolves the tuple type positionally (`SchemaConverter.cpp:723-731`) but the flattened subcolumn name by string. The PR's opt-in comment 'a tuple element is a real leaf in the file, so the format can serve `t.x` on its own' is false for a positional tuple hint. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `getTypedNodesForOptimization` (FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:858) now admits `StorageFile` via `storageAllowsTransformer` -> `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` (StorageFile.h:132) -> `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement` (FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:428) replaces the function with a `ColumnNode` named `t.1` -> the Parquet reader resolves that flattened name by string lookup (`SchemaConverter.cpp:232`, `sample_block->findPositionByName(node.name, ...)`) against the file's real field names `t.x`/`t.y` -> no match -> synthetic missing column filled with defaults. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Analyzer/Passes/FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:428`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Analyzer/Passes/FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp#L428) — builds `t.<element>` subcolumn name; new guards do not check `hasExplicitNames` - [`src/Storages/StorageFile.h:132`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/StorageFile.h#L132) — `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` returns true unconditionally - [`src/Storages/StorageURL.h:374`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/StorageURL.h#L374) — same opt-in for `url()` - [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.h:106`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.h#L106) — same opt-in for `s3()`/`azure()` - [`src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/SchemaConverter.cpp:232`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/SchemaConverter.cpp#L232) — flattened subcolumn name resolved by string lookup, never positionally **Impact:** Silent wrong results for any `file()`/`s3()`/`url()` Parquet read that declares a positional (unnamed) `Tuple` in the structure argument — a documented, supported way to read a struct written by an external writer (Spark, pandas, Arrow) without repeating its field names. Affects both the v3 and the legacy Parquet reader. With `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query is rejected instead. ORC is not affected. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `5c9f28ed5a2c5`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/43170dc7-eed8-4aac-9ac4-ab16ab01d90b) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that a positional (unnamed) Tuple structure hint still returns the file's values. SET enable_analyzer = 1; SET optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 1; INSERT INTO FUNCTION file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(x UInt64, y String)') SELECT tuple(number, toString(number)) FROM numbers(3) SETTINGS engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; SELECT tupleElement(t, 1), tupleElement(t, 2) FROM file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)') ORDER BY 1; SELECT count() FROM file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)') WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 0 0 1 1 2 2 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 0 0 0 0 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> In `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement`, refuse the rewrite when `!data_type_concrete.hasExplicitNames()` and the storage only opted in through `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` (the element name is an ordinal that no file schema carries). Alternatively make `SchemaConverter` resolve an ordinal-named subcolumn positionally when the parent tuple hint is unnamed, matching what it already does for the whole tuple. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same declared-vs-physical name mismatch may exist for other formats reached through `StorageFile`/`StorageObjectStorage` that resolve subcolumns by name; only Parquet, ORC, CSV and JSONEachRow were probed here (CSV and JSONEachRow behave identically with and without the rewrite). Found during automated review of [PR #113383](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113383). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr113383_001` </details> cc @groeneai @alexey-milovidov (from #113383)

signal.title: Fix reading a tuple element through a positional Tuple structure hint
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 Reading a tuple element through a positional structure hint returned default values instead of the file's data. Over a Parquet file written as `t Tuple(x UInt64, y String)`: ```sql SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('p.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)'); -- returned 0, 0, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2 ``` `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matched no rows, and with `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query failed with `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN`. Silent wrong results, on default settings. Root cause: an unnamed tuple names its elements `1`, `2`, ..., so `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` rewrote `tupleElement(t, 1)` to the subcolumn `t.1`. The existing guards there consult the storage snapshot, which is built from the structure argument and does contain `t.1`. The Parquet reader then resolves a flattened element name by string against the file's real field names `t.x`, `t.y`, found no match, and substituted a missing column filled with defaults. The fix suppresses the rewrite when the element name is a bare ordinal and the source resolves subcolumn names against a file schema. Named hints keep their pushdown, and storages serving subcolumns from their own metadata (MergeTree and friends) are unaffected. This regressed in #113383 and is master-only: that merge is an ancestor of no release branch and is in no release tag, hence `Not for changelog`. That category also skips `Bugfix validation`, so the reddening check below is the evidence. Validated on a Debug build, with a regression arm added to `04706_tuple_subcolumn_pushdown_parquet`: - Reddening: removing only the new guard term makes the new arm fail while the pre-existing arms stay green. - Preservation: `t.x` pushdown survives for a named hint by name and by ordinal, and `t.1` still pushes down for MergeTree's unnamed tuple. - `04706`, `04707`, `04708`, `04873` pass; a `subcolumn`/`tuple_element`/`functions_to_subcolumns` sweep has no failure absent from an unmodified-master control; 50 randomized runs pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115000&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115000](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115000+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix logical error for IN with an identical non-constant tuple on both sides in the old analyzer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID 2508-3457: ```sql EXPLAIN PIPELINE graph = 0, graph = 0, compact = 1 SELECT 'null', (SELECT tuple(materialize(NULL), NULL) GLOBAL IN (materialize(NULL), NULL)) GROUP BY ALL SETTINGS transform_null_in = 1 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=38215c1758332de1ea8a4b5a620ba8364586f6c6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 It reaches the old interpreter through a scalar subquery, and reduces to `SELECT (materialize(1), 2) IN (materialize(1), 2) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0`. Release builds catch the exception but still reject the query with an empty identifier name: `Code: 47 ... Unknown identifier: ; there are columns: dummy, 1, materialize(1), 2, ...`. Root cause: a literal's `unique_column_name` is assigned lazily, only when `ActionsMatcher::visit(const ASTLiteral &)` runs, and `getNameAndTypeFromAST` requires it. The old interpreter's row-wise `IN` rewrite visits the left argument first, and here the right-hand `tuple` renders to the same column name as the left one, so `visit(right_argument, data)` takes the common-subexpression early return and never descends into the right-hand children. The loop that follows then asks for the name and type of each raw child, and a literal child is still unnamed. The fix visits each child before naming it. That call site was the only one of the eight `getNameAndTypeFromAST` callers in the file not already preceded by a `visit()` of the node it names. `visit` is idempotent, so the added call is a no-op when the child is already indexed. The abort is gone after the change, with the result now matching `enable_analyzer = 1` on 20 shapes (including `NULL` with `transform_null_in`, `nullIn`, `GLOBAL IN`, `LowCardinality`, array and tuple literal children, `indexHint`, and the query above). 13 shapes that already worked are unchanged, with byte-identical `EXPLAIN actions = 1` output. Removing the added line reinstates the abort. Introduced by #104993 and present only on master, so no backport is needed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993

signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87206 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103537 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112457 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `BAD_DATA_PART_NAME` ("Trying to get part name in new format for old format version") on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` created with the deprecated positional syntax under `allow_deprecated_syntax_for_merge_tree`. A mutation could be reported as done on a replica that had not applied it, and the table could stay readonly after a restart. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #112457 ([`Upgrade check (amd_release)` report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112457&sha=f888781eb610bfabdc8c8675d835b99482bec8a2&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29)). No related open issue found. A table created with `ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree(date, key, granularity)` uses date-based (V0) part names. `MergeTreePartInfo::getPartNameAndCheckFormat` cannot produce one, because the min/max dates it needs are not part of a `MergeTreePartInfo`, so it throws. Two `ActiveDataPartSet` entry points take only an info and regenerate the name that way; each had exactly one caller, and both callers already held the name and threw it away. This change passes the name at both call sites, as in `536b611c96a757e`, which fixed the `ATTACH PARTITION` instance of this bug. V0 name formatting is untouched, and current-format tables are unaffected because the name-taking overload re-parses to the same info and runs the same insertion code. The linked report contains both failures: - `ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue::getPartNamesToMutate` builds `mutation.parts_to_do`. The throw left it empty, so a mutation reported `is_done` on a replica that never mutated its part, and `mutations_sync = 2` returned success while that replica still served pre-mutation values. Regressed by #87206, which changed `produced_parts` to hold infos instead of names. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkPartsImpl` builds the set of empty unexpected parts. The throw aborted `ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread`, leaving the table readonly. Regressed by my own #103537, which replaced a name-based call with an info-based one. The V0 gap in `MergeTreeData::restorePartFromBackup` that the throw-site comment describes is a different code path, absent from both stacks, and is not addressed. A new stateless test asserts `parts_to_do` on the frozen replica: it fails on master (`parts to do 0`) and passes here (`parts to do 2`), and 50/50 randomized runs pass. `checkPartsImpl`'s state needs parts fabricated on disk, so that half is covered by three V0 cases added to `gtest_active_data_part_set.cpp`, all of which fail with this change reverted. `00062_replicated_merge_tree_alter_zookeeper_long` and `00652_replicated_mutations_zookeeper` still pass.

signal.title: Skip writing all-default columns during MergeTree INSERT
signal.text: ## Summary During MergeTree INSERT, columns whose values are entirely type-defaults (e.g., all zeros for `UInt64`, all empty strings for `String`, all `NULL`s for `Nullable`) are detected and excluded from the part's column list before constructing `MergedBlockOutputStream`. This avoids writing unnecessary `.bin` files (Wide parts) or data streams (Compact parts), saving disk space for sparse-update workloads where most columns in each INSERT are left at their type's default. The optimization is opt-in via the MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` (off by default). It additionally requires `serialization_info_version` to be set to `with_missing_columns` (the format version that records frozen defaults for missing columns), so that a cluster pinned to a lower version for compatibility never writes parts that older servers cannot read. The block itself is passed intact to the writer, so skip indices, projections, primary index, and min-max index are all computed from the full data. Reading a part that lacks a column fills it with type-defaults automatically — the same mechanism used by `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` on existing parts. To keep reads stable, a structured `missing_columns` array is recorded in the part's `serialization.json` (a new `WITH_MISSING_COLUMNS` serialization-info version). Each entry carries the column name and a `type_default` marker. On read, `fillMissingColumns` consults this marker and fills a missing column with its type-default even if the column later gains a new `DEFAULT` expression, so that a subsequent `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN ... DEFAULT` does not retroactively change the values that were actually inserted. The marker is propagated through merges, mutations, and on-the-fly `ALTER RENAME COLUMN`, so the inserted type-defaults survive part-lifecycle operations. The `MissingColumnInfo` struct also reserves a `DefaultKind::Expression` variant for future use (issue #92475: `ALTER MODIFY DEFAULT` freezes old expression into parts). This PR only writes `type_default` markers; reading an `expression` marker throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` to fail closed until Phase 2 implements expression evaluation. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/4968, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/92475 **On-disk format (`serialization.json`):** ```json { "missing_columns": [ { "name": "b", "default": "type_default" } ], "version": 2 } ``` **Changes:** - Add MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` (default `false`). - Add `IColumn::hasOnlyTypeDefaults` with optimized overrides for `ColumnVector`/`ColumnDecimal` (`memoryIsZero`), `ColumnString`/`ColumnArray` (zero offsets), `ColumnNullable` (all-`1` null map), `ColumnSparse` (no stored non-default values), and `ColumnTuple` (delegates to sub-columns). - Filter all-default columns in `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` (`skipEmptyColumnsOnInsert`). Columns with a `DEFAULT`/`MATERIALIZED`/`ALIAS` expression are never skipped. A column is skipped only when `IDataType::getDefault()` coincides with the column's zero representation (`isDefaultAt(0)` on a column filled via `getDefault()`), which correctly excludes types like `Date32` (type-default 1900-01-01 ≠ memory-zero) and `Enum` (first declared value ≠ 0). Patch parts are excluded, and at least one physical column is always kept. - Gate the optimization on `serialization_info_version >= with_missing_columns`. The populating step is authoritative about the part format version, so `SerializationInfoByName::getVersion` never silently upgrades a part past the configured value (which would make older servers reject it during a rolling upgrade). - Record the missing columns in `serialization.json` via `SerializationInfoByName` (new `WITH_MISSING_COLUMNS` version). Only `type_default` markers are written; `expression` markers are rejected on read until Phase 2. The list is written in sorted order so that identical parts produce identical checksums on different replicas. - Propagate the missing-columns marker through the part lifecycle: through merges (`MergeTask`, for columns that end up absent from the merged part), through mutations (`MutateTask::getColumnsForNewDataPart`, including renames of missing columns), through compact-part renames (`splitAndModifyMutationCommands`), and through on-the-fly `ALTER RENAME COLUMN` on read (`IMergeTreeReader::fillMissingColumns` translates the requested name back through `alter_conversions`). - Add a stateless test with 46 cases covering: basic skip; all-default keeps one column; merges (horizontal and vertical); mutation; `Nullable`; key columns; `DEFAULT` expression not skipped; `Array`; `Tuple`; `ColumnSparse` source; compact parts; `LowCardinality`; stable values across `ALTER ... DEFAULT`; a non-zero-default `Enum`; marker across mutation/merge/rename after `ALTER DEFAULT`; version gate; DETACH/ATTACH TABLE; DETACH/ATTACH PARTITION; BACKUP/RESTORE; FREEZE; CHECK TABLE; MATERIALIZE COLUMN; CLEAR COLUMN; lightweight DELETE; chained mutations; INSERT SELECT; REPLACE PARTITION; ATTACH PARTITION FROM; ALTER ADD/DROP COLUMN; projections; FixedString; Map; mixed parts merge; Date/DateTime; pre-ADD-COLUMN + skip merge; type-changing mutation; compact-part rename+mutation; Date32 regression. - Add an integration test (`test_skip_empty_columns`) with 6 cases: replicated consistency; merge marker propagation across replicas; mixed-version version gate; backward-compat fallback for old parts; restart durability; REPLACE PARTITION across replicated tables. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): MergeTree INSERT can now skip writing columns whose values are entirely type-defaults (zeros, empty strings, `NULL`s), saving disk space for sparse-update workloads. Enabled by the MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` together with `serialization_info_version = 'with_missing_columns'`. Missing columns carry frozen defaults in `serialization.json`, so a later `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN ... DEFAULT` does not retroactively change the inserted values. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is not required (bug fix, no new user-facing feature) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=98472&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/98472](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F98472+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Optimization of `GROUP BY` in the presence of `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT`
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimize `GROUP BY ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT` and `GROUP BY ... LIMIT` queries by maintaining a bounded heap during aggregation to prune groups that cannot appear in the result, significantly reducing memory usage and execution time for high-cardinality grouping. Controlled by the `enable_group_by_top_k_optimization` setting. Based on the initial implementation by [Dmitriy Terenichev](https://github.com/Dmitry909) ([#78553](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78553)). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/72610 Query shapes that benefit from this optimization: - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key ORDER BY key ASC LIMIT N` -- single key, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key LIMIT N` -- single key, no ORDER BY - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2, k3 ASC LIMIT N` -- 3+ keys, full match - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, ORDER BY is a prefix of GROUP BY - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 1 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 2 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 LIMIT N` -- composite keys, no ORDER BY - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL ORDER BY URL ASC LIMIT N` -- String keys - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL LIMIT N` -- String keys, no ORDER BY Not supported (optimization is skipped): - `ORDER BY agg()` (ORDER BY aggregate function, not a GROUP BY key) (handled by [another PR](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/98607)) - `WITH TOTALS`, `HAVING`, `GROUPING SETS`, `CUBE`, `ROLLUP` - `LIMIT WITH TIES` - ~~Non-final aggregation (distributed partial aggregation)~~ - `max_rows_to_group_by` is set - `rows_before_limit_at_least` mode (exact count) - a COLLATE on any of the matched GROUP BY keys (a COLLATE on a later ORDER BY column past the full key prefix cannot affect which groups qualify and does not disable the optimization) - ORDER BY columns that are not a leading prefix of GROUP BY keys <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96630&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96630](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96630+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: macOS binary signing: prod key via dedicated signing runner
signal.text: Cuts macOS cask signing over to the prod Apple Developer ID key. The sign job now runs on a dedicated `release-runner` pool and assumes `release_signing` in the security account (445567100269) to `kms:Sign`, instead of riding the shared `ec2_admin` cross-account grant on the PoC key. Plain `sts:assume-role`, no GitHub OIDC handshake, so the signing identity stays portable if CI ever moves off GitHub self-hosted. Depends on the pool + role (clickhouse-private) and the trust swap (security-integrations) landing first. Nothing signs with the prod key until those apply. signal.title: Not a fix: "Not-ready Set" exception when buildOrderedSetInplace fails
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107924 `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildOrderedSetInplace` (the speculative set build run during primary key analysis for `IN` subqueries) used to consume the subquery `source` plan up front. If the in-place build then failed silently (e.g. due to subquery timeout with `timeout_overflow_mode = 'break'`, where the executor stops without throwing and without setting `is_created`), the set remained permanently unbuilt and `FunctionIn` threw "Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument". The core fix — running the in-place pipeline against a clone of the source plan so that `DelayedCreatingSetsStep::makePlansForSets` can still build the set after a silent failure — has meanwhile been merged in #107924, which falls back to the original destructive build when the source plan contains a step that does not implement `IQueryPlanStep::clone`. After merging master, this PR carries the remaining hardening on top of #107924: - `clone` implementations for eleven more query-plan steps: `JoinStep`, `FillingStep`, `ExtractColumnsStep`, `FractionalLimitStep`, `FractionalOffsetStep`, `MergingAggregatedStep`, `NegativeLimitStep`, `NegativeLimitByStep`, `NegativeOffsetStep`, `StreamInQueryResultCacheStep`, `ReadFromQueryResultCacheStep`. `IN` subqueries whose plans contain these steps (e.g. `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL`, joins planned as `JoinStep`, subqueries going through the query result cache) previously took the destructive fallback, where a silent in-place failure still reproduces the "Not-ready Set" exception; with clone support they take the non-destructive path and recover. - `JoinStep::clone` covers only the join algorithms whose `IJoin` implementation supports cloning: `HashJoin`, `ConcurrentHashJoin`, `ConstantJoin` and `FullSortingMergeJoin`. `JoinSwitcher` (`join_algorithm = 'auto'`), `SpillingHashJoin`, `MergeJoin` / `PartialMergeJoin` and `GraceHashJoin` keep the pre-existing destructive fallback: `IJoin::isCloneSupported` also gates `optimizeJoin`, `convertOuterJoinToInnerJoin` and `QueryPipelineBuilder`, so widening it would silently enable join swapping and outer-to-inner conversion for never-validated stateful spilling algorithms. This limitation is documented at the throw site, and `04649_not_ready_set_with_non_clonable_join_algorithms` pins that those algorithms still produce correct results (the `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` stays internal). - `FilledJoinStep` (`StorageJoin` and dictionary joins) and `JoinStepLogicalLookup` (direct key-value joins) intentionally remain non-clonable as well: they wrap live storage-backed join state with no safe copy semantics (`IJoin::clone` constructs an empty join rather than copying the filled state). The constraint is documented at both classes. - Copying a `QueryResultCacheWriter` (which is what `StreamInQueryResultCacheStep::clone` does) now carries over both the original's `query_start_time` and its `skip_insert` decision. On the successful in-place build path the copy is the only writer that is ever finalized, so otherwise `query_cache_min_query_duration` would be measured from the clone point and an already cache-resident key would be buffered into a throwaway buffer instead of being skipped. Pinned by `04652_query_result_cache_subquery_clone_min_query_duration` and `04653_query_result_cache_subquery_clone_skip_insert`. - `QueryPlan::clone` now preserves `max_threads` and `concurrency_control`, so a pipeline built from a cloned plan runs under the same resource contract as the original instead of defaulting to `max_threads == 0` with concurrency control disabled. - The Planner no longer plants query result cache steps into a *logical* plan. A logical plan is not executed where it is built: it is serialized and shipped to another node (parallel replicas with `serialize_query_plan = 1`, see `createRemotePlanForParallelReplicas`), while `StreamInQueryResultCacheStep` and `ReadFromQueryResultCacheStep` hold node-local state (a `QueryResultCacheWriter`, or the cached chunks) that has no serialized representation. Before this, `query_cache_for_subqueries = 1` together with parallel replicas and `serialize_query_plan = 1` failed the whole query with `Method serialize is not implemented for StreamInQueryResultCache`. The cache is still populated and read by the plan the initiator executes itself. - Regression tests using the `prepared_sets_build_ordered_set_inplace_fail` failpoint: `04095_global_not_in_parallel_replicas` (the original parallel-replicas reproducer), `04492_not_ready_set_with_fill_subquery` (a `WITH FILL` subquery source plan), `04550_not_ready_set_with_join_subquery`, `04648_not_ready_set_with_query_result_cache_subquery` (both the cache write and the cache read path) and `04649_not_ready_set_with_non_clonable_join_algorithms`. The original failure was observed in the [Stress test (amd_tsan)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=d0432097aed783bd35054dce2edcefe0c4e5122c&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29) on master, where `considerEnablingParallelReplicas` triggers `selectRangesToRead`, which calls `buildOrderedSetInplace` for primary key analysis. Note on the changelog category: the "Not-ready Set" exception is a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, so reproducing it on the unfixed build aborts the server on the sanitizer builds that the per-arch Bugfix validation jobs run on, and the validation harness deliberately treats a mid-run server death as inconclusive rather than as a reproduced bug. Automated bugfix validation is therefore structurally impossible for this fix, and the user-visible bug fix for the common plan shapes already shipped with #107924; the remaining hardening here is classified as an Improvement. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Extend the non-destructive speculative in-place set build for `IN` subqueries (introduced in [#107924](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107924)) to more query-plan shapes: `clone` is implemented for eleven more query-plan steps, including clone-supported joins via `JoinStep`, `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL` via `FillingStep`, and the query result cache steps. Such subqueries now preserve the original source plan and can recover from a silent in-place build failure instead of throwing "Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument". A cloned query plan now preserves `max_threads` and `concurrency_control` of the original plan. Also fixed `Method serialize is not implemented for StreamInQueryResultCache` when `query_cache_for_subqueries = 1` is used together with parallel replicas and `serialize_query_plan = 1`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=102192&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/102192](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F102192+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
