signal.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW`
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `WINDOW VIEW` feature is removed, together with the `WATCH` statement and the `windowID` function. It has been non-functional since version 24.12 (inserts into the source table were silently not delivered to window views) and was never supported by the analyzer, which is enabled by default since 24.3. The settings `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, and `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` are kept as obsolete no-ops. The time-window functions `tumble`, `tumbleStart`, `tumbleEnd`, `hop`, `hopStart`, and `hopEnd` are kept. If you still have window views defined, drop them before upgrading: a server that finds a window view in its metadata fails to start (`Cannot parse definition from metadata file ... (SYNTAX_ERROR)`), the same way the removal of the `Lazy` database engine behaves. Similar functionality will be reimplemented on top of streaming queries (issue [#114738](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738)). The removal, in detail: - `src/Storages/WindowView/` (`StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`), `WatermarkTransform`, the `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery` parser, and the whole `WATCH` statement stack (`ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual) — window views were the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` statement was already documented as deprecated. - The `ASTCreateQuery` watermark/lateness fields and their AST JSON serialization and validation. The `clickhouse_json` boundary fails closed rather than silently reinterpreting legacy payloads: `ASTCreateQuery::readJSON` rejects a set `is_window_view`, watermark strategy or `allowed_lateness` flag and the `watermark_function` / `lateness_function` children (otherwise such a payload deserialized as an ordinary `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and was executed as an immediate-population table create), while `ASTViewTargets::readJSON` rejects the `Inner` target kind, which nothing produces any more and which formatted back to parser-impossible `INNER ENGINE ...` SQL. Both are covered by `04892_ast_json_removed_window_view_state`; the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder`; window-view special cases in `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`, `StorageFactory`, `DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DDLDependencyVisitor`, `QueryFuzzer`, BuzzHouse, and the ArrowFlight table-type mapping. - The `windowID` function and the `UInt32` single-argument forms of `tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` (they only accepted `windowID` output). The rest of the time-window function family stays, since these are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY` and are exactly the vocabulary for the streaming-queries replacement. - The keywords `WATCH`, `EVENTS`, `ALLOWED_LATENESS`, and `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` (the `WATERMARK` keyword stays: the streaming-queries `WATERMARK FOR` clause uses it), the error code `QUERY_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_WINDOW_VIEW`, and the corresponding fuzzer dictionary and ANTLR grammar entries. - Kept for compatibility: `QueryViewsLogElement::ViewType::WINDOW` (so existing `system.query_views_log` tables keep their schema) and `ViewTarget::Inner` (so old DDL log entries still parse), following the same pattern as the `LIVE VIEW` removal. - The `allow_experimental_window_view` constraint in `tests/docker_scripts/stress_tests.lib` is kept (only the constraint, not the profile value, which would mark an obsolete setting as changed and add a `system.warnings` entry): the upgrade check runs the previous release's suite under the previous release's binary, whose window-view tests are not dropped afterwards because `--upgrade-check` implies `--fake-drop`, and the leftover metadata would then stop the new server from starting. - Tests: the four remaining window-view tests are removed. The pure time-window-function coverage of `01049_window_view_window_functions` moved to a new `04891_time_window_functions` test, which also pins the new `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` behavior of `tumbleStart(UInt32)`. - Docs: the `Window View` section of `CREATE VIEW`, the `WATCH` page (with its navigation entries and locale twins) are removed and the old-slug redirects retargeted; the window-view entries are removed from the generated settings/functions reference pages (second commit, hence the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label): the `window-view.mdx` settings page, the four settings' entries in the pages/manifest/navigation/settings explorer, and the `windowID` section of `time-window-functions.mdx`. The unrelated drift accumulated on master since the last nightly regeneration is deliberately not included; the nightly docs-autogen job will pick it up. Why now: the feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024 — commit `ceae84c87a2` removed the explicit view-dependency registration and `DDLDependencyVisitor` never extracted the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so inserts into the source table were silently not pushed to window views, and direct inserts failed with `std::out_of_range` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years. It was never ported to the analyzer (with `enable_analyzer = 1`, the default, existing window views load permanently inert), its tests were removed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 because they were inherently flaky, and it kept costing triage time (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 is a recent server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`). The full assessment, including the plan for reimplementing this functionality on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`, `WATERMARK FOR`, emit-on-watermark windowed aggregation), is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114747](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114747+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.text: Implement the deserialized columns cache that keeps columns in memory. In comparison to the uncompressed cache, this saves time on deserialization and copying. Closes #82335. signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN racing a concurrent merge
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107114 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114399 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception (`Temporary part ... already added`) when `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` runs concurrently with a real merge, or with another `DRY RUN`, on the same parts. ### Description `MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun` executes a real `MergeTask` but, unlike the real optimize/merge paths, takes no `CurrentlyMergingPartsTagger` and no merge lock, so it never registers its source parts as "being merged". A concurrent real merge on the same parts computes the same result part name and reserves the same `tmp_merge_<result>` directory. The second reservation trips `TemporaryParts::add` -> `LOGICAL_ERROR "Temporary part ... already added"`, aborting the server on debug and sanitizer builds. Seen on 17 unrelated PRs over the 30 days to 2026-08-11 (CIDB `default.checks`, 17 rows / 17 distinct PRs), never on master. The dry-run part is throwaway, so its directory need not be named after the result part. It is now `tmp_merge_dry_run_<uuid>`, making the collision impossible on both `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`. A UUID rather than a counter, because the directory can live on storage shared with other servers, where a process-local counter restarts and repeats itself. Leaving the part name out also avoids a length trap: appending a token to it can exceed the 255-byte filename limit while the real merge of the same parts still succeeds. Part names are not length-capped (an all-integral partition key spells its values out, so ten `Int64` fields plus an `IPv4` reach 226 bytes) and `MergeTree` prepends `delete_tmp_` before removal, leaving 8 bytes. The new name has a fixed size. It is never parsed back into a part name and still starts with `tmp_merge_`, which the cleaner and the startup skip logic select by. Only a `dry_run_` suffix takes the new path, so top-level and projection merges keep byte-identical names. Not a duplicate of the `DRY RUN` fix linked above (rows_sources under a soft timeout). Tracking issue: #114399. Test `03823_optimize_dry_run_merge_race` races two `DRY RUN`s on the same parts via a new failpoint pausing after the directory is reserved, at part-name lengths 7, 9 and 226, asserting the real merge succeeds at 226 and each `DRY RUN` really merged. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110916&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110916](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110916+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Bound the shutdown wait for cancelled backups and restores
signal.text: Bound the shutdown wait for cancelled backups and restores <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): With `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0`, a `BACKUP` or `RESTORE` whose I/O did not return kept the server from terminating on a single `SIGTERM`, because shutdown waited for it to reach a final status with no timeout. That wait is now bounded by `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and new backups and restores are refused once shutdown has begun. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105 Reported by @ PedroTadim, who [asked me to take it](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105#issuecomment-5326577830). The issue stays open. **Cause.** Shutdown waits with `status_changed.wait` - no timeout, predicate on the operation status only, so it lasts as long as the operation. `cancelAll` does not help: cancellation is polled per file (`checkTimeLimit()` before `writeFile`), and within a file `BackupImpl` uses the `copyData` overload with no cancellation hook, so a thread parked in a read never sees it. **Change**, all inside the `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0` branch of `Server.cpp`: refuse new operations, bound the wait at `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and on non-convergence feed the forced exit that already handles `!joined_refresh_tasks`. That exit is `_exit`, so the unbounded `thread_pools->wait()` in `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` is never reached rather than bounded. `addInfo` refuses after its dedup early-return: `UNFINISHED` for internal operations (retriable in `DDLWorker`), `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` otherwise. **Not fixed here.** The default `= 1` branch is untouched, so the hang is still reachable with stock settings: that setting is documented as waiting for backups to *finish*, so capping it changes the guarantee and is your call. Also unchanged: the per-file cancellation granularity, and `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` reached without this guard (failed startup script), where bounding its status waits just moves the block to the pool join. An abandoned backup keeps its `CREATING_BACKUP` row and can leave partial files. **Validation.** The new tests wedge a backup with the existing `backup_pause_on_start` failpoint, which parks the thread before any `checkTimeLimit()` check, so the operation never sees its own cancellation. The oracle is whether `stop_clickhouse()` escalated to `SIGKILL`, not elapsed time and not a log line (`_exit` discards the async log queue). One arm requires self-exit and fails on master; a second raises the setting to 600 and requires the server to keep waiting, so a hardcoded deadline fails it. 50/50 stable; sibling shutdown and on-cluster cancel tests pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Support asynchronous inserts in the Prometheus remote-write protocol
signal.text: The Prometheus remote-write protocol handler now honors the `async_insert` setting (enabled in the user profile or passed as a URL query parameter of the handler): data from multiple concurrent remote-write requests is batched in the asynchronous insert queue before forming parts, which reduces the number of parts created in the inner tables of a `TimeSeries` table under a high rate of small remote-write requests. Since `async_insert` is enabled by default, remote-write requests are batched by default; add `async_insert=0` to the handler URL or disable the setting for the user to keep the previous synchronous behavior. A request is acknowledged only after the data is flushed to all inner tables of the `TimeSeries` table, regardless of the `wait_for_async_insert` setting, because the remote-write protocol treats an acknowledged write as durable. If the flush fails, the request returns an error instead of an acknowledgement, so the sender retries it. Deduplication on flush is forcibly disabled on this path (both `deduplicate_insert` and `async_insert_deduplicate`, since the former overrides the latter): a flushed block combines data from multiple remote-write requests, so its hash differs on every retry anyway, and the inner tables of the `TimeSeries` engine handle duplicates themselves. Verified manually with a local server and real remote-write requests: a request without settings goes through the asynchronous insert queue and the data is visible immediately after the acknowledgement; `async_insert=0` keeps the synchronous path; four concurrent requests are flushed as a single batch insert; a failing inner table (a `CHECK` constraint on an external `DATA` target table) returns HTTP 500 with no acknowledgement and no data written. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The Prometheus remote-write protocol now supports asynchronous inserts: data from multiple concurrent remote-write requests is batched before forming parts, following the `async_insert` setting (enabled by default; add `async_insert=0` to the handler URL to keep the synchronous behavior). A request is acknowledged only after the data is flushed to all inner tables of the target `TimeSeries` table. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115688&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115688](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115688+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Allow creating a Distributed table over a table function
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106189 Allow creating a `Distributed` table over a table function, in the same way the `remote`/`cluster` table functions already accept an arbitrary table expression. Previously `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Distributed(...)` only accepted `Distributed(cluster, database, table[, sharding_key[, policy_name]])`, where `database` and `table` had to be string literals or identifiers. `StorageDistributed` itself already supported being backed by a table function (`remote_table_function_ptr`), but that capability was only reachable through the `remote`/`cluster`/`clusterAllReplicas` table functions. This change lets the engine take a table function directly: ```sql CREATE TABLE t ENGINE = Distributed(cluster, table_function()[, sharding_key[, policy_name]]); -- e.g. CREATE TABLE distributed_numbers ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards, numbers(100)); ``` mirroring the `cluster('cluster_name', table_function())` signature. The second engine argument is treated as a table function only when it is a call to a registered table function; any other expression is still interpreted as a database name, so the existing `Distributed(cluster, database, table, ...)` form is unaffected. The structure is inferred from the table function when the columns are omitted. `INSERT` into a table-function-backed `Distributed` table is rejected with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, since there is no concrete remote table to route rows to. As a side effect, `INSERT INTO FUNCTION cluster('cluster', table_function())` now fails with this clear error instead of silently building a broken `INSERT INTO <empty>` query for the shards. ### Relationship to #106189 This is complementary to #106189 (`Remote`/`RemoteSecure` storage engines): that PR adds address-based engines over an ad-hoc cluster, while this one lets the configured-cluster `Distributed` engine take a table function. The table-function `INSERT` guard in `StorageDistributed::write` is aligned with #106189 (identical exception message, guard placed only in `write`). The `read` path here additionally handles the case where the remote database/table names are empty (a table-function-backed `Distributed` stores empty names rather than the `system.one` placeholder that #106189's engines inherit from the `remote` table function); this also makes the shared `read` path robust for #106189's engines. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow creating a `Distributed` table over a table function, e.g. `CREATE TABLE t ENGINE = Distributed(cluster, numbers(100))`, in the same way as the `cluster`/`remote` table functions accept a table function. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add `/dialect`, `/lang`, `/language` client commands
signal.text: Adds client-side `/dialect`, `/lang` and `/language` commands - an equivalent of `SET dialect = '...'` that is handled before parsing, so it also works when the current dialect cannot express a `SET` query (for example, to leave `kusto` or `promql`). The active non-default dialect is shown in the prompt, and a plain `SET dialect = '...'` keeps the prompt in sync. Implementation notes: - The prompt is rendered by `getPrompt` on every line from a template that keeps the `{display_name}` placeholder: the current dialect is appended to the display name in parentheses (with a separating space if the display name is non-empty), and the `:) ` smiley is appended at the end, preserving the previous behavior for the default dialect. A custom prompt without `{display_name}` gets the dialect appended at its end. - The command works in `clickhouse-client`, `clickhouse-local`, and the embedded client (SSH/web terminal). - `clickhouse-local` also recognizes the command in noninteractive scripts: a standalone dialect-command line splits the script, so each chunk is parsed with the dialect selected before it. A line that belongs to inline `INSERT ... FORMAT` data or to an unfinished statement (an open string literal or bracket) stays a part of the SQL, and the other text-level meta-commands keep working. A rejected command aborts the script, exactly like a rejected `SET dialect`. - Documentation: a new "Switching the SQL dialect" section on the client page. - Test: `04892_client_dialect_command.expect`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added client-side commands `/dialect`, `/lang`, and `/language` to `clickhouse-client` and `clickhouse-local`, so you can switch the active SQL dialect before parsing - it also works when the current dialect cannot express a `SET` query, for example to leave `kusto` or `promql`. signal.title: Uncompressed Keeper snapshots are written as 0-byte files; node cannot restart
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format=false`, every snapshot Keeper writes to a local disk is 0 bytes although it logs `Created persistent snapshot N`. On the next restart Keeper dies with `Failure to load from latest snapshot ... Cannot read all data. Bytes read: 0 ... Manual intervention is necessary for recovery. Problematic snapshot can be removed but it will lead to data loss (CORRUPTED_DATA)`.** - **Root cause:** In the non-zstd branch the file buffer is wrapped BY REFERENCE (`std::make_unique<CompressedWriteBuffer>(*writer)`), so finalizing `compressed_writer` (:903) only pushes bytes into `writer`'s in-memory buffer; `compressed_writer->sync()` (:906) is the base no-op for that class and `writer.reset()` (:910) destroys the file buffer without `finalize`/`next`, discarding everything. The zstd branch passes ownership (`wrapWriteBufferWithCompressionMethod(std::move(writer), ...)`), so finalize/sync propagate — which is why only the uncompressed path is broken. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `KeeperStateMachine::create_snapshot` -> `writeSnapshotToDisk` -> `KeeperSnapshotManager::writeSnapshotFile` (KeeperStateMachine.cpp:1027, local-disk branch) -> KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:896. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:896`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp#L896) — non-owning CompressedWriteBuffer over the file write buffer - [`src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:910`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp#L910) — writer.reset() without finalize/sync - [`src/Coordination/KeeperStateMachine.cpp:1027`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperStateMachine.cpp#L1027) — local-disk snapshots go through writeSnapshotFile **Impact:** Any Keeper/ClickHouse deployment with `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format=false` silently writes empty snapshots. The node refuses to start after any restart and recovery requires deleting the snapshot, which ClickHouse's own message describes as data loss; a leader also has nothing usable to send to a recovering follower. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `ac58c4e749468`). ### How to reproduce ```python import pytest import helpers.keeper_utils as keeper_utils from helpers.cluster import ClickHouseCluster cluster = ClickHouseCluster(__file__) node_zstd = cluster.add_instance( "node_zstd", main_configs=["configs/keeper_zstd.xml"], stay_alive=True, with_remote_database_disk=False ) node_plain = cluster.add_instance( "node_plain", main_configs=["configs/keeper_plain.xml"], stay_alive=True, with_remote_database_disk=False ) SNAPSHOT_DIR = "/var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots" @pytest.fixture(scope="module") -- def started_cluster(): -- try: cluster.start() yield cluster -- finally: cluster.shutdown() @pytest.mark.parametrize("node_name", ["node_zstd", "node_plain"]) -- def test_snapshot_survives_restart(started_cluster, node_name): node = cluster.instances[node_name] keeper_utils.wait_until_connected(cluster, node) zk = keeper_utils.get_fake_zk(cluster, node.name) zk.create("/test_uncompressed_snapshot", b"somedata") idx = keeper_utils.send_4lw_cmd(cluster, node, cmd="csnp").strip() node.wait_for_log_line(f"Created persistent snapshot {idx} with path") sizes = node.exec_in_container(["bash", "-c", f"stat -c '%n %s' {SNAPSHOT_DIR}/snapshot_*"]).strip() print(f"{node_name} SNAPSHOT_FILES: {sizes}") node.restart_clickhouse() keeper_utils.wait_until_connected(cluster, node) zk = keeper_utils.get_fake_zk(cluster, node.name) assert zk.get("/test_uncompressed_snapshot")[0] == b"somedata" # configs/keeper_zstd.xml and configs/keeper_plain.xml are identical single-node keeper # configs (tcp_port 9181, server_id 1, local log/snapshot paths, four_letter_word_white_list *), -- # except that keeper_plain.xml adds inside <coordination_settings>: # <compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format>false</compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format> ``` ### Expected behavior ``` Both parameterizations pass: the snapshot file is non-empty for both settings and the node restarts and still serves /test_uncompressed_snapshot. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` node_zstd SNAPSHOT_FILES: /var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots/snapshot_13_ebe6b90817820fc1.bin.zstd 440 -> PASSED node_plain SNAPSHOT_FILES: /var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots/snapshot_15_4d88ed92c255dd85.bin 0 -> FAILED (Exception: Cannot start ClickHouse, see additional info in logs) node_plain clickhouse-server.err.log: 2026.08.19 01:42:55.320161 <Error> void DB::KeeperDispatch ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Finalize and sync the underlying file buffer in the non-zstd branch, e.g. after `compressed_writer->finalize()` add `writer->finalize(); writer->sync();` (or give the LZ4 branch ownership of `writer` the way the zstd branch does). </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same non-owning wrap exists at KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:687 (`serializeSnapshotToBuffer`), but there the sink is `WriteBufferFromNuraftBuffer` whose `getBuffer()` finalizes, so that path is correct. Found during automated review of [PR #111715](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111715). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr111715_001` </details> cc @al13n321 @antonio2368 (from #111715) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115553 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1802` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Do not use a non-deterministic expression as a join key when rewriting a comma or `CROSS` join
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112965 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for a comma or `CROSS` join whose `WHERE` compares columns of two tables through a non-deterministic expression such as `rand`. Such a query could return rows that contradict its own `WHERE` clause, because rewriting the join into an `INNER` join moved the expression into the join key, where it is evaluated again per row of each side. ### Description At default settings this query returns rows where `r.a` is not `3`: ```sql CREATE TABLE l (a UInt64) ENGINE = Memory; CREATE TABLE r (a UInt64) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO l SELECT number % 16 FROM numbers(500); INSERT INTO r SELECT number % 16 FROM numbers(500); SELECT uniqExact(r.a), countIf(r.a != 3) FROM l, r WHERE rand(l.a) % 16 = r.a AND rand(l.a) % 16 = 3; ``` Expected `1 0`. Master returns `10 29`: the second conjunct pins the key to `3`, yet 29 of the returned rows hold a different `r.a`. Only the new analyzer is affected, with `enable_analyzer = 0` the same query returns `1 0`. `CrossToInnerJoinPass` moves an `equals` conjunct out of the `WHERE` into the join `ON` and rebuilds the `WHERE` from the conjuncts it did not take. In the key position the expression is evaluated per row of each joined side instead of once per cross-product row, so the key a row was hashed under is unrelated to the value the surviving conjunct checked. The fix refuses a condition as a join key when its subtree holds a window function, a stateful function, one that is not deterministic in the scope of the query, or one fixed per executing node. A refused condition stays in the `WHERE`, exactly as `cross_to_inner_join_rewrite = 0` leaves it. The predicate is `isDeterministicInScopeOfQuery`, so `now`, `currentUser` and `randConstant` keep their rewrite. Several functions of that class did not declare the property and now do, so the pass compares no function names. `query_plan_merge_filter_into_join_condition` moves the same class of predicate into a join key and is fixed separately in #112965. No issue is linked because there is no existing report: I found this while auditing the pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112938&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112938](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112938+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix signed integer overflow in condition_variable::wait_for with huge timeouts
signal.text: A wait-timeout setting that reaches `std::condition_variable::wait_for` unchecked overflows the chrono conversion inside it. libc++ evaluates `wait_for(d)` as `steady_clock::now() + d` in nanoseconds, multiplying a millisecond duration by 1000000: a timeout above ~9.2e12 ms overflows Int64, and one above the Int64 millisecond range even turns into a negative duration, so the wait returns at once and the caller busy-loops instead of waiting. UBSan aborts the server; a release build silently wraps. The setting that reaches it in practice is `interactive_delay`, a plain unbounded `UInt64` of microseconds: the server waits `interactive_delay / 1000` milliseconds for the next result chunk in `ConcurrentBoundedQueue::popImpl`, through the lazy output format, on both the `TCPHandler` and the `clickhouse-local` path. Found by serverfuzz on master, and again in the stress test of an unrelated pull request — https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112177&sha=e601607e228ad5d736ad491220ebf4b62d531d51&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112177): ``` /ClickHouse/contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/__chrono/duration.h:93:79: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 18584892780430 * 1000000 cannot be represented in type '_Ct' (aka 'long long') ... #6 ConcurrentBoundedQueue<DB::Chunk>::popImpl<true>(...) src/Common/ConcurrentBoundedQueue.h:73 #8 DB::LazyOutputFormat::getChunk(unsigned long) src/Processors/Formats/LazyOutputFormat.cpp:25 #11 DB::TCPHandler::processOrdinaryQuery(DB::QueryState&) src/Server/TCPHandler.cpp:1540 SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior ``` Reproduces deterministically: ``` clickhouse-local --query "SELECT 1 SETTINGS interactive_delay = 100000000000000000" ``` Fix: clamp the timeout to one year before constructing the chrono duration, via a small shared helper `saturatedMilliseconds`. The same cap is already used for `CancellationChecker` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96450); it is applied here to the remaining `wait_for` sites that take a user-controlled millisecond timeout, and `saturatedSeconds`/`saturatedSecondsFrom` cover the seconds-typed timeouts and the query cache expiry built as `now() + seconds(query_cache_ttl)`. A `Milliseconds`- or `Seconds`-typed setting can no longer carry such a value in the first place: `SettingFieldTimespan` rejects a value that does not fit into Int64 microseconds, so the clamp there is only defence in depth. That check landed on master after this branch was cut and supersedes the saturating conversion this pull request originally added to `SettingsFields`, which is dropped along with its unit tests in favour of master's stricter ones. What is left for the clamp is every setting that is not a timespan — above all `interactive_delay`. Keeper has its own coordination waits with a different bound; they are handled separately in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112088. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112088 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112177 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a signed integer overflow when a wait-timeout setting, such as `interactive_delay`, was set to a huge value: the wait could time out immediately instead of waiting, and the server could abort under the Undefined Behavior Sanitizer. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106961&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/106961](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F106961+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: INSERT rejected with NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK when an ALIAS column declares STATISTICS
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A table created with an ALIAS column carrying explicit `STATISTICS(...)` accepts INSERTs on 26.4-26.7 but rejects every INSERT after this PR: `Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. The table becomes effectively read-only after upgrade; SELECT, merges and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` keep working.** - **Root cause:** The insert path uses `ColumnsStatistics::build` (hard `getByName`) while the merge path uses `ColumnsStatistics::buildIfExists`, which skips columns absent from the block ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:690-700`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L690-L700)). Statistics on non-physical columns are otherwise treated as unsupported — `addImplicitStatistics` skips Alias/Ephemeral columns (Statistics.cpp:927-929) and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS` rejects them via `columns.hasPhysical` (StatisticsDescription.cpp:181) — but the inline `CREATE TABLE ... col T ALIAS expr STATISTICS(...)` form has no such check (ColumnsDescription.cpp:260-261). Flipping `materialize_statistics_on_insert` to `true` turns that latent inconsistency into a hard INSERT failure. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeSink::writeNewTempPart` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp:409`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp#L409)) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:848`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L848)) -> `ColumnsStatistics` ctor collects every column whose statistics description is non-empty, including ALIAS columns ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:644-647`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L644-L647)) -> `ColumnsStatistics::build` looks the column up with `block.getByName` ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684)), and an ALIAS column is never in the written block. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:849`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L849) — insert path calls ColumnsStatistics::build on the written block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684) — build() uses block.getByName, which throws for a column not in the block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:646`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L646) — ColumnsStatistics ctor does not skip Alias/Ephemeral columns - [`src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp:181`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp#L181) — ALTER path rejects statistics on non-physical columns; the inline CREATE path does not **Impact:** Any table whose DDL puts `STATISTICS(...)` on an ALIAS column stops accepting INSERTs after upgrading to 26.8 (or after `SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1`). The error is an internal-sounding `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` at write time with no hint that statistics caused it, and there is no DDL-time warning. `ALTER TABLE ... DROP STATISTICS <alias_col>` is not a workaround either, since that path also refuses non-physical columns. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `2746afad95f`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/63424d1d-98a2-4f38-92d8-552f32129820) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that INSERT works when an ALIAS column declares statistics. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; SET allow_statistics = 1; SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; CREATE TABLE t_alias_statistics (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT a, b FROM t_alias_statistics ORDER BY a; DROP TABLE t_alias_statistics; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 1 2 2 3 3 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 10. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.1:19020. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (query: INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3);) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Use `statistics.buildIfExists(block)` on the insert path (matching `MergeTask`'s `BuildStatisticsTransform`), or skip Alias/Ephemeral columns in the `ColumnsStatistics` constructor the way `addImplicitStatistics` does. Rejecting the DDL instead is the wrong lever: the same code path parses metadata on ATTACH/startup, so existing tables would fail to load. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same `build` vs `buildIfExists` asymmetry would also fire for any other future column kind that is present in the metadata but absent from the written block. Found during automated review of [PR #109454](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109454). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr109454_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov @rschu1ze @egor-click (from #109454)

signal.title: Run the documentation examples in CI
signal.text: #108556 made the SQL examples embedded in `system.documentation` runnable, but nothing runs them, so they go stale again as soon as behaviour changes: since then a steady stream of one-off fixes has been needed (#109421, #109965, #110459, #112287, ...). This adds a runner and a CI job that execute every structured example rendered from the embedded `examples` fields, and brings their documented responses back in line with what the server actually does. Hand-written SQL fences in free-form description Markdown are explicitly out of scope for this runner. ### The runner `tests/docs_examples/runner.py` reads every structured example rendered from the embedded `examples` fields in `system.documentation` on a running server and executes it. Hand-written SQL fences in free-form description Markdown are not parsed or run. The examples of one entity run **in order, in a single session, in a database of their own**: a documentation page is written to be followed from top to bottom, so one example commonly creates the table a later one queries. It is plain Python and can be pointed at a dedicated server with permission to create and drop databases; even without `--global-objects`, it creates and removes scratch databases: ``` python3 tests/docs_examples/runner.py --port 8123 python3 tests/docs_examples/runner.py --port 8123 --filter '^argM' --verbose ``` Each example gets one of three outcomes: * `ok` — it ran, and its output matches the documented response (or it documents no response, or it documents an exception and indeed threw it); * `error` — it failed to run (or documents an exception and did not throw it); * `output` — it ran, but its output differs from the documented response. Everything that is not `ok` is listed in `tests/docs_examples/known_failures.txt` with the reason for it. The run fails if an example that is not on the list fails, and also if a listed one starts passing, so the list can only shrink. A few entries are marked `unstable`, for the examples whose output is random enough to sometimes match the documented one. An example that documents an exception is expected to throw it from its **last** statement — what comes before is setup that has to succeed — and when the documented response names an error code, the exception has to carry the same one. The message text is not compared: it holds a version number and a query pipeline description that are not part of what the example teaches. The server the job starts runs in `Etc/UTC`. Many examples convert between a date with time and a number, or hash a `DateTime`, without naming a time zone, and the documented responses are the ones of a `UTC` server; without pinning it, the run would only reproduce on a machine whose time zone matches. The comparison pins the Pretty rendering to the plain form the documented responses are written in — no row numbers, no colour, long column names spelled out in full, no readable-number tip, a named tuple printed as a tuple — so that it is about the data and the shape of the result rather than about a rendering default that changed after a page was written. ### The job `ci/jobs/docs_examples_job.py` starts a server from the shipped configuration plus the fragments in `programs/server/config.d` (macros, the legacy geobase, the natural language processing data, Keeper, the test clusters) and `programs/server/users.d` (the localhost-only network of the `default` user, access management, query logging), and two fragments of its own in `tests/docs_examples/config.d` and `tests/docs_examples/users.d`, so the features the examples demonstrate are actually configured, and configured the way the shipped server configures them. The one thing the examples add to the shipped user configuration is stated explicitly: the `queryID`, `initialQueryID` and `initialQueryStartTime` examples read from three shards at `127.0.0.{1..3}`, so `default` is allowed in from the whole loopback network rather than from `127.0.0.1` alone. It publishes an HTML report naming every failing example with its source file, its query and both responses. The job runs on pull requests and on master, next to the other jobs that run a corpus of queries against a server. ### What it found **Examples that did not run.** All of these are fixed here: * examples that were never a query: a bare expression (`factorial(10)`), a syntax template with placeholders sitting in an `Examples` block (the `iceberg*`, `paimon*`, `deltaLake*`, `oss`, `cosn` and `mergeTree*` table functions — moved to the `syntax` field, where they belong), a leaked C++ string literal, a MySQL session transcript, an unbalanced parenthesis, a stray `\G` left over from a `clickhouse-client` session; * an example calling the wrong function: `YYYYMMDDhhmmssToDateTime` demonstrated `YYYYMMDDToDateTime`; * examples reading a table nothing creates: `salary`, `Employees`, `t`, `key_val`, `encryption_test`, `student_ttest`, `points`, `example_table`, ... — each page now creates its own; * pages that cannot be followed top to bottom, because every example re-creates the same table and the second one hits `TABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS`; * arguments the function rejects: an H3 index that is not a valid directed edge, S2 cell ids that do not form a valid rectangle, a signed weight for a weighted quantile, an `INSERT ... FORMAT JSONEachRow` without the semicolon that ends its data, a cipher the build does not provide; * examples of an error whose response was prose ("Raises a `NO_COMMON_TYPE` exception") or a paste from version 19.14, now written as the exception the server prints — the runner treats a documented exception as an expectation to fail. **Responses that no longer match.** 621 of them are regenerated from what the server prints, after checking that the output is identical across two runs on a fresh server. Most were stale column names (`avg(x)` for a column named `t`, `argMax(a, tuple(b, a))` for what is now printed as `argMax(a, (b, a))`) or hand-typed values that never came from a server (`[4, 3, 2, 1]` where the server prints `[4,3,2,1]`, `'dcba'` where it prints `dcba`), but some were genuinely wrong results. **Examples that documented no response.** An example that documents no response is accepted as soon as it runs, so a deterministic example with an empty response is a page that shows no result and a query nothing verifies. Every one of those now carries what the server prints: the quantized `*Transposed` distance functions, `s2RectAdd`, `isValidASCII`, `MVTEncodeGeom`, `firstSignificantSubdomain`, `viewExplain`, `numbers_mt` and `zeros_mt`. What stays empty is what has no response to document: the `ai*` functions call an external model provider, `fuzzQuery` is random, `currentHandler` and `currentRequestURL` describe the request that ran them, and `SELECT * FROM numbers_mt() LIMIT 10` reads an infinite stream with several threads. **Examples that needed a dataset nobody has.** `anyHeavy`, `categoricalInformationValue`, `topK`, `IPv4NumToStringClassC`, `IPv6NumToString`, `arrayEnumerateUniq`, `bar`, `indexHint`, `transform` and `evalMLMethod` demonstrated themselves on `ontime`, `metrica.hits`, `test.hits`, `hits_all`, `test.visits` or `trips`. Each of them now builds a small table of its own, so the example is one a reader can run. `naiveBayesClassifier` and its two variants train a dictionary on an inline set of token counts instead of naming one that does not exist. The four `flameGraph` "examples" were not examples at all — their documented response was a `clickhouse client ... | flamegraph.pl` command line — so they are recipes in the description now, and the function has one example that runs. **What is left in the known-failures file** is what a test server cannot produce: examples that call an external model provider, need a trained CatBoost model, a TLS certificate or a geobase hierarchy the test configuration does not carry; responses that describe the machine or the build (a host name, a source path, a version, a disk size); and outputs that are random or depend on the time. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113024&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113024](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113024+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Expand `url` glob patterns lazily
signal.text: A pattern passed to `url` was expanded into the full direct product before the query started, so `glob_expansion_max_elements` limited how large a pattern was allowed to be rather than how much of it a query needed. A query that stops early paid for the whole address space up front, and was rejected outright when that space was large: ```sql SELECT * FROM url('https://clickhouse-public-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/wikistat/original/pageviews-20200101-{0..10000}{0..10000}00.gz', LineAsString) LIMIT 3 -- Code: 36. DB::Exception: first argument generates too many result addresses. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` `RemoteDescriptionGenerator` produces the addresses of a pattern one at a time instead. Numeric intervals stay symbolic, so `{0..10000}{0..10000}` costs two factors rather than a hundred million strings, and the odometer over them walks the same order the materializing code produced - the last factor varies fastest. `parseRemoteDescription` is now a thin wrapper that checks the arithmetic total and drains the generator, so there is still one parser of the syntax, and `remote`, `mysql` and `postgresql` - which need every address at once to build a cluster - behave exactly as before, down to the error messages. Three places on the `url` path stopped materializing: - `getSampleURI` takes a single address. It only reads hive partitioning and virtual columns off a path, and used to expand the whole pattern to look at its first element. - `StorageURLSource::DisclosedGlobIterator` generates in batches and applies the `_path` / `_file` filter to each. A pattern that fits into one batch keeps the exact post-filter size, which is what empty-glob detection and the number of streams are derived from, so nothing observable changes for it. - Schema inference pulls addresses through a producer and stops at the first one it can read. The limit therefore applies to the addresses a query actually reads. The batch is `min(1000, glob_expansion_max_elements)` and the default limit is 1000, so every pattern that works today is still served in a single batch and behaves bit for bit as it did; only patterns that used to be rejected behave differently. Reading a huge pattern in full is still rejected. Groups holding the separator, such as `{a,b}` in `{a,b}{c,d}`, are still expanded eagerly and bounded by the limit, because the direct product needs their alternatives up front. A `..` anywhere inside braces makes the whole group a numeric interval, so such a group can only hold literal text. Verified against a locally built server: the query above now returns rows; `{1..1000}` at the default limit still reads exactly 1000 addresses; `_path` filtering, failover options, `remote`, `mysql` and every malformed-pattern error message are byte-identical to an unmodified `master` binary. The `url` over-limit message now names `url` instead of `remote`, which is the only intentional difference. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/49234 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115581 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `url` table function and the `URL` table engine now expand glob patterns lazily instead of materializing every address before the query starts. `glob_expansion_max_elements` now limits how many addresses a query actually reads rather than how large the pattern is, so a query that stops early - for example under a `LIMIT` - can use a pattern that describes far more addresses than the limit. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115680&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115680](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115680+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not let an alias give `randConstant` a second value in one query
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112938 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `randConstant` returning two different values in one query when its calls carry different aliases. `randConstant` is documented to hold a single value for the whole query, and `SELECT randConstant() = randConstant()` already returned `1`, but adding aliases as in `SELECT randConstant() AS a, randConstant() AS b` produced two unrelated values. ### Description ```sql SELECT randConstant() = randConstant() -- 1 SELECT a = b FROM (SELECT randConstant() AS a, randConstant() AS b) -- 0 <-- wrong ``` `randConstant` is documented to return "a single random value that remains constant across all rows in the current query execution", and its argument is documented as existing only "to prevent common subexpression elimination when the same function call is used multiple times in a query". So two bare calls must agree, and asking for a second value is spelled `randConstant(1), randConstant(2)`. `RandomConstantOverloadResolver::buildImpl` draws a new value on every call, so identical calls have to share one built `FunctionBase` to fold to one constant. `resolveFunction` arranges that with `functions_cache`, keyed by `getTreeHash`. That hash covers the alias, so the two aliased calls missed each other in the cache, each folded to its own literal, and no later common subexpression elimination could bring them back together — by then they were two different literals. With `enable_analyzer = 0` the same query returns `1`, so this is analyzer-only. The key now ignores aliases. An alias renames an expression and never changes the value the `FunctionBase` captures, so aliased calls share what bare calls share. What separates two calls is still their arguments, which the hash covers. Dropping the alias from the key widens what the cache can match, and stateful functions must not be matched: the cache is global across query scopes, so two scalar subqueries that differ only by an alias would have ended up sharing one `blockNumber` counter and reading two different numbers. Stateful functions are therefore excluded from the cache alongside `getSetting` and `rowNumberInAllBlocks`, and the last row of the test covers it by comparing the two counters (their absolute values are not a property of the fix - they count the blocks the server has already passed through the function). The change is narrower than the cache's reach suggests. Only a function folded through its own `FunctionBase` can be split this way; anything evaluated per row, such as `rand` or `generateUUIDv4`, is deduplicated later by ordinary common subexpression elimination, which already ignored aliases — `SELECT rand() AS a, rand() AS b, a = b` reads `1` on `master` today. To bound it rather than argue it, I swept all 57 zero-argument non-deterministic functions, comparing each one aliased and bare, before and after: `randConstant` is the only function whose result changes, from `0` to `1`, and no bare result moves at all. Test `05028` fails on exactly its four aliased rows without the change. Its five controls — the bare comparison, the distinct-argument row (four arguments rather than two, so it cannot flake on a value collision), the across-rows row, and the `now` and `rand` rows — pass either way. Verified by building and running against the branch build: `05028` plus the five existing tests that read `randConstant` (`03611`, `01418`, `00912`, `04327` across shards, `03047` under mutations) all pass. The 382-test `analyzer` family was run on both arms of an exact A/B on the same tree — the one-line change reverted, rebuilt, rerun — and the two arms are identical: 352 pass and the same 18 fail on both, all of them for missing fixtures in my local server rather than for this change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115384&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115384](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115384+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Follow-ups for CREATE HANDLER: parse limits of the stored query, docs, refactoring
signal.text: Follow-ups from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 (`CREATE HANDLER`). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 **Requested in review of #106231:** - The two predicates over `IAST::QueryKind` that describe the `readonly` mode - whether a query of that kind is rejected under it, and whether `readonly = 2` still lets it produce side effects - moved out of `SQLDefinedHandlerFromAST` into `Interpreters/QueryKindUnderReadonly.h`; `queryKindRequiresMutatingMethod` is renamed to `isQueryKindRejectedUnderReadonly` after the property it reports. The handler code keeps the statement-level refinements and the HTTP-method fences. - `currentHandler` and `currentRequestURL` were registered with `IntroducedIn` 26.6 (the development version when they were written); they are released in 26.8. **The one unresolved review finding:** a request could still lower the parse limits of a handler's query. `HTTPHandler::processQuery` relaxed `max_parser_depth` / `max_parser_backtracks` *before* applying the settings the request supplies, and a request names settings freely - so `GET /h?max_parser_depth=1` put the caller's value back and broke a handler the server itself had accepted. `max_query_size` had the same hole and did not even need a hostile request: a stored query longer than its default value is creatable and reloadable (both parse without a size limit) but failed on every invocation. The fix went through review iterations and landed as a per-query flag rather than context settings: `executeQuery` receives `QueryFlags::parse_server_owned_query_without_limits` (set by `PredefinedQueryHandler`, from which `SQLDefinedQueryHandler` inherits) and lifts `max_parser_depth` / `max_parser_backtracks` / `max_query_size` only while parsing the stored query text itself. The query context keeps the request's limits, so the request-controlled construction snippets (`select` / `filter` / `order` / `page`) and everything else are still parsed under the caller's own limits - the request can neither break the server's stored text nor borrow its unlimited parse. The flag propagates through `PARALLEL WITH` and `EXECUTE AS` subqueries. New tests `04897_handler_request_parser_limits` (including a `?max_parser_depth=1&filter=(((((1)))))` case that must keep failing) and `04898_handler_large_query_invocation`, both verified to fail without the fix. **Documentation:** the `CREATE HANDLER` page was written into `docs/en/sql-reference/statements/create/handler.md` - a path in the legacy Docusaurus tree that `9440ca729a3` had already removed - so the only documentation of `CREATE HANDLER` / `ALTER HANDLER` / `DROP HANDLER` was published nowhere. It moves to `docs/reference/statements/create/handler.mdx`, with the frontmatter and internal links converted to that tree's conventions and the page registered in `docs/reference/navigation.json`. `docs/en/operations/system-tables/handlers.md` was a leftover copy of the generated `docs/reference/system-tables/handlers.mdx` whose hand-written `SHOW HANDLERS` / secret-masking paragraph had been lost; that paragraph is restored and the legacy copy deleted. The statement is now cross-referenced from the HTTP interface page, the `DROP` page and the `ALTER` overview, and the anchored (`RE2::FullMatch`) semantics of `URL REGEXP` are documented. Verified locally: all 30 SQL-defined-handler stateless tests pass against a server built from this branch (the 31st match of the `handler` filter, `03354_tcp_handler_async_insert_bug`, is unrelated and needs a writable `/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files`), and `04844_handler_deep_query_invocation` still passes without the fix, confirming it covered only the session-level limit. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed HTTP handler invocation so request-level `max_parser_depth`, `max_parser_backtracks`, and `max_query_size` no longer break stored handler queries, and published the `CREATE HANDLER`, `ALTER HANDLER`, and `DROP HANDLER` documentation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114883&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114883](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114883+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Store and ingest Prometheus native histograms in the TimeSeries engine
signal.text: ## Summary First slice of Prometheus native-histogram support for the `TimeSeries` engine (storage + ingestion). Today, `timeseries[].histograms[]` in a remote-write request is parsed and silently dropped with a 204; a Prometheus sender configured with `send_native_histograms: true` loses all histogram data. This PR makes that data storable and queryable via SQL: - **Storage**: a new optional `HISTOGRAMS` target table on the `TimeSeries` engine (alongside `DATA`/`TAGS`/`METRICS`), enabled with `SETTINGS store_native_histograms = 1` or an explicit `HISTOGRAMS [db.table | INNER ENGINE ...]` clause. One row per histogram sample, mirroring the `prompb.Histogram` message for lossless round-trip: `id`, `timestamp`, `flags` (is_float / counter-reset hint / gauge / stale marker), `schema`, `zero_threshold`, `count`, `sum`, `zero_count`, positive/negative spans and bucket values, and `custom_values` for NHCB (schema −53). Bucket values are stored as absolutes (int-flavor deltas are decoded at ingest). A `timeSeriesHistograms(db.table)` table function mirrors `timeSeriesData` for introspection. - **Ingestion**: `PrometheusRemoteWriteProtocol` reads `timeseries[].histograms[]` — both the int (delta-encoded) and float flavors — validates span/bucket consistency (rejecting the request with `INCORRECT_DATA`/HTTP 400 on malformed data), preserves counter-reset hints and stale markers, updates the tags table's `min_time`/`max_time` from histogram timestamps, and counts ingested histograms in a new `PrometheusRemoteWriteHistograms` profile event. The decoding is factored so a future remote-write 2.0 message path can reuse it. The vendored protobuf gains upstream's `custom_values = 16` field. - **Backward compatibility**: tables without the `HISTOGRAMS` target work exactly as before — `CREATE`, `ATTACH`, and remote writes are unchanged; histogram samples sent to such a table are dropped with a rate-limited warning (and the profile event), so the loss is at least observable, instead of today's silent drop. Everything stays behind `allow_experimental_time_series_table`. PromQL evaluation over histograms (`histogram_quantile` etc.), the HTTP query API JSON shapes, and remote-read output are explicitly out of scope for this PR and build on this storage layer. Open design questions (called out for reviewers): whether the `flags` gauge bit should be dropped as redundant with `counter_reset_hint == GAUGE`, and whether new tables should get the `HISTOGRAMS` target by default under the experimental flag rather than opt-in. ## Tests - Stateless: `CREATE`/`SHOW CREATE` round-trip with and without the target, external histograms-table validation, `timeSeriesHistograms()` reads, `ATTACH` of a pre-histogram definition. - Integration (`test_prometheus_protocols/test_native_histograms.py`): remote-write of int, float, NHCB, and stale-marker histograms with spans, zero bucket and negative buckets, asserting every stored column; mixed float samples + histograms in one request; drop-with-warning on a 3-target table; invalid spans and negative decoded counts → 400. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` table engine can now store Prometheus native histograms: a new optional `HISTOGRAMS` target table (enabled with `store_native_histograms = 1`), ingestion of native histograms from the Prometheus remote-write protocol, and a `timeSeriesHistograms` table function for reading them. signal.title: Fix flaky 04511_reader_executor_disk_cache
signal.text: `04511_reader_executor_disk_cache` fails on master with ``` cold_read_from_source 1 executor_populated_cache 1 -warm_served_from_cache 1 +warm_served_from_cache 0 ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=2101f9b0850389d7fddfefd04d2577162c8958c3&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20sequential%2C%202%2F2%29 It also fails on unrelated pull requests in `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, sequential, 2/2)` (4 of 14 reruns there). No tracking issue exists. ### What goes wrong The third check asserted `warm < cold`, comparing the `ReaderExecutorBytesFromSource` totals of a cold and a warm `SELECT`. That is a proxy, and a partially populated cache inverts it. With more than one reading thread each stream builds its own `ReaderExecutor` over the same file. `DiskCacheWriter` appends only at the segment's live write offset, so whichever stream loses the downloader race contributes nothing, and the cold read leaves the segment partially populated. The warm read then re-fetches such a segment from its start — `claimLeadRole`'s `available` prefix is deliberately unused, see the *\"Coarse by design\"* note in `ReaderExecutor::readThroughCaches` — so it can move *more* source bytes than the cold read did. The failing job's server log and `query_log` show exactly that: the cold read populated 285856 of the 801126-byte segment and read 1658884 bytes from source; the warm read then read 2480460. Across the 28 runs of that job the cold total was a constant 1658884 while the warm total was 0, 801126, 1372817, 1479995 or 2480460, purely as a function of how the streams interleaved. ### The fix Pin the reads to a single thread, so the cold read populates the segment completely, and assert the strong property instead of the proxy: the warm read must touch the source not at all (`warm = 0`). Verified over 54 runs of the test with randomized settings against a local minio: `cold` is now a stable 800461 (one clean pass over the file instead of two or three overlapping ones) and `warm` is 0 in every run. The re-fetch-from-segment-start behaviour itself is left alone — it is a documented limitation of the experimental `ReaderExecutor` with a follow-up already noted in the code, not something to change in a CI fix. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115643&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115643](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115643+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not report "Server died" when the server is stalled but alive
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115080 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112393 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel)` on master @ `756b18a3921e` reported a single failing leaf `Server died` while its own aggregate said `Failed: 0, Passed: 10925, Skipped: 164`. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=756b18a3921e9a5daec71d5c4413bfdad78a8275&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%29 The server did not die. It stopped making progress process-wide at `22:14:47` for 116 s, ran for 31 s, stalled again for 107 s, then recovered on its own 89 s *after* the hung check had declared it dead, and shut down cleanly at the end of the job. What the artifacts say about those two stalls: - 0.34 s of CPU burnt across 224 s of wall time, and no `OSCPUWait` either - the threads were not starved, they were parked. - Not one log line, from any of the ~1400 threads, including the embedded Keeper and every `BackgroundSchedulePool` task; on resume they all logged in the same millisecond, and several reported `Execution took` 119-168 s. - The sampling profiler collected 99 samples/minute against a 24000/minute baseline, so the timer signals were not being delivered either. - The co-tenant `seaweedfs` hit its 5-minute heartbeat at `20:16:32.4298`, mid-stall, to the microsecond - the box was fine. - No `<Fatal>` line, no sanitizer report, empty `dmesg`, no failed test. That is a whole-process stop-the-world in the sanitizer runtime, not a ClickHouse deadlock, and it is not something the server can avoid. Root cause of the *report*: `check_server_liveness` spends at most ~165 s (10 attempts, 10 s socket timeout, back-off) and the caller turned "the probe gave up" straight into the abort. A failed probe says the server is not answering; it does not say the server is gone. So the verdict is now split by the evidence that is actually available, in a new `HungCheckMonitor`: - the server process is gone: abort on the first failed probe, at master's latency, unchanged; - the process is still there: keep probing, and only call it a hang after `GRACE_WITH_LIVE_PROCESS = 600 s` of silence. A server that really is deadlocked is still reported, just later, and the extra wait is bounded and small next to a multi-hour job. Not being able to tell whether a process is there (no `ps`, or a server on another host) reads as gone, so master's behaviour is kept whenever there is no positive evidence of a live process. `get_server_pid` picks the first server it can see, so in a multi-replica setup a surviving replica delays the verdict on a dead main server by the grace; it does not lose it. The re-probes inside the grace use a single attempt on a 10 s gate: the retry budget has already been spent proving the server unresponsive, and repeating it would block the parent loop for minutes per iteration. While the server answers, the probe is byte-for-byte what it was. Applied to the incident: the first probe would have failed at ~165 s, the server answered again at ~285 s, and the run would have continued with the other 2000 tests instead of being thrown away. Not claimed: this does not make the stall go away, and it does not touch the `Server died` leaf that #115080 renames or the probe scheduling that #112393 reworks. Both touch the same region, so the second to merge needs a rebase. Validation: `ci/tests/test_hung_check_alive_grace.py` drives the class on a fake clock with the probe and the PID lookup stubbed out - no server, no `ps`. 6 tests; four mutations (no grace, PID evidence ignored, no interval gate, always the full retry budget) each redden a named case. Full `ci/tests`: 817 passed, the 2 pre-existing `test_max_failures_exit_code` failures reproduce identically on pristine master here (they need a running server). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115692&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115692](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115692+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: [#76518] Fix the input table function hint when the column is used twice in insert select
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/76518 `INSERT ... SELECT` from a table function that infers its schema (`file`, `url`, `s3`, `s3Cluster`, `input`, ...) failed when the same source column was selected more than once: ```sql INSERT INTO http (x, y) SELECT size AS x, size AS y FROM s3Cluster(...); -- Cannot add column size: column with this name already exists. (ILLEGAL_COLUMN) ``` The structure of the table function is guessed from the insertion table by mapping every `SELECT` expression to the insertion table column at the same position. When the same identifier is selected twice, the same column was added to the hint twice, which is not allowed. Now the column is added to the hint only once. A source column has a single type, so when the insertion table columns it is mapped to disagree on the type, the hint is ambiguous: it is dropped and the structure is inferred from the data instead, the same way it already happens when an asterisk is mixed with a column list. With `use_structure_from_insertion_table_in_table_functions = 1`, where the hint is mandatory, the ambiguity is reported as an error. Both the analyzer (`QueryAnalyzer::resolveTableFunction`) and the old query interpretation path (`Context::executeTableFunction`) are fixed, because the query failed with `enable_analyzer` set to both `0` and `1`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the error `Cannot add column ...: column with this name already exists` on `INSERT SELECT` from a table function such as `file`, `s3` or `input`, when the same source column is selected more than once. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105982&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/105982](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F105982+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78465 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78465 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a mutation that references the `_sample_factor` virtual column failing mid-execution with `Unexpected const virtual column: _sample_factor` and leaving the mutation stuck. A mutation now reads it as `1`, the same value a query without `SAMPLE` returns. ### Description `_sample_factor` is registered with `VirtualsMaterializationPlace::Reader`, so a reader is expected to supply its value. `ReadFromMergeTree` publishes it into `shared_virtual_fields` and the normal read pool copies that map into every read task, which is why `SELECT` resolves it. The per-part path used by mutations and merges does not: `createMergeTreeSequentialSource` seeds only `_part_index` and `_part_starting_offset`, so `fillVirtualColumns` falls through to a throw. `ALTER TABLE t UPDATE u = _sample_factor WHERE ...` therefore starts, then fails per part with `Code 341` wrapping `Code 16`, and the mutation entry stays stuck. The fix seeds the field where the sibling already does. The value is `1` because no `SAMPLE` clause reaches this path: `used_sample_factor` is declared `1.0` and is overwritten only for an actual `SAMPLE` clause, which a mutation predicate cannot carry. It is a literal constant, identical on every replica, so it is safe on ReplicatedMergeTree and SharedMergeTree. The net change against master is 3 lines of source plus one test. This replaces the analysis-time rejection this PR previously carried, so the guard it added earlier is gone and `MutationsInterpreter.cpp` is now untouched. That guard decided column identity from raw AST identifier names, which cannot distinguish an `ALIAS` over a virtual column from an `ALIAS` over a real `Tuple`, because `ColumnsDescription` deliberately omits alias subcolumns. One of the six holes measured rejected `a Tuple(_table UInt8) ALIAS tup` over a real `tup`, which master and 26.7.2 both accept, so dropping the guard also removes that regression. Scope is `_sample_factor` only, which is what the issue reports. `_table` and `_database` derive from the local storage id, and a mutation persists what it reads, so seeding them could diverge replicas, while rejecting them for every MergeTree would be a new restriction. That design is filed separately, and their current mid-execution failure is unchanged here.
