signal.title: Tag functional tests averaging over 60s under MSan with `no-msan`
signal.text: MSan stateless jobs are the slowest functional-test jobs in CI and sit right at the edge of the 9000 s job timeout. In a recent run the private `Stateless tests (amd_msan, distributed cache, meta in keeper, s3 storage, sequential, 2/2)` job spent 8324 s of its 9000 s budget on tests and was then killed during teardown, even though all 526 tests had passed. MSan is ~5.8× slower than release on the same tests, and the cost is concentrated in a long tail: under MSan, 8 tests take over 180 s each, and the 30 slowest account for ~48% of a sequential shard's runtime. This tags every functional test whose mean duration under MSan exceeds 60 s with `no-msan`, except two tests that would otherwise lose all sanitizer coverage. ### How the set was chosen From `play.clickhouse.com`, over the public MSan stateless checks (`Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, N/M)` and `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, sequential, N/2)`, excluding the flaky-check and selected-tests flavors): ```sql SELECT test_name, count() AS runs, avg(test_duration_ms)/1000 AS avg_s FROM checks WHERE check_name LIKE 'Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, %' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%flaky%' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%selected%' AND test_status = 'OK' AND check_start_time >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY test_name HAVING runs >= 20 AND avg_s > 60 ORDER BY avg_s DESC ``` 351 tests matched. 30 of them no longer exist in `master` (reverted, split into smaller tests, or removed), leaving 321. One of those, `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata`, already carried `no-msan`; two more remain under MSan to retain their only sanitizer coverage, so 318 files change here. Only `OK` runs are counted, so timeouts and failures do not inflate the averages. ### Initial expected effect The following estimates were calculated before retaining the two sanitizer-coverage tests. | Flavor | MSan test time per commit | Removed | Share | |---|---|---|---| | parallel | 129025 s | 24766 s | 19.2% | | sequential | 11236 s | 4108 s | 36.6% | ### 25 slowest of the tagged tests | Test | Mean under MSan | Runs | |---|---|---| | `03988_cached_read_big_at` | 384.6 s | 9014 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_replicated` | 337.2 s | 9116 | | `03008_deduplication_several_mv_into_one_table_nonreplicated` | 308.8 s | 9118 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_nonreplicated` | 282.6 s | 9118 | | `04039_merge_tree_snapshot_teardown_race` | 275.2 s | 9347 | | `01195_formats_diagnostic_info` | 234.6 s | 9278 | | `02475_bson_each_row_format` | 206.1 s | 9264 | | `00626_replace_partition_from_table_zookeeper` | 202.5 s | 9323 | | `01019_alter_materialized_view_atomic` | 192.5 s | 9340 | | `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata` | 190.4 s | 1806 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long` | 182.8 s | 9339 | | `00746_sql_fuzzy` | 180.5 s | 9340 | | `03755_large_primary_key_explain` | 180.2 s | 9337 | | `02943_variant_type_with_different_local_and_global_order` | 180.2 s | 9284 | | `02448_clone_replica_lost_part` | 177.4 s | 9263 | | `02372_analyzer_join` | 176.3 s | 9345 | | `04327_cluster_functions_huge_num_streams_no_crash` | 171.8 s | 9261 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long_oldanalyzer` | 168.9 s | 9346 | | `01079_bad_alters_zookeeper_long` | 166.8 s | 9322 | | `01747_system_session_log_long` | 165.9 s | 9014 | | `03208_array_of_json_read_subcolumns_1` | 165 s | 9339 | | `00429_long_http_bufferization` | 160.9 s | 9277 | | `04411_deep_nested_field_to_type` | 156.8 s | 9262 | | `01383_log_broken_table` | 156.4 s | 9340 | | `03326_protobuf_schemas_race` | 155.1 s | 9279 | (318 tests are tagged in total; the full list is the diff.) ### Trade-off A large share of these are the ZooKeeper, replication, mutation and race tests — precisely where MSan is most likely to find real uninitialized-memory bugs. signal.title: Preserve unchanged TOAST values in MaterializedPostgreSQL
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/83517 Preserve PostgreSQL columns encoded as unchanged TOAST references in `MaterializedPostgreSQL` replication instead of replacing them with default values. The consumer resolves the previous value from an earlier row in the same replication buffer when possible. Otherwise, it reads the current row from the nested `ReplacingMergeTree` by replica identity, batching key lookups to avoid a query per value. The old replica identity tuple is used when an update changes the key. An unchanged TOAST value in a replica identity column is rejected because the replication message does not contain a value that could identify the row. The integration test covers a regular update, multiple updates of the same row in one PostgreSQL transaction, and a replica identity change. The user-facing documentation is updated for both `MaterializedPostgreSQL` engines. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `MaterializedPostgreSQL` now preserves unchanged PostgreSQL `TOAST` values during updates instead of replacing them with default values. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111552](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111552+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not treat a cast to String from a type that can hold NULL as safe
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115294 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Code: 349. Cannot convert NULL value to non-Nullable type` when a `has` or `notHas` predicate carries a NULL array element and the primary key is a `String`, `Array(String)` or `Map(String, String)`, and fixed wrong results when that element is a `Dynamic` or `Variant` holding NULL. The NULL is now dropped from the set during key analysis, as it already was for other key types. ### Description No related open issue. Reproduces on 26.7.4.55: ```sql CREATE TABLE a3 (k String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO a3 VALUES ('a'); SELECT count() FROM a3 WHERE has([CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(String)')], k); -- Code: 349. Cannot convert NULL value to non-Nullable type. ``` `ENGINE = Memory` answers `0` for the same data, and key analysis raises the error, so no rewrite avoids it. `canBeSafelyCast` declared `Nullable(X) -> String` safe, but `String` cannot hold a NULL. `tryPrepareSetColumnsForIndex` trusts that and exits early through the non-accurate `castColumn`, which throws. Every other target answers "not safe" and routes to `castColumnAccurateOrNull`, which filters unrepresentable elements out; this pair never reached it. `Array` and `Map` inherit it by recursion. The switch made the same claim for `Dynamic` and `Variant`, which carry NULL in a discriminator. There it gave wrong results rather than an error: the NULL became `''`, entered the set index and pruned away rows keyed `''`. A `Nullable` target represents it, so those two stay safe against one. That routes more targets into `castColumnAccurateOrNull`, which refuses a target it cannot wrap in `Nullable`. All four guards over such a cast tested only the outer type, so a `Tuple(Array(String))` key passed and then raised `Code: 43`; the `EmbeddedRocksDB`/`KeeperMap`/`Redis` helper had no check at all. Each now asks the cast about the target, and that helper also strips the `LowCardinality` encoding, as the key-analysis guards did. Scalar, `Nullable`, `LowCardinality` and plain `Tuple` keys keep their pruning; a container key scans when its element is Nullable-nested. Both tests fail without this change and pass with it, 50/50 under randomization. Two of my open PRs touch this. #115294 is orthogonal but appends to the same test, so the second to merge rebases it. #112890 makes two of the same `canBeSafelyCast` changes without these guards, so alone it raises that `Code: 43` for a container key. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115647&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115647](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115647+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signal.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, event_date, event_time, key`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Print invisible characters as escape sequences in Vertical format
signal.text: ### What this PR does Non-printable characters (NUL, SOH, etc.) were silently swallowed in `Vertical` output format. Since `Vertical` is a "pretty" format, C0 control characters (`0x00`..`0x1F`) and `DEL` (`0x7F`) are now displayed as Unicode "Control Pictures" (`U+2400`..`U+2421`, e.g. `␀`, `␉`, `␊`, `␡`), which unlike C-style escape sequences cannot be confused with the literal characters they represent. The new setting `output_format_vertical_display_control_characters` (enabled by default) restores raw-byte output when disabled. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85179 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Display non-printable control characters as Unicode "Control Pictures" in `Vertical` format by default; the new setting `output_format_vertical_display_control_characters` can be disabled to restore raw-byte output. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101774&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/101774](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F101774+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix `clickhouse-local` printing TSV instead of PrettyCompact in interactive mode
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105249 Interactive `clickhouse-local` on master renders query results as `TSV` instead of the terminal default `PrettyCompact`. `applyCmdOptions` seeds the `default_format` setting on `global_context` as the fallback format of the sessions of the embedded protocol listeners (`SYSTEM START LISTEN`), where it must match a real `clickhouse-server` (`TabSeparated`). `client_context` is copied from `global_context` and inherits the seed, and the per-query output-format resolution introduced in #105249 treats a non-empty `default_format` setting as the fallback format, so the seed overrode the interactive display default. (#105249 guarded `--vertical` against exactly this failure mode, but the plain interactive default slipped through: it is the one case where `is_default_format` stays true.) The fix clears the seeded value on `client_context`, in `makeFormatOptionsPrivateToTheClient`, which already handles the mirror image of this problem for the `format` / `input_format` / `output_format` settings. This client renders results from its own `ClientBase::default_output_format`, so the seed is not needed there. Explicit choices keep working: an explicit `--default_format` on the command line is left in place (guarded by `cmd_settings->isChanged`), and a later `SET default_format = ...` or an in-query `SETTINGS` clause lands on `client_context` after the clearing. The served sessions still get the fallback through `global_context`. Verified against the master CI binary (26.8.1.1658, where the regression reproduces): emulating the fix by forcing an empty `default_format` on the client restores `PrettyCompact`, while `SET default_format = 'JSONEachRow'` and `SETTINGS default_format = 'CSV'` continue to be honored. The added `04927_local_interactive_default_format.expect` test fails on current master and passes with the fix emulated; the listener-side default is already covered by `04501_local_http_default_format.expect`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a regression on master (not present in any release): interactive `clickhouse-local` rendered query results as `TSV` instead of `PrettyCompact`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115360&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115360](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115360+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix PromQL query_range step validation for equal start and end
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Reject zero and negative `step` values in one-point Prometheus range queries.** ### Summary Prometheus rejects zero and negative query resolution steps for `/api/v1/query_range`, including requests where `start == end`. ClickHouse currently skips step validation when the timestamps are equal. This means a request such as: `query=vector(1)&start=10&end=10&step=0` can return a successful one-point matrix instead of an error. This change validates `step` for `QUERY_RANGE` independently of the timestamp range. Instant queries keep their internal `step=0` behavior. ### Why this matters Prometheus-compatible clients expect the same validation for one-point range queries. Returning a successful result for an invalid request can hide client-side errors. ### Tests - Add HTTP integration coverage for `step=0` and `step=-1` when `start == end`. - Keep coverage for a valid positive-step one-point range. - Validate the changed C++ translation unit and Python test syntax. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115679&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115679](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115679+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Resume a NATS JetStream subscription after a reconnect
signal.text: A `NATS` table reading from a JetStream stream can stop consuming for good after the NATS server restarts, while still looking subscribed and healthy. An asynchronous JetStream pull subscription asks for more messages only when one is delivered, and when the NATS client reconnects it re-sends the `SUB` line but not the pull request the broker was holding. A broker that goes away without answering that request - a hard kill, a network partition, or a graceful restart that lands in the milliseconds between a re-subscribe and its request being parked - leaves the table subscribed and permanently silent. That is what `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write` hits when the consumer is still behind at the moment the broker is stopped: all 100000 rows were published and acknowledged into the stream, but the ones not yet delivered are never fetched again, so the view stays short of them and the test fails with `ClickHouse lost some messages: 92807`. It fails this way on about 0.2% of runs since the NATS tests came back on 2026-07-30, and at the same rate before and after #112828 recovered the closed-subscription case on 2026-08-13 (88 of 46693 runs before, 27 of 15428 after), which is what points at the window that fix leaves open. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=c260929910ea94be9a359bb69bf5e33d7b3a40e4&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%204%2F4%29 Recovery so far keyed only on a subscription the NATS client had closed, which is what a graceful shutdown produces by answering the outstanding pull request. This reports a reconnect as well, by comparing the reconnect count the client keeps for the connection against the one taken when we subscribed, and re-subscribes through the same path. Only JetStream consumers do this: a core NATS subscription really is restored by the `SUB` line, and re-subscribing it would drop buffered messages nothing redelivers. The recovery is applied both by the background streaming task and by an in-flight direct `SELECT`, whose source retains its consumer until the query finishes. The window this closes is the residual documented in #112828, so `_restart_nats` no longer retries until a restart lands outside it, and a new test reaches that state deterministically with `SIGKILL`, which answers nothing and so leaves no closed subscription to fall back on. Verified locally with a release build, running the module through `ci.praktika`: - new test with the fix: passed twice (65 s, 146 s); - new test with `src/Storages/NATS` reverted to `master` and everything else unchanged: `AssertionError: consumption did not resume, view holds 10 of 20 keys` - the messages published after the restart never arrive; - the five existing restart tests plus `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write`, all six passed with the fix. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112828 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `NATS` engine table reading from a JetStream stream (`nats_stream`) silently stopping to consume messages after the NATS server restarted or the connection was re-established. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115343&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115343](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115343+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Map kv tokenizer minimal
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110757 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110454 Adds a `keyValuePairs` text-index tokenizer for `Map(String, String)` columns. Every `(key, value)` pair of a row becomes one token, so `WHERE m['key'] = 'value'` is answered by a single exact token lookup with direct read, instead of reading the map column. An index on `mapKeys(m)` or `mapValues(m)` cannot do this: it knows that some key exists and that some value exists, but not that they belong to the same pair. This is a minimal first increment of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110757 by @UnamedRus, split up as discussed in the review of that pull request. Only the tokenizer and `m['key'] = 'value'` are here; `m['key'] IN (...)`, `mapContainsKey`, `mapContainsValue`, the `LIKE` and prefix/suffix forms, and the new `mapContainsKeyValue` / `mapContainsKeyValueLike` functions are left for follow-ups. As a result nothing outside the tokenizer, the index aggregator and the index condition needs to change: `TextIndexAnalyzer`, `MergeTreeReaderTextIndex` and `optimizeDirectReadFromTextIndex` are untouched. The token layout is `varint((length(key) << 1) | is_rest) ‖ key ‖ value`. The length prefix keeps the key/value boundary unambiguous, so keys and values may contain arbitrary bytes, and it makes the tokens of one key a contiguous range of the sorted dictionary, which a later range scan can use. `is_rest` marks a key's non-first occurrence in a row, so the lookup matches the same occurrence as `m['key']` when a row contains duplicate keys. Restrictions, all rejected at table creation: keys and values must be `String` or `LowCardinality(String)` (`FixedString` would store padding bytes that a searched constant does not have, silently missing rows), and `preprocessor`, `postprocessor` and `support_phrase_search` are not accepted. `m['key'] = ''` is also true for rows that do not contain the key at all, so that predicate falls back to a scan. This doesn't close issue #110454, because it asks for Map text-index support broadly and this only covers exact element equality. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): New text index tokenizer `keyValuePairs`, which indexes a `Map(String, String)` column directly and answers `map['key'] = 'value'` from the index without reading the map column. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115579&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115579](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115579+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix singleValueOrNull state serialization
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105733 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105734 ## TL;DR `singleValueOrNull` can return the wrong result after an aggregate state crosses a merge, storage, distributed, or generic-format boundary. The function must return: - the value when exactly one distinct non-NULL value was seen - `NULL` when no value or multiple distinct values were seen The old state format stored only the first value. It did not store the semantic flags needed to distinguish these cases. This PR adds a versioned state format that preserves the complete semantic state and keeps old version `0` states readable. ## What was wrong `singleValueOrNull` keeps two pieces of state in addition to the stored value: - `first_value`: whether any value has been seen - `is_null`: whether different values have been seen, so the result must be `NULL` Before this change: - merging a state that was already `NULL` did not propagate `is_null` - serialization stored only the underlying value - deserialization lost both semantic flags This caused two user-visible problems: 1. A state containing one value, for example `42`, could be deserialized and finalized as `NULL`. 2. A state that had seen two different values could be deserialized as the first stored value, even though its correct result was `NULL`. The second case is especially dangerous because it can silently change a predicate result. ## Why this matters `singleValueOrNull` is used by ClickHouse for single-value and subquery semantics, including `ALL` and `ANY` comparisons. Returning a concrete value instead of `NULL` can change the result of a query. This is not only a display issue. It can change filtering and comparison behavior after: - MergeTree persistence - parallel aggregation - distributed aggregation - aggregate state exchange between servers - generic formats such as `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes` ## What this changes - Adds state version `1`. - Version `1` serializes both `first_value` and `is_null`. - Keeps version `0` readable for existing tables and older peers. - Treats a non-empty version `0` payload conservatively as `NULL`, because the old bytes cannot distinguish one value from multiple distinct values. - Adds protocol revision `54493`, so version `1` is used only when both peers support it. - Makes version selection consistent for combinator-wrapped states. - Fixes version forwarding for `ForEach`, `Map`, and `OrDefault` paths. - Updates the Native format and protocol documentation. The merge propagation part is already covered by #105734. This PR focuses on the serialization and state-versioning part. ## Compatibility Existing version `0` bytes remain readable. However, the old format did not contain enough information to recover every historical result exactly. In particular, a non-empty payload could mean either: - one value was seen - multiple distinct values were seen and the result should be `NULL` For that reason, version `0` is handled conservatively. New states use version `1`, which preserves the distinction correctly. ## Tests - MergeTree persistence for a valid single-value state. - MergeTree persistence for a multiple-values state. - Conservative handling of a legacy version `0` state containing multiple values. - `singleValueOrNullIf` round trip through `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes`. - `singleValueOrNullForEach` round trip through `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes`. - `singleValueOrNullMap` round trip through `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes`. - `quantileDeterministicForEach` state round trip through MergeTree. - Versioned type coverage for `singleValueOrNullOrDefault`. - Native format and protocol documentation updates. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Preserve `singleValueOrNull` semantic state during serialization. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115519&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115519](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115519+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Disable 1MB Head prefetch for small random access files (Parquet)
signal.text: ClickHouse have an throughput optimization. If object is small (<20MB), there is 1MB prefetch of object beginning. But there are formats, (Parquet specifically), which are being read from footer. And quite commonly, you don't even need to read rest of object, if statistics in footer says so. So, making prefetch of first 1MB, if it doesn't cover footer as well (whole file <1MB) is not helpful. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Avoid a redundant object-storage GET request when reading random-access formats from object storage. signal.author: UnamedRus

signal.title: Role settings profiles are not enforced on SET ROLE only at session-start
signal.text: ### Company or project name EnterpriseDB ### Describe the unexpected behaviour `SETTINGS PROFILE ... TO <role>` silently has no effect if the role activated with `SET ROLE` (or HTTP `?role=`) mid-session. It fails to change settings imposed by the profile and fails to enforce `CONST`ness of settings that the settings profile locks. The settings profile is only applied if the role is active when the session is initiated. This is surprising and undocumented. <details> <summary>Detailed explanation</summary> Attaching a settings profile to a role via `CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE ... TO <role>` causes the profile's settings and constraints to be applied **only when the role is enabled at connect time** (typically via `DEFAULT ROLE`). When the same role is activated in an existing session with `SET ROLE <role>` (or in an HTTP request with the `?role=<role>` query parameter) the role's privileges and row policies engage, but the profile does not: neither its settings values, nor its `CONST` / `READONLY` / `MIN` / `MAX` constraints, nor its `readonly = N` enforcement take effect. This is not documented on the [`CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/create/settings-profile), [`SET ROLE`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/set-role), or [Settings profiles](https://clickhouse.com/docs/concepts/features/configuration/settings/settings-profiles) pages. It has security implications for anyone building a trusted-gateway pattern where a single service user connects, activates a per-request role, and expects the role's profile (e.g. `readonly = 1 CONST`) to confine the session. </details> ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? Tested on 26.8.1.1731 & 26.3.17.1 ### How to reproduce On Clickhouse 26.3.17.1 or 26.8.1.1731 (tested), such as the default clickhouse container image. Configuration should have `custom_settings_prefixes: SQL_,custom_` (only required for the `CONST` demo): ```sh mkdir -p ~/ch-config.d cat > ~/ch-config.d/custom-prefixes.xml <<'EOF' <clickhouse> <custom_settings_prefixes>SQL_,custom_</custom_settings_prefixes> </clickhouse> EOF docker run -d --name ch \ -p 8123:8123 -p 9000:9000 \ -v ~/ch-config.d:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d:ro \ clickhouse/clickhouse-server:latest ``` ### `readonly = 1 CONST` profile is not applied on `SET ROLE` ``` -- Setup CREATE ROLE ro_role; GRANT SELECT ON system.one TO ro_role; CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE ro_profile SETTINGS readonly = 1 TO ro_role; CREATE USER probe IDENTIFIED WITH plaintext_password BY 'x'; GRANT ro_role TO probe; ALTER USER probe DEFAULT ROLE NONE; -- role is granted but not default ``` Reconnect as `probe` and observe: ``` $ clickhouse-client --user probe --password x --query " SET ROLE ro_role; SELECT value FROM system.settings WHERE name = 'readonly'; SET some_random_setting = 1; " 0 -- readonly is still 0 (profile not applied) -- SET succeeded (would fail with READONLY if readonly = 1 were engaged) ``` Compare with the connect-time variant: ```sql ALTER USER probe DEFAULT ROLE ro_role; ``` ``` $ clickhouse-client --user probe --password x --query " SELECT value FROM system.settings WHERE name = 'readonly'; SET some_random_setting = 1; " 1 -- readonly is now 1 (profile applied) Code: 164. DB::Exception: ... : Cannot modify 'some_random_setting' setting in readonly mode. ``` ### HTTP `?role=` has the same behaviour <details> <summary>Show repro steps for http connections</summary> Same setup as Reproducer 1, with `probe` reverted to `DEFAULT ROLE NONE`. Send an HTTP request activating the role via query param: ``` $ curl -sS -G 'http://localhost:8123/' \ --data-urlencode "user=probe" --data-urlencode "password=x" \ --data-urlencode "role=ro_role" \ --data-urlencode "query=SELECT value FROM system.settings WHERE name = 'readonly'" 2 ``` Note: the HTTP interface reports `readonly = 2` by default for URL-supplied queries (its own convention), not `1`. The role's profile pinning `readonly = 1` should would override this but the profile actually had no effect. Confirm this with a `SET`: ``` $ curl -sS -G 'http://localhost:8123/' \ --data-urlencode "user=probe" --data-urlencode "password=x" \ --data-urlencode "role=ro_role" \ --data-urlencode "query=SET max_threads=3" # (empty body, exit 0 - the SET succeeded) ``` Under a real `readonly = 1` the `SET` would fail with code 164 `READONLY`. Compare with the connect-time variant (`ALTER USER probe DEFAULT ROLE ro_role`): ``` $ curl -sS -G 'http://localhost:8123/' \ --data-urlencode "user=probe" --data-urlencode "password=x" \ --data-urlencode "query=SET max_threads=3" Code: 164. DB::Exception: Cannot modify 'max_threads' setting in readonly mode. (READONLY) ``` The role's grants let the query run. Only the former engages the profile. Dropping `?role=ro_role` on the first URL still returns `SELECT count() FROM system.one` correctly via HTTP-interface defaults, so the test uses `SET` rather than `SELECT` to distinguish "role activated" from "profile applied". </details> ### `CONST` binding on a custom setting is not enforced under `SET ROLE` When connecting directly as a role with a settings profile that enforces a setting as `CONST` and trying to `SET` the a setting, clickhouse reports an error like ``` Code: 452. DB::Exception: Setting custom_pinned_value should not be changed. ``` When switching to the role with `SET ROLE` instead, the setting change is permitted. <details> <summary>Show reproducer</summary> > [!NOTE] > Requires `custom_settings_prefixes` to include `custom_` server-side. Setup: ```sql CREATE ROLE ro_role_custom; GRANT SELECT ON system.one TO ro_role_custom; CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE ro_custom_profile SETTINGS custom_pinned_value = 'pinned' CONST TO ro_role_custom; CREATE USER probe2 IDENTIFIED WITH plaintext_password BY 'x'; GRANT ro_role_custom TO probe2; ALTER USER probe2 DEFAULT ROLE NONE; ``` As `probe2`: ``` $ clickhouse-client --user probe2 --password x --query " SET ROLE ro_role_custom; SET custom_pinned_value = 'overridden'; SELECT getSetting('custom_pinned_value'); " overridden ``` The profile pins the setting `CONST 'pinned'` on the role, but the user is free to rewrite it after `SET ROLE`. Compare with connect time: ```sql ALTER USER probe2 DEFAULT ROLE ro_role_custom; ``` ``` $ clickhouse-client --user probe2 --password x --query " SET custom_pinned_value = 'overridden'; " Code: 452. DB::Exception: Setting custom_pinned_value should not be changed. ``` Cleanup: ```sql DROP USER probe2; DROP SETTINGS PROFILE ro_custom_profile; DROP ROLE ro_role_custom; ``` </details> ### Related: `readonly = 1` does not restrict role membership changes Moved to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115691 ### Expected behavior | Path | Expected (from current docs) | Actual (26.3.17.1 and 26.8.1.1731) | |---|---|---| | `DEFAULT ROLE role_with_profile` at connect | Profile applies | Profile applies ✓ | | `SET ROLE role_with_profile` mid-session | Profile applies (unstated) | Profile does NOT apply ✗ | | HTTP `?role=role_with_profile` | Profile applies (unstated) | Profile does NOT apply ✗ | | `SET ROLE NONE` under `readonly = 1` | Refused (unstated) | Succeeds ✗ | ### Error message and/or stacktrace As shown in repro steps above ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context A "trusted gateway" pattern is to: 1. Connect once as a service user. 2. Stamp a per-request setting (`SET somecustomsetting_confining_access = 'some_confining_scope'`). 3. Activate a role that carries a row policy reading that setting (`SET ROLE <reader_role>`). 4. Trust the role's attached profile to have engaged `readonly = 1 CONST` and to enforce the custom setting `CONST`, so user-supplied SQL forwarded on the same session cannot rewrite either to escape the safeguard 5. Use `somecustomsetting_confining_access` in row-security policies. The undocumented behaviour above makes step 4 silently a no-op. I worked around it. The gateway forces `readonly = 1` itself and relies on grants to confine roles. But the workaround isn't obvious and the failure mode is silent. An incorrectly-designed gateway looks correct, passes casual functional tests, and only fails against a knowledgeable attacker or deeper exploration.

signal.title: Fix AI functions under-reporting provider usage
signal.text: AI functions under-report what the provider was actually called and billed for. With the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1`, a failing `aiEmbed` logs an exception row showing `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`; flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause 1: counters die while unwinding.** `embedTexts` accumulated into a local `EmbeddingResult` returned by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so failed calls are still counted. The providers lost their token counts the same way. **Cause 2: usage read after validation.** `call` and `embed` parsed `usage` only after validating the response body, so a `200` the provider had already billed for reported no tokens once a check rejected it. This is not only a `system.query_log` undercount: `AIQuotaTracker` never saw those tokens either, so `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query` could not trip and a query with `ai_function_throw_on_error = 0` kept issuing billed requests past its cap. **Fix.** One rule in three places: the accumulator lives in caller-owned storage and is published from a scope guard, so every exit reports it. `embedTexts`, `IAIProvider::call` and `IAIProvider::embed` fill an out-parameter instead of returning by value, and both providers read `usage` before the checks that can reject the body. **Not covered.** `aiSimilarity` scores rows only once every batch is embedded, so its row counters are zero on a throwing exit — no row was scored, even though the first row's operands were embedded and billed. A test pins that. The text path also still publishes its `ProfileEvents` at the end of `executeImpl`, so a throwing text query loses them there; https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 adds that guard. **Tests.** Seven integration tests. The six regression tests were each verified to fail with the source reverted and to pass with it restored; the `aiSimilarity` one records a deliberate choice rather than a fix, so it passes either way. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed AI functions under-reporting provider usage in `system.query_log` and in per-query quotas: counters accumulated before a failed request were dropped, and tokens for a response the provider billed for but that failed validation were never counted. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114905&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114905](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114905+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Keep table aliases in stored query bodies when restoring under a new name
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115479 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a bug where restoring a database or table under a new name dropped the table aliases from the bodies of stored views, so reading a restored view failed with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`. Closes #115479. ### Description Closes: #115479 A renaming restore rewrote the table references inside a stored view body but discarded the alias on each one, so the view was permanently broken: its `FROM` named a table with no alias while its projection still qualified columns by that alias. ```sql CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT a.id FROM testdb.t1 AS a; BACKUP DATABASE testdb TO Disk('backups', 'r'); RESTORE DATABASE testdb AS renamed FROM Disk('backups', 'r'); SELECT * FROM renamed.v; -- Code: 47. UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER: Unknown expression identifier `a.id` ``` Root cause: the alias is state on the reference node itself, not on the `ASTTableExpression`. `DDLRenamingVisitor::visitTableExpression` substituted a freshly built `ASTTableIdentifier` for the reference, so every field other than the name was lost, and the formatted body was persisted into the restored metadata. The fix renames the reference in place with `ASTTableIdentifier::resetTable`, so the alias, `parametrised_alias` and `prefer_alias_to_column_name` survive by construction. This is option 2 from the issue. Its `has_uuid` caveat does not apply on master: `ASTTableIdentifier` has no `formatImplWithoutAlias` override there and nothing reads `has_uuid` on the node past parse time, so a stale flag is inert; #114277 already carries the clearing line, so either merge order is correct. `resetTable` itself is untouched, and its only other caller, `InJoinSubqueriesPreprocessor`, requires a non-empty alias. Sibling carrier, so you do not have to ask: `replaceTableNameInArgument` rebuilds the reference the same way for `joinGet`/`dictGet`/`IN`. An alias does parse there but is not resolvable (`SELECT 1 IN (db.t AS a), a` already fails with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`), so dropping it has no reachable consequence and is left alone. `RESTORE TABLE db.v AS other.v` alone does not reproduce: only the view is remapped, so the visitor early-returns. Already-written backups are not repaired. Validated by a new `.sh` test: five aliased shapes plus four boundary controls, red before and green after, plus 50/50 randomized runs. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115645&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115645](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115645+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Remove `WasmEdge` in favor of `wasmtime`
signal.text: Removes the `WasmEdge` WebAssembly runtime, leaving `wasmtime` as the only engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime` has been the default and recommended engine, and `WasmEdge` was only reachable by explicitly setting `webassembly_udf_engine` to `wasmedge`. Keeping a second implementation of `IWasmEngine` alive costs a vendored C++ submodule (plus `spdlog`, which nothing else in the tree used), a second engine backend to maintain, and CI lanes configured to switch the server over to it. What is removed: - The `contrib/wasmedge` submodule and `contrib/wasmedge-cmake`, along with `contrib/spdlog`, which existed only to build `WasmEdge`. - `src/Interpreters/WebAssembly/WasmEdgeRuntime.{h,cpp}`, the `USE_WASMEDGE` build option and its `system.build_options` row. - `IWasmEngine::requiresFuelSpecialization`, which existed only to distinguish `WasmEdge` (no fuel specialization) from `wasmtime`. The per-fuel-mode module cache is now unconditional. - The `--wasm-engine` option of `tests/config/install.sh` and the `WasmEdge` CI job option, so the affected stateless lanes are renamed: - `amd_msan, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → `amd_msan, {parallel,sequential}` - `amd_llvm_coverage, old analyzer, s3 storage, DBReplicated, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → the same name without `WasmEdge` `webassembly_udf_engine` is kept as the engine selector; `wasmtime` is now its only accepted value, and any other value is rejected with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG` as before. Because `WasmModuleManager` is constructed eagerly during startup (`Server::main` → `Context::setUserScriptsPath` → `Context::initWasmModuleManager`), a server whose config still says `wasmedge` will refuse to start with `Unknown WebAssembly engine 'wasmedge', available engines: 'wasmtime'` rather than fail lazily on first use. Silently aliasing `wasmedge` to `wasmtime` was rejected on purpose: it would be a fallback that hides a stale config. Verified locally on an `aarch64` build: `system.build_options` reports `USE_WASMTIME = 1` with no `USE_WASMEDGE` row; all 23 stateless WebAssembly UDF tests pass (including `04259_wasm_udf_enable_fuel`, which exercises both fuel modes and therefore the module cache path simplified here); and a server configured with `wasmedge` fails startup with the message above. No test coverage is lost. `wasmtime` is disabled under MemorySanitizer (false positives from JIT-generated code), which is why the MSan lanes ran with `WasmEdge` — but every stateless test that executes a WebAssembly module is tagged `no-msan`, so those lanes exercised no WebAssembly UDF code; the option only rewrote the server config. The two `*_ast_json_*` tests that mention `LANGUAGE WASM` only round-trip the query through `parseQueryToJSON` and never instantiate a module. On the coverage lane, those tests now run against `wasmtime` instead of `WasmEdge`. On binaries where `wasmtime` cannot be built, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDF support is now disabled entirely. Enabling `allow_experimental_webassembly_udf` makes the server fail during startup with `WebAssembly UDF support is disabled because ClickHouse was built without wasmtime`; it no longer exposes a module manager that can only fail later at runtime. The `wasmedge` mentions left in `docs/reference/settings/server-settings/settings/other.mdx` and in the localized `docs/<locale>/` trees are generated output and are refreshed by the docs autogeneration workflow. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Removed the `WasmEdge` engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime`, which has always been the default, is now the only supported value of the `webassembly_udf_engine` server setting. A server configured with `<webassembly_udf_engine>wasmedge</webassembly_udf_engine>` will not start; remove that setting or set it to `wasmtime`. On binaries where `wasmtime` is unavailable, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDF support is unavailable and enabling it prevents server startup. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115316&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115316](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115316+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add SHARED REGEXP path placement policy to JSON
signal.text: Adds `SHARED REGEXP 'pattern'` to `JSON` type declarations so matching root-relative flattened paths are always stored in shared data instead of competing for dedicated dynamic-path subcolumns. This is useful for high-cardinality path families whose promotion would displace more useful paths. Matching is partial by default, like `SKIP REGEXP`. Set the persisted `JSON` type parameter `shared_regexp_use_partial_match=0` to require full-string matching. Typed paths take precedence over `SHARED REGEXP`; `SKIP` and `SKIP REGEXP` continue to discard matching data. Rules are evaluated against the complete path from the original `JSON` root, including derived sub-objects. The rules are compiled once into an immutable `RE2` matcher, with bounded rule count and pattern sizes. A single rule uses direct `RE2` matching and multiple rules use `RE2::Set`. `JSON` columns without rules keep a null matcher, their existing binary type encoding, and their existing row-placement path. Metadata snapshots are copied lazily only when retained placement provenance actually changes a type. Placement provenance is stored in part column metadata and retained by default through horizontal and vertical merges, wide and compact mutations, column renames, lightweight-update patch materialization, and `Array`/`Nullable`/`Tuple`/`Map` wrappers. Removing a rule therefore does not unexpectedly promote already-shared paths during a later rewrite. Set the `MergeTree` table setting `allow_json_shared_data_paths_repromotion=1` to opt into reconsidering those paths. Policy-only metadata changes inside `Variant` are documented as unsupported. The `Native` binary type encoding uses `JSON` encoding version 1 only when a policy is present; ordinary `JSON` types remain byte-identical version 0. The canonical `JSON` documentation and `Native` format specification are updated accordingly. Testing includes 18 focused unit tests and 9 stateless scenarios covering syntax, partial/full matching, root-relative sub-objects, all supported wrappers, flattened `Native` and `RowBinary` paths, horizontal/vertical merges, compact/wide mutations, renames, statistics, and both lightweight-patch application paths. An 88.6 MB real Elasticsearch `indices_stats` document produced 143,555 flattened paths; all 143,290 paths targeted by `^indices[.]` remained in shared data and none became dynamic. A one-run end-to-end smoke comparison was 1.66 s without the policy and 1.69 s with it, with a 0.055% max-RSS difference; these small differences are noise-level, not a statistical benchmark. **Scope note:** `SKIP`/`SKIP REGEXP` already applied inconsistently between array-shaped and object-shaped occurrences of the same path on `master`, independent of `SHARED REGEXP` (a path skipped when the value at that path is an object could still surface when the value is an array of objects). This PR's fix for `SKIP REGEXP` on dynamically inferred nested objects closes one instance of that inconsistency; the underlying array-vs-object gap predates this PR and is not otherwise addressed here. **Scope note:** for a value dynamically inferred as its own nested `JSON` object (an inconsistent-shape array/object under a dynamic path), a policy-only `ALTER` followed by a plain read correctly picks up the new `SHARED REGEXP`/`SKIP REGEXP` rules for that nested object. A `allow_json_shared_data_paths_repromotion=1` merge or mutation that rewrites such a part afterward does not: it reconstructs the nested object's dynamic-path structure from cached per-column type state that a policy change doesn't refresh, so paths inside it can still be placed according to the rule in effect when the object was first materialized. This is opt-in (`allow_json_shared_data_paths_repromotion` defaults to off) and not fixed by this PR. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `SHARED REGEXP` rules to the `JSON` data type to keep matching paths in shared data, with configurable full-string matching and explicit control over re-promoting paths after rules are removed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114414&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114414](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114414+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add the `logsql` dialect: LogsQL, the query language of VictoriaLogs
signal.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental `logsql` dialect: LogsQL, the log query language of VictoriaLogs, can now be used to query ClickHouse tables with logs. Enable it with `SET allow_experimental_logsql_dialect = 1, logsql_table = '<table>', dialect = 'logsql'` (plus `logsql_database`, `logsql_time_column`, and `logsql_message_column` as needed). LogsQL queries are translated at parse time into ordinary `SELECT` queries, so text filters expect `String`-backed log columns, while the `math` pipe applies raw arithmetic and needs numeric operand columns (`String` field values are not coerced to numbers). Documentation entry for user-facing changes. - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Implementation notes: - Nearly the whole language is supported: the filters (words, phrases, prefixes, `field:value`, `:=`, `~`, comparisons, `range`, `in` with subqueries, `contains_any`/`contains_all` with subqueries, `seq`, `len_range`, `string_range`, `ipv4_range`, `ipv6_range`, `pattern_match*`, `contains_common_case`/`equals_common_case`, `json_array_contains_any`, `i()`, full `_time:` filters with `day_range`/`week_range`, `_stream:{...}` selectors), and the pipes `fields`, `delete`, `copy`, `rename`, `limit`, `offset`, `sort`/`first`/`last` (including `rank` and `partition by`), `stats` (with `by`-buckets, per-function `if`, `switch`, `rate`), `where`, `uniq`, `top`, `math`, `extract`, `extract_regexp`, `format`, `unpack_json`, `unpack_logfmt`, `join`, `union`, `unroll`, `running_stats`, `total_stats`, `len`, `hash`, `coalesce`, `decolorize`, `split`, `unpack_words`, `time_add`, `sample`, `generate_sequence`, `field_values`, `json_array_len`, `json_array_concat`, `replace`, `replace_regexp`, `pack_json`, `pack_logfmt`. On typed (non-`String`) columns, filters that emit string functions fail with a type error instead of applying VictoriaLogs' schemaless per-value matching. The numeric stats functions (`sum`, `avg`, `median`, `quantile`, `stddev`, `rate_sum`) parse the numeric value out of every field value and skip the values that are not numbers, like VictoriaLogs, which computes its stats in `float64`; a numeric column is therefore aggregated with `Float64` precision and not exactly. - The dialect is modeled on the existing `kusto`/`prql`/`promql`/`polyglot` dialects: a parser under `src/Parsers/LogsQL/` builds a ClickHouse `ASTSelectQuery` directly, so all downstream machinery (analyzer, distributed queries, query log) works as usual. Relational pipes map to real SQL constructs: `join` to `LEFT`/`INNER JOIN ... USING`, `union` to `UNION ALL`, `running_stats`/`total_stats` and the `rank`/`partition by` clauses to window functions. - The lexer and the grammar mirror the reference implementation in VictoriaLogs (`lib/logstorage` of `VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs`, Apache 2.0), including Go-style string literals, compound tokens (`foo-bar.com:123/x`), comments with `#`, and the exact filter/pipe syntax. The test queries are reused from the VictoriaLogs parser tests: 675 of its 878 valid parser-test queries run end-to-end against a ClickHouse table, and 605 of its 612 invalid queries are rejected. - The implicit table is configured by the `logsql_database`/`logsql_table` settings (like `promql_database`/`promql_table`). The special fields `_time` and `_msg` are mapped to columns via `logsql_time_column`/`logsql_message_column`, so real tables (e.g. `system.text_log` with `event_time`/`message`) can be queried after setting those. - Word and phrase filters translate to `hasToken`/`match` with token boundaries, so tables with `tokenbf_v1` indexes on the message column benefit from index analysis. - Documented deviations from VictoriaLogs: word boundaries follow ClickHouse tokenization (ASCII alphanumerics; VictoriaLogs also treats `_` and non-ASCII letters as word characters); numeric comparison filters parse `String` field values per row (rows with non-numeric values do not match) and compare typed numeric columns exactly, but the per-row parsing of field values understands plain numeric text only (decimal integers, floats, scientific notation, `inf`/`nan`) - LogsQL-only spellings such as `10KiB`, `1h`, `0x10`, or `1_000` are supported in query literals but are treated as non-numeric when stored in a field value, whereas VictoriaLogs parses them there too; equality with a non-numeric value compares with the native column type instead of VictoriaLogs' string semantics; `count(field)` counts non-NULL values instead of non-empty strings; `pattern_match*` placeholders are approximated with regular expressions (VictoriaLogs uses a greedy matcher with extra boundary rules); `seq()` matches substrings in order without word-boundary checks. - The only constructs that remain `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (with clear errors naming the construct) are the ones with no ClickHouse meaning: VictoriaLogs storage introspection (`block_stats`, `blocks_count`, `query_stats`, `value_type`, `histogram` buckets, `set_stream_fields`, `stream_context`), features that require the dynamic set of fields of a schemaless store (`facets`, `field_names`, wildcard field selectors like `foo*:filter`, stats over all fields like `sum(*)`, `unpack_json` without a `fields` list), `unpack_syslog` (a stateful wall-clock-dependent parser), and `collapse_nums` (its number-boundary rules require lookaround which RE2 lacks). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113207&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113207](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113207+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Perf: use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators.** ### Summary The PromQL `and`, `or`, and `unless` lowering only needs to know whether a value is present at each step. This targets the general set-operator path. The exact-group fast path is separate. ### Changes - Use `Array(UInt8)` presence masks instead of `Array(UInt64)` counts. - Use `groupBitOrForEach` for the per-step presence reduction. - Share the mask expression between `and`, `or`, and `unless`. - Keep the shared set-operator validation and presence-mask construction in a common lowering helper. - Keep the existing NULL filtering and join behavior. - Cover all three operators in the plan-shape test. - Keep the original 8,000-series baseline workload. - Add a sparse fan-in workload with 1,000 matching groups and four physical replicas per group, with `replica` excluded by `on(instance)`. The compact presence mask is built with: ```sql groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values)) ``` Because `isNotNull()` produces a `UInt8` 0/1 value, bitwise OR is exactly the presence reduction needed by the set operators. The aggregate state is a zero-initialized `UInt8`, avoiding the generic `max(UInt8)` initialized-state bookkeeping. ### Benchmark The checked-in workload contains two variants, each using 300 query steps: - Baseline: 8,000 series with one series per matching group. - Sparse fan-in: 8,000 series with four replicas per matching group and staggered 50% sample presence. Queries match on `instance` while retaining `replica` in the physical labels. The second variant exercises the actual per-step presence reduction across multiple rows in each `on(...)` group. ### Benchmark result This operator-step microbenchmark runs the old `countForEach(values)` expression and the new `groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values))` expression over the same workload shapes. - ClickHouse 26.7.3.19 - 200 iterations per case - QPS from `clickhouse-benchmark` - Memory from `system.query_log` | Workload | Before | After | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Baseline | 68.3 QPS, p50 13 ms, 40.0 MiB | 79.6 QPS, p50 11 ms, 30.1 MiB | +16.5% QPS, -24.9% memory | | Sparse fan-in | 119.4 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | 122.7 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | +2.8% QPS, no material memory change | ### Tests - Verified that `groupBitOr` is registered for integer inputs and that the `ForEach` combinator accepts array arguments. - Updated the plan-shape checks for `and`, `or`, and `unless` to require `groupBitOrForEach` and reject `countForEach`. - Existing end-to-end set-operator coverage continues to exercise mixed, NULL, and missing-step behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115224&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115224](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115224+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1796` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.text: Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110761 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `input_format_try_infer_ipv4` and `input_format_try_infer_ipv6` settings (both disabled by default) that allow ClickHouse to automatically infer `IPv4`/`IPv6` types from string fields during schema inference for text formats, following the same pattern as `input_format_try_infer_dates`. --- ## What does this PR do? Adds two new opt-in format settings that allow ClickHouse to automatically infer `IPv4`/`IPv6` types from string values during schema inference for text formats, following the same pattern as the existing `input_format_try_infer_dates` / `input_format_try_infer_datetimes` settings. ## New settings | Setting | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | `input_format_try_infer_ipv4` | `false` | Infer `IPv4` from strings matching IPv4 address format | | `input_format_try_infer_ipv6` | `false` | Infer `IPv6` from strings matching IPv6 address format | ## How it works In `insertIntoSharedData` (`JSONExtractTree.cpp`), after the existing Date/DateTime inference chain, two new blocks attempt to parse the string as IPv4/IPv6 using the already-existing `IPv4Node::tryParse` / `IPv6Node::tryParse` methods. On a match, the value is encoded with its native binary type (`BinaryTypeIndex::IPv4`/`IPv6`) instead of falling back to `String`. ## Storage benefit | Value | As String | As IPv4 | |---|---|---| | `"192.168.100.200"` | 15 bytes | 4 bytes | | `"10.0.0.1"` | 8 bytes | 4 bytes | <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110766&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110766](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110766+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Implement PromQL range functions present_over_time, absent_over_time, quantile_over_time and predict_linear
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/57545 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: implemented range functions `present_over_time()`, `absent_over_time()`, `quantile_over_time()` and `predict_linear()`. ### Description Implements four PromQL functions over range vectors that were previously rejected with a not-implemented error: - `present_over_time(v range-vector)` — for each grid point, `1` if its staleness window contains at least one sample, otherwise the series is dropped. - `absent_over_time(v range-vector)` — an empty vector if the range vector has any samples, otherwise a 1-element synthetic series with value `1` and the labels inferred from the selector's equality matchers (matching Prometheus `absent_over_time` / `absent` semantics). - `quantile_over_time(phi scalar, v range-vector)` — the φ-quantile of the sample values in each grid point's window, computed with the R-7 (inclusive) method (`quantileExactInclusive`). φ outside `[0, 1]` yields ±Inf and NaN φ yields NaN, as in Prometheus. - `predict_linear(v range-vector, t scalar)` — simple linear regression over the in-window samples, extrapolated `t` seconds past the evaluation time. **Implementation** - Two new grid aggregate functions: - `timeSeriesPresentToGrid` — `1` if a window has any sample, else `NULL`. - `timeSeriesQuantileToGrid` — R-7 inclusive quantile over a window (non-invertible summary that collects window values and sorts them in `getResult`). Both are registered inline in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesHelpers.cpp`. `predict_linear` reuses the existing `timeSeriesPredictLinearToGrid` aggregate (the `is_predict` variant of the linear-regression aggregate). - `present_over_time` is wired through `applyFunctionOverRange`'s `impl_map`. `quantile_over_time` and `predict_linear` have dedicated translators because they take an extra scalar argument. - `absent_over_time` builds a per-series presence grid via `present_over_time`, then at runtime counts present series per grid point (`countForEach`) and inverts the result, so it works whether or not the metric exists (a selector on a missing metric is a runtime subquery, not a compile-time-empty one). Output labels are derived from the selector's matchers, like `absent()`. No parser changes were needed — the grammar already accepts these function names and `getFunctionResultType` already returns the correct result types. **Testing**: new parser cases in `gtest_PromQLParser.cpp` for `present_over_time` and `absent_over_time` (`quantile_over_time` / `predict_linear` were already covered); new stateless test `04551_promql_phase3_range_functions.sh` exercising all four functions (present/absent, quantile at φ = 0 / 0.5 / 1, predict_linear at offsets 0 and 60) against a multi-series TimeSeries table, with values verified against Prometheus semantics. **Update: time-varying `predict_offset` / `phi`** `predict_linear`'s `t` and `quantile_over_time`'s `phi` now also accept a per-grid-point-varying PromQL scalar (e.g. `time()` in a range query), not just a constant or single-row scalar. This is handled by two new, self-contained aggregate functions, `timeSeriesPredictLinearVaryingToGrid` / `timeSeriesQuantileVaryingToGrid`, which take the varying value as a 3rd `Array(Float64)` argument instead of a fixed aggregate parameter (ClickHouse aggregate parameters are bound once per instance and can't vary per row). They're isolated from `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase` (shared by ~10 other `timeSeries*ToGrid` functions) to avoid regression risk to those. Since these are public SQL aggregate functions, not just an internal translator detail, they validate that the 3rd-argument array is identical across every row/merged state and throw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` otherwise, rather than silently using whichever array was seen first. **Scope note**: the varying value is normalized to `Array(Float64)` in the translator so it works for `Float32`-valued `TimeSeries` tables too, not just `Float64`. However, the PromQL scalar's *own* grid representation (`fromFunctionTime.cpp`'s `SCALAR_GRID` output for `time()`) is cast to `Array(scalar_data_type)`, which is the *table's value type* — for a `Float32`-valued table, that means `time()`'s own raw values (Unix timestamps, ~1.7e9) already lose precision (~128-unit rounding at that magnitude) before my code ever sees them. This is a pre-existing property of `scalar_data_type` being shared between value-precision and timestamp-scalar-precision, not something this change introduces, but this change is what makes it reachable for `predict_offset`/`phi`. It only matters when the varying value is derived from `time()` on a non-`Float64` table. A bare `time()` (also inside `scalar()`/`vector()`) is rebuilt at native timestamp precision and works; any arithmetic around it (e.g. `predict_linear(m[5m], time() - 60)` or a `phi` normalized from `time()`) would see the already-rounded evaluation time, so `makeVaryingScalarPrecisionSafe` rejects it with `CANNOT_EXECUTE_PROMQL_QUERY` instead of returning silently wrong results — this is documented in the supported-functions tables. Fixing the root cause would mean changing `fromFunctionTime.cpp`'s shared `SCALAR_GRID` representation, which has ~15 other callers — out of scope here. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112842&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112842](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112842+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Offer the `/`-commands of the client, and name them when misspelled
signal.text: Typing `/` at the beginning of the input now shows the client's own commands (`/clear`, `/help`, `/man`) as as-you-type hints, and typing more of a name narrows the list down. `Tab` completes the command being typed, which is also how they are completed when the instant hints are disabled (`--hints 0`, `--highlight 0`, `--disable_suggestion`). Until now these commands could only be found in the documentation; now the prompt itself lists them. A mistake in the name of a command is reported as such, with the commands it may have meant, instead of being parsed as SQL and reported as a syntax error at the `/`: ``` :) /hepl Exception on client: Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unknown command `/hepl`. Maybe you meant: ['/help']. Type `/` at the beginning of the line to see all the commands. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` An argument given to a command that takes none (`/clear now`) is reported the same way. Batch `clickhouse-client` still parses such input as the SQL it is, exactly like it already does for `help` and `clear`; `clickhouse-local` reports it like the interactive client. The commands come from a single list, `clientSlashCommands`, shared by the hints, the completion and the diagnostics. An offered command replaces the whole typed prefix including the `/`, which `replxx` counts as a word break character and would otherwise leave in place. The offer is off for `keeper-client` and `clickhouse-disks`: they reuse the same line reader, and a leading `/` is the beginning of a path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `/`-commands of the client (`/help`, `/man`, `/clear`) are now offered by the line editor: typing `/` at the beginning of the input lists them as hints, and `Tab` completes the command being typed. A mistake in the name of a command is reported with the similar commands suggested, instead of being parsed as SQL. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115039&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115039](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115039+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Store only the keys in the join hash table when no right row is read
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `LEFT ANTI JOIN`, and `LEFT SEMI JOIN` where no column of the right table is selected, only need to know whether a join key is present on the right side. Such joins now build a hash table that stores the keys alone, without a reference to a right row, and release the right-hand blocks as they are built. This makes them up to 40% faster and can halve the memory they use. Controlled by the new setting `enable_join_key_only_hash_tables`, which is enabled by default. --- --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115301&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115301](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115301+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]
