signal.title: Implement PromQL functions max_over_time() and min_over_time()
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/57545 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: implemented functions `max_over_time()` and `min_over_time()`. ### Description Implements `max_over_time(v range-vector)` and `min_over_time(v range-vector)`, previously reported as not implemented. Unlike `sum`/`count`, max/min are not invertible monoids, but they are commutative and associative (merge = `max(a, b)`/`min(a, b)`), so the new header (`AggregateFunctionTimeseriesExtremumOverTime.h`, templated on a bool `is_max_`) reuses `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesSlidingSum`'s existing non-invertible sliding-window fallback (the same two-stacks/recompute machinery already shipped and tested via `deriv`/`predict_linear`) — no new windowing logic was needed. `Bucket == Summary` directly, following `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesToGridSparse`'s (`last_over_time`'s) simplest-case shape, since max/min don't depend on sample order. The comparison is NaN-aware (`candidate > current || isnan(current)`), matching Prometheus's own "a NaN currently held as the running extremum is unconditionally overwritten by the next sample" semantics. Registered `timeSeriesMaxToGrid`/`timeSeriesMinToGrid` in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesHelpers.cpp` and added the two `impl_map` entries in `applyFunctionOverRange.cpp` with `drop_metric_name = true`, matching `rate`/`increase`/`delta`'s convention. **Verified against Prometheus 3.5.0.** **Testing**: new SQL-level test (`04628_max_min_over_time_timeseries_functions.sql`) including an `AggregatingMergeTree` serialize/deserialize/merge round-trip, plus cases in `tests/integration/test_prometheus_protocols/test_evaluation.py` covering both functions over a series with decreases (so results differ meaningfully from `last_over_time`), including a more complex nested query. This flips 13 queries of the PromQL compliance suite from unsupported to passed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112354&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112354](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112354+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add TLP and NoREC correctness oracles to the server-side AST fuzzer
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a lifetime bug in `ColumnAggregateFunction::convertToValues` that could produce incorrect results or an exception for `-State` aggregates combined with `-OrDefault` / `-OrFill` under `WITH TOTALS`, `ROLLUP`, or `CUBE`. The bug was found by the TLP and NoREC correctness oracles this PR adds to the server-side AST fuzzer (internal testing infrastructure, controlled by the new experimental `ast_fuzzer_oracle` setting, with a dedicated CI job running the oracle-enabled fuzzer against the release build). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Not a user-facing feature — this is internal testing infrastructure. --- **Summary** Integrates two metamorphic testing oracles from the SQLancer project into the built-in server-side AST fuzzer: - **TLP WHERE** (Ternary Logic Partitioning): for a query with `WHERE p`, verifies that `SELECT ... FROM t` produces the same sorted result set as `SELECT ... WHERE p UNION ALL SELECT ... WHERE NOT p UNION ALL SELECT ... WHERE isNull(p)`. - **NoREC** (Non-optimizing Reference Engine Construction): verifies that `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE cond` equals `SELECT countIf(cond) FROM t`. Instead of generating queries from scratch (as SQLancer does), the oracles check queries that the AST fuzzer already produces and executes successfully. Applicable queries must be simple SELECTs (no JOINs, DISTINCT, GROUP BY, HAVING, LIMIT, QUALIFY, window/aggregate functions) with a WHERE clause against a real table. Non-deterministic functions are detected and skipped. On mismatch, throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` which crashes the server — making bugs immediately visible in CI. **CI integration:** - New job **"AST fuzzer (amd_release, oracle)"** in PR checks, using the release (RelWithDebInfo) build. - Enabled via `AST_FUZZER_ORACLE=1` environment variable which applies `ast_fuzzer_runs=1` and `ast_fuzzer_oracle=1` as server default profile settings. **Testing done:** - Oracle verified with 1000+ passes on non-empty tables (200–500 rows). - Found a real correctness bug during testing: `WHERE (x > 0) AND -2147483648` incorrectly returns 0 rows on MergeTree (INT_MIN truncated to `UInt8` → 0 in the filter path). <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Adds new oracle-execution paths and a new `ast_fuzzer_oracle` setting inside `executeQuery`, plus new CI jobs/config; although gated behind an experimental setting, it touches core query execution and introduces new failure/exit-code handling that could affect CI stability. > > **Overview** > Introduces an experimental `ast_fuzzer_oracle` mode that runs a new `QueryOracleChecker` after each successfully executed fuzzed SELECT, applying multiple metamorphic correctness checks (TLP variants, NoREC, DQP, identity predicate rewrites, and subquery wrapping) and throwing `AST_FUZZER_ORACLE_MISMATCH` on mismatches. > > Extends fuzzing/CI plumbing to support this mode: the AST fuzzer now preserves oracle-friendly query structure (`oracle_mode`), the client/fuzzer job detects oracle mismatches via a dedicated exit code with better log artifact upload, and PR/Master workflows add a new **"AST fuzzer (amd_release, oracle)"** job plus fuzzer config tweaks to enable the setting during that run. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 840494d51c91400e72706015de939dd1b2f0140f. signal.title: Add the `default_session_user` server setting
signal.text: Adds a way to configure which user is assumed when a client connects without specifying a user name, instead of the hardcoded `default`. - A new server setting, `default_session_user` (default `default`), is applied when the user name is empty: an HTTP request without the `user` parameter and `X-ClickHouse-User` header (including Basic credentials with an empty username and a key without a user), a native protocol `Hello` packet with an empty user name (previously rejected, now accepted), MySQL and PostgreSQL handshakes with an empty user name, a gRPC query without `user_name`, an Arrow Flight call without an `authorization` header (or with Basic credentials with an empty user name), and the web terminal auth message without a user field. Setting the value to an empty string prohibits connections without a user name. HTTP handlers with a fixed user (the `user` key inside `handler` of an `http_handlers` rule, or the `user` key of a `prometheus` protocol) authenticate as their configured user and ignore the setting, including the empty reject mode. - Composable protocol endpoints (the `protocols` section) can override the setting per endpoint with a `default_session_user` key, so different listening ports can serve different anonymous users. The key is looked up from the endpoint's module through `impl` references, and the endpoint is restarted on config reload when the value changes. - Interserver connections never use the default session user: they identify themselves with a special marker instead of a user name and are authenticated by the cluster secret and the initial user. Configuring `default_session_user` on an `interserver` composable protocol is rejected as a configuration error. The `NativeProtocol.md` specification and the composable protocols documentation are updated accordingly. Covered by the new integration test `test_default_session_user` (all protocols including gRPC and Arrow Flight, per-endpoint overrides, the explicit reject mode, fixed-user handlers on an endpoint with the reject mode, and a two-node cluster with a secret verifying that remote queries still run as the initiating user). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added the `default_session_user` server setting: the user to authenticate as when a client connects without specifying a user name (previously hardcoded to `default`; the native, MySQL, and PostgreSQL protocols now accept an empty user name instead of rejecting it, and Arrow Flight honors the setting instead of its own hardcoded `default`). Composable protocol endpoints in the `protocols` section can override it per endpoint with a `default_session_user` key, so different listening ports can serve different anonymous users. Setting it to an empty string prohibits connections without a user name. Interserver connections never use the default session user. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110179&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110179](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110179+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` takes no merge guard and collides with a concurrent merge on the same temporary directory: `Temporary part tmp_merge_all_1_1_1 already added`
signal.text: ### Describe the bug `MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun` runs a real `MergeTask`, but unlike the real optimize and merge paths it takes no `CurrentlyMergingPartsTagger` and no merge lock, so it never registers its source parts as being merged. A concurrent merge (background, or another `DRY RUN`) over the same parts therefore computes the same result part name and reserves the same `tmp_merge_<result>` directory. The second reservation trips `TemporaryParts::add`: ``` Logical error: 'Temporary part tmp_merge_all_1_1_1 already added' ``` This aborts the server on debug and sanitizer builds. On a release build it is a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception, so the `OPTIMIZE` fails instead. ### How to reproduce * ClickHouse version: `26.8.1.1` (git hash `199c583bffc735ff2994f9fee1c9dcc6d3b746c6`), reproduced on all sanitizers and both architectures. * Non-default settings: none required. Reached whenever `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` overlaps a merge on the same parts. Failing query, from the AST fuzzer in `Stress test (amd_debug)`: ```sql OPTIMIZE TABLE table_for_concurrent_alter DRY RUN PARTS 'all_1_1_0' CLEANUP ``` `query_log` for that server shows 9 concurrent `OPTIMIZE TABLE table_for_concurrent_alter` statements against the same table inside the same second (`10:41:57.016` .. `10:41:57.371`, mixing plain, `FINAL` and `CLEANUP`), so the dry run and a real merge over the same source parts overlap. Race window: `MergeTask::ExecuteAndFinalizeHorizontalPart::prepare` computes `local_tmp_prefix + future_part->name` and calls `getTemporaryPartDirectoryHolder` on it. For the dry run the suffix is empty, so the name is byte-identical to the name the real merge of the same parts derives. ### Expected behavior `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` is side-effect free by contract, so it must never make a concurrent merge fail, and must never abort the server. ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 2026.08.11 10:41:57.462234 [ 10293 ] {4dbac054-4094-40cf-a43d-b223bafe8dfa} <Fatal> : Logical error: 'Temporary part tmp_merge_all_1_1_1 already added'. 2026.08.11 10:41:57.463010 [ 10293 ] {4dbac054-4094-40cf-a43d-b223bafe8dfa} <Fatal> : Format string: 'Temporary part {} already added'. 5. src/Storages/MergeTree/TemporaryParts.cpp:28:15: DB::TemporaryParts::add(String const&) 6. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeData.cpp:3888:21: DB::MergeTreeData::getTemporaryPartDirectoryHolder(String const&) const 7. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeData.cpp:3939:44: DB::MergeTreeData::claimTemporaryPartDirectory(std::shared_ptr<DB::IDisk> const&, String const&, bool) const 8. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp:587:66: DB::MergeTask::ExecuteAndFinalizeHorizontalPart::prepare() const 9. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp:1293:16: DB::MergeTask::ExecuteAndFinalizeHorizontalPart::execute() 10. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp:2620:24: DB::MergeTask::execute() 11. src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.h:622:18: DB::MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun(...) 12. src/Interpreters/InterpreterOptimizeQuery.cpp:135:26: DB::InterpreterOptimizeQuery::execute() 13. src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:1956:40: DB::executeQueryImpl(...) 15. src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:2373:27: DB::executeASTFuzzerQueries(...) ``` ### CI occurrences CIDB `default.checks`, 30-day window, `test_name LIKE '%Temporary part%already added%'`: 17 rows, 17 distinct pull requests, none on master, first `2026-07-17 20:22:10`, last `2026-08-11 08:23:45`. Every architecture and sanitizer is represented (`amd_debug`, `amd_tsan`, `amd_msan`, `arm_debug`, `arm_release`, `arm_tsan`, `arm_msan`, `arm_asan_ubsan, s3`), all in `Stress test (*)`. 15 of the 17 carry `optimizeDryRun` on the throwing thread. The remaining 2 throw from the real merge side of the same collision, so the dry run is the holder rather than the victim: `StorageMergeTree::optimize` -> `MergePlainMergeTreeTask` (PR 102499), and `MergeFromLogEntryTask::executeInnerTask` -> `ReplicatedMergeMutateTaskBase` (PR 111842). CIDB does not record who held the directory, so for those two the holder is inferred rather than proven. Sample report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112788&sha=fefac8e9d3ccc43a53f8091e8d07a29b6d4761d2&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 Filed at the request of @alexey-milovidov in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112788#issuecomment-5260029553. The earlier issue for the same message, #86050, was closed as completed on 2026-02-08; #91132 was closed on the same grounds, attributed to #91792 (`MergePlainMergeTreeTask`). Neither covers the `optimizeDryRun` producer, whose first CI sighting is 2026-07-17. ### Fix My open PR #110916 fixes this by naming the throwaway dry-run directory `tmp_merge_dry_run_<uuid>` instead of after the result part, which makes the collision impossible on both `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`. The guard is still absent from master (`DRY_RUN_TEMP_INFIX` has 0 hits in `src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.h` on `origin/master`).

signal.title: Use bloom filter skip index for arrayJoin(col) IN (set) and arrayJoin(col) = const
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109516 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109844 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `bloom_filter` skip index on an `Array` column is now used for `arrayJoin(column) IN (set)`, `arrayJoin(column) GLOBAL IN (set)` and `arrayJoin(column) = const`, the same way it was already used for `hasAny(column, set)` and `has(column, const)`. Previously these `arrayJoin ...` forms fell back to a full scan. ### Description `MergeTreeIndexConditionBloomFilter` only accepted the argument of `IN` / `=` as an indexed column directly or one of a few wrappers (`tuple`, map subcolumns, JSON paths). `arrayJoin(tags)` matched none, so the atom became `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` and nothing was pruned, while `hasAny(tags, ...)` / `has(tags, ...)` already pruned. This PR recognizes `arrayJoin(indexed_array_column)` on the left side and maps: - `arrayJoin(arr) IN (set)` (and `GLOBAL IN`) to the same granule test as `hasAny(arr, set_elements)` (`traverseTreeIn`); - `arrayJoin(arr) = const` to the same granule test as `has(arr, const)` (`traverseTreeEquals`). `arrayJoin` only multiplies rows, so a granule matches only if one of its array elements belongs to the set / equals the constant, which is what the bloom filter evaluates for `hasAny` / `has`. `NOT IN` / `!=` are intentionally not handled: a granule containing a set element / the constant can still yield rows whose value is outside the set / differs. Both derivations hash the constant after converting it towards the indexed element type, and SQL comparison coerces more widely than that conversion does. Where the two disagree the index was probed with bytes the predicate never compares, or the conversion threw during index analysis. Both are now gated on a proven-matching hash domain: an identical element and constant type, or integer against integer. Everything else is declined, leaving a full scan and keeping a conversion error reachable at execution rather than turning it into pruned granules. Integer widening and a `LowCardinality` wrapper stay admitted, so the pruning this PR adds is unchanged. Verified with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that the `arrayJoin ...` forms prune like `hasAny` / `has`, that `NOT IN` / `!=` do not prune, and that results are identical with the skip index on and off for every declined domain and for the `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` case. Test: `04365_bloom_filter_arrayJoin_in`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109536&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109536](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109536+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add a full-featured AI agent to the client (the `?` command)
signal.text: Turns the primitive `??` "generate one SQL query" helper in the client into a full interactive AI agent, available with a single `?` (`??` is kept as an alias). The agent works over a live connection: it is given the context of the recent queries in the session (with results truncated to the first and last lines to save tokens, plus error messages) and can use tools to read the query history from `system.user_query_log`, inspect the schema (`SHOW`/`DESCRIBE`/`SHOW CREATE`), consult the embedded documentation (`system.documentation`, the same source as the `help` command), run read-only queries without confirmation under a sandbox (`readonly = 1`, a 30-second and a 10 GiB limit, no table functions reaching outside of the server's tables; if the session forbids applying these limits, the query fails instead of running without them), and run any other query after asking the user for confirmation. Queries it runs are echoed and executed on the user's connection and displayed exactly as if the user had typed them; it prints its thoughts and tool calls as it works, and the conversation keeps its context across `?` invocations within a session. When no client-side AI provider is configured (neither the `ai` section of the client configuration nor the `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variables), the agent falls back to the server-side `aiGenerate` function of the connected server (or of `clickhouse-local`) when it has default credentials configured for it (`ai_function_text_default_credentials`), so it works with no client-side setup when the administrator has already enabled AI functions. Implementation lives in `src/Client/AI/`: the agent loop (`AIAgent`), two model backends (`AIAgentTransport`: native tool-calling via `ai-sdk-cpp`, and a text tool-call protocol on top of `aiGenerate`), the tools (`AIAgentTools`), the read-only statement allowlist (`AIQueryValidation`), and the recent-query context buffer (`QueryContextBuffer`). Unit tests cover the tool-call protocol parsing, the read-only validation, and the context buffer; the end-to-end loop (both backends and the confirmation gate) was validated by driving `clickhouse-local` against a mock OpenAI endpoint. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The embedded AI assistant of `clickhouse-client` and `clickhouse-local` is now a full agent, invoked with a single `?`. It sees the recent queries and their results, explores the schema and the documentation, runs read-only queries on its own (and other queries with confirmation) displayed as if you typed them, and can use the server-side `aiGenerate` function when no client-side AI provider is configured. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114043&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114043](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114043+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Drop stale totals and extremes ports in MergingAggregatedStep
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113708 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not required. The only shape found to reach this logical error needs `inject_random_order_for_select_without_order_by`, documented as only useful for testing and development, so no released configuration is known to be affected. It is fuzzer-reachable (BuzzHouse randomizes it), which is how the abort was found. ### Description Found 2026-08-08 by `AST fuzzer (amd_debug)` (STID 0993-250f, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112384&sha=32e19e343e8bbf3cc8bb41f5bdaad2471caa7c05&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29)) on PR 112384 as a bystander: `Logical error: Block structure mismatch in function connect between Limit and MergingAggregatedBucketTransform`. It aborts in `Port.cpp:22` `connect` from `MergingAggregatedMemoryEfficientTransform.cpp:577`, so at pipeline construction, not execution. `MergingAggregatedStep::transformPipeline` inherited the pipeline's totals and extremes ports, then attached its merging transforms to them. `addMergingAggregatedMemoryEfficientTransform` uses the `StreamType`-less `Pipe::addSimpleTransform` overload, so the getter also runs on `totals_port`. The transform it creates has an empty input header, while that port still carries the aggregate-state header, hence the mismatch. Where the transform is not attached to those ports, the stale port survives into `TotalsHavingStep`, which requires it to be null. The fix mirrors `AggregatingStep.cpp:398-399`, the other half of two-stage aggregation: drop the current totals and extremes, which this step invalidates and are recalculated afterwards. One call before the branch point covers all three merge branches, the extremes stream and all five construction sites. The other caller needs no drop: it builds pipes from `SourceFromNativeStream`, so neither port exists. Reachability decides the category: two `Merge` children must reach the step still carrying a totals port, and the setting named above is the only producer found among candidates measured with an instrumented `hasTotals`. The guard is worth adding anyway, since the state is constructible today. The test asserts the build-time shapes and each arm's merge branch with `EXPLAIN PIPELINE`, plus values against a hand-derivable ground truth. Two unrelated defects, identical on both sides of this change: `Chunk info was not set for chunk in GroupingAggregatedTransform`, owned by #113266, and the same setting over `merge()` loses a child's rows. An earlier revision of this line attributed the first to `MaterializingTransform` dropping chunk info; that is wrong, since it only calls `detachColumns`/`setColumns` and the `ISimpleTransform` default swaps `chunk_infos` through. Issue 113708 reports this guard firing over `merge()` through a set-operation plan with no `MergingAggregatedStep`; that did not reproduce, so this PR does not close it. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114027&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114027](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114027+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Push subcolumn reads into subqueries
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75538 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/92455 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Read only the requested subcolumns of columns exported by subqueries, CTEs and `UNION ALL` branches instead of the whole columns. Ordinary views benefit when `analyzer_inline_views = 1`. For example, `SELECT data.a FROM (SELECT * FROM table)` with a `JSON` column `data` now reads only the subcolumn `data.a` from the table. Controlled by the new setting `optimize_push_subcolumns_into_subqueries` (enabled by default). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) --- When a subcolumn of a column exported by a subquery is requested, it is resolved into the `getSubcolumn` function over the whole column: `SELECT data.a FROM (SELECT * FROM test)` reads the whole `data` column from the table and extracts the subcolumn afterwards. The new query tree pass `PushSubcolumnsIntoSubqueries` adds the subcolumn to the subquery projection and replaces the `getSubcolumn` function with a reference to it. If the whole column is not used anywhere else, it is then removed from the subquery projection by the subsequent `RemoveUnusedProjectionColumns` pass, so only the subcolumn is read from the table. The pushdown works through several levels of subqueries, CTEs and `UNION ALL` branches, and also applies to `Tuple`, `Nullable`, `Array` and other types with subcolumns. Ordinary views benefit when `analyzer_inline_views = 1`. `UNION ALL` subqueries are supported: the subcolumn is added to every branch at the same position, all-or-nothing, and only when the branch types match exactly (the subcolumn of the least supertype is not guaranteed to be the supertype of the branch subcolumns). The `DISTINCT`, `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` modes deduplicate or match rows over all projection columns, so such subqueries are not rewritten (nor are recursive CTEs). The pushdown is skipped when it could change the query result: - when the subquery uses `DISTINCT`, `GROUP BY`, aggregate functions, or `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL` (an added projection column would change the result or would not be valid); - when the subquery is on a side of a `JOIN` that can be filled with default values for non-matched rows (`getSubcolumn` of a default value is not always equal to the default value of the subcolumn type, e.g. for the `null` subcolumn of `Nullable` columns); a shared subquery node (an ordinary CTE referenced several times) found in any such position is ineligible for all of its occurrences; - in the outer query with aggregation, an occurrence of `getSubcolumn` is only replaced when it is evaluated before the aggregation step (`WHERE`, `JOIN ON`, arguments of aggregate functions) or when the whole expression is an aggregation key; - when the column types diverge, e.g. under `join_use_nulls` or `group_by_use_nulls`; - when the whole column is also read in the outer query, including uses by correlated subqueries and uses under a different exported name of the same physical column (`SELECT tup AS x, tup FROM t`, or a trivial `ALIAS` storage column next to its base column), and uses of an exported column the pushed subcolumn is a part of (`SELECT x.b, tup FROM (SELECT tup.a AS x, tup FROM t)`, where the live `tup` export already reads everything `tup.a.b` reads; an export of a sibling or of a deeper subcolumn does not block the pushdown, it reads less than the whole column): the subquery would then read both the whole column and the subcolumn from the table, while extracting the subcolumn from the already read column is cheaper. For a `UNION ALL` target the alias equivalence of exported names is detected in every branch (the pushdown is applied to all branches or to none), so a single branch exporting the same physical column under another name that stays alive blocks the rewrite. The decision counts only sibling subcolumns that are validated as actually pushable into the target (in a side-effect-free dry run): when two subcolumns of the same exported column are requested and only one of them can be pushed (e.g. the other is shadowed by a same-named storage column inside the subquery), nothing is pushed, since the unpushable sibling keeps the whole column alive. - for references of a reused `MATERIALIZED` CTE (`enable_materialized_cte`): the temporary table serves all references of the CTE, so pruning the parent column there would require proving that no reference needs the whole column. Single-use materialized CTEs are inlined by the analyzer and take the ordinary subquery path (subcolumn reads over materialized CTEs are currently broken on master independently of this change, see https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113623). Subqueries spelled with an alias list, e.g. `SELECT x.a FROM (SELECT json FROM t) AS s(x)`, are supported. Trivial `ALIAS` columns (an `ALIAS` whose body is just another column of the same table, possibly chained) exported by a subquery are followed down to the underlying storage column. A subquery can also export a derived subcolumn (e.g. `SELECT json.a AS x FROM ...` over a deeper subquery keeps a `getSubcolumn(json, 'a')` projection expression); reading a subcolumn of such an export composes the paths (`a` + `b` -> `a.b`), so the pushdown continues through derived exports down to the base table. Conversely, when no name of such an alias-equivalent class of exports remains referenced in the outer queries, the never-referenced sibling exports are dead together with the replaced ones (all of them are removed by `RemoveUnusedProjectionColumns`), so they do not block the pushdown through the deeper levels of subqueries; the alias-equivalent classes are taken from every branch of a `UNION ALL` target. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112688&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112688](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112688+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix substreams cache key collision between streams of one column
signal.text: The substreams cache was keyed by the subcolumn name, which escapes nothing, so two streams of one column could share a cache slot even when their files differ: for `Array(Tuple(`size0` UInt64))` the array sizes are written to `c.size0` and the tuple element to `c%2Esize0`, and both render to the cache key `size0`. The reader then handed the wrong column to the wrong deserializer - wrong values, `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA` or a logical error - and such a table could not be merged. The data on disk is correct, so existing parts read correctly after this fix. Affected are a `Tuple` element named like an automatic substream of an enclosing `Array` or of a sibling element, and a `JSON` typed path named like a substream of a sibling path or like one of `JSON`'s internal streams. The wide reader uses the cache for every read, the compact reader only for subcolumn reads. `StorageLog` and `StorageTinyLog` use the same cache and are fixed too. Both caches are now keyed by the file name rendering minus the column prefix, which is injective. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115632 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix reading a column that has two streams whose names differ only by escaping, for example a `Tuple` element named `size0` inside an `Array`, or a `JSON` typed path named like a substream of a sibling path. Such columns returned wrong values, failed with `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA` or a logical error, and made the table unmergeable. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115670&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115670](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115670+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Take the Cascades sort limits from the plan, not the ambient context
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115571 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113422 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the sort limits the Cascades optimizer applies to a sort it adds for a subquery. `max_rows_to_sort`, `max_bytes_to_sort`, `sort_overflow_mode`, the external-sort thresholds and `min_free_disk_space_for_temporary_data` were read from the ambient query context, which for a separately-planned subquery holds the enclosing query's values, so a subquery's `SETTINGS` clause was silently discarded in both directions: a tightened limit was not enforced, and a raised one was overridden by the outer query's stricter value. ### Description A scalar subquery gets its own `QueryPlanOptimizationSettings`, but `buildContext` seeded `OptimizerContext::sort_settings` from `CurrentThread::get().tryGetQueryContext()`, the enclosing query's context while the subquery is planned. `SortingEnforcer` builds its `SortingStep` from that copy, so every sort limit it carries came from the wrong scope. Further down, the same function already read four other settings from `optimization_settings`, so this was also a two-source inconsistency. Measured on `cc440c911383a00`: a subquery asking for `max_rows_to_sort = 10, sort_overflow_mode = 'throw'` under a permissive outer query returns a value instead of throwing; reversed, an outer query at `10, 'throw'` with the subquery raising it to `1000000, 'break'` throws instead of returning. Both invert with this change, while the no-Cascades control and the top-level-limit arm are unaffected. Every setting involved is experimental and off by default, so this needs an unusual but supported configuration. Same defect class as #113422 (merged) and #115571, at a third consumer; this is the residual I disclosed on #115571. The fix extends that seam: `QueryPlanOptimizationSettings` carries the sort limits and `buildContext` builds `SortingStep::Settings` from them. `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_sort` stays a raw ratio there and is resolved inside `buildContext`: resolving it reads the memory trackers and rejects an out-of-range value, so doing it in the settings constructor would widen that error to all queries. The new test's last two statements pin the surface. The new test covers both directions plus two controls. It fails on master, and reverting only the seeding line while keeping the new fields reddens it again. Also noticed, not fixed here: one `OptimizerContext` holds one `sort_settings` for the whole memo, so a plan with sorts from two scopes uses one of them, where the non-Cascades path is per-sort. Separate root cause, unmeasured under Cascades. The statistics hint and cost-config there remain ambient; those are query parameters, with no per-subquery scope to inherit. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115674&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115674](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115674+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add UUID2 data type with correct sorting
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110066 Introduces `UUID2`, a variant of the `UUID` data type with correct (lexicographic) sorting. ## Motivation For historical reasons, the `UUID` data type sorts by the *second half* of the value. This is unexpected and, in particular, hurts the performance of primary indexes built on `UUIDv7` columns, whose most significant bits are a timestamp: with sorting by the second half, primary-key analysis cannot prune granules by the timestamp. ## What this does `UUID2` stores the 128-bit value as a plain big-endian integer of the 16 canonical bytes, so that natural integer comparison of the underlying value matches the textual (lexicographic) order and the canonical byte order used by most other systems. It reuses the `UUID` column and `Field` representation (like `DateTime` reuses `UInt32`), so sorting is correct with no extra comparison code, and its binary/interchange serialization is the canonical big-endian byte order. - `UUID1` is an alias of the current `UUID` type. - A new setting `uuid_type_version` (default `1`) controls whether the bare name `UUID` resolves to `UUID` (`1`) or `UUID2` (`2`) at `CREATE`/`ALTER` time. The resolved concrete type is materialized into the stored table definition (including nested types such as `Array(UUID)`), so reads never depend on the session setting and existing tables are never rewritten. The default will be flipped to `2` in a later, separate change. - Conversions to/from `String`, `UInt128`, `FixedString(16)` and `UUID`, plus `toUUID2` / `toUUID2OrZero` / `toUUID2OrNull`. - Parity across functions (`hex`/`bin`, `reinterpretAs*`, `UUIDv7ToDateTime`, `UUIDToNum`, `empty`/`notEmpty`, `min`/`max`, hashing, `uniq`), formats (`RowBinary`, `Native`, `JSON`, `CSV`, `TSV`, `Arrow`, `Parquet`, `Avro`, `BSON`, `MsgPack`, `Protobuf`, `CapnProto`, `JSONExtract`) and storage (`generateRandom`, `bloom_filter` skip index). The `UUID` type is unchanged (verified: still sorts by second half, identical conversions, default `uuid_type_version = 1`). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a new data type `UUID2`, a variant of `UUID` that sorts by its textual (lexicographic) representation instead of by the second half of the value. The setting `uuid_type_version` (default `1`) selects whether the type name `UUID` resolves to `UUID` or `UUID2`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110084&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110084](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110084+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Auto-escape XML special characters in from_env config substitutions
signal.text: ### What this PR does When direct config values loaded via `from_env` contain XML special characters (`&`, `<`, `>`), the `ConfigProcessor` failed with `SAXParseException` because the raw value was concatenated directly into an XML string. Direct values are now escaped before being embedded into the XML DOM, so an environment variable can hold any XML-1.0-legal value — including one that looks like an XML fragment (taken as literal text) and one that contains the `]]>` sequence the XML grammar forbids in character data. Existing `<include from_env="..."/>` substitutions continue to interpret their value as an XML subtree. Upgrade note: a direct `from_env` value that was XML-entity-encoded for the old XML parser (for example `a&b`) now resolves to its exact literal bytes and must be set raw (`a&b`) instead. This migration is documented and covered by an integration regression. The contents of a ZooKeeper node referenced via `from_zk` may be a whole subtree. A value beginning with `<` is parsed as an XML fragment (both for a structural `<include>` and for a leaf substitution), which is kept for backward compatibility because earlier versions always interpreted a `from_zk` value as XML. An explicit `<include from_zk="..." yaml="true"/>` parses a non-`<` value as a YAML subtree. Without `yaml="true"`, the value remains literal text, so `<include>` is also the generic "replace this element with the node contents" form and may carry a leaf value such as a secret. Whitespace surrounding that `<include>` becomes part of the leaf value, so direct leaf substitutions such as `<password from_zk="..."/>` or `<some_setting from_zk="..."/>` are recommended when exact bytes matter. Those direct leaf substitutions keep a non-`<` value as literal text using its exact original bytes, so existing *plain-text* scalar substitutions and secrets keep working unchanged on upgrade. There is one deliberate behavior change on upgrade: a leaf value that was XML-entity-encoded to satisfy the old parser (which reparsed every `from_zk` value as XML and rejected a raw `&`, `<` or `>` as not well-formed) is now kept as its exact original bytes. A value stored as `a&b` used to decode to `a&b`, but now resolves to the literal `a&b`; such values must be stored raw (`a&b`) instead. This is documented in `docs/concepts/features/configuration/server-config/configuration-files.mdx` and covered by an integration regression. Upgrade note: the same literal-text behavior applies to direct ordinary-element `from_env` substitutions such as `<profiles from_env="..."/>`. Existing XML-subtree imports in that form must migrate to `<profiles><include from_env="..."/></profiles>`; this is documented and covered by an integration regression. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78835 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry: Fixed direct config substitutions via `from_env` failing when XML-1.0-legal values contain XML special characters like `&`, `<`, `>`, or the `]]>` sequence; existing `<include from_env="..."/>` XML-subtree substitutions are unchanged. An explicit `<include from_zk="..." yaml="true"/>` substitution can read a YAML subtree wherever the generic `<include>` form is used, including inside a leaf element, so it must not be used for a literal secret or setting. Without the explicit `yaml="true"` attribute, a non-`<` value is literal text, but direct non-`<` leaf `from_zk` substitutions are recommended for exact-byte secrets/settings, because surrounding whitespace of an `<include>` becomes part of a leaf value. Values beginning with `<` continue to be interpreted as XML fragments for backward compatibility. Upgrade note: a direct `from_env` value or a non-`<` leaf `from_zk` value that was previously XML-entity-encoded (for example `a&b`) now resolves to its exact literal bytes and must be stored raw (`a&b`) instead. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101773&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/101773](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F101773+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Ask for continuation in single-line mode when query is incomplete
signal.text: ### What this PR does In single-line interactive mode, pressing Enter on an incomplete query (one where the parser reaches the end of input still expecting more tokens) no longer sends it and shows a syntax error. Instead, a newline is inserted into the same edit buffer, exactly like pressing Alt+Enter, so the whole query stays under a single prompt and the arrow keys can navigate and edit across all of its lines. A trailing `;` still forces submission (for example, to deliberately submit an incomplete query and see its syntax error). This replaces the earlier approach that printed a separate `:-] ` continuation prompt and read additional lines, which prevented cross-line editing and could split pasted queries. The completeness check is now passed to `ReplxxLineReader` as a callback and consulted from the `commit_action` bound to Enter. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/64886 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): In single-line interactive mode, `clickhouse-client` now keeps an incomplete query under a single prompt and lets you continue it on the next line (like pressing Alt+Enter) instead of sending it immediately. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (not required for this change) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101785&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/101785](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F101785+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix compiled `if`/`multiIf` on a negative `Time` value
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `if` and `multiIf` returning a large positive value instead of a negative one when a `Time` branch is combined with `Time64`, `DateTime` or `DateTime64` and the expression is JIT-compiled. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115381 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114168 (found there in review; a separate mechanism) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103390 A negative `Time` value read through a JIT-compiled `if`/`multiIf` comes back as a huge positive number: ```sql SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-01:00:00'), toTime64('00:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(1); -- executions 1-3: -01:00:00.000 -- execution 4+: 999:59:59.000 ``` No `SETTINGS` clause is needed to hit this: `compile_expressions` defaults to `1` and `min_count_to_compile_expression` to `3`, so the 4th execution of the expression in a session silently changes the answer. `enable_time_time64_type` also defaults to `1`. The wrong value is ticks `4294963696` = `2^32 - 3600`, i.e. the negative `Int32` tick count zero-extended to 64 bits. Root cause: `typeIsSigned` in `src/DataTypes/Native.cpp` did not list the `Time` family, so the widening cast emitted by `FunctionIfBase::compileImpl` asked whether `Time` is signed, got `false`, and LLVM emitted `zext` where `sext` was required. `Time` is `DataTypeNumberBase<Int32>` and is the only member of the date/time family that widens on this path, which is why the defect is specific to it. `Time64` is included in the same predicate for correctness of the contract: `isDecimal()` matches only `TypeIndex::Decimal32..256` and so does not cover `TypeIndex::Time64` - the same reason `isDateTime64()` is listed separately. No wrong-result carrier reaches the `Time64` half today, so it is not given a test that could not fail. Validation: five wrong-result carriers plus a `Nullable(Time)` case are covered by the new test. The reference values were taken from the non-compiled path on an unpatched binary, so the oracle is independent of this change. With the predicate token removed the test fails on 7 of 13 lines; non-negative `Time`, large-negative `Time`, and `DateTime64` controls are unchanged. 50/50 runs under settings randomization pass.

signal.title: Perf: fuse TimeSeries tag extraction and NULL map
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Build the TimeSeries extracted-tag value and NULL map in one pass.** ## What changed `timeSeriesExtractTag` used to: - scan the groups and build a `ColumnString`; - scan every output string again with `getDataAt(i).empty()`; - build the nullable map in a separate loop. The collector already knows whether the requested tag was found during the first scan. This change lets it fill the final `ColumnString` and NULL map together. - Removes the second output scan. - Removes the separate NULL-map insertion loop. - Preserves the old empty-value NULL behavior. - Keeps the existing `Nullable(String)` result and missing-tag behavior. ## Why this is safe - The collector still uses the same group validation and shared lock. - Present tags write their value and the same empty-value check used previously. - Missing tags write the default string and a NULL bit. - TimeSeries SQL tag construction normally removes empty tag values before storing groups. ## Benchmark Added an isolated workload that extracts an early-hit tag (`tag00`), a late-hit tag (`tag15`), and a missing tag from 16-tag groups. It repeats 4,096 groups over 20 million rows with one thread and a large block size so tag lookup and NULL-map construction dominate the setup. ## Tests - Extended `03779_time_series_tags_functions` to check both present and missing tags with `isNotNull` and `isNull`. - Added a mixed-row test with alternating present and missing groups to verify NULL-map alignment. - Added `tests/performance/timeseries_extract_tag.xml`. - Compiled the changed translation units with the existing Release compile commands. - Ran `git diff --check` and validated the benchmark XML. Related to [#115656](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115656). That PR fuses tag-name and tag-value extraction for `timeSeriesTagsToGroup`; this PR fuses extracted values with NULL-map construction for `timeSeriesExtractTag`.

signal.title: Let the promql dialect keep tokens the SQL lexer rejects
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed PromQL queries with regex label matchers (`=~`, `!~`) being rejected under `--dialect promql`. Closes #115071. --- Under `--dialect promql`, `ParserPrometheusQuery` reads the raw query text and hands it to the PromQL grammar; it walks the SQL tokens only to find where the statement ends. But `tryParseQuery` scans those tokens for lexer errors *before* the parser runs, and `~` is not a SQL token, so the query was rejected before it ever reached the PromQL grammar: ``` $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance="host1"}' Code: 471. ... The name of a TimeSeries table to use with promql dialect is not specified $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance=~"host2|host3"}' Code: 62. ... Unrecognized token: Syntax error: failed at position 13 (~) ``` The equality matcher gets through to a missing-setting error; the regex matcher dies at the `~` with a **SQL** lexical error. It is not specific to `-q` — stdin and `--queries-file` fail identically. The grammar itself already has the tokens (`PromQLLexer.g4`: `RE : '=~'`, `NRE : '!~'`), and the same expression works when passed as a string to the table function, which is what makes the limitation easy to miss. `IParser` gains `consumesRawText()`, false by default and overridden by `ParserPrometheusQuery`. `tryParseQuery` skips its two lexical-error rejections for such parsers, since a token the SQL lexer does not recognise is not an error for a parser that reads the text itself. No call site changes, and any future dialect parser in the same position gets the behaviour by overriding one method. This is safe because the lexer does not stop at an unrecognised character — it consumes it and returns an `Error` token (`Lexer.cpp:546`), so statement-boundary detection still finds the terminating semicolon. Kusto solves the same problem with an entire parallel `parseKQLQuery.{h,cpp}`; PromQL needs only the boundary scan, so a virtual on `IParser` seemed proportionate. Happy to go the separate-entry-point route instead if maintainers prefer the consistency. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Split the release-branch db disk integration job into 6 batches so it fits its session timeout
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108498 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Integration tests (amd_asan_ubsan, db disk, N/4)` runs only on release branches and every shard is cut by its own session timeout: ``` !!!!!!! xdist.dsession.Interrupted: session-timeout: 7200.0 sec exceeded !!!!!!! ``` The split does not fit the budget. The job runs on `AMD_MEDIUM`, where `integration_test_job.py:722` sizes workers as `min(ncpu // MAX_CPUS_PER_WORKER, mem_gb // MAX_MEM_PER_WORKER) = min(16 // 5, 61 // 11) = 3` (confirmed in `job.log`: `ncpu: 16`, `mem_gb: 61`, `-n 3 --dist=loadfile`). The parallel phase gets `session_timeout_parallel = 3600 * 2 = 7200` s, so one shard has 7200 x 3 = **21 600 worker-seconds**, while the integration corpus measures at least **~90 800 s** on master and **~86 500 s** on 26.6 (a lower bound: measured durations cover 1 013 of the 1 044 test modules in the tree) - a quarter of it is **~22 000 s**, i.e. over 100 % of the budget before any scheduling loss. Whichever modules the workers happen to be running when the clock expires get reported as failures, which is why both the failing modules and the failing shard index differ from branch to branch. Measured (CIDB, 12 d, `pull_request_number = 0`); `timeout runs` counts SHAs whose run emitted the `Timeout` pseudo-test: | branch | shard | SHAs | timeout runs | avg test-seconds | /3 workers | % of 7200 s | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 26.7 | 1/4 | 28 | 28 | 21 649 | 7 216 | 100.2 % | | 26.7 | 3/4 | 28 | 28 | 21 567 | 7 189 | 99.8 % | | 26.6 | 4/4 | 47 | 47 | 21 636 | 7 212 | 100.2 % | | 26.6 | 2/4 | 47 | 42 | 21 294 | 7 098 | 98.6 % | | 26.5 | 3/4 | 33 | 27 | 21 410 | 7 137 | 99.1 % | | 26.4 | 3/4 | 35 | 21 | 21 792 | 7 264 | 100.9 % | Those per-shard figures are censored: the run is cut at the budget, so the sum clusters just under 21 600 because the clock ran out, not because the work was 21 600 s. The true demand is at least that. The sibling `db disk, old analyzer, N/6` job runs the same corpus on the same runner with the same sanitizer build, the same worker count and the same budget, and has **0** timeouts (13 263 - 17 445 test-seconds per shard, 61-81 % of budget; 256 master SHAs). That sibling also gives an uncensored measurement of the corpus, since its runs are not truncated. On 26.6 sha `7367c762184ba3f6bce70b7905084f326654e305` its six shards summed to 13 800 / 15 130 / 15 379 / 16 745 / 14 180 / 13 429 = **88 663 test-seconds**, worst shard 77.5 % of budget. Split that same measured total 4 ways instead and a shard needs 22 166 s, **102.6 %** of the 21 600 worker-second budget; 6 ways gives 14 777 s, 68.4 %. This change gives the `db disk` job the same 6-way split. With real measured per-module durations, the assignment produced by the in-tree `get_optimal_test_batch()`: ``` origin/master 4-way: worst 7904s (109.8%) mean 7569s (105.1%) over-budget shards 4/4 origin/master 6-way: worst 5521s ( 76.7%) mean 5046s ( 70.1%) over-budget shards 0/6 origin/26.6 4-way: worst 7462s (103.6%) mean 7207s (100.1%) over-budget shards 3/4 origin/26.6 6-way: worst 5443s ( 75.6%) mean 4805s ( 66.7%) over-budget shards 0/6 ``` 6 rather than 8 follows `e1b6984c9341e96`, which reverted the `old analyzer` sibling from 8 back to 6. The worst 6-way shard sits at about 77 % of budget, so a ~25 % corpus growth re-opens this; 6 is the value that both fits today and matches that decision. Runner cost is roughly unchanged: two more concurrent `AMD_MEDIUM` jobs per release-branch push, each about two thirds of the work of an old shard, against runs that currently burn a full two hours only to be aborted. #### A shard times out with zero test failures The clearest evidence that the timeout is the cause and the test failures are the symptom is shard 4/4 on 26.6 sha `3ffa9682053c719b7e7edd8e94f49d858e4aa7eb`: ``` !!!!!!! xdist.dsession.Interrupted: session-timeout: 7200.0 sec exceeded !!!!!!! ========== 1405 passed, 40 skipped, 31 warnings in 7249.47s (2:00:49) ========== ``` Last progress marker `[gw2] [ 94%]`. Shard 1/4 on sha `7367c762184ba3f6bce70b7905084f326654e305` reached `[gw3] [ 96%]` and reported `7 failed, 1062 passed, 79 skipped, 9 errors in 7302.32s`. So today roughly 4-6 % of each over-budget shard never executes, and the truncation is reported as test failures. #### Two plausible causes that the measurements rule out Memory pressure: `grep -c "Out of memory"` and `grep -c "OOM"` are both 0 on those two `job.log` files, the 4/4 log has no `node down` line at all and still timed out, and the harness's own `OOM in dmesg` check reports zero rows for every `db disk` shard over 20 days. Stale `RAW_TEST_DURATIONS`: 26.7 carries the refreshed table and has the worst timeout rate of any branch (28/28 on 1/4, 28/28 on 3/4). A better duration table only rebalances within a total that does not fit; the static table's 4-way spread is 9 188 / 9 184 / 9 283 / 9 188 s, an imbalance of 1.1 %. #### Batch count alone does not imply overload Two other 4-way integration jobs are healthy and are deliberately left alone: `arm_binary, distributed plan, N/4` (0 timeouts over 258 SHAs, 9 680-11 177 test-seconds per shard) and `amd_cfi, N/4` (0 timeouts, 8 940-11 099). They run the same module set - `get_parallel_sequential_tests_to_run` globs the whole corpus and its only corpus filter is gated on `amd_llvm_coverage`, which neither takes - and their per-shard module counts are in the same range as this job's (arm_binary 239-284 per shard against `db disk`'s 189-229). What differs is the build: they run `CH_ARM_BINARY` and `CH_AMD_CFI`, this job runs `CH_AMD_ASAN_UBSAN`. Comparing the same module measured under both, the median per-module ratio is 2.03 for asan against arm_binary (87 734 s against 44 484 s over 1 032 common modules) and 2.12 against cfi (89 267 s against 42 759 s over 1 038). So a sanitizer build roughly doubles the wall-clock of an identical corpus, which is why 4 batches fit one and not the other. All seven parametrized integration jobs were checked against CIDB; `db disk, N/4` is the only one over budget. #### Notes `.github/workflows/release_branches.yml` is regenerated with `python3 -m ci.praktika yaml` rather than edited by hand, and is committed here so that `_check_yaml_up_to_date` does not have to push a corrective commit. It is the only generated workflow that names this job. Check names change from `db disk, N/4` to `db disk, N/6`, so dashboards, mute lists or saved queries keyed on the old literal stop matching and CIDB history does not carry over. The same rename already happened for the `old analyzer` sibling in `e1b6984c9341e96`. No in-tree consumer hardcodes the old names. This PR's own CI cannot exercise ReleaseBranchCI, so it does not test the change. After it reaches a release branch the `db disk, N/6` shards should show no `Timeout` rows. Release branches do not receive master CI-config commits after they are cut - each runs ReleaseBranchCI from its own committed `release_branches.yml`, and `git rev-list --count $(git merge-base origin/master origin/26.6)..origin/26.6 -- ci/defs/job_configs.py` is 0 - so merging this fixes 26.8 and later, but not the live branches. Could a maintainer apply the appropriate `vX.Y-must-backport` label once this is merged? A version-specific label expands to that release plus every newer active branch, so `v26.4-must-backport` would cover 26.4 through 26.7 in one go. I am not hand-authoring release-branch PRs. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112261&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112261](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112261+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Implement PromQL functions absent and count_values
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/57545 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: implemented `absent` and `count_values`, including range queries and `by`/`without` aggregation modifiers. ### Description Implements two PromQL operations that previously returned a not-implemented error and require result construction beyond transforming a fixed per-series values array. - `absent(v instant-vector)` aggregates sample presence across all input series independently at every grid point and emits one synthetic sample with value 1 only where the input is empty. For a direct selector, including `offset` and `@` modifiers, it performs Prometheus-compatible equality-matcher label inference while excluding `__name__`; complex expressions produce an unlabeled result. Label inference deliberately mirrors Prometheus's historic monotonic `has` map: after the first accepted equality matcher for a label name, a later matcher can delete the inferred label but cannot unlock that name for another equality matcher. An empty exact-match value is canonicalized as label absence, matching Prometheus `labels.Builder::Set`. - `count_values(label, v instant-vector)` unrolls each series' grid values, sets or overwrites the requested value label, groups by label set, grid point, and formatted sample value, counts each bucket, and repacks sparse counts into nullable grid arrays. Both `by (...)` and `without (...)` are supported, including removing the generated label or using `__name__` as the destination. Destination label names follow Prometheus 3.x UTF-8 validation—non-empty valid UTF-8—rather than the legacy ASCII label-name pattern. A new internal `timeSeriesPrometheusValueToString` function reproduces Go's fixed shortest-roundtrip formatting used by Prometheus, including `-0`, `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`. The supported-function documentation for `prometheusQuery` and `prometheusQueryRange` is updated accordingly. **Verified against Prometheus 3.5.0** with direct response comparisons covering sparse range points, inferred labels (including equality/regex/equality ordering and empty exact-match values), grouping modifiers, empty inputs, metric-name and non-legacy UTF-8 destination labels, floating-point label strings, and result ordering. **Testing**: added `test_function_absent` and `test_aggregation_operator_count_values` integration coverage in `tests/integration/test_prometheus_protocols/test_evaluation.py`. All six modified C++ translation units compile locally with zero warnings or errors. The focused queries were exercised against a local `TimeSeries` table and compared with Prometheus 3.5.0. The clean-master integration module collects all 25 tests, including both additions, but no test body ran locally because the Docker daemon was unavailable and the module-scoped cluster fixture failed during setup; containerized integration execution is left to CI. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112795&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112795](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112795+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Push the release changelog and version bump to master directly instead of via PRs
signal.text: Direct pushes to `master` by `robot-clickhouse` are allowed again, so the release job no longer needs a pull request and the `CH Inc sync` / merge-queue round-trip to land its changes. Push them straight to `master` instead. - Patch release: push the generated changelog artifacts (`utils/list-versions/version_date.tsv`, `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md`, `SECURITY.md`, the `docker/keeper` and `docker/server` `Dockerfile`s) directly, dropping the `auto/<tag>` changelog PR. Idempotent — it skips when `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md` is already on `master`. - New release: push the post-release master version bump directly, dropping the `bump_version_<v>` PR and its enqueue. Idempotent — it skips once `master`'s version file already describes the bump (comparing the version, not the file, since `VERSION_GITHASH` is recomputed from the moving tip) and retries on a non-fast-forward. Both pushes re-fetch and retry when the tip moves. With no release PRs left to land on `master`, the merge-queue machinery is removed: `merge_prs`, `_enqueue_release_pr`, `update_release_info`, and the `merge_created_prs` step. AutoReleases' `_assert_no_open_version_bump_prs` guard goes too, since no such PR is ever opened now. The release-branch Release PR (`release`/`release-lts`) is unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113528&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113528](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113528+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Resolve the client hostname in `ClientInfo` on demand
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112496 --> Split out of #112496. `ClientInfo::fillOSUserHostNameAndVersionInfo` resolved the local FQDN through `getFQDNOrHostName`, a blocking `getaddrinfo` that also dlopens the NSS modules. Every `clickhouse local` and `clickhouse client` invocation paid for it even when nothing ever asked for the name, and a resolver that is slow or unreachable sat on the startup path with no short timeout. `getClientHostName` resolves it on first use instead, and `getFQDNOrHostName` caches process-wide, so the readers — `system.processes`, `query_log`, `session_log` and the TCP handshake — see the same value as before. When the name arrives from a peer in `ClientInfo::read` it describes that peer rather than us, so it is kept as received and never re-resolved locally. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The client hostname is now resolved when it is first reported instead of on every `clickhouse client` and `clickhouse local` invocation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115491&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115491](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115491+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: feat(promql): Parse Prometheus Query API POST bodies as urlencoded form
signal.text: The Prometheus Query API (`QueryAPIImpl`) read parameters only from `HTMLForm(settings, request)`, which parses the URL query string. For POST requests with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, the PromQL `query` and range parameters live in the body, so they were empty and clients such as `prometheus/client_golang` saw failed or empty evaluations. `QueryAPIImpl` now uses `HTMLForm(settings, request, *request.getStream())` for POST and PUT so the body is merged with any query string (same behavior as `HTMLForm::load`). `RemoteWriteImpl` and `RemoteReadImpl` keep the default path so the raw body stream is not consumed before protobuf handling. Using the [prometheus/compliance](https://github.com/prometheus/compliance) PromQL harness, the reported pass count rose from **4 / 539 (~0.7%)** to **205 / 539 (~38%)** in one full run—about **+37 percentage points** and **~51×** more passing queries versus that baseline, consistent with POST clients no longer sending an empty `query` from the server’s perspective. signal.title: Never cancel a query before its `max_execution_time` has elapsed
signal.text: `CancellationChecker::appendTask` derived a query's cancellation deadline from the current time truncated to whole milliseconds, and then aligned it up to the 100 ms grid the worker batches deadlines on. The alignment normally hides the truncation, but when the deadline already sits on the grid - one query in a hundred - it adds no padding, and the deadline lands up to 1 ms before `now + max_execution_time`. The query is then cancelled ahead of its own timeout and fails with a self-contradictory message: ``` Code: 159. DB::Exception: Timeout exceeded: elapsed 999.672 ms, maximum: 1000 ms. (TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED) ``` The current time is now rounded up to a whole millisecond instead, which is the direction the code around it already promises: *"Tasks may be cancelled slightly later than their exact timeout, but never before"*. Only the `throw` overflow mode was affected: in `break` mode the checker re-reads the elapsed time before acting on the deadline, so an early wake-up does nothing. This is what makes `02122_join_group_by_timeout` flaky - it asserts that a `max_execution_time = 1` cancellation takes at least 1000 ms, and `query_duration_ms` is measured from a stopwatch that starts before the deadline is computed. The failure shows up as `query_duration 1` becoming `query_duration 0`, always on one of the two `throw`-mode queries and never on the `break`-mode ones. In the server logs of both `Fast test` runs below, the query was cancelled early - at 999.672 ms and at 999.630 ms of its 1000 ms timeout. The deadline computation moved into `CancellationChecker::taskDeadlineMs` so that the invariant can be tested directly: the new unit test checks every sub-millisecond phase of `now` against every phase of the grid, for a range of timeouts, and fails with the old truncation. CI reports of the flaky test: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=gh-readonly-queue/master/pr-113021-93e2851fddb5add7bad5b28bcef780be2f6ff7bb&sha=bef88e3d96ecb0f57a0f8d81f6b7ee2117db19fd&name_0=MergeQueueCI&name_1=Fast%20test - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=gh-readonly-queue/master/pr-110451-2f02abe52a79c02fb554728f14d8fa847dcbc1e6&sha=2eba84a8a12a21c36516158d4fbe9530d3f0af8c&name_0=MergeQueueCI&name_1=Fast%20test The truncation is as old as the checker itself. Before deadlines were aligned to a grid in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95563 the deadline was plainly `floor(now) + timeout`, i.e. early for every query rather than for one in a hundred; and the assertion that catches it was only sharpened from `round(query_duration_ms / 1000) BETWEEN 1 AND 60` to `query_duration_ms BETWEEN 1000 AND 60000` in daf1b4980b1, which is why the flake is recent. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A query could be cancelled up to 1 ms before its `max_execution_time` had passed, failing with a self-contradictory `Timeout exceeded: elapsed 999.672 ms, maximum: 1000 ms`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114559&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114559](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114559+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Allow overriding the HTTP method for SELECT through the url table function and URL engine
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/62352 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `http_method='POST'` — as a key-value argument of the `url` table function and the `URL` table engine, or through the `http_method`/`method` named collection keys — now applies to `SELECT` queries: reads use `POST` instead of the default `GET`, for servers that accept only `POST`. Schema inference follows the configured method. `PUT` keeps its write-only meaning: a `SELECT` through a configuration with `http_method='PUT'` still uses `GET`. ### Implementation notes - `IStorageURLBase::getReadMethod()` now returns `POST` when the configured `http_method` is `POST`. `PUT` still applies to writes only (pre-signed upload URLs, #44326), and `INSERT` behavior is unchanged: `POST` by default, `PUT` when configured. - The write path no longer mutates the shared `http_method` member when defaulting to `POST` — the storage instance is shared between queries, so persisting the write default would have flipped subsequent reads of the same table from `GET` to `POST` (and raced concurrent reads). - Schema inference (`getTableStructureAndFormatFromData` and the URL read-buffer iterator) uses the same effective read method instead of hardcoded `GET`, for both `url()`/`URL` and `urlCluster`. - The `http_method = '...'` (or `method = '...'`) key-value argument is parsed by `StorageURL::evalArgsAndCollectHeaders` alongside `headers(...)`, kept in the `CREATE` AST (so it survives `SHOW CREATE TABLE` and DETACH/ATTACH), validated to be `POST`/`PUT`, and rejected when the URL scheme dispatches to another backend (`file://`, `s3://`, ...), mirroring `headers(...)`. - In the analyzer, the argument's left-hand identifier is excluded from column resolution (`skipAnalysisForArguments`), like `headers(...)`. - Documentation for the `url` table function and the `URL` engine is updated. The new stateless test `04869_url_select_http_method` asserts the method actually used on the wire via `system.query_log.http_method`: default `GET`, `POST` override for both the data and the schema-inference requests, `PUT`-configured `SELECT` staying on `GET`, the `URL` engine path, rejection of unsupported methods, and persistence of the argument in the table DDL. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
